nodes.title: Basis of Presentation
nodes.heading: 16.1.1 Basis of Presentation
nodes.start_phrase: The accompanying consolidated financi al statements have been prepared in accordance with GAAP and include the consolidated accounts of PepsiCo, Inc. and the affiliates that we control.
nodes.summary: The excerpt is Note 1 to PepsiCo’s consolidated financial statements, covering Basis of Presentation and Our Divisions. It states that the financials are prepared in accordance with GAAP, consolidate PepsiCo and controlled affiliates, and use the equity method for affiliates where the company has significant influence but not control; intercompany items are eliminated. Venezuelan subsidiaries are excluded due to exchange and operating restrictions. It defines cost classifications (production-related costs in cost of sales; distribution/storage/delivery and merchandising in SG&A). It highlights the extensive use of estimates (e.g., sales incentives, taxes, share-based compensation, pensions/retiree medical, intangible lives and impairment), noting increased uncertainty from the Russia‑Ukraine conflict and inflation/high interest rates. The fiscal year ends on the last Saturday in December, with a 53‑week year in 2022; North America reports on a weekly basis and all international operations report on a monthly calendar (standardized by Q4 2021). The 2022 quarters were 12, 12, 12, and 17 weeks; amounts are in millions, per-share amounts are diluted, and some prior-period reclassifications were made. The company is organized into seven segments: FLNA, QFNA, PBNA, Latin America, Europe, AMESA, and APAC, and operates via company operations, bottlers, and third parties in 200+ countries and territories, with largest operations in the U.S., Mexico, Russia, Canada, China, the U.K., and South Africa. Divisional accounting policies align with Note 2 except for allocation methodologies for share-based compensation, pension/retiree medical, and derivatives. Share-based compensation is allocated to divisions as incremental employee cost with specified percentages by division for 2020–2022; differences arising from changes in assumptions are recorded in corporate unallocated expenses.

nodes.title: Our Divisions
nodes.heading: 16.1.2 Our Divisions
nodes.start_phrase: We are or ganized into seven reportable segments (also referred to as divisions), as follows:
nodes.summary:
- The document outlines the company’s seven reportable segments (divisions) and their scopes:
  - Frito-Lay North America (FLNA): U.S. and Canada convenient foods.
  - Quaker Foods North America (QFNA): U.S. and Canada branded foods (cereal, rice, pasta, etc.).
  - PepsiCo Beverages North America (PBNA): U.S. and Canada beverages.
  - Latin America (LatAm): Beverages and convenient foods across Latin America.
  - Europe: Beverages and convenient foods across Europe.
  - Africa, Middle East and South Asia (AMESA): Beverages and convenient foods across these regions.
  - Asia Pacific, Australia, New Zealand and China region (APAC): Beverages and convenient foods across these areas.
- Operations are executed via company facilities and partners (authorized bottlers, contract manufacturers, and other third parties), serving 200+ countries and territories, with largest operations in the U.S., Mexico, Russia, Canada, China, the U.K., and South Africa.
- Divisional accounting generally follows Note 2 policies, except for allocation methodologies related to:
  - Share-based compensation
  - Pension and retiree medical expense
  - Derivatives
- Share-based compensation:
  - Treated as incremental employee compensation and allocated to divisions; divisions are held accountable for this cost.
  - Allocation percentages by division (2022 / 2021 / 2020):
    - FLNA: 13% / 13% / 13%
    - QFNA: 1% / 1% / 1%
    - PBNA: 20% / 19% / 18%
    - LatAm: 6% / 5% / 6%
    - Europe: 11% / 13% / 16%
    - AMESA: 5% / 6% / 6%
    - APAC: 3% / 2% / 2%
    - Corporate unallocated: 41% / 41% / 38%
  - Variances arising from changes in assumptions (market-driven and outside division control) are recorded in corporate unallocated expenses.

nodes.title: Our Divisions - Introduction
nodes.heading: 16.1.2 Our Divisions
nodes.start_phrase: We are or ganized into seven reportable segments (also referred to as divisions), as follows:
nodes.summary: Overview of PepsiCo’s seven reportable segments: Frito-Lay North America (FLNA) and Quaker Foods North America (QFNA) for branded convenient foods in the U.S. and Canada; PepsiCo Beverages North America (PBNA) for beverages in the U.S. and Canada; Latin America (LatAm); Europe; Africa, Middle East and South Asia (AMESA); and Asia Pacific, Australia and New Zealand, and China region (APAC), which cover all beverage and convenient food businesses in their respective geographies. The company produces, markets, distributes, and sells via its own operations, authorized bottlers, contract manufacturers, and other third parties in 200+ countries and territories, with largest operations in the U.S., Mexico, Russia, Canada, China, the U.K., and South Africa. Division accounting policies align with Note 2, except allocation methodologies for share-based compensation, pension and retiree medical expense, and derivatives.

nodes.title: Share-Based Compensation Expense
nodes.heading: 16.1.2.1 Share-Based Compensation Expense
nodes.start_phrase: Our divisions are held accountable for share-based compensation expense and, therefore, this expense is allocated to our divisions as an incremental employee compensation cost.
nodes.summary:
- Organization structure: The company is organized into seven reportable segments—Frito-Lay North America (FLNA), Quaker Foods North America (QFNA), PepsiCo Beverages North America (PBNA), Latin America (LatAm), Europe, Africa/Middle East/South Asia (AMESA), and Asia Pacific/Australia/New Zealand/China (APAC)—with clear scope for each region and product set.
- Global operations: Products are made, marketed, distributed, and sold via company operations, authorized bottlers, contract manufacturers, and third parties in 200+ countries and territories; largest operations are in the U.S., Mexico, Russia, Canada, China, the U.K., and South Africa.
- Accounting/allocations: Divisions follow company accounting policies except for specific allocation methodologies related to share-based compensation, pension and retiree medical expense, and derivatives.
- Share-based compensation: Treated as incremental employee cost and allocated to divisions by set percentages (2020–2022 ranges: FLNA ~13%, QFNA ~1%, PBNA ~18–20%, LatAm ~5–6%, Europe ~11–16%, AMESA ~5–6%, APAC ~2–3%); assumption-change variances are recorded in corporate unallocated expenses.
- Pension and retiree medical: Division results include service costs measured at fixed discount rates; differences versus disclosed discount rates are recognized in corporate unallocated expenses.
- Derivatives: Commodity derivatives (agricultural products, energy, metals) are centrally managed; non-hedge-accounting derivatives are marked to market through corporate unallocated expenses, while divisions reflect the economic impact when underlying commodity costs are recognized; no trading/speculative intent.
- Financial performance by division (2020–2022): Net revenue and operating profit/(loss) are provided for each division and in total. In 2022, total net revenue was $86,392 million and total operating profit was $11,512 million, including corporate unallocated expenses of $(2,103) million; Europe recorded an operating loss in 2022.
- Notable items/footnotes:
  - Impairment and other charges related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, brand portfolio impairment, and other items.
  - 2022 “Juice Transaction” gains: $3,029 million in PBNA and $292 million in Europe; total after-tax gain $2,888 million ($2.08 per share).
  - 2021 revenue increases in AMESA and APAC reflect acquisitions of Pioneer Foods and Be & Cheery, respectively.

nodes.title: Pension and Retiree Medical Expense
nodes.heading: 16.1.2.2 Pension and Retiree Medical Expense
nodes.start_phrase: Pension and retiree medical service costs measured at fixed discount rates are reflected in division results.
nodes.summary:
- Explains accounting treatment for pension and retiree medical service costs: divisions reflect service costs measured at fixed discount rates, while variances versus the discount rate disclosed in Note 7 flow through corporate unallocated expenses.
- Describes centralized management of commodity derivatives (agricultural, energy, metals): derivatives not qualifying for hedge accounting are marked to market with gains/losses recorded in corporate unallocated expenses (cost of sales or SG&A). The economic impact is later reflected in division results when underlying commodity costs are recognized, insulating divisions from mark-to-market volatility. Derivatives are used for hedging, not speculation.
- Presents net revenue and operating profit/loss by division for 2020–2022:
  - 2022 total division net revenue: $86,392 million; total operating profit: $11,512 million after corporate unallocated expenses of $(2,103) million.
  - Division highlights (2022): FLNA strong profits; PBNA large revenue and profit; Europe reported an operating loss; LatAm, AMESA, APAC profitable.
- Notes significant items affecting results:
  - 2022 gains from the Juice Transaction recorded in PBNA ($3,029 million) and Europe ($292 million), total after-tax $2,888 million ($2.08/share).
  - Impairment and other charges related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and brand portfolio/other impairments.
  - 2021 revenue increases in AMESA and APAC linked to acquisitions (Pioneer Foods and Be & Cheery).

nodes.title: Derivatives
nodes.heading: 16.1.2.3 Derivatives
nodes.start_phrase: We centra lly manag e commodity derivatives on behalf of our divisions.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines how pension and retiree medical service costs are recorded: divisions reflect service costs using fixed discount rates, while the variance to the discount rate disclosed in Note 7 is captured in corporate unallocated expenses.
- Describes centralized management of commodity derivatives (agricultural, energy, metals): non-hedge-accounted positions are marked to market with gains/losses in corporate unallocated expenses (COGS or SG&A), later flowing to divisions when underlying commodity costs are recognized; instruments are used for hedging, not speculation.
- Provides net revenue and operating profit/(loss) by division (FLNA, QFNA, PBNA, LatAm, Europe, AMESA, APAC) for 2020–2022, plus totals and corporate unallocated expenses; notes Europe’s operating loss in 2022 and significant profit growth in PBNA.
- Highlights special items and footnotes: impairment and other charges tied to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and brand portfolio; 2022 gains from the Juice Transaction ($3,029m PBNA, $292m Europe; after-tax $2,888m or $2.08/share); and 2021 revenue increases in AMESA and APAC from the Pioneer Foods and Be & Cheery acquisitions (see Note 13).

nodes.title: Net Revenue and Operating Profit/(Loss)
nodes.heading: 16.1.2.4 Net Revenue and Operating Profit/(Loss)
nodes.start_phrase: Net revenue and operating profit/(loss) of each division are as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Explains how pension and retiree medical service costs are measured at fixed discount rates within divisions, with variances versus disclosed discount rates recorded in corporate unallocated expenses.
- Describes centralized management of commodity derivatives (agriculture, energy, metals), mark-to-market treatment for non-hedge-accounting positions booked in corporate unallocated expenses, and subsequent reflection in division results when underlying commodity costs are recognized; clarifies derivatives are for hedging, not trading.
- Presents divisional net revenue and operating profit/loss for 2020–2022 (FLNA, QFNA, PBNA, LatAm, Europe, AMESA, APAC), including corporate unallocated expenses and consolidated totals.
- Notes significant items:
  - 2022 gains from the Juice Transaction in PBNA and Europe, with after-tax and per-share impacts.
  - 2021 revenue growth in AMESA and APAC tied to acquisitions (Pioneer Foods and Be & Cheery).
- Disaggregates net revenue between beverages and convenient foods for international divisions and consolidated PepsiCo for 2020–2022; includes a note on revenue share from company-owned bottlers and the margin profile difference versus concentrate sales.
- Details 2022 impairment and other charges related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict in the Europe division, including:
  - Impairment of intangible assets, PPE, credit loss and inventory allowances, and other costs.
  - Total pre-tax and after-tax amounts and EPS impact.
  - Cross-references to related notes for accounting policies and further information.

nodes.title: Disaggregation of Net Revenue
nodes.heading: 16.1.2.5 Disaggregation of Net Revenue
nodes.start_phrase: Our primary performance obligation is the distribution and sales of beverage and convenient food products to our customers.
nodes.summary:
- Disaggregation of net revenue between Beverages and Convenient Foods by international divisions and consolidated for 2022–2020:
  - LatAm: 10% Beverages / 90% Convenient Foods (stable across years)
  - Europe: shifted from 55%/45% in 2020–2021 to 50%/50% in 2022
  - AMESA: 30%/70% (stable across years)
  - APAC: ~25%/75% (20%/80% in 2021)
  - PepsiCo consolidated: moved from 45%/55% in 2020–2021 to 40%/60% in 2022
- Footnote on beverage revenue mix: company-owned bottlers generated ~35% of consolidated net revenue in 2022 and ~40% in 2021–2020; finished goods beverage operations yield higher net revenue but lower operating margins versus concentrate sales to bottling partners.
- Impairment and other charges:
  - Recognition of charges related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, brand portfolio impairments, and other impairments.
  - 2022 Europe division Russia-Ukraine conflict pre-tax charges totaled $1,415 million:
    - Intangible asset impairment: $1,198 million
    - Property, plant and equipment impairment: $125 million
    - Allowance for expected credit losses: $12 million
    - Inventory write-downs: $29 million
    - Other: $51 million
    - Classified as: $140 million in cost of sales, $77 million in SG&A, and $1,198 million in impairment of intangible assets
  - After-tax impact: $1,124 million; reduction to net income attributable to PepsiCo of $(0.81) per share.
  - References to additional details in Notes 2 and 4.

nodes.title: Impairment and Other Charges
nodes.heading: 16.1.2.6 Impairment and Other Charges
nodes.start_phrase: We recogn ized Russ ia-Ukraine conflict charges, brand portfolio impairment charges and other impairment charges as described below .
nodes.summary:
- Disaggregation of net revenue by product type and region (2020–2022):
  - Consolidated mix shifted toward convenient foods: Beverages/Convenient Foods at 40%/60% in 2022 (45%/55% in 2021 and 2020).
  - Regional mix in 2022: LatAm ~10%/90%; Europe ~50%/50%; AMESA ~30%/70%; APAC ~25%/75%.
  - Beverage revenue from company-owned bottlers was ~35% of consolidated net revenue in 2022 (~40% in 2021 and 2020); finished-goods beverage operations yield higher net revenue but lower operating margins than concentrate sales.

- Impairment and other charges recorded in 2022:
  - Russia–Ukraine conflict (Europe): $1,415 million pre-tax (intangible asset impairments $1,198; PPE $125; credit losses $12; inventory write-downs $29; other $51); after-tax $1,124; EPS impact $(0.81).
  - Brand portfolio actions: $648 million pre-tax; after-tax $522; EPS impact $(0.38). Key items:
    - PBNA: $160 related to termination of Bang energy drinks distribution (distribution rights and inventory).
    - LatAm: $71 loss and impairment tied to sale of certain non-strategic brands.
    - Europe: $253 primarily from discontinuing/repositioning juice and dairy brands in Russia.
    - AMESA: $159 from sale/discontinuation of non-strategic investments/brands (investment, PPE, intangibles).
    - APAC: $5 PPE impairment related to discontinuation of a non-strategic brand in China.
  - Other impairments of indefinite-lived intangibles: $1,555 million pre-tax; after-tax $1,301; EPS impact $(0.94). Notable items:
    - FLNA: $88 (baked fruit convenient food brand).
    - Europe: $1,264 (SodaStream).
    - AMESA: $31 (certain Pioneer Foods juice brands).
    - APAC: $172 (Be & Cheery).

- COVID-19 charges (nature and trend):
  - Costs included employee compensation and protection, expected credit losses, upfront customer payments and adjustments, inventory write-downs, returns, and other expenses.
  - Total pre-tax charges declined: $774 million (2020), $148 million (2021), $95 million (2022); 2021 included income from favorable estimate adjustments in some divisions.

- Corporate unallocated expenses:
  - Include corporate HQ costs; commodity derivative and FX transaction gains/losses; business transformation initiatives; unallocated R&D; insurance/benefits; tax-related contingent consideration; acquisition/divestiture-related items; gains/losses on certain equity investments; and other items.

- Other division information (assets and capital spending):
  - Total assets were ~$92.2 billion in 2022 (vs. ~$92.4 billion in 2021); capital spending increased to ~$5.2 billion in 2022 (from ~$4.6 billion in 2021 and ~$4.2 billion in 2020).
  - PBNA and Europe represent the largest divisional asset bases; corporate assets declined in 2022 primarily due to lower cash and cash equivalents.

nodes.title: COVID-19 Charges
nodes.heading: 16.1.2.7 COVID-19 Charges
nodes.start_phrase: Operating profit includes certain pre-tax charges taken as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic related to incremental employee compensation costs, such as certain leave benefits and labor costs, employee protection costs, allowances for expected credit losses and upfront payments to custome rs and their related adjustments for changes in estimates as conditions improve, inventory write-downs, product returns and other expenses.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of COVID-19-related pre-tax items included in operating profit, covering incremental employee compensation and leave, protection costs, expected credit loss allowances and upfront customer payments (and subsequent estimate adjustments), inventory write-downs, product returns, and other expenses.
- Divisional breakdown of COVID-19 charges for 2022, 2021, and 2020 across FLNA, QFNA, PBNA, LatAm, Europe, AMESA, and APAC, with totals of 95 (2022), 148 (2021), and 774 (2020). A footnote explains that certain income amounts (e.g., PBNA in 2021) stem from improved credit loss projections and lower at-risk balances.
- Definition of Corporate Unallocated Expenses, including corporate HQ costs; commodity derivative and FX transaction gains/losses; business transformation initiatives; unallocated R&D; insurance and benefit programs; tax-related contingent consideration; acquisition/divestiture-related items; gains/losses on equity investments; and other items.
- “Other Division Information” presenting total assets (2022 and 2021) and capital spending (2022, 2021, 2020) by division and in total. Highlights include:
  - Total division assets of 88,284 (2022) vs. 86,188 (2021); total assets including Corporate of 92,187 (2022) vs. 92,377 (2021).
  - Capital spending totals of 5,207 (2022), 4,625 (2021), and 4,240 (2020), with significant spend in PBNA and FLNA.
  - Corporate assets primarily comprise cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term investments, derivatives, property, plant and equipment, pension assets, and tax assets; the 2022 decline mainly reflects lower cash and cash equivalents.

nodes.title: Corporate Unallocated Expenses
nodes.heading: 16.1.2.8 Corporate Unallocated Expenses
nodes.start_phrase: Corporate unallocated expenses include costs of our corporate headquarters, centrally managed initiatives such as commodity derivative gains and losses, foreign exchange transaction gains and losses, our ongoing business transformation initiatives, unallocated research and development costs, unallocated insurance and benefi t programs, tax-related contingent consideration, certain acquisition and divestiture-related char ges, certain gains and losses on equity investments, as well as certain other items.
nodes.summary:
- Summary of COVID-19-related pre-tax charges that affected operating profit, detailing types of costs (employee compensation and protection, credit loss allowances and customer upfront payments, inventory write-downs, product returns, and other expenses).
- Division-level COVID-19 charges presented for 2020–2022 across FLNA, QFNA, PBNA, Latin America, Europe, AMESA, and APAC, with total charges declining from 2020 to 2022 and a 2021 income item for PBNA due to improved credit-related estimates.
- Definition of corporate unallocated expenses, covering headquarters costs, centrally managed items (commodity derivative and FX gains/losses), business transformation, unallocated R&D, insurance/benefits, tax-related contingent consideration, acquisition/divestiture charges, and gains/losses on equity investments.
- Other division information providing total assets (2022, 2021) and capital spending (2022, 2021, 2020) by division, plus consolidated totals.
- Separate disclosure of corporate assets and capital spending, noting that the 2022 change in corporate assets was primarily due to lower cash and cash equivalents.

nodes.title: Other Division Information
nodes.heading: 16.1.2.9 Other Division Information
nodes.start_phrase: Total assets and capital spending of each division are as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Summary of COVID-19-related charges included in operating profit, covering incremental employee compensation and protection costs, expected credit loss allowances and adjustments, upfront payments to customers, inventory write-downs, product returns, and other expenses; multi-year (2020–2022) divisional breakdown with totals and a note explaining income adjustments due to improved credit projections.
- Description of corporate unallocated expenses, including corporate headquarters costs, commodity derivative and FX transaction gains/losses, business transformation initiatives, unallocated R&D, insurance and benefit programs, tax-related contingent consideration, acquisition/divestiture-related items, gains/losses on equity investments, and other items.
- Division-level “Other Information” tables showing total assets and capital spending by division (with corporate totals), including a note on corporate assets composition and the 2022 decrease primarily from lower cash and cash equivalents.
- Amortization of intangible assets and depreciation/other amortization by division for 2020–2022, plus corporate totals.
- Net revenue and long-lived assets by country, with totals, and footnotes defining long-lived assets (PP&E, intangible assets, investments, etc.), impairment considerations, and noting 2021 net revenue increases linked to the Be & Cheery and Pioneer Foods acquisitions.
- Beginning of Note 2 — Significant Accounting Policies: Revenue recognition policy stating revenue is recognized upon shipment or delivery when control transfers; merchandising activities are fulfillment costs recorded in SG&A and are immaterial in contract context; certain taxes are excluded from net revenue; DSD policy to remove/replace damaged or out-of-date products.

nodes.title: Net revenue and long-lived assets by country are as follows:
nodes.heading: 16.1.2.10 Net revenue and long-lived assets by country are as follows:
nodes.start_phrase: Long-lived assets represent property , plant and equipment, indefinite-lived intangible assets, amortizable intangible assets, investments in noncontrolled affiliates and other investments included in other assets.
nodes.summary:
- Presents divisional amortization of intangible assets and depreciation/other amortization for 2020–2022, showing relatively stable intangible amortization (total $90 in 2020, $91 in 2021, $78 in 2022) and rising total depreciation/other amortization ($2,458 in 2020 to $2,685 in 2022). PBNA and FLNA account for the largest depreciation; corporate depreciation is modest and steady.
- Provides net revenue by country for 2020–2022 and long‑lived assets by country for 2021–2022. The U.S. is the largest market and asset base; total net revenue increased from $70,372 (2020) to $86,392 (2022). Russia shows a decline in long‑lived assets from 2021 to 2022; some countries (e.g., U.K., South Africa) show revenue changes year over year.
- Defines long‑lived assets as including property, plant and equipment, intangible assets (both indefinite‑lived and amortizable), investments in noncontrolled affiliates, and other investments; assets are reported in the country of primary use. Noncontrolled affiliate investments are tested for impairment upon significant operating or macroeconomic changes.
- Notes that 2021 net revenue increases include effects of acquisitions: Be & Cheery (China) and Pioneer Foods (South Africa).
- Summarizes revenue recognition policy: revenue is recognized upon shipment or delivery when control transfers; merchandising activities occur after control transfer, serve as fulfillment of the shipping/delivery obligation, and are recorded in SG&A; sales, use, VAT, and certain excise taxes are excluded from net revenue.
- States typical sales terms do not provide a right of return; under DSD (and certain warehouse distribution), the company removes and replaces damaged or out‑of‑date products to maintain quality and freshness.

nodes.title: Note 2 — Our Significant Accounting Policies
nodes.heading: 16.2 Note 2 — Our Significant Accounting Policies
nodes.start_phrase: We recognize revenue when our performance obligation is satisfied.
nodes.summary:
- Division-level amortization and depreciation: Presents 2020–2022 amounts for amortization of intangible assets and for depreciation and other amortization by division (FLNA, QFNA, PBNA, LatAm, Europe, AMESA, APAC) and Corporate, with consolidated totals.
- Country breakdowns: Provides net revenue by country for 2020–2022 and long-lived assets by country for 2021–2022, covering the United States, Mexico, Russia, Canada, China, the United Kingdom, South Africa, and an “All other countries” category, with overall totals.
- Definitions and accounting for long-lived assets: Explains that long-lived assets include property, plant and equipment, indefinite- and finite-lived intangible assets, investments in noncontrolled affiliates, and certain other investments; assets are reported in the country where primarily used; investments in noncontrolled affiliates are evaluated for impairment upon significant operating or macroeconomic changes; cross-references to relevant notes.
- Acquisition impacts: Notes that 2021 net revenue increases reflect acquisitions (Be & Cheery and Pioneer Foods), with a reference to the acquisitions note.
- Revenue recognition policy (Significant Accounting Policies, Note 2): Revenue is recognized when control transfers (generally upon shipment or delivery) for beverage and convenient food products; merchandising activities occur after control transfer, are considered fulfillment activities recorded in SG&A, and are immaterial; sales, use, value-added, and certain excise taxes are excluded from net revenue; standard terms typically do not allow returns; for direct-store-delivery (including certain chilled products), damaged and out-of-date items are removed and replaced, with a similar policy for certain warehouse-distributed products.

nodes.title: Revenue Recognition
nodes.heading: 16.2.1 Revenue Recognition
nodes.start_phrase: We recognize revenue when our performance obligation is satisfied.
nodes.summary:
- Presents divisional amortization and depreciation details for 2020–2022:
  - Breaks out amortization of intangible assets and depreciation/other amortization for FLNA, QFNA, PBNA, LatAm, Europe, AMESA, and APAC, plus Corporate.
  - Company totals show relatively stable intangible asset amortization (about $78–$91) and rising depreciation/other amortization (from ~$2.46B in 2020 to ~$2.69B in 2022).
  - PBNA and FLNA account for the largest depreciation/other amortization amounts.

- Provides net revenue and long-lived assets by country:
  - Reports net revenue for 2020–2022 and long-lived assets for 2021–2022, with the United States as the largest market and asset base.
  - Includes detail for Mexico, Russia, Canada, China, the U.K., South Africa, and “All other countries.”
  - Explains what constitutes long-lived assets and that assets are reported where primarily used; notes impairment evaluation for noncontrolled affiliates.
  - Notes 2021 revenue increases tied to the acquisitions of Be & Cheery and Pioneer Foods.

- Outlines significant accounting policies on revenue recognition:
  - Revenue recognized upon shipment or delivery when control transfers.
  - Merchandising activities after control transfer are fulfillment costs recorded in SG&A; sales, use, VAT, and certain excise taxes are excluded from revenue.
  - No general right of return, but company replaces damaged/out-of-date products in DSD and certain warehouse channels; reserves recorded for expected replacements.
  - Describes credit terms (generally 30 days U.S., 30–90 days internationally) and expected credit loss methodology, including forward-looking factors (e.g., high interest and inflation).
  - Notes customer concentration risk, with Walmart and affiliates representing ~14% of 2022 consolidated net revenue.

- Details “Total Marketplace Spending” (sales incentives, discounts, advertising, and marketing):
  - Most incentives and discounts are recorded as reductions of revenue; includes payments for displays, distribution, shelf space, price promotions, and bottler funding.
  - Many programs are based on annual targets; accruals require judgment and are trued up when actuals are known; advertising/marketing recognized as incurred.
  - Longer-term arrangements (e.g., fountain pouring rights) involve upfront payments amortized over economic/contractual lives; remaining prepaid balances disclosed.
  - Interim reporting allocates forecasted annual incentives and certain marketing costs to interim periods based on proportional revenue/volume; changes in estimates recognized when identified.

nodes.title: Total Marketplace Spending
nodes.heading: 16.2.2 Total Marketplace Spending
nodes.start_phrase: We offer sales incentives and discounts through various programs to customers and consumers.
nodes.summary:
- Accounts receivable, credit terms, and expected credit loss methodology, including use of aging, historical write-offs, customer data, and forward-looking factors (e.g., high interest rates and inflation). Notes concentration of credit risk with major customers; Walmart accounted for ~14% of 2022 consolidated net revenue (including concentrate sold via independent bottlers).
- Total marketplace spending and trade promotion accounting: sales incentives/discounts treated primarily as reductions of revenue; programs include in-store displays, distribution gains, shelf-space payments, price promotions, and bottler funding. Accruals based on annual targets, historical experience, and management judgment; differences typically insignificant.
- Longer-term customer arrangements (e.g., fountain pouring rights): upfront payments recognized over the shorter of economic or contractual life; remaining balances of $242 million (2022) and $262 million (2021) recorded in prepaid and other assets.
- Interim reporting policy: allocation of forecasted full-year sales incentives and certain advertising/marketing costs to interim periods based on proportional revenue or volume; annual financials not affected by the interim allocation.
- Advertising and marketing: SG&A classification; spend of $5.2B (2022), $5.1B (2021), $4.6B (2020); advertising expense $3.5B (2022 and 2021) and $3.0B (2020). Deferred advertising components (media/service prepayments, promotional inventory, production costs) totaled $40M (2022) and $53M (2021) in prepaid assets.
- Distribution costs (shipping, handling, merchandising) reported in SG&A: $15.0B (2022), $13.7B (2021), $11.9B (2020).
- Internal-use software: capitalization criteria and components (external costs, direct labor/benefits, interest); amortized straight-line over 5–10 years. Software amortization $123M (2022), $135M (2021), $152M (2020); net capitalized software $1.1B (2022) and $0.8B (2021).
- Commitments and contingencies: recognition when loss is probable and estimable; covers litigation, certain taxes, environmental matters, and contractual obligations.
- Research and development: continued investment to drive innovation; consumer research excluded (in marketing). R&D expense $771M (2022), $752M (2021), $719M (2020), recorded in SG&A.
- Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangibles: not amortized; annual (Q3) or more frequent impairment assessments using qualitative or quantitative approaches. Qualitative factors include macroeconomic, industry, legal/regulatory conditions (e.g., Russia-Ukraine conflict, high interest and inflationary environment).

nodes.title: Distribution Costs
nodes.heading: 16.2.3 Distribution Costs
nodes.start_phrase: Distribution costs, including the costs of shipping and handling activities, which include certain merchandising activities, are reported as selling, general and administrative expenses.
nodes.summary:
- Advertising and marketing (within SG&A): $5.2B (2022), $5.1B (2021), $4.6B (2020); advertising expense specifically: $3.5B (2022, 2021) and $3.0B (2020). Deferred advertising costs (media/service prepayments, promotional materials in inventory, and production for future media) are expensed when first used and recorded as prepaid expenses and other current assets: $40M (12/31/22) and $53M (12/25/21).
- Distribution costs: Shipping and handling (including certain merchandising) reported in SG&A; expenses were $15.0B (2022), $13.7B (2021), and $11.9B (2020).
- Software costs: Policy to capitalize internal-use software after the preliminary stage when use is probable; includes external services/materials, direct employee compensation/benefits, and interest; recorded in PP&E and amortized straight-line over 5–10 years. Amortization: $123M (2022), $135M (2021), $152M (2020). Net capitalized software/development: $1.1B (12/31/22) and $0.8B (12/25/21).
- Commitments and contingencies: Exposure to litigation, certain taxes, environmental matters, and contractual/commercial obligations; liabilities recognized when loss is probable and estimable.
- Research and development: Ongoing investment to drive innovation; consumer research excluded (in other marketing). R&D expense (in SG&A): $771M (2022), $752M (2021), $719M (2020).
- Goodwill and other intangibles: Indefinite-lived intangibles and goodwill not amortized; impairment assessed at least annually (Q3) or as needed using qualitative/quantitative methods. Qualitative factors considered include macroeconomic conditions (e.g., Russia-Ukraine conflict, high interest rates, inflation), industry/competitive, and legal/regulatory environments.

nodes.title: Software Costs
nodes.heading: 16.2.4 Software Costs
nodes.start_phrase: We capitalize certain computer software and software development costs incurred in connection with developing or obtaining computer software for internal use when both the preliminary project stage is completed and it is probable that the software will be used as intended.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of selling, general and administrative (SG&A) components and related policies and amounts.
- Advertising and marketing: SG&A included $5.2B (2022), $5.1B (2021), $4.6B (2020); advertising expense specifically $3.5B (2022 and 2021) and $3.0B (2020). Deferred advertising costs (media/personal service prepayments, promotional materials in inventory, production costs of future media) recorded as prepaid expenses and other current assets; balances of $40M (Dec 31, 2022) and $53M (Dec 25, 2021).
- Distribution costs: shipping and handling (including certain merchandising) reported in SG&A; expenses of $15.0B (2022), $13.7B (2021), $11.9B (2020).
- Software costs: capitalization criteria for internal-use software (post-preliminary stage; probable use); capitalizable elements include external services/materials, direct employee compensation/benefits, and interest. Capitalized within property, plant and equipment; amortized straight-line over approximately 5–10 years. Amortization expense of $123M (2022), $135M (2021), $152M (2020). Net capitalized software/development of $1.1B (2022) and $0.8B (2021).

- Note 5 — Income Taxes:

nodes.title: Method of Accounting and Our Assumptions
nodes.heading: 16.6.1 Method of Accounting and Our Assumptions
nodes.start_phrase: The fair value of share-based award grants is amortized to expense over the vesting period, primarily three years.
nodes.summary:
- Tax matters
  - Policy to establish valuation allowances on deferred tax assets when realization is not more likely than not.
  - As of Dec 31, 2022, approximately $9 billion of undistributed international earnings intended to be reinvested outside the U.S. for the foreseeable future.
  - While future distributions would not incur U.S. federal tax expense, no deferred tax liabilities have been recorded for potential foreign exchange impacts, foreign withholding, or state taxes; the unrecognized tax expense on these earnings is not practicable to estimate.

- Share-based compensation program (Note 6)
  - Program aligns employee and shareholder interests under the PepsiCo, Inc. Long-Term Incentive Plan (LTIP); awards include stock options, RSUs, PSUs, and long-term cash.
  - Eligible executives may elect stock options, RSUs, or a mix; options are granted at a 4:1 ratio versus RSUs. Certain senior executives receive a fixed mix: 66% PSUs and 34% long-term cash tied to pre-established performance targets.
  - Authorized and unissued shares may be used to settle awards; 37 million shares remained available for future grants as of Dec 31, 2022.
  - Share-based compensation expense (primarily in SG&A): total of $376M (2022), $322M (2021), $274M (2020), including equity and liability awards; acquisition/divestiture and restructuring charges were minimal.
  - Income tax benefits recognized: $62M (2022), $57M (2021), $48M (2020); excess tax benefits: $44M (2022), $38M (2021), $35M (2020).
  - Unrecognized compensation cost of $396M for nonvested awards to be recognized over about two years.

- Accounting policies and assumptions
  - Awards measured at grant-date fair value and expensed over the vesting period (primarily three years); retirement-eligible employees’ expense recognized through the date they first become retirement-eligible.
  - Forfeiture rates estimated using historical data; expense recorded only for awards expected to vest.
  - No backdating, repricing, or retroactive grants; any repricing would require shareholder approval under the LTIP.

- Stock options
  - Accounted for using a Black-Scholes model; options are granted at fair market value and generally have a 10-year term.
  - Key weighted-average Black-Scholes inputs:
    - Expected life: 7 years (2022, 2021), 6 years (2020)
    - Risk-free rate: 1.9% (2022), 1.1% (2021), 0.9% (2020)
    - Expected volatility: 16% (2022), 14% (2021, 2020)
    - Dividend yield: 2.5% (2022), 3.1% (2021), 3.4% (2020)
  - 2022 option activity:
    - Beginning outstanding: 10.1M; granted: 2.4M at $163.54; exercised: 1.6M; forfeited/expired: 0.5M.
    - Ending outstanding: 10.5M at $124.63 with 6.08 years remaining; aggregate intrinsic value about $589M.
    - Exercisable: 4.9M at $101.02 with 3.50 years remaining; intrinsic value about $390M.
    - Expected to vest: 5.3M at $144.58 with 8.29 years remaining; intrinsic value about $190M.

nodes.title: Stock Options
nodes.heading: 16.6.2 Stock Options
nodes.start_phrase: A stock option perm its the holder to purchase shares of PepsiCo common stock at a specified price.
nodes.summary:
- Section outlines PepsiCo’s share‑based compensation policies and activity.
- Expense recognition: records share‑based compensation expense only for awards expected to vest, using estimated forfeiture rates. The company does not backdate, reprice, or grant awards retroactively; any repricing would require shareholder approval under the long‑term incentive plan.
- Stock options:
  - Options allow purchase of common stock at a set price; all grants have exercise prices at fair market value on grant date and typically a 10‑year term.
  - Accounting: fair value method using Black‑Scholes at grant date.
  - Assumptions disclosed for 2020–2022 (expected life, risk‑free rate, volatility, dividend yield) and the basis for each assumption (historical exercise behavior, U.S. Treasury rates, historical volatility over expected life, and dividend policy/forecasts).
  - 2022 activity table summarizing options outstanding, granted, exercised, and forfeited/expired, with weighted‑average exercise prices, remaining contractual life, and aggregate intrinsic value; details for exercisable and expected‑to‑vest options also provided.
- Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and Performance Stock Units (PSUs):
  - RSUs deliver one share at vesting; PSUs deliver shares based on performance against specified financial metrics, with payout ranging from minimum to maximum per award terms.
  - Dividend equivalents accrue during vesting and pay in cash if/when the award vests.
  - Fair value measured at market price on grant date.
  - 2022 activity table showing awards outstanding, granted, converted (vested/settled), and forfeited; includes weighted‑average grant‑date fair value, remaining contractual life, and aggregate intrinsic value, plus expected‑to‑vest amounts and PSU threshold/target/maximum ranges.
- Long‑term cash awards:
  - Granted to certain executives; payout based on relative total shareholder return versus peers and achievement of a performance target over a three‑year period.
  - Classified as liability awards and remeasured through the performance period using a Monte Carlo simulation model.

Expected to vest as of 12/31/22: 5,979 units, $141.94 weighted-average grant-date fair value, 1.17 years remaining, $1,080,138 intrinsic value.

nodes.title: Note 7 — Pension, Retiree Medical and Savings Plans
nodes.heading: 16.7 Note 7 — Pension, Retir ee Medical and Savings Plans

- Pension and retiree medical accounting/policies:

nodes.start_phrase: Effective December 31, 2022, we merged two U.S. qualified defined benefit pension plans, PepsiCo Employees Retirement Plan I (Plan I), mostly inactive participants, and PepsiCo Employees Retirement Plan A (Plan A), mostly active participants, with Plan I remaining.
nodes.summary: Note 7 details PepsiCo’s pension, retiree medical and savings plans, including a 12/31/2022 merger of U.S. qualified defined benefit plans (Plan A into Plan I; benefits unchanged; aimed at risk/volatility reduction; no material pre-tax expense impact) and a 2022 transfer of $145 million of pension and retiree medical obligations and related assets to TBG in the Juice Transaction. Prior changes include: Canada salaried accrual freeze effective 1/1/2024 and hourly plan closed to new non‑union hires 1/1/2022; U.K. defined benefit accrual freeze 3/31/2022; U.S. salaried accrual freeze effective 12/31/2025; 2020–2022 U.S. reorganizations transferring participants among Plan A, Plan I, and creating Plan H (hourly) with enhanced pay credits (raising 2021 expense by $45 million) and a 2021 expense decrease of $70 million from the 2020 freeze; post‑freeze designs include employer contributions and matching to defined contribution plans. Actuarial gains/losses are recognized in AOCI and amortized if exceeding 10% of the greater of plan assets/obligations, over average remaining service life (Plan A ~9 years, Plan H ~11 years, retiree medical ~9 years) or remaining life expectancy (Plan I ~27 years; ~26 in 2023). 2022 year-end metrics: U.S. pension PBO $11.543b and assets $11.148b (funded status $(395)m), International pension PBO $2.603b and assets $3.195b (funded status $592m), retiree medical PBO $714m and assets $196m (funded status $(518)m); net loss in 2022 arose primarily from lower actual asset returns partly offset by higher discount rates. 2022 benefit costs totaled $489m (U.S. pension), $(35)m (International pension), and $2m (retiree medical), including settlement/curtailment and special termination effects; U.S. settlement charges were $318m in 2022 ($246m after-tax; $0.18/share) and $205m in 2020 ($158m after-tax; $0.11/share). Key 2022 assumptions included U.S. discount rate for PBO 5.4% (International 5.3%; retiree medical 5.4%) and expected return on assets 6.7% U.S. (International 5.3%; retiree medical 5.7%). Approximately $625m of pension PBO relates to plans not funded due to unfavorable tax treatment. Estimated future benefit payments: pension $945m (2023) rising to $5.1b (2028–2032 total) and retiree medical $90m (2023) and $330m (2028–2032 total), excluding modest Medicare subsidies.

nodes.title: Funding
nodes.heading: 16.7.1 Funding
nodes.start_phrase: Contributions to our pension and retiree medical plans were as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Presents a funding summary for pension and retiree medical plans, including a table of discretionary and non-discretionary contributions for 2020–2022. A footnote highlights large discretionary contributions to U.S. qualified defined benefit plans: $150 million (2022), $500 million (2021), and $325 million (2020).
- Outlines 2023 funding plans: a $125 million discretionary contribution made in January 2023 with an additional $125 million expected in Q3 2023; expected non-discretionary contributions of approximately $90 million to U.S. and international pension plans and approximately $55 million for retiree medical benefits.
- Notes ongoing evaluation of opportunities to reduce risk and volatility in pension and retiree medical plans.
- Describes plan asset strategy: actively managed accounts; periodic review against obligations, market conditions, risk tolerance, and cash needs; objective to meet benefit obligations as they come due; plan assets are owned by the plans (not the company) though asset performance affects obligations.
- Details investment policy: diversified portfolio of equity, high-quality debt, and real estate; permitted use of derivatives (futures and currency forwards) to mitigate interest rate and foreign currency risks.
- States expected long-term rates of return on U.S. plan assets: 7.4% for 2023 and 6.7% for 2022.
- Provides target U.S. asset allocation for 2023 and 2022: 56% fixed income, 22% U.S. equity, 18% international equity, 4% real estate; actual allocations may vary with periodic rebalancing.
- Explains methodology for expected return assumptions: based on strategy and long-term asset class returns, considering volatility, correlations, historical experience, interest rates, and inflation; assumptions reviewed annually. Market-related value uses actual fair value for fixed income; other asset classes use an alternative market-related approach.

nodes.title: Plan Assets
nodes.heading: 16.7.2 Plan Assets
nodes.start_phrase: Our pensio n plan investment strategy includes the use of actively managed accounts and is reviewed periodically in conjunction with plan obligation s, an evaluation of market conditions, tolerance for risk and cash requirements for benefit payments.
nodes.summary:
- Funding of pension and retiree medical plans: detailed 2020–2022 contributions split between discretionary and non-discretionary, including large discretionary U.S. qualified plan contributions; 2023 expectations of $250 million additional discretionary U.S. pension funding plus ~$90 million non-discretionary pension and ~$55 million retiree medical contributions.
- Ongoing efforts to reduce risk and volatility in pension and retiree medical plans.
- Plan asset strategy: diversified mix of equity, high-quality fixed income, and real estate; use of derivatives (futures, currency forwards) to manage interest rate and FX risk; regular monitoring and rebalancing; assets are plan-owned.
- Expected returns and methodology: long-term return assumption of 7.4% for 2023 (vs. 6.7% for 2022); expected return set by asset class assumptions, volatility, correlations, and macro factors; smoothing of non-fixed income gains/losses over five years to reduce volatility.
- Target U.S. plan asset allocation for 2022/2023: 56% fixed income, 22% U.S. equity, 18% international equity, 4% real estate.
- Fair value hierarchy disclosures: detailed Level 1/2/3 categorizations for U.S. and international plan assets at 2022 and 2021 year-ends, covering equities, government and corporate bonds, MBS, insurance contracts, cash, and real estate commingled funds (measured at NAV); notes on valuation methods, fund concentration, and redeemability; Level 3 changes not significant; certain retiree medical assets restricted for U.S. health benefits.
- Notable year-over-year change: total U.S. plan assets declined from $16.2 billion (2021) to $11.3 billion (2022); international plan assets declined from $4.6 billion to $3.2 billion.
- Retiree medical cost trend: 6% average increase assumed in 2023 and 2022; ultimate 4% by 2046; impact limited by a cap on the company’s share of costs.
- Savings plan: U.S. 401(k) with company match based on service; additional employer contributions for certain salaried employees not in a defined benefit plan; company contributions were $283 million (2022), $246 million (2021), $225 million (2020).
- Debt obligations (Note 8): summary of short- and long-term debt at year-end 2022 and 2021, including current maturities, commercial paper, and notes due 2023–2060 with effective interest rates; disclosure of unamortized net discounts; reference to interest rate derivatives; international debt increased to $304 million (from $38 million) via external borrowings and credit lines.

nodes.title: Retiree Medical Cost Trend Rates
nodes.heading: 16.7.3 Retiree Medical Cost T rend Rates
