nodes.title: Optional Redemption
nodes.heading: Optional Redemption
nodes.start_phrase: The 2029 notes are redeemable as a whole or in part, at our option, at any time and from time to time prior to April 22, 2029,
nodes.summary:
- The document outlines issuer optional redemption (call) terms for multiple series of Sterling and Euro senior notes, including make-whole provisions before specified par-call dates and par redemption thereafter.
- Sterling Notes:
  - 2029 and 2034 notes may be redeemed, in whole or in part, at any time.
  - Prior to three months before maturity, redemption price equals the greater of 100% of principal or the present value of Remaining Scheduled Payments (principal and interest excluding accrued to redemption), discounted on an ACTUAL/ACTUAL (ICMA) basis at the Comparable Government Bond Rate (based on U.K. gilts) plus 20 bps, plus accrued interest.
  - On or after the par-call date (three months before maturity), redeemable at 100% of principal plus accrued interest.
  - Definitions provided:
    - Comparable Government Bond Rate: yield-equating price set by an independent investment bank using the middle market price of a selected U.K. government bond at 11:00 a.m. London time, three business days before redemption.
    - Comparable Government Bond: the U.K. government bond with maturity closest to the assumed note maturity (three months prior to stated maturity), or another appropriate gilt as determined with broker/market-maker input.
    - Remaining Scheduled Payments: all remaining principal and interest due after the redemption date (with the next interest payment reduced by accrued interest if redemption is not on a coupon date), using the assumed earlier maturity dates for the 2029 and 2034 notes.
- Euro Notes:
  - Series covered: 2024, 2026, 2027, May 2028, July 2028, 2031, 2032, 2033, 2039, 2050; all redeemable, in whole or in part, at any time.
  - Prior to the par-call date, redemption price equals the greater of 100% of principal or the present value of Remaining Scheduled Payments discounted on ACTUAL/ACTUAL (ICMA) at the Comparable Government Bond Rate (based on German government bonds) plus a series-specific spread, plus accrued interest. Spreads/par-call windows:
    - 2024: +15 bps; one month prior to maturity.
    - 2026: +17 bps; three months prior; 30–60 days’ prior notice specified.
    - 2027: +15 bps; three months prior.
    - May 2028: +20 bps; three months prior.
    - July 2028: +20 bps; three months prior; 30–60 days’ prior notice specified.
    - 2031: +20 bps; three months prior.
    - 2032: +15 bps; three months prior.
    - 2033: +15 bps; three months prior.
    - 2039: +20 bps; six months prior.
    - 2050: +20 bps; six months prior.
  - On or after each series’ par-call date, redeemable at 100% of principal plus accrued interest.
  - Definitions provided mirror the Sterling Notes, but reference German government bonds for the Comparable Government Bond and Rate; Remaining Scheduled Payments defined similarly (with coupon-date adjustment).
- General redemption mechanics:
  - Interest ceases on redeemed notes from the redemption date (unless the issuer defaults on payment).
  - Funds sufficient to pay redemption price and accrued interest will be deposited with the trustee or its agent on or before the redemption date.
  - If fewer than all notes of a series are redeemed, selection follows applicable depositary procedures.
  - The issuer may repurchase notes in the open market and hold or cancel them.
  - Notice of redemption will be transmitted 30–60 days before redemption, except shorter periods for certain series: 15 days for the 2039 notes; 10 days for the 2024, May 2028, 2029, 2032, 2033, 2034, and 2050 notes. The issuer calculates the redemption price.
- Payment of Additional Amounts (tax gross-up):
  - The issuer agrees to pay additional amounts (as additional interest) so non-U.S. holders receive net payments on principal and interest free of U.S. withholding taxes, subject to specified exceptions and limitations.
  - The excerpt begins listing exceptions for Sterling Notes, including cases where the holder (or beneficial owner/related party) has certain U.S. connections (e.g., U.S. trade or business or permanent establishment; U.S. citizenship/residency; classifications like personal holding company, passive foreign investment company, or controlled foreign corporation, or corporations with accumulated earnings to avoid U.S. tax).

nodes.title: Payment of Additional Amounts
nodes.heading: Payment of Additional Amounts
nodes.start_phrase: We will, subject to the exceptions and limitations set forth below , pay as additional interest on the notes such additional amounts as are necessary in order that the net payment by us of the principal of and interest on the notes
nodes.summary:
- Redemption mechanics: The issuer will notify holders of any redemption and is responsible for calculating the redemption price for notes or portions redeemed.
- Payment of Additional Amounts (tax gross-up): For holders who are not United States persons, the issuer will pay additional amounts so that net principal and interest received (after U.S. withholding) equals the amounts otherwise due, subject to enumerated exceptions.
- Exceptions to gross-up (vary by series but generally include):
  - Taxes due to the holder’s (or beneficial owner’s) U.S. nexus (e.g., engaging in a U.S. trade or business, permanent establishment, U.S. citizenship/residency, certain anti-deferral statuses, 10-percent shareholder status, or certain bank lending situations).
  - Holders that are not the sole beneficial owner (or are fiduciaries/partnerships/LLCs) to the extent a beneficial owner would not qualify.
  - Failure to comply with required certifications or information reporting to obtain an exemption.
  - Taxes not imposed by withholding by the issuer or paying agent.
  - Taxes arising from changes in law or interpretation effective more than 15 days after payment becomes due or provided for.
  - Estate, inheritance, gift, sales, excise, transfer, wealth, capital gains, personal property, or similar non-withholding taxes.
  - Withholding avoidable by using another paying agent.
  - Late presentation of notes (over 30 days after due/provided-for date).
  - Certain bank-related acquisitions of notes.
  - FATCA-related withholding (Code Sections 1471–1474 and related rules).
  - For the 2026 Notes and July 2028 Notes only: EU savings directive-type withholding on payments to individuals.
- Series-specific listings: Separate exception lists are provided for Sterling Notes; 2026 Notes and July 2028 Notes; and 2024, 2027, May 2028, 2031, 2032, 2033, 2039, and 2050 Notes, with largely similar exceptions and the EU directive item applying only to the 2026 and July 2028 Notes.
- Tax law supremacy: Notes remain subject to applicable tax laws and interpretations; no additional payments will be made beyond those under “Payment of Additional Amounts.”
- Definitions provided: “United States” (including states, D.C., and political subdivisions) and “United States person” (U.S. citizens/residents for tax purposes, entities organized under U.S. law, and certain estates/trusts).
- Redemption for tax reasons: If a post-offering change in U.S. tax law/interpretation would obligate the issuer to pay additional amounts, the issuer may redeem the affected series in whole (not in part) on 30–60 days’ notice at 100% of principal plus accrued interest to (but excluding) the redemption date.
- Certain covenants—Limitation of Liens: The issuer and its restricted subsidiaries will not incur or guarantee debt secured by liens on principal property or on stock/interests of restricted subsidiaries unless the notes (and, at option, other non-subordinated debt) are secured equally and ratably; upcoming text will detail permitted exceptions.

nodes.title: Redemption for Tax Reasons
nodes.heading: Redemption for T ax Reasons
nodes.start_phrase: If, as a result of any change in, or amendment to, the laws (or any regulations or rulings promulgated under the laws) of the United States (or any taxing authority in the United States),
nodes.summary:
- Defines a “United States person” for tax purposes, including estates and trusts subject to U.S. federal income tax regardless of source.
- Redemption for Tax Reasons: If changes in U.S. tax laws, regulations, rulings, or their official interpretation after the relevant prospectus supplement cause or are expected (per an independent counsel’s written opinion) to require the issuer to pay “additional amounts” on the notes, the issuer may redeem all (but not part) of the affected series at 100% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest, with 30–60 days’ notice.
- Certain Covenants – Limitation on Liens: The issuer and its restricted subsidiaries will not incur or guarantee debt secured by liens on principal property or on equity/interests in restricted subsidiaries unless the notes are secured equally and ratably (or prior), with customary exceptions to be listed elsewhere.

nodes.title: Certain Covenants
nodes.heading: Certain Covenants
nodes.start_phrase: We will not, and will not permit any of our restricted subsidiaries to, incur , suffer to exist or guarantee any debt secured by a lien on any principal property
nodes.summary:
- Snippet of U.S. tax definitions, referencing U.S. persons and estates/trusts subject to U.S. federal income tax.
- Redemption for tax reasons: if post-offering changes in U.S. tax law would require the issuer to pay “Additional Amounts,” the issuer may redeem an entire series of notes (not partially) at 100% of principal plus accrued interest, with 30–60 days’ notice.
- Covenant limiting liens: the company and its restricted subsidiaries will not secure debt with liens on principal property or stock/interests of restricted subsidiaries unless the notes are equally and ratably secured, subject to customary exceptions, including:
  - pre-existing liens,
  - liens existing when an entity becomes a restricted subsidiary,
  - acquisition, construction, or improvement liens (including within 365 days of acquisition/operation),
  - intra-group liens,
  - governmental liens/requirements,
  - extensions, renewals, or refundings of permitted liens.
- General secured debt basket: additional secured debt permitted up to 15% of consolidated net tangible assets without equally and ratably securing the notes.
- Flexibility to transfer or redesignate: the indenture does not restrict transfers of principal property to unrestricted subsidiaries or redesignations to unrestricted status; such unrestricted subsidiaries may incur secured debt without requiring equal and ratable liens on the notes.
- Consolidation, merger, or sale of substantially all assets permitted if the successor is a U.S.-organized corporation that assumes the obligations, no default exists post-transaction, and an opinion of counsel confirms compliance; the successor is substituted as obligor and the issuer is released.
- Beginning of definition of “consolidated net tangible assets”: total assets of the company and restricted subsidiaries minus depreciation, amortization, and other valuation reserves (full definition continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Consolidation, Merger or Sale of Assets
nodes.heading: Consolidation, Mer ger or Sale of Assets
nodes.start_phrase: We may consolidate or merge with or into, or convey or transfer all or substantially all of our assets to, any entity (including, without limitation, a limited partnership or a limited liability company); provided that:
nodes.summary:
- States that unrestricted subsidiaries may incur secured debt without requiring the notes to be equally and ratably secured.
- Outlines the consolidation, merger, or sale of substantially all assets covenant:
  - Permitted if the surviving or successor is a U.S. (or D.C.) corporation that assumes the notes via a supplemental indenture.
  - No default or event of default may exist immediately after the transaction.
  - An opinion of counsel must be delivered to the trustee.
  - The successor becomes the obligor and the original issuer is released from obligations under the indenture and notes.
- Provides key definitions:
  - Consolidated net tangible assets: total assets of the company and restricted subsidiaries minus depreciation/valuation reserves, current liabilities (excluding intercompany), and intangibles, per U.S. GAAP.
  - Debt: indebtedness for borrowed money.
  - Principal property: significant plants, offices, or warehouses owned or leased, excluding those deemed immaterial by the Board.
  - Restricted subsidiary: any subsidiary not designated as unrestricted.
  - Subsidiary: entities majority-owned, directly or indirectly, by the company or its subsidiaries.
  - Unrestricted subsidiary: subsidiaries primarily engaged in finance-related businesses, holding companies of such subsidiaries, or those designated as unrestricted by the Board.
- Introduces the Events of Default section for the notes (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Events of Default
nodes.heading: Events of Default
nodes.start_phrase: An “Event of Default” under the notes of a given series means:
nodes.summary:
- Defines key terms used in the indenture, including:
  - Debt (indebtedness for borrowed money)
  - Principal property (material plants, offices, warehouses, unless deemed immaterial by the Board)
  - Subsidiary, Restricted subsidiary, and Unrestricted subsidiary (with criteria based on business activities, assets, and Board designation)
  - References to balance-sheet elements (current liabilities, intangibles like goodwill, trademarks, patents, unamortized debt discount) prepared under U.S. GAAP for certain calculations
- Outlines Events of Default for each series of notes, including:
  - Failure to pay interest (30 days), principal/premium when due, or sinking/purchase fund payments (30 days)
  - Breach of covenants (other than payment defaults) continuing for 90 days after notice
  - Specified bankruptcy/insolvency events for PepsiCo
  - Any additional events specified in a prospectus supplement
- Describes remedies upon default:
  - Acceleration of the entire principal and accrued interest by the trustee or holders of at least 51% of the series; automatic acceleration upon certain bankruptcy events
  - Rescission of acceleration by holders of at least 51% if all continuing Events of Default (other than resulting solely from acceleration) are cured/waived and no conflict with judgments
  - Majority holders may waive past defaults other than payment defaults or those requiring unanimous consent to amend
- Sets holder enforcement mechanics:
  - Holders of at least 51% may direct the trustee after written notice, request, and offering reasonable indemnity; a 60-day waiting period applies unless conflicting directions are received from a majority
  - Individual suits to enforce payment on due dates are preserved
- Establishes trustee duties and notices:
  - During an Event of Default, the trustee must act with prudent person standard; action requires reasonable security/indemnity if requested by holders
  - Trustee must notify holders within 90 days of a default, but may withhold notice (except for payment defaults) if in holders’ best interests
- Provides for amendments and waivers:
  - Amendments without holder consent permitted to: reflect trustee succession; cure ambiguities/defects; provide for assumption after merger/consolidation or asset transfer; add holder benefits; add guarantors; secure notes; establish note forms; maintain Trust Indenture Act qualification; or make immaterial changes
  - Other amendments require consent of holders of a majority in aggregate principal amount of the affected series; the text indicates further limitations (e.g., changes typically requiring unanimous consent) continue beyond the excerpt

nodes.title: Modification and Waiver
nodes.heading: Modification and W aiver
nodes.start_phrase: The indenture may be amended or modified without the consent of any holder of notes in order to:
nodes.summary:
- Trustee default notices: Within 90 days of a default, the trustee must notify noteholders of that series, unless cured/waived; notice may be withheld (if no payment default) when the trustee, in good faith, deems withholding in holders’ interests.
- Amendments without holder consent: Permitted for administrative or beneficial changes, including successor trustee recognition, curing ambiguities, assumption after merger/asset transfer, adding rights for holders, adding guarantors, securing notes, establishing note forms, maintaining Trust Indenture Act qualification, and other immaterial changes.
- Amendments with majority consent: Other changes to the indenture or notes require consent of holders of at least a majority in aggregate principal amount of the affected series.
- Changes requiring each affected holder’s consent: No amendment may, without unanimous affected-holder consent, reduce principal/interest/premium or extend maturity; alter redemption terms; change payment currency; lower consent thresholds; impair enforcement/suit rights; waive payment defaults; reduce interest rate or extend interest payment time; adversely affect ranking; or release a guarantor except as permitted by the indenture.
- Satisfaction, discharge, and covenant defeasance: The issuer may terminate obligations under the indenture when all notes of a series have been delivered for cancellation, or when all outstanding notes are due/within one year of becoming due or to be redeemed within one year (additional conditions implied but text is truncated).

nodes.title: Satisfaction, Discharge and Covenant Defeasance
nodes.heading: Satisfaction, Discharge and Covenant Defeasance
nodes.start_phrase: We may terminate our obligations under the indenture, when:
nodes.summary:
- Outlines amendments to the notes that cannot be made without each affected holder’s consent, including changes that reduce principal, interest, or premium; extend maturity or interest payment times; alter redemption terms; change payment currency; lower consent thresholds; impair the right to sue for payment; waive payment defaults; adversely affect ranking; or release guarantors except as permitted by the indenture.
- Describes satisfaction and discharge of the indenture for a series when all notes are canceled or due/redeemable within one year with adequate funds irrevocably deposited, all other sums paid, and delivery of officers’ certificate and counsel opinion confirming compliance.
- Explains legal defeasance, under which the issuer is deemed to have discharged the debt of a series while certain obligations survive (holders’ rights to payment, administrative obligations regarding notes and payment agency, trustee rights, and defeasance provisions).
- Explains covenant defeasance, releasing the issuer from specified covenants so that related breaches no longer constitute Events of Default for that series, while non-payment and bankruptcy/insolvency remain Events of Default.
- Sets conditions for legal or covenant defeasance, including: irrevocable deposit of cash and/or U.S. (or equivalent) government obligations sufficient to pay all amounts (supported by an accountant’s opinion); tax opinions confirming no adverse U.S. federal income tax recognition; absence of continuing defaults (and a 91-day bankruptcy/insolvency look-back for legal defeasance); no trustee conflict under the Trust Indenture Act; no breach of other agreements; no creation of an unregistered investment company under the 1940 Act; and delivery of officers’ certificate and counsel opinion confirming all conditions are met.

nodes.title: Book-Entry, Delivery and Settlement
nodes.heading: 33.2.10 Book-Entry, Delivery and Settlement
nodes.start_phrase: We have obtained the information in this section concerning Clearstream and Euroclear and their book-entry systems and procedures from sources that we believe to be reliable.
nodes.summary:
- Focuses on book-entry, delivery, and settlement arrangements for notes cleared through Clearstream and Euroclear.
- States that information about Clearstream/Euroclear is from sources believed reliable; issuer disclaims responsibility and notes rules/procedures may change at any time.
- Notes were initially issued as fully registered global notes, deposited with a common depositary and registered in the name of its nominee for Clearstream/Euroclear; global notes are transferable only in whole to Clearstream/Euroclear or their nominees.
- Investors may hold interests directly as participants or indirectly through participant organizations; holdings and transfers are recorded in Clearstream/Euroclear book-entry systems; addresses for both clearing systems are provided.
- Distribution and secondary market trading occur through Clearstream/Euroclear participants and settle in same-day funds; payments to beneficial owners are made in sterling for sterling notes and euros for euro notes, unless otherwise specified.
- Clearstream/Euroclear maintain electronic securities/payment transfer, processing, depositary, and custodial links enabling issuance, holding, and cross-border trading without physical certificates; special clearance/settlement procedures support cross-border trades.
- Policies of Clearstream/Euroclear govern payments, transfers, and exchanges; the issuer does not control or take responsibility for their records or operations; the systems act under their own agreements and may modify or discontinue procedures at any time.
- Beneficial owners will not have notes registered in their names, will not receive physical certificates, and are not considered holders under the indenture (including for issuer/trustee reports); they must rely on the depositary and relevant participants to exercise holder rights.
- Certificated notes: subject to certain conditions, global notes may be exchanged for definitive certificated notes in minimum denominations of £100,000 plus £1,000 multiples (sterling) or €100,000 plus €1,000 multiples (euro); detailed conditions are not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Book-Entry, Delivery and Settlement - Introduction
nodes.heading: 33.2.10 Book-Entry, Delivery and Settlement
nodes.start_phrase: We have obtained the information in this section concerning Clearstream and Euroclear and their book-entry systems and procedures from sources that we believe to be reliable.
nodes.summary: This introduction explains that the notes were issued solely in book-entry form as fully registered global notes deposited with a common depositary and registered in the name of its nominee for Clearstream Banking, S.A. (42 Avenue JF Kennedy, L-1855 Luxembourg) and Euroclear Bank SA/NV (1 Boulevard Roi Albert II, B-1210 Brussels); transfers of global notes may be made only in whole to Clearstream or Euroclear or their nominees. Investors hold beneficial interests through participants or indirect participants, with ownership, transfers, and payments recorded in Clearstream/Euroclear books; distribution and secondary trading clear through these systems in same-day funds, with payments in sterling for sterling notes and euro for euro notes (subject to any prospectus supplement). Clearstream/Euroclear maintain electronic links enabling cross-border clearance without physical certificates. Their policies govern payments, transfers, and exchanges; the issuer disclaims responsibility for their records, does not supervise them, and notes their rules/procedures may change or be discontinued at any time. Beneficial owners are not registered holders under the indenture, will not receive definitive certificates or issuer/trustee reports, and must rely on the depositary and participant procedures to exercise holder rights.

nodes.title: Certificated Notes
nodes.heading: 33.2.10.1 Certificated Notes
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to certain conditions, the notes represented by the global notes are exchangeable for certificated notes in definitive form of like tenor in minimum denominations of £100,000 principal amount and integral multiples of £1,000 in excess thereof with respect to the sterling notes and €100,000 principal amount and integral multiples of €1,000 in excess thereof with respect to the euro notes if:
nodes.summary:
- Describes the roles of Clearstream and Euroclear, their electronic links, and special cross-border clearance and settlement procedures that allow notes to be issued, held, and transferred without physical certificates.
- States that payments, transfers, and exchanges are governed by Clearstream/Euroclear policies; the issuer has no responsibility for their records or operations and does not supervise them; these systems may modify or discontinue procedures at any time.
- Clarifies that beneficial owners holding through the clearing systems are not registered holders under the indenture, will not receive physical notes or be treated as holders for report delivery, and must rely on the depositary and its participants to exercise holder rights.
- Outlines when global notes can be exchanged for certificated notes of like tenor and specified minimum denominations: if the common depositary is unwilling, unable, or unqualified and no successor is appointed within 90 days; if the issuer elects not to keep all notes of a series in global form; or upon a continuing default that permits acceleration.
- Specifies denominations for certificated notes: sterling notes at £100,000 minimum with £1,000 increments; euro notes at €100,000 minimum with €1,000 increments; otherwise, global notes are not exchangeable except for a replacement global note registered to the common depositary or its nominee.
- Details same-day payment and transfer procedures for certificated notes: execution at a London office/agency (initially the paying agent) or by mailed check; holders providing instructions receive wire transfers of immediately available funds; no service charge for transfer registration, though taxes/governmental charges may apply.
- Confirms payments cover principal, interest, and any additional amounts.

nodes.title: Same-day Payment
nodes.heading: 33.2.10.2 Same-day Payment
nodes.start_phrase: Payments (including principal, interes t and any additional amounts) and transfers with respect to notes of any series in certificated form may be executed at the office or agency maintained for such purpose within the City of London (initially the office of the paying agent maintained for such purpose) or, at our option, by check mailed to the holders thereof at the respective addresses set forth in the register of holders of the applicable notes of such series, provided that all payments (including principal, interest and any additional amounts) on notes in certificated form, for which the holders thereof have given wire transfer instructions, will be required to be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the accounts specified by the holders thereof.
nodes.summary:
- Conditions for exchanging global notes into certificated notes: (1) the common depositary is unwilling, unable, or no longer qualified and no successor is appointed within 90 days; (2) the issuer elects not to have a series represented by a global note; or (3) a continuing default allows acceleration of maturity.
- Exchange mechanics: exchangeable notes are issued in authorized denominations and registered in names as directed by the common depositary; otherwise, global notes are not exchangeable except into another global note of the same aggregate denomination registered to the common depositary or its nominee.
- Same-day payment and transfer procedures for certificated notes: payments of principal, interest, and any additional amounts may be made at an office/agency in the City of London (initially the paying agent) or by mailed check; holders who provide wire instructions must receive payment by wire of immediately available funds. No service charge for registration of transfer, but applicable taxes/governmental charges may be required.
- Reference to Exhibit 10.6: “The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Defined Benefit Program (PIRP-DB),” amended and restated effective January 1, 2023.

nodes.title: ARTICLE I - HISTORY AND GENERAL INFORMATION
nodes.heading: 34.1 ARTICLE I - HISTORY AND GENERAL INFORMATION
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan came into operation on and took ef fect from September 1, 1980, and was comprised of the “PepsiCo International Retirement Plan T rust Indenture” and the “Plan Rules”, and was later amended and restated in its entirety , effective September 2, 1982.
nodes.summary:
- Traces the Plan’s history: established September 1, 1980; restated September 2, 1982.
- 2003 restructure: Plan Rules split into Plan A (trust-funded under the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Trust Indenture) and Plan B (corporate pay-as-you-go).
- 2005 amendment for individuals subject to U.S. taxation: no new, increased, or enhanced benefits may arise; benefits determined as if employment ended before becoming U.S.-taxable.
- 2010 consolidation: Plan A and B merged into a single governing document called the Defined Benefit Program (DB Program or PIRP-DB), applying to members and related claimants from January 1, 2010; expressly prevents any duplication of benefits.
- 2011 creation of a Defined Contribution Program (DC Program) for selected international employees (e.g., those on expatriate assignments and selected senior globalists on U.S. tax-equalized packages); DC has a separate document; together, DB and DC comprise a single Plan.
- Subsequent DB Program restatements: effective January 1, 2016; January 1, 2019; and January 1, 2021. The 2021 restatement freezes the DB Program as of end of day December 31, 2025:
  - All DB accruals and recognition of pensionable service/salary/compensation end no later than December 31, 2025; post-2025 service not used in averaging.
  - Members may still earn Service for vesting and “entitlement Service” and meet age thresholds for favorable early retirement factors after 2025 while employed.
  - For formulas using projection/proration, the denominator is projected as if no freeze, the numerator reflects the freeze through December 31, 2025, and the resulting fraction is then frozen; members may still meet conditions after 2025 that eliminate the need for this projection/proration.
- Current restatement effective January 1, 2023: narrows the definition of Eligible Employee.
- Clarifies funding and legal status: at all times unfunded and unsecured for U.S. Internal Revenue Code and ERISA purposes; benefits are obligations of each executive’s employer and executives are unsecured general creditors; intended to be ERISA-exempt as a non-U.S. plan primarily for nonresident aliens.

nodes.title: ARTICLE II - DEFINITIONS AND CONSTRUCTION
nodes.heading: 34.2 ARTICLE II - DEFINITIONS AND CONSTRUCTION
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this governing legal document for the DB Program, they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context:
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is from Article II (Definitions and Construction) of a governing legal document for a defined benefit (DB) program. It sets out key definitions to be used throughout the plan unless context dictates otherwise. Defined terms include:
- Active Member: a member currently eligible to accrue Pensionable Service (admitted under Article III) who has not retired, withdrawn, or otherwise ceased eligibility.
- Actuarial Equivalent: determined by reference to the Standard Actuarial Factors in Part B, Section 2.1 of the PepsiCo Employees Retirement Plan A, with specified applicability and special rules.
- Actuary: the actuary or firm appointed by the Vice President.
- Annuity Starting Date: the first day of the first month for which any pension benefit is payable.
- Approved Transfer: company-approved employment changes that move a member to, or second them into, the U.S. or otherwise cause them to become a U.S. Person.
- Associated Company: entities controlled by or associated with the Corporation that, with the Vice President’s ongoing consent, agree to the plan’s terms and are included as Employers.
- Corporation: PepsiCo, Inc., a North Carolina corporation, including its successors.

nodes.title: Definitions.
nodes.heading: 34.2.1 2.01 Definitions.
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this governing legal document for the DB Program, they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context:
nodes.summary:
This excerpt is Article II of the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Defined Benefit Program (PIRP‑DB) and sets out core definitions and interpretation rules used throughout the DB Program. It:

- Defines participant and employment status terms that drive eligibility and accruals: Active Member, Member, Eligible Employee (primarily full‑time salaried Third Country Nationals outside the U.S., with limited grandfathering and VP discretion), Service (including vesting vs. entitlement Service, breaks in service, leave rules), Pensionable Service (crediting rules and VP discretion), and Entry Date.
- Establishes family/survivor status terms affecting benefit form and beneficiaries: Eligible Spouse, Eligible Domestic Partner (with detailed qualification via civil union, benefits enrollment, or other evidence, plus timing and exclusivity rules), and Dependant.
- Specifies organizational and employer scope: Corporation (PepsiCo, Inc.), PepsiCo Organization (controlled group under IRC §414), Associated Company, Employers and Approved Employer, and PepsiCo Salaried Plan.
- Covers U.S. tax residency and mobility concepts that affect plan participation: U.S. Person (citizen, green card, substantial presence/election, and tax return rule), Third Country National, Approved Transfer, and Status Change.
- Defines compensation and benefit measurement terms: Salary (what counts/excludes, treatment upon employer change within the organization, currency conversion, and VP discretion), Pension (forms), Normal Retirement Age and Date, Annuity Starting Date, Actuarial Equivalent (by reference to PepsiCo plan factors), and Actuary.
- Assigns administrative authority: Vice President (Global Benefits & Wellness) as the key decision‑maker with broad discretion across definitions and crediting.
- Provides construction/interpretation rules for the document: gender/number usage, measuring years and partial periods (including leap years), meaning of “hereof/hereunder,” treatment of examples/“including” as non‑limiting, and the hierarchy of document subdivisions.

nodes.title: Construction.
nodes.heading: 34.2.2 2.02 Construction.
nodes.start_phrase: In this document for the DB Program where the context does not otherwise determine, words importing the masculine gender shall include the feminine gender and words importing the singular number shall include the plural number and vice versa.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “U.S. Person” for the plan by reference to U.S. tax law (IRC §7701(b)), including U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (or applicants), and resident aliens (e.g., via substantial presence or election). Also treats anyone required to file a U.S. individual income tax return as a U.S. Person for Section 9.14 unless the Vice President determines the individual has no U.S.-source earned income from the PepsiCo organization for that year.
- Defines “Vice President” as the Vice President, Global Benefits & Wellness of PepsiCo, Inc., or, if that role is vacant/eliminated, the person performing most (or the largest share) of that position’s prior duties.
- Sets construction/interpretation rules for the DB Program:
  - Gender/number neutrality (masculine includes feminine; singular includes plural and vice versa).
  - Time-period calculations: a “year” is any 365 consecutive days (366 if including Feb 29) without double-counting days; permits prorated calculations for partial years/months; authorizes the Vice President to count certain periods in days or full calendar months (each month as 1/12 of a year).
  - “Hereof,” “hereunder,” etc., refer to the entire DB Program.
  - Examples and “including” are read as “without limitation.”
  - Document hierarchy and citation conventions: articles (Roman numerals), sections (Arabic with decimal), subsections (lower-case letters), paragraphs (Arabic in parentheses), subparagraphs (lower-case Roman numerals), and clauses (upper-case letters), with rules for intra-section cross-references.

nodes.title: ARTICLE III - MEMBERSHIP
nodes.heading: 34.3 ARTICLE III - MEMBERSHIP
nodes.start_phrase: Every person who the V ice President determines is an Eligible Employee shall be eligible for Membership.
nodes.summary:
- Article III defines Membership rules for the DB Program.
- 3.01 Eligibility: Any person the Vice President determines to be an Eligible Employee is eligible for Membership.
- 3.02 Admission:
  - (a) Grandfathering/continuation: 
    - Individuals who were Active Members immediately before January 1, 2021 remain Active Members on and after that date, as long as consistent with the DB Program as amended (including after the Restatement Date).
    - Individuals who were Members but not Active Members immediately before January 1, 2021 continue as Members on and after the Restatement Date, subject to the same consistency condition.
  - (b) New admissions:
    - A non-member deemed an Eligible Employee by the Vice President is admitted upon the Vice President’s approval, effective on the Entry Date coinciding with or immediately following the later of service commencement or becoming an Eligible Employee.
    - No Eligible Employee or other person may be admitted to or continue in Membership without the Vice President’s approval.

nodes.title: Eligibility for Membership.
nodes.heading: 34.3.1 3.01 Eligibility for Membership.
nodes.start_phrase: Every person who the V ice President determines is an Eligible Employee shall be eligible for Membership.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Article III – Membership rules for a DB Program.
- Eligibility: Any individual the Vice President determines to be an “Eligible Employee” is eligible for membership.
- Continuation of pre-2021 members:
  - Individuals who were Active Members immediately before January 1, 2021 remain Active Members from that date forward, subject to consistency with the DB Program as amended on/after January 1, 2021 and the Restatement Date.
  - Individuals who were Members (but not Active) immediately before January 1, 2021 continue as Members under the same conditions.
- Admission of new members: Non-members deemed Eligible Employees by the Vice President may be admitted upon the Vice President’s approval, effective on the Entry Date that coincides with or immediately follows the later of (i) commencement of Service or (ii) becoming an Eligible Employee.
- Governance/approval: No Eligible Employee or other person may be admitted to or continue membership without the Vice President’s approval.

nodes.title: Admission to Membership.
nodes.heading: 34.3.2 3.02 Admission to Membership.
nodes.start_phrase: Every person who was an Active Member of the DB Program immediately prior to January 1, 2021 shall continue as an Active Member of the DB Program from and after January 1, 2021, to the extent such Active Membership is and remains consistent with the provisions of the DB Program, as amended and in ef fect on and after January 1, 2021 (and thereafter , as amended and in ef fect on and after the Restatement Date).
nodes.summary:
- Article III—Membership outlines who is eligible and how individuals are admitted to the DB Program.
- Eligibility (3.01): Any person the Vice President determines to be an “Eligible Employee” is eligible for membership.
- Continuation of existing members (3.02(a)): 
  - Individuals who were Active Members immediately before January 1, 2021 continue as Active Members from that date onward, provided this remains consistent with the DB Program as amended on/after January 1, 2021 and the Restatement Date.
  - Individuals who were Members but not Active Members before January 1, 2021 continue as Members under the same consistency condition.
- Admission of new members (3.02(b)): 
  - Non-members deemed Eligible Employees by the Vice President are admitted upon Vice President approval, effective as of the Entry Date that coincides with or immediately follows the later of the start of their Service or the date they become Eligible Employees (both as determined by the Vice President).
- Approval requirement: No Eligible Employee or other person may be admitted to or continue in membership without the Vice President’s approval.

nodes.title: ARTICLE IV - REQUIREMENTS FOR BENEFITS
nodes.heading: 34.4 ARTICLE IV - REQUIREMENTS FOR BENEFITS
nodes.start_phrase: A Member shall be entitled to a Normal Retirement Pension if his employment with both his Employer and the PepsiCo Organization terminates on his Normal Retirement Age.
nodes.summary:
- Article IV outlines the requirements for different pension benefits and the conditions under which a Member becomes eligible, consistently requiring termination of employment with both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization.

- Section 4.01 – Normal Retirement Pension:
  - Eligibility upon termination at Normal Retirement Age.
  - Annuity Starting Date is the first day of the month coincident with or following termination.
  - Paid in the normal form under Section 5.02 unless an optional form is elected under Section 5.03.
  - Benefit calculated per Table A.

- Section 4.02 – Early Retirement Pension:
  - Eligibility upon termination on or after age 55 but before Normal Retirement Age, with at least 10 years of Service.
  - Default Annuity Starting Date is the Normal Retirement Date, but the Member may elect an earlier start (first day of any month after termination and before Normal Retirement Date) via written election to the Vice President.
  - Benefit computed as if retiring at Normal Retirement Date, using Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service as of termination.
  - Reduction of 4/12 of 1% for each month benefits begin before age 62.

- Section 4.03 – Special Early Retirement Pension:
  - Eligibility upon termination on or after age 50 but before 55, with at least 10 years of Service, only if authorized by the Vice President.
  - Annuity Starting Date is the first day of the month after authorization.
  - Benefit computed per Table A using Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service as of termination.
  - Reduction of 4/12 of 1% for each month benefits begin before age 62.

- Section 4.04 – Deferred Vested Pension:
  - Applies to Members terminating employment before becoming eligible for Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement Pensions (introductory clause provided; details not shown).

nodes.title: Normal Retirement Pension.
nodes.heading: 34.4.1 4.01 Normal Retirement Pension.
nodes.start_phrase: A Member shall be entitled to a Normal Retirement Pension if his employment with both his Employer and the PepsiCo Organization terminates on his Normal Retirement Age.
nodes.summary:
- Article IV outlines eligibility and benefit rules for different pension types.
- Normal Retirement Pension: Payable when employment with both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization ends at Normal Retirement Age. Annuity starts the first day of the month on/after termination. Paid in the normal form (Sec. 5.02) unless an optional form is elected (Sec. 5.03). Amount calculated per Table A.
- Early Retirement Pension: Available upon termination with both entities at age 55+ but before Normal Retirement Age, with 10+ years of Service. Default annuity start is the Normal Retirement Date, but the member may elect any month after termination and before Normal Retirement Date. Benefit computed per Table A as if retiring at Normal Retirement Date, using Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service at termination; reduced by 4/12 of 1% for each month benefits begin before age 62.
- Special Early Retirement Pension: Possible upon termination at ages 50–54 with at least 10 years of Service, only if authorized by the Vice President. Annuity starts the first day of the month after authorization. Calculated per Table A as if retiring at Normal Retirement Date, using Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service at termination; reduced by 4/12 of 1% per month benefits begin before age 62.
- Across early and special early pensions, reductions reflect commencement before age 62; calculations reference Table A and the member’s Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service as of termination.
- Deferred Vested Pension: Applies to members who terminate with both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization before qualifying for Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement (details continue beyond the provided text).

nodes.title: Early Retirement Pension.
nodes.heading: 34.4.2 4.02 Early Retirement Pension.
nodes.start_phrase: A Member shall be entitled to an Early Retirement Pension if his employment with both his Employer and the PepsiCo Organization terminates on or after age 55 but before his Normal Retirement Age, and after he has completed 10 or more years of Service.
nodes.summary:
- Article IV outlines eligibility and calculation rules for different retirement benefits.
- 4.01 Normal Retirement Pension:
  - Eligibility: termination of employment with both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization at Normal Retirement Age.
  - Annuity Starting Date (ASD): first day of the month coincident with or following termination.
  - Payment form: normal form under Section 5.02 unless an optional form is elected under Section 5.03.
  - Calculation: per Table A.
- 4.02 Early Retirement Pension:
  - Eligibility: termination at age 55 or later but before Normal Retirement Age, with 10+ years of Service.
  - ASD: ordinarily the Normal Retirement Date; member may elect the first day of any month after termination and before Normal Retirement Date.
  - Calculation: as if retiring at Normal Retirement Date, using Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service at termination; reduced by 4/12 of 1% for each month commencement precedes age 62.
- 4.03 Special Early Retirement Pension:
  - Eligibility: termination at age 50–54 with at least 10 years of Service, only if authorized by the Vice President.
  - ASD: first day of the month after VP authorization.
  - Calculation: as if retiring at Normal Retirement Date, using Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service at termination; reduced by 4/12 of 1% for each month commencement precedes age 62.
- 4.04 Deferred Vested Pension:
  - Applicability: members who terminate before qualifying for Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement Pensions (details not included in the excerpt).
- Common requirements across provisions:
  - Termination must be from both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization.
  - Benefits are generally calculated per Table A and may use Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service as of termination.

nodes.title: Special Early Retirement Pension.
nodes.heading: 34.4.3 4.03 Special Early Retirement Pension.
nodes.start_phrase: A Member may be entitled to receive a Special Early Retirement Pension if his employment with both his Employer and the PepsiCo Or ganization terminates on or after age 50 but before age 55 and after completion of not less than 10 years of Service and only if such Special Early Retirement Pension payments have been authorized by the V ice President.
nodes.summary:
- Article IV outlines eligibility and calculation rules for various pension benefits.
- Normal Retirement Pension (Section 4.01):
  - Eligibility: Employment with both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization ends at the Member’s Normal Retirement Age.
  - Annuity Starting Date: First day of the month coincident with or immediately following termination.
  - Form of payment: Normal form under Section 5.02 unless an optional form is elected under Section 5.03.
  - Benefit amount: Calculated per Table A.
- Early Retirement Pension (Section 4.02):
  - Eligibility: Termination with both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization on or after age 55 but before Normal Retirement Age, with at least 10 years of Service.
  - Annuity Starting Date: Ordinarily the Normal Retirement Date; Member may elect the first day of any month after termination and before the Normal Retirement Date.
  - Benefit amount: Computed per Table A as if retiring at Normal Retirement Date, using Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service as of termination; if commencing before Normal Retirement Date, reduced by 4/12 of 1% for each month commencement precedes the date the Member would have attained age 62.
- Special Early Retirement Pension (Section 4.03):
  - Eligibility: Termination on or after age 50 but before age 55, with at least 10 years of Service, and only if payments are authorized by the Vice President.
  - Annuity Starting Date: First day of the month after the Vice President authorizes the Special Early Retirement Pension.
  - Benefit amount: Computed per Table A as if retiring at Normal Retirement Date, using Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service as of termination; reduced by 4/12 of 1% for each month commencement precedes the date the Member would have attained age 62.
- Deferred Vested Pension (Section 4.04(a)):
  - Applicability: Members who terminate employment with both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization before becoming eligible for Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement Pensions.

nodes.title: Deferred Vested Pension.
nodes.heading: 34.4.4 4.04 Deferred Vested Pension.
nodes.start_phrase: This Section 4.04 applies to a Member who terminates employment with both his Employer and the PepsiCo Organization before becoming eligible for a Normal Retirement Pension, Early Retirement Pension or Special Early Retirement Pension.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article IV outlines the requirements for pension benefits, defining eligibility, start dates, benefit calculations, reductions, vesting, and treatment of service across employment changes.
- 4.01 Normal Retirement Pension:
  - Eligible when employment with both the Employer and the PepsiCo Organization ends at Normal Retirement Age.
  - Annuity Starting Date is the first day of the month on/after termination.
  - Paid in the normal form (Section 5.02) unless an optional form is elected (Section 5.03).
  - Benefit calculated under Table A.
- 4.02 Early Retirement Pension:
  - Eligibility: termination on/after age 55 but before Normal Retirement Age, with 10+ years of Service.
  - Default Annuity Starting Date is the Normal Retirement Date, but the Member may elect to commence earlier on the first day of any month after termination and before Normal Retirement Date.
  - Amount computed per Table A as if retiring at Normal Retirement Date, using Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service at termination.
  - Reduction of 4/12 of 1% per month for commencement before age 62.
- 4.03 Special Early Retirement Pension:
  - Eligibility: termination on/after age 50 but before 55, with 10+ years of Service, only if authorized by the Vice President.
  - Annuity starts the first day of the month after authorization.
  - Amount computed per Table A as if at Normal Retirement Date, using Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service at termination.
  - Same reduction of 4/12 of 1% per month for commencement before age 62.
- 4.04 Deferred Vested Pension:
  - Applies to Members terminating before becoming eligible for Normal/Early/Special Early Retirement.
  - Must be vested under Sections 4.06 or 4.07.
  - Amount determined under Table A; if the Member remains employed within the PepsiCo Organization/any Employer after ceasing Active Membership, the amount is based on Highest Average Monthly Salary at final termination from both entities (subject to Sections 9.13 and 9.14) and Pensionable Service at that termination.
  - Commences at the later of termination from both entities or Normal Retirement Date; Member may elect commencement on/after age 55 (or later of termination).
  - Early commencement reduction follows the PepsiCo Salaried Plan “Vested Pension” factors (not the 4/12 of 1% factors in 4.02/4.03).
  - Rehire: if later re-eligible, Active Membership resumes; prior Service and Pensionable Service aggregate with new service unless the earlier benefit was cashed out (Section 5.05).
- 4.05 Late Retirement Pension:
  - For Members who continue working past Normal Retirement Age.
  - Annuity starts the first day of the month on/after termination.
  - Salary and Pensionable Service after Normal Retirement Date are credited unless the Vice President prospectively determines otherwise.
- 4.06 Vesting:
  - Full vesting after 5 years of Service, or earlier upon death or disability while employed.
  - Disability determined by the Vice President under applicable standards.
  - Subject to Section 9.14 and Table A(I)(c).
- General notes:
  - “Highest Average Monthly Salary” and detailed formulas are in Table A.
  - References to other plan sections include 5.02, 5.03, 5.05, 9.13, 9.14, and the PepsiCo Salaried Plan reduction factors.

nodes.title: Late Retirement Pension.
nodes.heading: 34.4.5 4.05 Late Retirement Pension.
nodes.start_phrase: A Member who continues employment with the PepsiCo Or ganization or any Employer after his Normal Retirement Age shall be entitled to a Late Retirement Pension.
nodes.summary:
- Defines eligibility and calculation rules for a Deferred Vested Pension once a member meets vesting under Sections 4.06/4.07.
- Pension amount is determined by Table A; for members who remain employed after ceasing Active Member status, benefits are based on Highest Average Monthly Salary at final termination from both the Employer and PepsiCo Organization (subject to Sections 9.13 and 9.14) and Pensionable Service through that termination date.
- Commencement of a Deferred Vested Pension is the later of termination from both the Employer and PepsiCo Organization or the Normal Retirement Date; members may elect to start any month after age 55 (or later if termination occurs after 55), with reductions using the PepsiCo Salaried Plan’s vested pension factors (not Early or Special Early Retirement factors in Sections 4.02 and 4.03).
- Rehire rule: a member entitled to a Deferred Vested Pension who becomes an Eligible Employee again is re-admitted to Active Membership; prior and subsequent Service and Pensionable Service are aggregated for the final pension calculation unless the earlier benefit was cashed out under Section 5.05.
- Late Retirement Pension: available if employment continues past Normal Retirement Age; annuity starts the first day of the month on or after termination from both entities; Salary and Pensionable Service after Normal Retirement Date are credited unless prospectively limited by the Vice President.
- Vesting: full vesting after 5 years of Service, or earlier upon death or disability while employed; disability is determined by the Vice President under applicable standards; subject to Section 9.14 and Table A(I)(c).
- Administrative notes and cross-references: Vice President handles elections and determinations; multiple references to Table A and plan sections governing limits and reduction factors.

nodes.title: Vesting.
nodes.heading: 34.4.6 4.06 Vesting.
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to Section 9.14 and to T able A (I)(c), a Member shall be fully vested in, and have a nonforfeitable right to, his Pension upon completing 5 years of Service, or if earlier , upon the death or disability of the Member while employed by the Employer or PepsiCo Or ganization.
nodes.summary:
- Defines eligibility and calculation rules for a Deferred Vested Pension for members who meet vesting requirements, with amounts determined by Table A.
- For members who remain employed by PepsiCo or an Employer after ceasing Active Membership, the Deferred Vested Pension is based on Highest Average Monthly Salary and Pensionable Service as of final termination from both the Employer and PepsiCo, subject to Sections 9.13 and 9.14.
- Commencement of a Deferred Vested Pension is the later of termination from both the Employer and PepsiCo or the Normal Retirement Date; members may elect to start any month after age 55 (or later termination), with early commencement reductions using the PepsiCo Salaried Plan’s vested pension factors (not Early/Special Early Retirement factors).
- If a member entitled to a Deferred Vested Pension is rehired as an Eligible Employee, they are re-admitted to Active Membership; prior and subsequent Service and Pensionable Service are aggregated for future pension calculation, unless the earlier benefit was cashed out under Section 5.05.
- Establishes a Late Retirement Pension for members working past Normal Retirement Age; the annuity start date is the first day of the month on or after termination from both the Employer and PepsiCo, and Salary and Pensionable Service after Normal Retirement Date are credited unless the Vice President prospectively decides otherwise.
- Sets vesting at 5 years of Service, or earlier upon death or disability while employed, subject to Section 9.14 and Table A(I)(c); the Vice President determines disability under appropriate standards.

nodes.title: Special Vesting for Approved Transfers and Status Changes.
nodes.heading: 34.4.7 4.07 Special Vesting for Approved Transfers and Status Changes.
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding Section 4.06 above, in the case of an Active Member who will have an Approved T ransfer during a Plan Y ear, the Active Member shall automatically have special vesting apply as of the last business day before the earlier of – (a) the Active Member ’s Approved T ransfer , or (b) the day the Active Member would become a U.S. Person in connection with the Approved T ransfer .
nodes.summary:
- Section 4.07 establishes special vesting rules tied to certain employment changes:
  - Automatic special vesting for Approved Transfers: An Active Member with an Approved Transfer during a Plan Year automatically receives special vesting effective the last business day before the earlier of the transfer date or the date the Member would become a U.S. Person due to the transfer.
  - Special vesting for Status Changes: An Active Member experiencing a Status Change may request special vesting effective the last business day before the change; the request and the Vice President’s approval must be finalized before the vesting date.
  - The effect of special vesting is to vest the Member to the same extent as would apply under Section 4.06 as of the special vesting date.
  - All rights under Section 4.07 are conditioned on the Plan remaining fully exempt from IRC Section 409A; Section 4.07 does not apply where inconsistent with that exemption.

- Section 4.08 addresses accruals after benefit commencement:
  - Applies when a Member earns Service and Pensionable Service after their Annuity Starting Date (excluding cashouts under Section 5.05).
  - Any suspended prior benefits and any additional benefits accrued after the prior commencement are paid at a subsequent Annuity Starting Date.
  - Suspension/continuation of prior benefits, benefit adjustments payable at the subsequent date, and elections of time and form of payment are governed by rules set by the Vice President, generally based on the PepsiCo Salaried Plan’s post-commencement accrual rules unless modified.

nodes.title: Accruals After Benefit Commencement.
nodes.heading: 34.4.8 4.08 Accruals After Benefit Commencement.
nodes.start_phrase: This section applies to a Member who earns Service and Pensionable Service for a period that is after his Annuity Starting Date under the preceding Sections of this Article IV (other than an Annuity Starting Date related to a cashout distribution under Section 5.05).
nodes.summary:
- Special vesting rules (Section 4.07):
  - Automatic special vesting for Approved Transfers: For an Active Member with an Approved Transfer in a Plan Year, special vesting automatically applies on the last business day before the earlier of (i) the Approved Transfer or (ii) the date the member would become a U.S. Person in connection with the transfer.
  - Special vesting for Status Changes: An Active Member may request special vesting before a Status Change; the Vice President must approve, and both the request and approval must be finalized before the effective date (the last business day before the Status Change).
  - Effect of special vesting: The member becomes vested to the same extent as under Section 4.06 as of the special vesting date.
  - 409A compliance override: These rights apply only to the extent the Plan remains fully exempt from IRC Section 409A; if inconsistent, Section 4.07 does not apply.

- Accruals after benefit commencement (Section 4.08):
  - Applies to members who earn Service and Pensionable Service after a prior Annuity Starting Date (other than a cashout under Section 5.05).
  - Any suspended prior benefits and additional accruals after that commencement are paid at a subsequent Annuity Starting Date.
  - Rules for suspension/continuation, benefit adjustments, and time/form of payment at the subsequent Annuity Starting Date are set by the Vice President, generally following the PepsiCo Salaried Plan’s post-commencement rules unless modified.

nodes.title: ARTICLE V - DISTRIBUTION OPTIONS
nodes.heading: 34.5 ARTICLE V - DISTRIBUTION OPTIONS
nodes.start_phrase: Section 5.02 sets forth the normal forms of payment for married and unmarried Members.
nodes.summary:
- Article V governs how pension benefits are distributed, distinguishing between normal and optional forms and tying availability to eligibility under Article IV.
- Marital status for normal forms is determined on the Member’s Annuity Starting Date; for optional forms, on the date the optional form is elected.
- Normal forms of payment:
  - Unmarried Members: Single Life Annuity—monthly payments start at the Annuity Starting Date and stop at the Member’s death.
  - Married Members: 50% Survivor Annuity—reduced monthly payments for the Member for life, with a 50% contingent survivor annuity to the Eligible Spouse beginning the month after the Member’s death and ending at the spouse’s death.
  - Reduction mechanics: For Annuity Starting Dates on/after January 1, 2019, the Member’s pension (per Table A) is adjusted to its Actuarial Equivalent to reflect the survivor benefit; for earlier dates, generally a 10% reduction applies (subject to Section 5.03(f)). Accrued benefits as of January 1, 1990, for certain Members are grandfathered and not subject to this reduction to the extent provided under prior plan terms.
- Optional forms of payment:
  - Married Members may elect a Single Life Annuity or a 75% Survivor Annuity instead of the normal form, regardless of eligibility for other options.
  - Both married and unmarried Members may elect alternative survivor options (details continue beyond the excerpt), with elections made on prescribed forms.
- References include Article IV (eligibility for benefits) and Table A (pension amount determination), with definitions centered on “Annuity Starting Date” and “Eligible Spouse.”

nodes.title: Distribution Options.
nodes.heading: 34.5.1 5.01 Distribution Options.
nodes.start_phrase: Section 5.02 sets forth the normal forms of payment for married and unmarried Members.
nodes.summary:
- Article V governs distribution options for pension benefits, specifying default (normal) and optional payment forms based on marital status.
- Section 5.01:
  - For normal forms, marital status is determined on the Annuity Starting Date; for optional forms, on the date the option is elected.
  - Distributions under Article V are only available if the Member meets benefit entitlement requirements under Article IV.
- Section 5.02 (Normal Forms of Payment):
  - Unmarried Members: Default is a Single Life Annuity—monthly payments begin at the Annuity Starting Date and end at the Member’s death.
  - Married Members: Default is a 50% Survivor Annuity—reduced monthly payments for the Member’s life, with a 50% contingent survivor annuity to the Eligible Spouse beginning the month after the Member’s death and ending at the spouse’s death.
  - Reduction rules: For Annuity Starting Dates on/after January 1, 2019, the Member’s pension (per Table A) is reduced to its Actuarial Equivalent to reflect the survivor benefit; for earlier dates, generally a 10% reduction applies (subject to Section 5.03(f)). Pre–January 1, 1990 accrued benefits under the prior plan terms may be exempt from this reduction.
- Section 5.03 (Optional Forms of Payment):
  - Married Members may elect a Single Life Annuity or a 75% Survivor Annuity instead of the normal form, regardless of eligibility for other options in subsections (b)–(d).
  - Survivor options are also available to both married and unmarried Members who waive the normal form (details continue beyond the provided text).
- Other references: Uses Table A for benefit amounts; defines Eligible Spouse; clarifies timing of survivor payments (first day of the month following the Member’s death).

nodes.title: Normal Forms of Payment.
nodes.heading: 34.5.2 5.02 Normal Forms of Payment.
nodes.start_phrase: An unmarried Member shall be paid his Pension in the form of a Single Life Annuity unless he elects otherwise in accordance with Section 5.03.
nodes.summary:
- Article V outlines when and how pension benefits can be paid, distinguishing between “normal” and “optional” forms of distribution.
- Marital status is determined at the Annuity Starting Date for normal forms (Section 5.02) and at the date of electing an optional form for optional forms (Section 5.03).
- Distributions under Article V are only available if the Member has satisfied benefit eligibility under Article IV.
- Normal forms of payment:
  - Unmarried Members: Single Life Annuity—monthly payments start at the Annuity Starting Date and cease at the Member’s death.
  - Married Members: 50% Survivor Annuity—reduced monthly payments to the Member for life, with 50% continuing to the Eligible Spouse after the Member’s death until the spouse’s death.
  - Reduction rules: For Annuity Starting Dates on/after January 1, 2019, the Member’s pension is reduced to its Actuarial Equivalent to reflect the survivor benefit; for earlier dates (subject to Section 5.03(f)), a 10% reduction applies. Pre-1990 accrued pensions under prior Plan terms may be exempt from these reductions to the extent provided.
- Optional forms of payment:
  - Married Members may elect a Single Life Annuity or a 75% Survivor Annuity instead of the normal 50% Survivor Annuity, regardless of eligibility for other options.
  - Both married and unmarried Members who decline the normal form may choose among survivor options (details to be specified on an election form; text truncated).

nodes.title: Optional Forms of Payment.
nodes.heading: 34.5.3 5.03 Optional Forms of Payment.
nodes.start_phrase: A married Member who elects not to receive benefits in the normal form may receive his Pension in the form of the Single Life Annuity described in Section 5.02(a) above or the 75 Percent Survivor Annuity described in (b)(2) below , regardless of whether he is eligible for the optional forms of payment described in (b), (c) and (d) below .
nodes.summary:
- Article V outlines pension distribution options and is available only if a Member meets Article IV benefit eligibility.
- Marital status for default forms is determined on the Annuity Starting Date; for optional forms, on the election date.

Normal forms of payment (Section 5.02):
- Unmarried: Single Life Annuity—monthly payments for life, end at death.
- Married: 50% Survivor Annuity—reduced payments for Member’s life with 50% to Eligible Spouse after death; reductions are actuarial equivalent for Annuity Starting Dates on/after 1/1/2019, generally 10% for earlier dates; pre-1/1/1990 accruals may be protected.

Optional forms (Section 5.03):
- For married Members: may elect Single Life Annuity or 75% Survivor Annuity regardless of other optional eligibility.
- Survivor options (available to married and unmarried):
  - 100%, 75%, or 50% Survivor Options: reduced lifetime benefit to Member with stated percentage continuing to designated Dependant; amounts are actuarial equivalents (pre-2019 fixed reductions of 20%, 15%, 10% respectively; possible subsidies for pre-1990 entitlements).
  - 10-Year Certain and Life: reduced lifetime payments with at least 120 payments guaranteed; remaining payments go to Dependant/estate; from 1/1/2010, remaining payments may be commuted to a lump sum actuarial equivalent without mortality reduction.
- Lump sum: actuarial equivalent of the Single Life Annuity using PepsiCo Salaried Plan factors; paid in one taxable year as soon as practicable after elected date; from 1/1/2010, interest added to late payments per plan practices; no interest during Member-elected deferral.
- Combination lump sum/monthly: Member elects whole-number percentages totaling 100% between a lump sum and a chosen monthly form; each portion calculated separately per applicable rules.
- Election/consent rules: elections must be made on required forms within VP-set periods; Dependant designation permitted with VP approval if not the Eligible Spouse; spousal consent required if a married Member names a non-spouse Dependant; no changes after commencement.
- Death before commencement: a timely, otherwise-valid optional election (including spousal consent) is deemed in effect at death; not effective if the named Dependant dies before first payment would have begun.

Special reduction for younger Dependants (pre-1/1/2019 start dates):
- If Dependant is >10 and ≤20 years younger: increase reduction by 5 percentage points.
- If >20 years younger: add an additional 0.2% per full year over 20.

Applicability restrictions (Section 5.04):
- Combination lump sum/monthly not available for Annuity Starting Dates before 1990.
- Deferred Vested Pensions: limited to Single Life, 50% Survivor, or 75% Survivor options; from 1/1/2015, a Lump Sum may be available to the extent offered on an ongoing basis under the PepsiCo Salaried Plan (Pension Equalization Plan participants are not excluded from this option).
- For Members entitled to a Pension before 1/1/1990, actuarial equivalencies may be adjusted by the Vice President to reflect subsidized survivor benefits.

General:
- Amounts often reference Table A and Actuarial Equivalent definitions.
- The Vice President sets forms, timing, approvals, and certain actuarial adjustments.

nodes.title: Applicability of Certain Options.
nodes.heading: 34.5.4 5.04 Applicability of Certain Options.
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding the preceding provisions of this Article V , the availability of certain distribution options shall be restricted in accordance with the terms of this Section 5.04.
nodes.summary:
- Posthumous effectiveness of a member’s elected optional form of payment: if a member leaves employment and dies before payments begin, the election (with required Eligible Spouse consent) is deemed in effect as of the first day of the month following death. This deemed effectiveness applies only once to the initial election, unless the Vice President approves otherwise before a subsequent election. If the specified Dependant for a Section 5.03(b) survivor option dies before the first installment would have been payable, that election is not honored.
- Additional reduction for much younger Dependants (Annuity Starting Dates before Jan 1, 2019): if the Dependant is more than 10 years younger than the member, the normal reduction is increased by 5 percentage points when the age gap is up to 20 years; if more than 20 years younger, add a further 0.2% per full year over 20.
- Applicability/restrictions on options (Section 5.04):
  - The form in Section 5.03(d) is unavailable for Annuity Starting Dates before 1990.
  - Deferred Vested Pensions (Section 4.04) may be paid only as a Single Life Annuity, 50% Survivor Option, or 75% Survivor Option; effective Jan 1, 2015, a Lump Sum is also available but only to the extent offered on an ongoing basis under the PepsiCo Salaried Plan (with the difference that participants here with a benefit under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan are not excluded from the lump sum).
  - For members entitled to a pension before Jan 1, 1990, actuarial equivalencies may be adjusted by the Vice President to reflect subsidized survivor benefits available under Section 5.02(b).
- Cashout provisions (Section 5.05):
  - Small benefit cashout: the Vice President may commute trivial pensions to a lump sum after termination from both the Employer and PepsiCo Organization, or after an internal transfer that stops active accruals, on a discretionary date, without member consent.
  - Discretionary cashout after benefit commencement (effective Jan 1, 2019): the Vice President may pay a lump sum if the present value of remaining payments is ≤ $75,000; amount determined using Section 5.03(c) lump-sum factors as of a VP-selected payment date.
- Dependant designation rules (Section 5.06):
  - Members electing a survivor option must designate a Dependant; they may change/revoke before the election’s effective date.
  - If married, naming a non-spouse Dependant requires the Eligible Spouse’s written consent; revocations do not require spouse consent.
  - Designations/changes/consents must follow VP rules, be on VP forms, and are effective only when filed with the VP.
  - For the survivor option in Section 5.03(b)(4), members may name both a primary and contingent Dependant; if none is properly designated, the election is not effective.

nodes.title: Cashout of Certain Benefits.
nodes.heading: 34.5.5 5.05 Cashout of Certain Benefits.
nodes.start_phrase: Where the total Pension payable to any person under the DB Program is, in the opinion of the Vice President, of an amount that is relatively trivial (when considered by itself or in relation to the potential administrative burden of continuing to keep track of such Pension under the DB Program), he may commute the whole of such Pension to a lump sum payable following (i) the relevant Member ’s termination of employment from both his Employer and the PepsiCo Or ganization, or (ii) a Member ’s transfer within the PepsiCo Or ganization that results in the Member ceasing to actively accrue all benefits under the DB Program, on a date determined in the discretion of the V ice President, without the consent of the Member .
nodes.summary:
- Brief reference to eligibility for favorable survivor benefit terms under Section 5.02(b).
- Section 5.05 (Cashout of Certain Benefits):
  - Small benefits: The Vice President may commute a trivial pension to a lump sum, payable after employment termination from the Employer and PepsiCo Organization or after a transfer that stops active accruals; timing at the Vice President’s discretion; no member consent required.
  - After benefit commencement: Effective January 1, 2019, the Vice President may pay a lump sum to a member already receiving non-lump payments if the present value of remaining payments is ≤ $75,000; the lump sum equals the actuarial equivalent using Section 5.03(c) factors as of a payment date set at the Vice President’s discretion.
- Section 5.06 (Designation of Dependant for survivor options):
  - Members electing a survivor option must designate a Dependant; they may change or revoke the designation before the election’s effective date.
  - If married and naming someone other than the Eligible Spouse, written spousal consent is required; revocations do not require consent.
  - Designations, changes, revocations, and required consents must follow Vice President–adopted rules, be on provided forms, in writing, and are effective only when filed with the Vice President.
  - For the survivor option in Section 5.03(b)(4), a primary and contingent Dependant may be named; absent a proper designation, that option is not effective.

nodes.title: Designation of Dependant.
nodes.heading: 34.5.6 5.06 Designation of Dependant.
nodes.start_phrase: A Member who has elected to receive all or part of his pension in a form of payment that includes a survivor option shall designate a Dependant who will be entitled to any amounts payable on his death.
nodes.summary:
- Cross-reference noting availability on favorable terms of a survivor benefit under Section 5.02(b).
- Section 5.05(a) Cashout of Small Benefits: The Vice President may commute a relatively trivial defined benefit pension to a lump sum, payable after the member’s termination from the employer/PepsiCo organization or upon a transfer that stops active accruals; timing is at the Vice President’s discretion and does not require the member’s consent.
- Section 5.05(b) Discretionary Cashout After Benefit Commencement: Effective January 1, 2019, the Vice President may convert an ongoing non–lump-sum pension into a lump sum if the present value of remaining payments is ≤ $75,000; the lump sum equals the actuarial equivalent using Section 5.03(c) factors as of a payment date chosen at the Vice President’s discretion.
- Section 5.06 Designation of Dependant: Members electing a form with a survivor option must designate a Dependant; they may change or revoke the designation before the election’s effective date. If married and naming a non-spouse Dependant, the Eligible Spouse’s written consent is required; revocations do not require spousal consent. All designations/changes/revocations and any required spousal consents must follow Vice President rules, be on provided forms, and are effective only when filed.
- Special rule for the survivor option in Section 5.03(b)(4): Members may name both a primary and contingent Dependant; if no Dependant is properly designated, that option election is not effective.

nodes.title: ARTICLE VI - DEATH BENEFITS
nodes.heading: 34.6 ARTICLE VI - DEATH BENEFITS
nodes.start_phrase: The surviving Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner , as applicable, of a Member who dies shall be entitled to certain survivor benefits if the requirements of this Article VI are satisfied.
nodes.summary:
- Article VI outlines death benefits for a Member’s surviving Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, generally determined under Section II of Table A, with specific rules in Sections 6.02 and 6.03.
- Section 6.01: If an Active Member, a Member in Service past Normal Retirement Date with at least 5 years of Service, or a Member eligible for Early or Special Early Retirement dies and is survived by an Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner (and is not covered by Section 5.03(e)), a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension is payable, calculated per Section II of Table A.
- Section 6.02: If a vested Member (per Sections 4.06 or 4.07) who has not started receiving benefits dies and is survived by an Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner (and is not covered by Section 5.03(e)), a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension is payable. It is calculated based on Salary and Pensionable Service as of the earlier of death or termination, as if the Member lived to the earliest start date of the vested benefit, elected a 50% Survivor Annuity, and died that same day. Coverage is funded by a reduction to the Member’s monthly benefit using the PepsiCo Salaried Plan methodology; waiver of this coverage requires Vice President approval.
