- Section 6.03: Form and timing of payment. The survivor benefit is generally a life annuity to the Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner; if the Member was eligible for Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement at death, the survivor may elect a single lump sum instead of an annuity. Payments start on the first day of the month on or after the Member’s death (subject to Section 6.04).

nodes.title: ARTICLE VI - DEATH BENEFITS - Introduction
nodes.heading: 34.6 ARTICLE VI - DEATH BENEFITS
nodes.start_phrase: The surviving Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner , as applicable, of a Member who dies shall be entitled to certain survivor benefits if the requirements of this Article VI are satisfied.
nodes.summary:
ARTICLE VI - DEA TH BENEFITS
The surviving Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner , as applicable, of a Member who dies shall be entitled to
certain survivor benefits if the requirements of this Article VI are satisfied. Except as provided in Sections 6.02 and 6.03, the
amount of any such benefit shall be determined in accordance with Section II of T able A.
6.01    Active and Retir ement-Eligible Members.

nodes.title: Active and Retirement-Eligible Members.
nodes.heading: 34.6.1 6.01 Active and Retirement-Eligible Members.
nodes.start_phrase: In the event of the death of an Active Member , a Member in Service after his Normal Retirement Date who had at his death completed at least 5 years of Service, or a Member entitled to an Early Retirement Pension under Section 4.02 or Special Early Retirement Pension under Section 4.03, if such Member is survived by an Eligible Spouse or an Eligible Domestic Partner and is not entitled at the time of death to the protection provided by Section 5.03(e), there shall be a Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension payable to the Member ’s surviving Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner (as applicable), calculated in accordance with the provisions of Section II of T able A.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes survivor benefits (Pre-Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s Pension) for an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner upon a Member’s death, with amounts generally determined under Section II of Table A.
- Defines eligibility for benefits when the deceased was: (a) an Active Member; (b) in service past Normal Retirement Date with at least 5 years of Service; or (c) entitled to Early or Special Early Retirement, provided the Member was not protected under Section 5.03(e).
- Provides survivor benefits for vested Members not covered by 6.01 who had not begun receiving their pension, contingent on having an Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner and not being protected under Section 5.03(e).
- Specifies the vested-benefit calculation: based on Salary and Pensionable Service as of the earlier of death or termination; computed as if the Member lived to the earliest start date, elected a 50% Survivor Annuity at that time, and died that same day.
- States that coverage for the pre-retirement survivor benefit is funded by a reduction to the Member’s monthly benefit, determined using the methodology and factors of the PepsiCo Salaried Plan; waiver of this coverage requires Vice President approval.
- Sets the form of payment to a life annuity for the surviving Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner, with an option for a single lump sum if the Member was eligible for Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement at death.
- Provides timing: payments generally commence on the first day of the month on or after the Member’s death, subject to Section 6.04 (text truncated thereafter).

nodes.title: Vested Members.
nodes.heading: 34.6.2 6.02 Vested Members.
nodes.start_phrase: In the event of the death of a Member who is not described in Section 6.01 above, who is vested under Section 4.06 or Section 4.07 and who has not yet commenced or received the Member ’s Pension, if such Member is survived by an Eligible Spouse or an Eligible Domestic Partner and is not entitled at the time of death to the protections provided by Section 5.03(e), there shall be payable a Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension (as applicable), which shall be calculated based on the Member ’s Salary and Pensionable Service as of the earlier of the Member ’s death or termination of employment.
nodes.summary:
- Article VI outlines death benefits for a Member’s surviving Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, generally determined under Section II of Table A, subject to exceptions in Sections 6.02 and 6.03.
- Section 6.01 (Active and retirement-eligible members): If an Active Member, a Member in Service past Normal Retirement Date with at least 5 years of Service, or a Member eligible for Early or Special Early Retirement dies, and is survived by an Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner and not covered by Section 5.03(e), a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension is payable per Section II of Table A.
- Section 6.02 (Vested members not covered by 6.01): If a vested Member (under Sections 4.06 or 4.07) dies before commencing benefits, and is survived by an Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner and not covered by Section 5.03(e), a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension is payable. It is calculated based on Salary and Pensionable Service as of the earlier of death or termination, as if the Member lived to the earliest start date, elected a 50% Survivor Annuity, and died that same day. Coverage is funded by a reduction to the Member’s monthly benefit, using the methodology/factors of the PepsiCo Salaried Plan; waiver of this coverage requires Vice President approval.
- Section 6.03 (Form and timing of payment): Death benefits are paid as a life annuity to the surviving Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner. If the Member was eligible for Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement at death, the survivor may elect a single lump sum instead. Payments commence on the first day of the month coinciding with or next following death (subject to Section 6.04; remaining timing language not fully shown).

nodes.title: Form and Time of Payment of Death Benefits.
nodes.heading: 34.6.3 6.03 Form and Time of Payment of Death Benefits.
nodes.start_phrase: Any Pension payable pursuant to this Article VI shall be payable for the surviving Eligible Spouse’ s or surviving Domestic Partner ’s life only; however , in the case of a Pension payable to a surviving Eligible Spouse or surviving Domestic Partner where the Member was eligible for a Normal, Early or Special Early Retirement Pension at death, the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner may elect to receive the Pension in the form of a single lump sum payment in lieu of the annuity payment.
nodes.summary:
- Article VI sets out death benefits for a Member’s surviving Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, generally determined under Section II of Table A, with exceptions in Sections 6.02 and 6.03 and subject to not having protection under Section 5.03(e).
- Section 6.01 (Active and retirement-eligible members): If an Active Member, a Member in Service past Normal Retirement Date with at least 5 years of Service, or a Member eligible for Early or Special Early Retirement dies and is survived by an Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner, a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension is payable, calculated per Section II of Table A.
- Section 6.02 (Vested members not covered by 6.01): If a vested Member (under Sections 4.06 or 4.07) dies before commencing benefits and is survived by an Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner, a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s Pension is payable. It is based on Salary and Pensionable Service as of the earlier of death or termination and calculated as if the Member lived to the earliest start date, elected a 50% Survivor Annuity, and died that day. Coverage is funded by a reduction to the Member’s monthly benefit, using the methodology of the PepsiCo Salaried Plan, and may be waived only with Vice President approval.
- Section 6.03 (Form and timing): Death benefits are generally paid as a life annuity to the surviving Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner; if the Member was eligible for Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement at death, the survivor may elect a single lump sum instead. Payments start on the first day of the month on or after death, or (if later) when the Member would have reached age 55. If starting before Normal Retirement Age, early commencement reductions under Sections 4.02, 4.03, or 4.04 apply.
- Section 6.04 (Disposition): The Vice President may direct payment or application of the benefit to one or more of the Member’s Dependants in such shares and forms as deemed appropriate and may authorize immediate commencement or lump-sum payment after death, notwithstanding other DC Program provisions.

nodes.title: Disposition of Death Benefits.
nodes.heading: 34.6.4 6.04 Disposition of Death Benefits.
nodes.start_phrase: Any benefit expressed to be subject to disposition in accordance with the provision of this Article VI shall be held by the V ice President with power to pay or apply the same to or for the benefit of such one or more of the Member ’s Dependants, as the V ice President shall think fit and if more than one in such shares as they shall likewise think fit.
nodes.summary:
- Early commencement of a pension payable to a Member’s Eligible Spouse before the Member’s Normal Retirement Age, with the benefit reduced per Sections 4.02, 4.03, or 4.04 based on the underlying pension type; reference to age 55 as a benchmark for such timing.
- Section 6.04 on Disposition of Death Benefits: grants the Vice President discretion to hold and distribute death benefits to one or more of the Member’s Dependants in such shares as deemed appropriate.
- Authorizes the Vice President to determine payment form and timing, including directing commencement or a lump-sum payment as soon as practicable after the Member’s death, notwithstanding other DC Program provisions.

nodes.title: ARTICLE VII - ADMINISTRATION
nodes.heading: 34.7 ARTICLE VII - ADMINISTRATION
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the V ice President, who shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as he deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the Vice President administers the Plan, with sole discretion to interpret provisions, issue regulations, and make determinations that are final, conclusive, and binding on all parties.
- Authorizes the Vice President to delegate any administrative duties to other persons or entities; actions by delegates are treated as actions by the Vice President.
- Provides a “facility of payment” rule allowing the Vice President to direct benefits to a legal representative or otherwise apply payments for a beneficiary who is legally disabled or incapacitated; such payments discharge the Plan’s liability.
- Confers exclusive discretionary authority on the Vice President to decide eligibility and benefit amounts; benefits are payable only if the Vice President determines entitlement.
- States that the Vice President’s decisions are subject to review only under the arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.
- Permits the Vice President to consider the Corporation’s intent when interpreting Plan provisions, even if other documents do not expressly contemplate that approach.
- Outlines a claims procedure for situations where a claim (by Members, putative Members, Dependants, or putative Dependants) is wholly or partially denied, and allows the Vice President to modify the procedure so long as the core review steps are maintained.
- The section ends mid-procedure description, indicating additional claims process details follow.

nodes.title: Authority to Administer Plan.
nodes.heading: 34.7.1 7.01 Authority to Administer Plan.
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the V ice President, who shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as he deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the Vice President administers the Plan with sole, discretionary authority to interpret provisions, issue regulations, and make determinations that are final and binding on all parties.
- Authorizes the Vice President to delegate any administrative duties or responsibilities to other persons or entities; actions by delegates are treated as actions of the Vice President.
- Provides a “facility of payment” rule allowing the Vice President to direct benefits to a legal representative or otherwise apply payments for the benefit of a person who is legally disabled or incapacitated; such payments fully discharge the Plan’s liability for those amounts.
- Confers exclusive discretionary authority on the Vice President over eligibility, benefit amounts, and Plan interpretation; benefits are payable only if the Vice President decides the claimant is entitled.
- Specifies that the Vice President’s decisions are to be reviewed, if at all, under an arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard and may take into account the Corporation’s intent even if not explicit in plan documents.
- Outlines a claims procedure for denied claims (including those by Members, putative Members, Dependants, and putative Dependants), with flexibility for the Vice President to modify procedures so long as core review steps are preserved; the section text ends mid-procedure.

nodes.title: Facility of Payment.
nodes.heading: 34.7.2 7.02 Facility of Payment.
nodes.start_phrase: Whenever , in the opinion of the V ice President, a person entitled to receive any payment of a benefit or installment thereof hereunder is under a legal disability or is incapacitated in any way so as to be unable to manage his financial af fairs, the Vice President may direct that payments from the Plan be made to such person’ s legal representative for his benefit, or that the payment be applied for the benefit of such person in such manner as the V ice President considers advisable.
nodes.summary:
- Article VII sets out Plan administration.
- The Vice President administers the Plan with sole, broad discretion to interpret provisions and issue regulations; all interpretations, determinations, and regulations are final and binding.
- The Vice President may delegate any duties or responsibilities to others, and actions by delegates are treated as actions by the Vice President.
- Facility of Payment: if a beneficiary is legally disabled or otherwise unable to manage finances, the Vice President may direct payments to a legal representative or apply them for the beneficiary’s benefit; such payments fully discharge Plan liability.
- Claims Procedure: the Vice President has exclusive discretionary authority to construe the Plan, determine eligibility and benefit amounts, and benefits are payable only if the Vice President so decides. Decisions are reviewed under an arbitrary-and-capricious (abuse of discretion) standard. The Vice President may consider the Corporation’s intent and may modify claims procedures so long as core steps are preserved. The procedure applies to claims by members, putative members, dependants, and putative dependants when claims are denied in whole or part.

nodes.title: Claims Procedure.
nodes.heading: 34.7.3 7.03 Claims Procedure.
nodes.start_phrase: The V ice President shall have the exclusive discretionary authority to construe and to interpret the Plan, to decide all questions of eligibility for benefits and to determine the amount of such benefits, and his decisions on such matters are final and conclusive.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the Vice President administers the Plan with sole, discretionary authority to interpret provisions, issue regulations, make determinations, and that such decisions are final and binding.
- Permits the Vice President to delegate duties to other persons or entities; actions by delegates are treated as actions by the Vice President.
- Provides a “Facility of Payment” allowing the Vice President to direct benefits to a legal representative or apply payments for the benefit of a person under legal disability or incapacity, with such payments fully discharging Plan liability.
- Sets out a claims and appeals procedure:
  - The Vice President has exclusive, absolute discretion to decide eligibility and benefit amounts; decisions are reviewed under an arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.
  - Upon denial, claimant receives written notice within 90 days (extendable to 180 with notice) stating reasons, Plan provisions relied on, what additional information is needed, and review procedures.
  - On review, claimants may submit comments and evidence; a decision is issued within 60 days (extendable to 120 with notice), with written reasons, Plan citations, and the right to free copies of relevant documents.
  - Any external review (court/arbitration) is limited to the record before the Vice President and requires exhaustion of internal remedies (including Section 7.07).
- Imposes a two-year statute of limitations for filing claims or legal actions for wrongful denial of benefits, accruing at the earliest of receipt of a benefit calculation, the identified benefit commencement date, or when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the claim’s facts; post-appeal correspondence does not toll or extend this period.

nodes.title: Limitations on Actions.
nodes.heading: 34.7.4 7.04 Limitations on Actions.
nodes.start_phrase: Any claim filed under Article VII and any action filed in any court or other tribunal by or on behalf of a former or current Employee, Member , Dependant or any other individual, person or entity (collectively , a “Petitioner”) for the alleged wrongful denial of Plan benefits must be brought within two years of the date the Petitioner ’s cause of action first accrues.
nodes.summary:
- Sets out denial notice requirements: within 90 days of the Vice President’s receipt of a claim, the claimant must get a written, understandable notice stating specific reasons for denial, citing the precise Plan provisions, identifying any additional information needed and why, and explaining the Plan’s review procedure and timelines.
- Allows a processing extension to 180 days for special circumstances, with advance written notice before the initial 90-day deadline specifying the reasons and expected decision date.
- Establishes appeal/review rights: a “full and fair review” by the Vice President, including the claimant’s right to submit comments, documents, and records, all of which must be considered even if not presented initially.
- Sets decision-on-review timelines: a written decision within 60 days of the review request, with one possible extension of up to 60 additional days if special circumstances are explained in advance.
- Requires the final decision to be understandable, give specific reasons with Plan citations, and inform the claimant of the right to receive, upon request and at no charge, all documents and information relevant to the claim.
- Limits any court, arbitration, or tribunal review to the administrative record before the Vice President at the time of determination and requires full exhaustion of internal remedies (per Section 7.07) before external review.
- Imposes a two-year statute of limitations for filing claims or legal actions for wrongful denial of benefits, running from the earliest of: receipt of the benefits calculation at issue, the payment commencement date identified by the Vice President, or the claimant’s actual or constructive knowledge of the claim’s factual basis.
- Clarifies that failure to file within two years bars the claim/action and that post-appeal correspondence or communications do not affect or extend this two-year period.

nodes.title: Restriction of Venue.
nodes.heading: 34.7.5 7.05 Restriction of Venue.
nodes.start_phrase: Any claim or action filed in court or any other tribunal in connection with the Plan by or on behalf of a Petitioner shall only be brought or filed in the state or federal courts of New Y ork, specifically the state or federal court, whichever applies, located nearest the Corporation’ s headquarters.
nodes.summary:
- Venue restriction: Any court action related to the Plan by or on behalf of a Petitioner must be brought exclusively in the New York state or federal court (as applicable) located nearest the Corporation’s headquarters.
- Vice President’s discretion: Specific references to the Vice President’s discretion do not limit the breadth or completeness of the Vice President’s discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Mandatory exhaustion of internal claims procedures (Section 7.03) before filing in court:
  - Exhaustion is to be interpreted as broadly as possible; steps may be taken to effect this intent.
  - Exhaustion is not excused for failure to respond to a Claim unless the claimant made it reasonably clear to the Vice President that a Plan Claim was being submitted.
  - Exhaustion is not excused for failure to provide documents unless all are true: (A) the Plan or law requires the documents; (B) the request was in writing, addressed to and actually received by the Vice President; (C) the Vice President failed to provide them within 6 months (or a longer reasonable period); and (D) the requester made it reasonably clear they were asserting a legal right to the documents.
  - A person not treated as a Member must clearly assert to the Vice President that they claim entitlement to Member status to satisfy “sufficient steps.”
  - The exhaustion requirement applies even if other, non-Claim disputes are more significant; to rights the Vice President may offer in novel or particular situations; to actual or potential rights; and even if no specific procedures exist—then the Vice President must promptly establish procedures or apply Section 7.03 by analogy.
  - The Vice President may make special arrangements to consider Claims on a class basis or to address unusual conflict-of-interest concerns.

nodes.title: Effect of Specific References.
nodes.heading: 34.7.6 7.06 Effect of Specific References.
nodes.start_phrase: Specific references in the Plan to the V ice President’ s discretion shall create no inference that the V ice President’ s discretion in any other respect, or in connection with any other provision, is less complete or broad.
nodes.summary:
- Restriction of venue: Any court or tribunal action related to the Plan by or on behalf of a Petitioner must be brought exclusively in New York state or federal courts located nearest the Corporation’s headquarters.
- Vice President’s discretion: Specific references to the Vice President’s discretion do not limit the overall breadth of that discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Mandatory exhaustion: A Claimant must fully exhaust the Plan’s internal claims procedures (Section 7.03) before filing any claim, suit, or action in court or another tribunal.
- Broad interpretation of exhaustion: Courts/tribunals are to interpret the exhaustion requirement as broadly as possible. Exhaustion is not excused:
  - For non-response unless the Claimant made it reasonably clear to the Vice President that a Plan Claim was being submitted.
  - For document requests unless (A) the Plan or law requires the documents, (B) the request is written, addressed to, and actually received by the Vice President, (C) the Vice President fails to provide them within 6 months or a reasonable longer period, and (D) the requester clearly asserted a legal right to the documents.
  - Individuals not treated as Members must clearly state to the Vice President that they claim entitlement to membership.
- Scope of exhaustion: Applies regardless of other concurrent non-Claim disputes, covers rights the Vice President may provide in novel or particular situations, includes actual or potential rights, and applies even if no specific procedures exist—then the Vice President must promptly establish procedures or apply Section 7.03 by analogy.
- Special arrangements: The Vice President may make special arrangements to consider a Claim on a class basis or to address unusual conflicts (text truncated thereafter).

nodes.title: Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan's Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court.
nodes.heading: 34.7.7 7.07 Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan's Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court.
nodes.start_phrase: Before filing any Claim (as defined below in this Section), including a suit or other action, in a court or in another tribunal, a Claimant (as defined below in this Section) must first fully exhaust all of the Claimant’ s rights under the claims procedure in Section 7.03.
nodes.summary:
- Restriction of venue: Any court action related to the Plan by or for a Petitioner must be filed exclusively in New York state or federal courts located nearest the Corporation’s headquarters.
- Vice President’s discretion: Specific references to the Vice President’s discretion do not limit the breadth or completeness of that discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Mandatory exhaustion of Plan remedies: Claimants must fully exhaust the Plan’s internal claims procedure (Section 7.03) before filing any lawsuit or tribunal action. The exhaustion requirement is to be interpreted as broadly as possible.
- Limits on excuses from exhaustion: Exhaustion is not excused unless the claimant clearly indicated a Plan Claim; document-request failures excuse exhaustion only if strict conditions are met (required by law/Plan, written request received by the Vice President, no response within 6 months or a reasonable longer period, and a clear assertion of legal right). Individuals not treated as Members must clearly assert entitlement to membership.
- Applicability of exhaustion: Applies even if other non-Claim disputes are more significant, to rights the Vice President may provide for novel issues, to actual or potential rights, and even when specific procedures haven’t been established (the Vice President will establish or analogize to Section 7.03).
- Special arrangements: The Vice President may implement class-based review or address conflicts to ensure maximum enforceability of the exhaustion requirement.
- Definitions:
  - Dispute: Any claim, dispute, issue, assertion, action, or other matter.
  - Claim: Any Dispute involving Plan interpretation, terms, legality, adoption/implementation, administration, benefit requests/recovery, alleged breaches of legal duty, or any matter the Vice President deems similar or related to the Plan.
  - Claimant: Broadly includes current/former Eligible Employees, Members, Dependents, their spouses, former spouses, estates, heirs, representatives, related entities/individuals, and groups of such persons.
- Policy intent: The Plan is to be administered in good faith and consistent with law; complete exhaustion is a contractual condition to promote efficient, uniform resolution and reduce unnecessary litigation expenses.

nodes.title: ARTICLE VIII - AMENDMENT AND TERMINATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VIII - AMENDMENT AND TERMINA TION
nodes.start_phrase: While the Corporation intends to continue the Plan indefinitely , it assumes no contractual obligation as to its continuance.
nodes.summary: Article VIII sets out the Corporation’s authority over the Plan’s amendment and termination. The Corporation intends to continue the Plan indefinitely but assumes no obligation to do so and may amend, terminate, or partially terminate it at any time in its sole discretion. Any change cannot reduce the amount of benefit a Member or Dependent is entitled to on the effective date of the change unless an equivalent amount is provided under another corporate plan or practice; however, specific forms of payment are not protected. Only the Corporation may amend the Plan, with or without retroactive effect, subject to this benefit-protection rule; other Employers have no amendment rights. The Corporation may terminate participation by itself or by one or more Employers, and if fewer than all Employers are terminated, the Plan continues for employees of the remaining Employers.

nodes.title: Continuation of the Plan.
nodes.heading: 8.01 Continuation of the Plan.
nodes.start_phrase: While the Corporation intends to continue the Plan indefinitely , it assumes no contractual obligation as to its continuance.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines the Corporation’s intent to continue the plan but disclaims any contractual obligation to do so.
- Reserves the Corporation’s sole discretion to amend, terminate, or partially terminate the plan at any time.
- Protects accrued benefits: amendments or terminations cannot reduce the benefits a Member or Dependant is entitled to on the effective date, unless an equivalent benefit is provided under another corporate plan or practice; specific payment forms are not protected.
- Authorizes the Corporation (and only the Corporation) to amend the plan, with or without retroactive effect, subject to the benefit-protection rule.
- Allows termination of the plan in whole, solely as to the Corporation’s participation, or as to one or more participating Employers; if not all Employers are terminated, the plan continues for employees of the remaining Employers.

nodes.title: Amendment.
nodes.heading: 8.02 Amendment.
nodes.start_phrase: The Corporation may , in its sole discretion, make any amendment or amendments to the Plan from time to time, with or without retroactive ef fect, subject to Section 8.01.
nodes.summary:
- The corporation plans to continue the Plan indefinitely but reserves the sole right to amend, terminate, or partially terminate it at any time.
- Amendments or termination cannot reduce the benefits a member or dependent is entitled to as of the change date, unless equivalent benefits are provided under another corporate plan; specific payment forms are not protected.
- Only the corporation may amend the Plan, with or without retroactive effect, subject to the benefit-protection rule; other employers have no amendment rights.
- The corporation may terminate the Plan for itself or for one or more participating employers; if not all employers are terminated, the Plan continues for employees of the remaining employers.

nodes.title: Termination.
nodes.heading: 8.03 Termination.
nodes.start_phrase: The Corporation may terminate the Plan, either as to its participation or as to the participation of one or more Employers.
nodes.summary:
- States the company’s intent to continue the plan indefinitely but disclaims any contractual obligation to do so.
- Reserves the corporation’s sole discretion to amend, terminate, or partially terminate the plan at any time.
- Protects participants’ and dependents’ accrued benefit amounts as of the amendment/termination date, unless an equivalent benefit is provided under another company plan or practice; specific forms of payment are not protected.
- Authorizes the corporation to make amendments with or without retroactive effect, subject to the accrued benefit protection; other participating employers have no amendment rights.
- Allows the corporation to terminate the plan as to itself or select employers; if terminated for fewer than all employers, the plan continues for employees of the remaining employers.

nodes.title: ARTICLE IX - MISCELLANEOUS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE IX - MISCELLANEOUS
nodes.start_phrase: The Employers’ obligations under the Plan shall not be funded, but shall constitute liabilities by the Employer payable when due out of the Employer ’s general funds.
nodes.summary:
- Declares the plan as unfunded; benefits are paid from employers’ general assets, and participants’ claims are no greater than those of unsecured general creditors.
- Allocates all administrative and management costs to employers (unless the Corporation agrees otherwise), apportioned by each employer’s share of total members at the time costs arise.
- Defines treatment of temporary absences: employees absent for reasons like sickness, accident, layoff, or vacation are deemed terminated after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military or national service does not count as termination while the employer considers the person employed or until permanent resignation.
- Authorizes withholding from benefits to satisfy any taxes, assessments, or duties deemed owed by the Vice President.
- Clarifies no guarantee of employment: the plan does not create an employment contract or restrict employers’ right to discharge with or without cause.
- Limits rights to those expressly provided by the plan; cessation of active membership upon termination of employment does not create grounds for damages against the employer or any PepsiCo organization member.

nodes.title: Unfunded Plan.
nodes.heading: 9.01 Unfunded Plan.
nodes.start_phrase: The Employers’ obligations under the Plan shall not be funded, but shall constitute liabilities by the Employer payable when due out of the Employer ’s general funds.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the plan as unfunded; employer obligations are paid from general assets, and participants have only the status of unsecured general creditors.
- Allocates all administrative and management costs to employers, apportioned by each employer’s share of plan members unless the Corporation agrees otherwise.
- Defines treatment of temporary absences: most absences lead to deemed termination after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military or national service absences are not deemed terminated while the employer considers the individual employed or until permanent resignation.
- Authorizes withholding from benefits to satisfy applicable taxes, assessments, or duties as determined by the Vice President.
- Clarifies the plan does not guarantee employment, create an employment contract, or limit the employer’s right to discharge employees with or without cause.
- Limits rights to those expressly provided by the plan; cessation of active membership upon termination does not create grounds for damages against the employer or the PepsiCo Organization.

nodes.title: Costs of the Plan.
nodes.heading: 9.02 Costs of the Plan.
nodes.start_phrase: Unless otherwise agreed by the Corporation, all costs, char ges and expenses of or incidental to the administration and management of the Plan shall be the costs, char ges and expenses of the Employers and shall be paid by each Employer based on the proportion of Members who are employed by such Employer as compared to the total number of Members at the time the cost or expense is incurred.
nodes.summary:
- States the plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from employers’ general assets and participants have only the status of unsecured general creditors.
- Assigns all plan administration and management costs to the employers, allocated by each employer’s share of total members, unless the corporation agrees otherwise.
- Defines treatment of temporary absences: most absences (e.g., sickness, accident, layoff, vacation) lead to deemed termination after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military/national service does not count as termination while the employer considers the person employed or until resignation.
- Authorizes the plan to withhold amounts from benefits to satisfy applicable taxes, assessments, or duties as determined by the Vice President.
- Clarifies the plan does not guarantee employment or continued employment; employers may discharge employees with or without cause.
- Limits rights to those expressly provided by the plan; termination and the resulting end of active membership do not create grounds for damages against the employer or the PepsiCo Organization.

nodes.title: Temporary Absence of Member.
nodes.heading: 9.03 Temporary Absence of Member .
nodes.start_phrase: If a Member is absent from duty by reason other than death, dischar ge, retirement or quitting ( e.g., sickness, accident, layof f, vacation), he shall be deemed to have terminated employment on the date that is 12 months after the date on which he is absent, unless the V ice President determines otherwise.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from employers’ general assets, and participants hold only unsecured creditor status.
- Specifies that plan administration and management costs are borne by employers, allocated based on each employer’s share of plan members, unless the corporation decides otherwise.
- Defines rules for temporary absences: a member is deemed terminated after 12 months of non-service (e.g., sickness, accident, layoff, vacation) unless the Vice President decides otherwise; full-time military or national service does not trigger termination while the employer considers the individual employed or until permanent resignation.
- Authorizes withholding from plan benefits to satisfy taxes, assessments, or duties as determined by the Vice President.
- Clarifies the plan does not create an employment contract or guarantee continued employment; employers may discharge employees with or without cause.
- Limits rights to those expressly provided in the plan and states that loss of active membership upon employment termination does not give rise to damages against the employer or the PepsiCo Organization.

nodes.title: Taxes, Etc.
nodes.heading: 9.04 Taxes, Etc.
nodes.start_phrase: In the event any tax or assessment or other duty is determined by the V ice President to be owing in respect of any benefit payable from the Plan, the Plan shall be entitled to withhold an amount not exceeding the amount of any such tax or assessment or other duty from the benefit payable and shall apply the same in satisfaction of said tax or assessment or other duty .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the employer’s general assets, and participants have only the rights of unsecured general creditors.
- Assigns all plan administration and management costs to the employers, allocated based on each employer’s share of total members, unless the corporation agrees otherwise.
- Defines treatment of temporary absences: an employee absent for reasons other than death, discharge, retirement, or quitting is deemed terminated after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military or national service does not constitute termination while the employer considers the individual employed or until resignation.
- Authorizes the plan to withhold from benefit payments amounts needed to satisfy applicable taxes, assessments, or duties as determined by the Vice President.
- Clarifies the plan does not constitute an employment contract, does not guarantee continued employment, and does not limit the employer’s right to terminate employment with or without cause.
- States no person has rights under the plan beyond its terms; termination and resulting loss of active membership do not create grounds for damages or increased damages against the employer or the PepsiCo Organization.

nodes.title: Nonguarantee of Employment.
nodes.heading: 9.05 Nonguarantee of Employment.
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing in the Plan shall be construed as a contract of employment between an Employer and any of its employees, or as a right of any such employee to continue in the employment of the Employer , or as a limitation of the right of an Employer to dischar ge any of its employees, with or without cause.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the plan as unfunded; employer obligations are paid from general assets, and participants have no greater rights than unsecured general creditors.
- Allocates administrative and management costs to employers, generally pro rata based on their share of participating members, unless the corporation agrees otherwise.
- Defines rules for temporary absences: most absences lead to deemed termination after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military or national service does not trigger termination while the employer treats the individual as employed or until permanent resignation.
- Authorizes withholding from benefits to cover taxes, assessments, or duties as determined by the Vice President.
- Clarifies the plan does not guarantee employment, confer a right to continued employment, or limit the employer’s right to discharge employees with or without cause.
- Limits rights to those expressly provided by the plan and states that cessation of active membership upon termination does not create grounds for damages against the employer or any member of the PepsiCo Organization.

nodes.title: No Right to Benefits.
nodes.heading: 9.06 No Right to Benefits.
nodes.start_phrase: No person, whether or not being a Member , shall have any claim, right or interest under the Plan except as provided by the terms of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- States the plan is unfunded; employer obligations are paid from general assets, and members have only unsecured creditor status.
- Assigns all administrative and management costs to employers, allocated proportionally by each employer’s share of total members, unless the corporation agrees otherwise.
- Defines treatment of temporary absences: employment is deemed terminated after 12 months of absence unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military or national service does not constitute termination while the employer regards the individual as employed or until permanent resignation.
- Authorizes the plan to withhold taxes, assessments, or duties from benefits to satisfy such obligations as determined by the Vice President.
- Clarifies the plan does not guarantee employment, continued employment, or limit the employer’s right to discharge employees.
- Limits rights to those expressly provided by the plan; termination and resulting loss of active membership do not create grounds for damages against the employer or the PepsiCo Organization.

nodes.title: Charges on Benefits and Recovery of Excess Payments.
nodes.heading: 9.07 Charges on Benefits and Recovery of Excess Payments.
nodes.start_phrase: All benefits in respect of a Member under the Plan shall stand char ged with and be subject to deductions therefrom of all sums in respect of losses to a member of the PepsiCo Or ganization or Employer or otherwise caused by misdemeanor of the Member and on production by the member of the PepsiCo Or ganization or Employer of proof satisfactory to the V ice President that any such loss ought to be made good by a Member .
nodes.summary:
- Plan benefits are subject to deductions to reimburse the Employer or PepsiCo Organization for losses caused by a Member’s misdemeanor, upon proof satisfactory to the Vice President; deducted amounts are paid to the affected entity and constitute valid discharge.
- Payments from the Plan cannot exceed the precise amounts, timing, and payees authorized by the Plan. Any excess, early, or misdirected payment (“Excess Payment”) must be promptly returned to the Plan.
- By virtue of membership, dependent status, or receipt of an Excess Payment, the recipient grants the Plan:
  - A constructive trust and first-priority equitable lien (with interest) on any Excess Payment and its proceeds or substitutes, binding any transferees.
  - A discretionary right of offset against other amounts payable by the Plan to the recipient, without limiting the Plan’s lien/trust rights.
  - The right to pursue legal or equitable actions in any chosen jurisdiction; recipients submit to such jurisdictions and waive residence-based defenses after receiving an Excess Payment.
- Recipients must take all actions requested by the Vice President to facilitate recovery of Excess Payments with interest. The section is intended to maximize, not limit, the Plan’s recovery rights.
- If the Vice President determines that a Member was terminated for cause or engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time up to the second anniversary of employment termination, the Member forfeits all pension benefits (past, current, and future), the pension is adjusted accordingly, and any previously paid amounts are recoverable.

nodes.title: Termination for Cause; Prohibited Misconduct.
nodes.heading: 9.08 Termination for Cause; Pr ohibited Misconduct.
nodes.start_phrase: (a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this Plan to the contrary , if the V ice President determines that a Member has been terminated for cause or engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time prior to the second anniversary of the date his or her employment with the PepsiCo Or ganization terminates, the Member shall forfeit his Pension (whether paid previously , being paid currently or payable in the future), and his or her Pension shall be adjusted to reflect such forfeiture and any previously paid Pension payments shall be recovered.
nodes.summary:
- Recovery and deductions: Member benefits can be reduced to compensate the Employer/PepsiCo Organization for losses caused by the Member’s misconduct upon proof satisfactory to the Vice President. Any overpayment, premature, or misdirected payment (“Excess Payment”) must be returned and is subject to a constructive trust and first-priority equitable lien with interest; the Plan may offset future payments, pursue legal/equitable remedies, require cooperation, and is granted broad, non-restrictive recovery rights.

- Forfeiture for cause/misconduct: If the Vice President determines a Member was terminated for cause or engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time up to two years after employment ends, the Member forfeits all pension benefits (past, current, and future), and previously paid amounts will be recovered; Members agree to repay.

- Prohibited Misconduct defined: Includes participating (broadly defined) in competing businesses dealing in “Covered Products” (wide range of beverages, snacks, cereals, pasta/rice, dairy, and products under development), soliciting PepsiCo employees, using/disclosing confidential information, acts contrary to company interests (e.g., Code of Conduct violations, insider trading, gross misconduct), and fraud. Whistleblower and Defend Trade Secrets Act safe-harbor protections are expressly preserved.

- Notices: Notices to the Plan are sufficient if delivered in writing to the Vice President; notices to Members may be sent to the last known address or via other reasonably available methods (including electronic).

- Plan documentation: Members are entitled, on request, to a copy of the governing legal document for the DB Program.

- Currency of payment: Benefits are paid in U.S. dollars or another eligible currency approved by the Vice President, with conversion applied for both annuity and lump-sum payments.

nodes.title: Notices.
nodes.heading: 9.09 Notices.
nodes.start_phrase: Any notice which under the Plan is required to be given to or served upon the Plan shall be deemed to be suf ficiently given to or served upon the Plan if it is in writing and delivered to the V ice President.
nodes.summary:
- Whistleblower carve-out: Confirms that nothing in the Plan restricts Members from communicating with government authorities about possible legal violations, participating in investigations, or receiving whistleblower awards; preserves the Corporation’s attorney-client privilege.
- Defend Trade Secrets Act notice: Describes immunity for confidential disclosures of trade secrets to government officials or attorneys for reporting/investigation, and in sealed court filings; allows use of trade secrets in retaliation lawsuits if filed under seal and not disclosed except by court order.
- Definitions:
  - “Participation” is broadly defined to include serving as a director, officer, employee, consultant, or contractor; giving input, advice, guidance, or suggestions; or providing recommendations/testimonials for a business or its products.
  - “Covered Products” includes a wide range of PepsiCo-related categories (e.g., beverages, juices, dairy, snacks, cereals, pasta, rice, pancake products) and any product/service the Member knew was under development by the PepsiCo Organization.
- Notices: How notices to the Plan (to the Vice President) and to Members (last known address or other reasonable methods, including electronic) must be delivered.
- Plan documentation: Members are entitled, upon request, to a copy of the governing legal document for the DB Program.
- Currency of payment: Benefits are payable in U.S. dollars or another eligible currency approved by the Vice President; annuity and lump-sum amounts are subject to currency conversion.

nodes.title: Plan Documentation.
nodes.heading: 9.10 Plan Documentation.
nodes.start_phrase: Every Member shall on demand be entitled to a copy of the governing legal document for the DB Program.
nodes.summary:
- Confirms that the Plan does not restrict members from communicating with government authorities about potential legal violations, participating in investigations, or receiving whistleblower awards, while the Corporation preserves attorney-client privilege.
- Provides Defend Trade Secrets Act (DTSA) notice: individuals are immune from liability for certain confidential disclosures of trade secrets to government officials or attorneys for reporting/investigation, or in sealed court filings; allows disclosure under seal in retaliation lawsuits, subject to court order for any further disclosure.
- Broadly defines “Participation” to include serving in roles (director, officer, employee, consultant, contractor), giving advice/input, or offering recommendations/testimonials for a business entity.
- Defines “Covered Products” tied to the PepsiCo Organization, including a wide range of beverages (e.g., carbonated soft drinks, tea, water, juice drinks, sports, coffee, energy, value-added dairy), juices, dairy, snacks (salty, sweet, meat, granola/cereal bars, cookies), hot cereals, pancake mixes and syrups, value-added rice and pasta, ready-to-eat cereals, dry pasta, and products/services under development known to the member.
- Section 9.09 (Notices): Specifies how notices are deemed sufficient—delivery to the Vice President for Plan notices; and delivery to a member’s last known address or other reasonably available method (including electronic) as determined by the Vice President for member notices.
- Section 9.10 (Plan Documentation): Members are entitled, on request, to a copy of the governing legal document for the DB Program.
- Section 9.11 (Currency of Payment): Benefits are paid in U.S. dollars or another eligible currency approved by the Vice President, with amounts converted from U.S. dollars for annuity and lump-sum payments (provision continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Currency of Payment.
nodes.heading: 9.11 Curr ency of Payment.
nodes.start_phrase: Payment of benefits under the Plan shall be made in United States dollars, or other "eligible currency ," as approved by the Vice President.
nodes.summary:
- Whistleblower and trade secret disclosures: The Plan explicitly permits Members to communicate with government authorities about possible legal violations, participate in investigations, and receive awards, without notifying the Corporation. The Corporation maintains attorney-client privilege. Under the Defend Trade Secrets Act, individuals have immunity for certain confidential disclosures of trade secrets to authorities or attorneys for reporting/investigating suspected legal violations, for filings made under seal, and in retaliation lawsuits if filings are under seal and disclosures follow court orders.
- Definitions for restrictive covenants: “Participation” broadly includes serving as a director, officer, employee, consultant, or contractor; providing advice or input; or offering recommendations/testimonials for another business. “Covered Products” include a wide range of PepsiCo-related categories (e.g., beverages of many types, juices, dairy, snacks, cereals, pasta, rice, syrups) and any product or service the Member knew or should have known was under development by the PepsiCo organization.
- Notices: Notices to the Plan must be delivered in writing to the Vice President. Notices to Members may be sent to the last known address or by another method (including electronic) reasonably available as determined by the Vice President.
- Plan documentation: Members are entitled, upon request, to a copy of the governing legal document for the DB Program.
- Currency of payment: Benefits are paid in U.S. dollars or another eligible currency approved by the Vice President. For annuities and lump sums, currency conversions use an exchange-rate methodology approved by the Vice President.
- Governing law: The Plan is governed by New York law.
- ERISA exemption: The Plan is intended to be exempt from ERISA as a plan maintained outside the U.S. primarily for nonresident aliens. Active Membership and opportunities to increase Highest Average Monthly Earnings after Active Membership are limited to nonresident aliens with assigned work locations outside the U.S. Permanent administrative records are intended to be kept outside the U.S.
- Section 409A exemption: The Plan is designed to be fully exempt from Internal Revenue Code Section 409A. No Member may receive a benefit enhancement based on compensation or service for any year in which the Member is a U.S. Person. Entitlement to any enhancement is determined after the year ends and only if the Member was not a U.S. Person. In the benefit commencement year, the Vice President may authorize an enhancement upon satisfactory determination the Member will not be a U.S. Person; otherwise benefits begin without that year’s enhancement, with adjustments in the following year if appropriate. The Vice President has broad authority to ensure the Plan remains exempt from Section 409A.

nodes.title: Governing Law.
nodes.heading: 9.12 Governing Law .
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall in all respects be governed by and interpreted according to the laws of the State of New Y ork.
nodes.summary:
- Currency conversion will use an exchange-rate methodology approved by the Vice President.
- Governing law: The plan is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
- ERISA exemption: The plan is intended to be exempt as a non-U.S. plan primarily for nonresident aliens; active membership and any post-termination increases in Highest Average Monthly Earnings are limited to nonresident aliens with work locations outside the U.S.; permanent records will be maintained outside the U.S.
- Section 409A exemption: Special operating rules ensure the plan remains fully exempt from IRC §409A; no benefit vesting or enhancements can arise from compensation or service while a participant is a U.S. Person; benefit enhancements are determined only after year-end confirmation that the participant was not a U.S. Person; in a benefit commencement year, the Vice President may allow an enhancement if satisfied the participant will not be a U.S. Person; otherwise benefits start without the enhancement and are adjusted the following year if appropriate; the Vice President has broad authority to enforce these rules.

nodes.title: Exemption from ERISA.
nodes.heading: 9.13 Exemption fr om ERISA.
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan is intended to be exempt from the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (“ERISA”), as a plan maintained outside of the United States primarily for the benefit of persons substantially all of whom are nonresident aliens of the United States.
nodes.summary:
- Benefits payable in selected currencies are converted using an exchange-rate methodology approved periodically by the Vice President.
- Governing law: The Plan is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
- ERISA exemption: The Plan is intended to qualify as a foreign plan exempt from ERISA, maintained outside the U.S. primarily for nonresident aliens. To preserve this status:
  - Active membership and any opportunity to increase Highest Average Monthly Earnings after active service (per Section 4.04(b)) are limited to nonresident aliens with assigned work locations outside the U.S.
  - Permanent administrative records and documentation are kept outside the U.S.
- Section 409A exemption: The Plan is operated to remain fully exempt from U.S. Internal Revenue Code Section 409A. Key rules include:
  - No benefit enhancement (vesting, increases, or enhancements) may arise from compensation or service while a participant is a U.S. Person.
  - Eligibility for any benefit enhancement for a calendar year is determined only after year-end, once it is confirmed the participant was not a U.S. Person for that year.
  - In the benefit commencement year, the Vice President may authorize an enhancement if satisfied the participant will not be a U.S. Person; otherwise benefits commence without that year’s enhancement, with adjustments the following year if appropriate.
  - The Vice President has broad authority to interpret and apply these rules to ensure continued exemption from Section 409A.

nodes.title: Exemption from Section 409A.
nodes.heading: 9.14 Exemption fr om Section 409A.
nodes.start_phrase: In order to permit this Plan to be completely exempt from United States Internal Revenue Code section 409A (“Section 409A”), this Plan shall be subject to the special operating rules and limitations in this Section 9.14, ef fective for any period to which Section 409A applies.
nodes.summary:
- Currency conversion: Benefits are calculated in a selected currency using exchange rates under a methodology approved by the Vice President.
- Governing law: The Plan is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
- ERISA exemption: The Plan is intended to be exempt from ERISA as a non-U.S. plan primarily for nonresident aliens. Active membership and post-termination increases to Highest Average Monthly Earnings are limited to nonresident aliens with work locations outside the U.S., and permanent administrative records are to be maintained outside the U.S.
- Section 409A exemption: Special rules ensure the Plan remains fully exempt from IRC Section 409A. No benefit enhancements can arise from compensation or service while a participant is a U.S. Person. Enhancements for a year are only granted after year-end confirmation that the member was not a U.S. Person; in the benefit commencement year, the Vice President may authorize an enhancement upon satisfactory determination of non-U.S. Person status, otherwise benefits commence without it and are adjusted the following year if confirmed. The Vice President has broad authority to ensure compliance with these requirements.

nodes.title: ARTICLE X - SIGNATURE
nodes.heading: ARTICLE X - SIGNA TURE
nodes.start_phrase: The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan, DB Program document, as amended and restated, is hereby adopted as of this 19th day of December , 2022, to be ef fective as of January 1, 2023 or as otherwise stated herein.
nodes.summary: Article X – Signature documents the formal adoption of the amended and restated PepsiCo International Retirement Plan, DB Program. It states the plan is adopted on December 19, 2022, effective January 1, 2023 (or as otherwise specified). The page includes execution by Ronald Schellekens, Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer, dated December 19, 2022, and Law Department approval by Jeffrey Arnold, Legal Director and Employee Benefits Counsel, dated December 9, 2022.

nodes.title: TABLE A - CALCULATION OF PENSIONS
nodes.heading: TABLE A - CALCULA TION OF PENSIONS
nodes.start_phrase: This section sets forth the formulas for calculating the Pension payable to a Member under Article IV or the Death Benefit payable to a Member ’s Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner , as applicable, under Article VI, but subject in all cases to the freeze of the Plan described in Article I.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Table A outlines formulas for calculating a Member’s pension under Article IV and references death benefits for an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner under Article VI, all subject to the Plan freeze in Article I.
- Part-time service: Benefits accrued while part-time (after VP designation as an Eligible Employee) are prorated by the Vice President to reflect part-time vs. full-time service levels.
- Pension form and timing: Describes the Single Life Annuity payable at Normal Retirement Date.
- Pre-1976 members (joined before Jan 1, 1976): Pension is the greater of:
  - 1.5% of Highest Average Monthly Salary × years of Pensionable Service; or
  - 3% of Highest Average Monthly Salary × years of Pensionable Service, capped at 15 years.
- Post-1975/newer members (joined on/after Jan 1, 1976; on/after Sep 1, 1980; or after Nov 12, 1998): Pension equals the sum of:
  - 3% of Highest Average Monthly Salary × up to the first 10 years of Pensionable Service; plus
  - 1% of Highest Average Monthly Salary × years of Pensionable Service beyond 10.
- Discretionary offsets: The Vice President may reduce calculated pensions by:
  - State pension and social security benefits attributable to service (excluding those from unmatched/unreimbursed voluntary member contributions); and
  - The annuity value of certain capital-sum retirement benefits from a state source or the Employer required by local law (e.g., termination indemnities).
- Definitions: “Highest Average Monthly Salary” is referenced for calculation and defined elsewhere in the plan.

nodes.title: TABLE A - CALCULATION OF PENSIONS - Introduction
nodes.source_heading: TABLE A - CALCULA TION OF PENSIONS
nodes.heading: TABLE A - CALCULA TION OF PENSIONS
nodes.start_phrase: This section sets forth the formulas for calculating the Pension payable to a Member under Article IV or the Death Benefit payable to a Member ’s Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner , as applicable, under Article VI, but subject in all cases to the freeze of the Plan described in Article I.
nodes.summary:

nodes.title: Member’s Pension
nodes.heading: (I) Member ’s Pension
nodes.start_phrase: The Pension payable (as a Single Life Annuity benefit) on retirement at Normal Retirement Date for Members who became members of the Plan before January 1, 1976 shall be the larger of the Pension calculated under this paragraph (a) or under paragraph (b) below .
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Defines formulas for calculating Member pensions (Article IV) and pre-retirement death benefits for Eligible Spouses/Domestic Partners (Article VI), all subject to the Plan freeze in Article I.
- Part-time service: Benefits for part-time Eligible Employees are prorated by the Vice President based on service level versus full-time at the work location.
- Pension at Normal Retirement (Single Life Annuity):
  - For Members before Jan 1, 1976: greater of (a) or (b).
    - (a) Greater of: 1.5% of Highest Average Monthly Salary (HAMS) × years of Pensionable Service; or 3% of HAMS × years of Pensionable Service, capped at 15 years.
    - (b) Tiered formula: 3% of HAMS × first 10 years of Pensionable Service, plus 1% of HAMS × years over 10.
  - For Members joining on/after specified dates (1976/1980/1998): pension calculated under (b) only.
- Discretionary reductions by the Vice President:
  - Offsets for state pension/social security attributable to service (excluding unmatched, unreimbursed voluntary contributions).
  - Annuity value of capital sum benefits from state/employer due to local legislation (e.g., termination indemnities).
  - Benefits or cash in lieu from other employer retirement plans covering the same Pensionable Service.
  - Severance or termination payments under agreements.
  - Value of prior benefits paid for service also counted under this DB Program.
  - Reductions/forfeitures for misconduct or discharge for cause (Sec. 9.08).
  - No offsets for unmatched, unreimbursed voluntary contributions; values adjusted for form/timing; calculated as of termination per VP-approved methodology.
- Alternative “extended wearaway” calculation:
  - Applies when offsets are taken unless VP deems unnecessary/impractical.
  - Counts only DB Program service not used in offsets (1)–(5); still applies misconduct reduction (6).
  - Pays the greater of standard vs. alternative result, subject to VP limit to mirror PepsiCo Salaried Plan extended wearaway intent.
- Highest Average Monthly Salary (HAMS):
  - One-twelfth of the average Salary over any 5 consecutive highest calendar years (or shorter actual service).
  - Years with no Salary disregarded; partial-year unpaid leave years can be excluded if it increases the average, substituting adjacent years.
- Deferred Vested Pension (Sec. 4.04): Greatest of three projections/allocations that blend service before/after Sept 30, 2003, using HAMS as of 9/30/2003 for pre-10/1/2003 service and HAMS at termination for post-9/30/2003 service, with proportional reductions based on actual vs. projected service to Normal Retirement Age and a 35-year service cap where stated.
  - For Members before Jan 1, 1976: greater of 1.5% of HAMS × years at termination or VP-determined actuarial amount.
  - Applicable offsets (from reductions above) are calculated at cessation of service per VP methodology.
- Pre-Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s Pension (Sec. 6.01):
  - If death after early retirement eligibility (Sec. 4.02): 50% of the pension the Member would have had with a 50% Survivor Annuity (Sec. 5.02(b)); reduced if commenced before the Member’s age 62.
  - If death before early retirement eligibility: 50% of the pension tied to a 50% Survivor Annuity right; payable from the first of the month after the later of death or the Member’s age 55; reduced if commenced before the Member’s age 65.

nodes.title: Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension
nodes.heading: (II) Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension
nodes.start_phrase: If a Member covered by Section 6.01 dies after the date he would have been entitled to retire early under Section 4.02,
nodes.summary:
- Defines the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s Pension for Members covered by Section 6.01.
- Benefit amount is 50% of the pension the Member would have received under a 50% Survivor Annuity (per Section 5.02(b)).
- If death occurs after the Member would have qualified for early retirement (Section 4.02): benefit is based on the pension as of the day before death and is reduced if commenced before the age the Member would have reached 62 (reductions per Section 4.02).
- If death occurs before the Member would have qualified for early retirement: benefit equals 50% of the pension as if the Member had the right to a 50% Survivor Annuity; payments start the first of the month after the later of death or when the Member would have turned 55, and are reduced if begun before the age the Member would have reached 65 (reductions per Section 4.04(c)).
- Clarifies timing of commencement and applicable reduction rules tied to specified ages and referenced plan sections.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ERW - EARLY RETIREMENT WINDOWS
nodes.heading: APPENDIX ER W - EARL Y RETIREMENT WINDOWS
nodes.start_phrase: This Appendix ER W supplements the main portion of the DB Program with respect to the rights and benefits of Covered Employees.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Appendix ERW (Early Retirement Windows) to the DB Program, which supplements the main plan regarding rights and benefits available to certain employees during specified restructuring periods.
- States that defined terms in bold/underlined have meanings set here; all other capitalized terms follow Section 2.01 of the DB Program.
- Defines “Covered Employee” as an Active Member who meets all of the following:
  - Is an Eligible Employee involuntarily terminated due to a Reorganization.
  - For the 2007/2008 Restructuring: last day of active employment is between the Effective Date and December 31, 2008 (inclusive), with a Severance Date on/after the Effective Date but no later than December 31, 2009.
  - For the 2008/2009 Restructuring: last day of active employment is between the Effective Date and August 31, 2009 (inclusive), with a Severance Date on/after the Effective Date but no later than December 26, 2009.
  - Is entitled to enhanced severance pay under the Severance Program (or severance under an approved agreement).
  - Receives written authorization from the Vice President to receive Appendix ERW benefits.
  - Signs, submits, and does not revoke a qualifying severance agreement releasing the Corporation, Associated Companies, and their personnel, with the Corporation determining that the agreement meets required substance, form, and timing and is entered under the Severance Program as part of the Reorganization.
- Clarifies that failure to meet any of the above conditions means the individual is not a Covered Employee and is ineligible for ERW benefits.
- Defines “Reorganization” as the reorganization, plant closing, or other event that triggered the relevant Severance Program.

nodes.title: Scope.
nodes.heading: ERW.1 Scope.
nodes.start_phrase: This Appendix ER W supplements the main portion of the DB Program with respect to the rights and benefits of Covered Employees.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Appendix ERW (Early Retirement Windows) as a supplement to the DB Program, defining rights and benefits for certain employees affected by organizational changes.
- Provides program-specific definitions, including “Appendix ERW,” “Covered Employee,” and “Reorganization.”
- Defines “Covered Employee” as an Active Member who:
  - Is an Eligible Employee involuntarily terminated pursuant to a Reorganization.
  - Falls within specific timing windows:
    - 2007/2008 Restructuring: last day of active employment between the Effective Date and Dec 31, 2008; Severance Date on/after the Effective Date and no later than Dec 31, 2009.
    - 2008/2009 Restructuring: last day of active employment between the Effective Date and Aug 31, 2009; Severance Date on/after the Effective Date and no later than Dec 26, 2009.
  - Is entitled to enhanced severance under the Severance Program (or qualifying severance under an approved agreement).
  - Receives written authorization from the Vice President to obtain ERW benefits.
  - Signs, submits, and does not revoke a qualifying severance agreement releasing the company and affiliates from liability, with the Corporation determining compliance with substance, form, and timing requirements and confirming it is under the Severance Program tied to the Reorganization.
- Clarifies that anyone not meeting all criteria is not a Covered Employee and is ineligible for ERW benefits.
- Defines “Reorganization” as the reorganization, plant closing, or other event triggering the applicable Severance Program.

nodes.title: Definitions and Program Specific Rules.
nodes.heading: ERW.2 Definitions and Pr ogram Specific Rules.
nodes.start_phrase: This section provides definitions for the following words or phrases in boldface and underlined.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose: Appendix ERW supplements the DB Program by outlining special early retirement (“Early Retirement Windows”) rights and benefits for certain employees affected by specified restructurings.
- Key definitions: Establishes “Covered Employee,” “Reorganization,” “Severance Date,” and identifies applicable “Severance Programs” and their Effective Dates for two events: 2007/2008 (Effective Date: Feb 4, 2008) and 2008/2009 (Effective Date: Apr 3, 2009).
- Covered Employee criteria: Must be an Active Member involuntarily terminated due to the Reorganization; fall within specified last day of active work and Severance Date windows; be eligible for enhanced severance; receive written VP authorization; and execute (and not revoke) a qualifying severance release meeting corporate requirements. Those failing any criterion are ineligible.
- Employment and date windows:
  - 2007/2008: Last active day between Effective Date and Dec 31, 2008; Severance Date on/after Effective Date but no later than Dec 31, 2009.
  - 2008/2009: Last active day between Effective Date and Aug 31, 2009; Severance Date on/after Effective Date but no later than Dec 26, 2009.
- Special Early Retirement Pension: Covered Employees meeting eligibility are treated as eligible under Section 4.03.
- Eligibility specifics:
  - Common: Must be a Covered Employee on the Severance Date.
  - 2007/2008: Age at least 50 but under 55 by Severance Date; at least 10 years of Vesting Service by Severance Date.
  - 2008/2009: Age at least 50 but under 55 by Pension Termination Date (earlier of Severance Date or 52 weeks after last active day); at least 10 years of Vesting Service by Severance Date (age and service rounded up to nearest whole year); must not return to employment with an Employer before Pension Termination Date; must not already qualify for Normal or Early Retirement.
- Overall effect: Creates time-limited early retirement eligibility for specified involuntarily terminated employees, contingent on age/service thresholds, severance program participation, required releases, and employer authorization.

nodes.title: Special Early Retirement.
nodes.heading: ERW.3 Special Early Retir ement.
nodes.start_phrase: Any Covered Employee who meets the eligibility requirements of subsection (a) below shall be treated as eligible for a Special Early Retirement Pension under Section 4.03.
nodes.summary:
- Defines key terms:
  - Severance Date: an Active Member’s final day of employment pursuant to the reorganization.
  - Severance Programs and Effective Dates for two restructurings:
    - 2007/2008: two named PepsiCo Transition Severance Programs; Effective Date February 4, 2008.
    - 2008/2009: two named PepsiCo Transition Severance Programs (Below Band I and Band I); Effective Date April 3, 2009.
- Establishes Special Early Retirement (SER) eligibility and treatment:
  - Covered Employees meeting criteria are eligible for a Special Early Retirement Pension under Section 4.03.
  - 2007/2008 eligibility: age 50–54 by Severance Date and at least 10 years of Vesting Service by Severance Date.
  - 2008/2009 eligibility: age 50–54 by Pension Termination Date (earlier of Severance Date or 52 weeks after last active day), at least 10 years of Vesting Service by Severance Date (age/service rounded up), no re-employment before Pension Termination Date, and not otherwise eligible for Normal or Early Retirement.
- Specifies benefit calculation:
  - Applies the Section 4.03 early commencement reduction of 4/12ths of 1% per month; subject to standard DB Program limits.
- Clarifies non-duplication and waivers:
  - SER under this appendix replaces SER under DB Program Section 4.03; no dual entitlement.
  - Not available to individuals eligible for special early retirement under the PepsiCo Salaried Plan unless a release is provided.
  - Acceptance of benefits constitutes an irrevocable waiver of other special early retirement claims under PepsiCo plans.
- Addresses equity treatment:
  - Covered Employees qualifying under this rule are deemed to meet “Retirement” for outstanding stock option and RSU awards under specified PepsiCo Long-Term Incentive Plans.
- Document transition note:
  - The excerpt concludes by introducing Exhibit 10.7: The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Defined Contribution Program (PIRP-DC), as amended and restated effective January 1, 2022.

structure.title: THE PEPSICO INTERNATIONAL RETIREMENT PLAN DEFINED CONTRIBUTION PROGRAM (PIRP-DC) As Amended and Restated Effective as of January 1, 2022
structure.heading: Exhibit 10.7 THE PEPSICO INTERNA TIONAL RETIREMENT PLAN DEFINED CONTRIBUTION PROGRAM (PIRP-DC) As Amended and Restated Effective as of January 1, 2022

- Scope: Outlines the structure, governance, and participant rights/obligations for PepsiCo’s international defined contribution retirement plan.
- Key sections:
  - Article I: History and general information about the plan.
  - Article II: Definitions and construction rules guiding interpretation.
  - Article III: Membership—eligibility, admission procedures, and active/inactive status.

nodes.title: ARTICLE I – HISTORY AND GENERAL INFORMATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE I – HIST ORY AND GENERAL INFORMA TION
nodes.start_phrase: PepsiCo, Inc. (the “Corporation”) first established the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan ef fective as of September 1, 1980.
nodes.summary:
- Article I outlines the history and general information of PepsiCo’s international retirement plan.
- Traces plan evolution: established in 1980, restated in 1982; in 2003 split into Plan A (trust-funded) and Plan B (corporate pay-as-you-go); in 2005 restricted benefit accruals for individuals subject to U.S. taxation (treating them as if employment ended before U.S. tax exposure); in 2010 merged Plan A and B into a single document forming the DB Program.
- Describes creation of the DC Program effective January 1, 2011 for selected international employees (expatriates where home-country plan participation is impractical and selected senior globalists on U.S. tax-equalized packages). The DC Program, governed by this document and also known as the PepsiCo International Pension Plan (PIPP), together with the DB Program constitutes a single Plan.
- Summarizes subsequent DC Program amendments: 2016 extension to certain localized employees outside their home country who previously participated in a company-sponsored retirement plan but lack an available company plan post-localization; 2019 recognition of same-sex and opposite-sex domestic partners for certain purposes for active/authorized-leave Members; restated in 2021; further amended and restated effective January 1, 2022.
- Clarifies funding and legal status: the Plan is unfunded and unsecured for U.S. Internal Revenue Code and ERISA purposes; benefits are obligations of each executive’s employer, with participants holding only unsecured general creditor rights; intended to be ERISA-exempt as a plan maintained outside the U.S. primarily for nonresident aliens.

nodes.title: ARTICLE II – DEFINITIONS AND CONSTRUCTION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE II – DEFINITIONS AND CONSTRUCTION
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this governing document for the DC Program, they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context:
nodes.summary:
- This section establishes defined terms for the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Defined Contribution Program (PIRP-DC), to apply unless context requires otherwise.
- Key definitions:
  - Approved Transfer: Employment changes initiated/approved by the Corporation (or by a Member’s Employer with Corporation approval) that lead to U.S.-based work or U.S. Person status, including transfers or secondments to the U.S. or its territories.
  - Associated Company: An entity controlled by or associated with the Corporation that, with the Vice President’s ongoing consent, agrees to the DC Program’s terms and is included as an Employer; plural form also defined.
  - Corporation: PepsiCo, Inc., a North Carolina corporation, or its successors.
  - Dependant: The person designated to receive a deceased Member’s PIRP-DC Account balance.
  - DB Program: The Plan’s defined benefit component, governed by “The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Defined Benefit Program (PIRP-DB),” as amended.
  - DC Program: The Plan’s defined contribution component, governed by “The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Defined Contribution Program (PIRP-DC),” as amended.
  - Distribution Valuation Date: The date set by the Vice President for valuing PIRP-DC Accounts for distributions under Article VI; currently the month-end immediately after the triggering event (example provided).
- The Vice President’s authority is highlighted for consenting to Associated Companies and setting Distribution Valuation Dates.

nodes.title: Definitions.
