nodes.heading: 2.01 Definitions.
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this governing document for the DC Program, they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Article II of the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan Defined Contribution Program (PIRP-DC), setting core definitions and construction rules used throughout the DC Program.
- Clarifies organizational roles and scope: defines the Corporation (PepsiCo, Inc.), Associated Companies, Employers, Approved Employers, the PepsiCo Organization (controlled group), and identifies the Vice President, Global Benefits & Wellness as the primary administrative authority.
- Defines participant categories and relationships: Member (Active/Inactive by cross-reference), Eligible Employee (with detailed eligibility pathways, including assignments, localization, lack of local plans, and senior globalists; part-time discretion), Eligible Spouse, Eligible Domestic Partner (with civil union, benefits enrollment, and other evidence pathways plus 60-day claim requirement and exclusivity rules), and Dependant.
- Outlines employment and service rules: Service, Break in Service, counting of prior/post-transfer service with VP approval, treatment of authorized leaves, and limitations on service with entities before they become Employers.
- Specifies compensation bases for benefit credits: Salary definitions for non-U.S. payroll (home notional base; includes annual bonus for post-1/1/2021 entrants and may include notional bonus with VP approval) and U.S. payroll (base plus annual bonus), with VP’s determinations conclusive.
- Details account structure and credits: PIRP-DC Account as an unfunded, notional bookkeeping account; Pay Credits and Interest Credits; Interest Rate basis (initially 30-year Treasury rate each September) with VP authority to change methodology within 409A constraints.
- Sets timing and valuation mechanisms: Plan Year, Valuation Date (business days; annual plus special dates for Approved Transfers/Status Changes), and Distribution Valuation Date (month-end after a distribution-triggering event; examples provided; VP may change dates).
- Defines status and mobility events: Approved Transfer (corporate-approved U.S.-related moves), Status Change (becoming a U.S. Person other than via Approved Transfer), and U.S. Person (IRS-based definitions, including substantial presence, green card, elections, and special filing rule for Section 9.14).
- Cross-references related plan components: distinguishes DC Program (PIRP-DC) from the DB Program (PIRP-DB) and defines the overall Plan.
- Establishes key effective/entry dates: Effective Date of the DC Program (January 1, 2011) and Entry Date for Membership as set by the VP.
- Emphasizes VP’s discretionary authority across eligibility, employer approval, service counting, valuation timing, interest methodology, interpretive principles, and administrative adjustments to prevent duplicate or disproportionate benefits.
- Includes construction rule for interpretation: gender-neutral and singular/plural usage to be read flexibly unless context dictates otherwise.

nodes.title: Construction.
nodes.heading: 2.02 Construction.
nodes.start_phrase: (a) Gender and Number : Unless the context clearly indicates to the contrary , (i) a reference to one or more genders shall include a reference to all the other genders, and (ii) the singular may include the plural, and the plural may include the singular ..
nodes.summary:
- Defines when employment Service is credited for employees transferring between an Employer and an Approved Employer: pre- or post-transfer service counts only with Vice President approval; service with a company before it became an Employer or PepsiCo Organization member is excluded unless expressly allowed by the Vice President.
- Defines “Status Change” as any non-Approved Transfer change that causes a Member to become a U.S. Person.
- Defines “U.S. Person” by reference to U.S. tax law (citizens, lawful permanent residents, substantial presence/election under IRC 7701(b)), and treats an individual as a U.S. Person for Section 9.14 in any year they must file a U.S. individual income tax return, unless the Vice President determines there is no U.S.-source earned income from a PepsiCo Organization member.
- Establishes “Valuation Date” rules for PIRP-DC Accounts: generally each business day as set by the Vice President; as of the Effective Date, the last day of each Plan Year for all Members; special valuation dates for Approved Transfers and certain Status Changes; the Vice President may change valuation dates with adjustments to avoid duplicate or disproportionate benefits; values are set as of the close of the valuation date (or prior business day if not a business day).
- Defines “Vice President” as the Vice President, Global Benefits & Wellness of PepsiCo, Inc., or the person performing most of that role’s duties if the position is vacant/eliminated.
- Provides construction/interpretation rules: gender and number usage is inclusive; “year” may be any 365/366-day period without double counting; benefits may be prorated for partial years/months; months may be counted as 1/12 of a year or in days at the Vice President’s discretion; “hereof,” “hereunder,” etc., refer to the entire DC Program; “including” and examples are to be read as “without limitation.”
- Outlines the document’s hierarchy and cross-referencing conventions: articles (Roman numerals), sections (Arabic with decimal), subsections (letters), paragraphs (numbers), subparagraphs (roman numerals), and clauses (capital letters), with rules for internal references within sections/subsections.

nodes.title: ARTICLE III – MEMBERSHIP
nodes.heading: ARTICLE III – MEMBERSHIP
nodes.start_phrase: Every person who the V ice President determines is an Eligible Employee shall be eligible for Membership.
nodes.summary:
- Defines Article III – Membership criteria and statuses within the plan.
- Eligibility (3.01): Individuals deemed “Eligible Employees” by the Vice President qualify for membership.
- Admission (3.02): Admission requires Vice President approval and the individual not being a U.S. Person at the relevant time; membership is effective as of the Entry Date. The “relevant time” includes a sufficient pre–Entry Date period to avoid PIRP-DC Accounts being treated as deferred compensation under U.S. Internal Revenue Code Section 409A. No one is admitted without Vice President approval.
- Membership status (3.03): A Member is Active only if (a) employed as an Eligible Employee, (b) not a U.S. Person, and (c) currently approved as Active by the Vice President; otherwise, the Member is Inactive.

nodes.title: Eligibility for Membership.
nodes.heading: 3.01 Eligibility for Membership.
nodes.start_phrase: Every person who the V ice President determines is an Eligible Employee shall be eligible for Membership.
nodes.summary:
- Defines membership criteria and process under Article III.
- Eligibility (3.01): An individual qualifies as an Eligible Employee only if the Vice President determines so.
- Admission (3.02): To be admitted, the person must be an Eligible Employee, a non-U.S. Person at the relevant time, and receive Vice President approval; admission is effective as of the Entry Date. Timing must ensure PIRP-DC Accounts are not treated as deferred compensation subject to U.S. IRC Section 409A. No one is admitted without Vice President approval.
- Status (3.03): A Member is Active only while (a) employed as an Eligible Employee, (b) not a U.S. Person, and (c) currently approved as Active by the Vice President. A Member is Inactive whenever any of these conditions are not met.

nodes.title: Admission to Membership.
nodes.heading: 3.02 Admission to Membership.
nodes.start_phrase: Every person who the V ice President determines is an Eligible Employee, and who is not during the relevant time a U.S. Person, shall, following the approval of his Membership by the V ice President, be admitted to Membership ef fective as of his Entry Date.
nodes.summary:
- Defines eligibility: any individual the Vice President designates as an Eligible Employee may qualify for membership.
- Sets admission requirements: membership requires Vice President approval and the individual must not be a U.S. Person during the relevant period; admission is effective on the Entry Date.
- Clarifies timing to avoid U.S. tax issues: the “relevant time” precedes the Proposed Entry Date sufficiently to prevent PIRP-DC Accounts from being treated as deferred compensation under Internal Revenue Code Section 409A.
- Establishes membership status:
  - Active Member: currently employed as an Eligible Employee, not a U.S. Person, and approved as Active by the Vice President.
  - Inactive Member: anyone who fails to meet all Active criteria at any time.
- Emphasizes control by the Vice President: no one is admitted to membership without the Vice President’s approval.

nodes.title: Active and Inactive Membership.
nodes.heading: 3.03 Active and Inactive Membership.
nodes.start_phrase: A Member shall be an Active Member during the period that he is – (a) employed as an Eligible Employee, (b) not a U.S. Person, and (c) currently approved for status as an Active Member by the V ice President.
nodes.summary: The section defines membership rules. Eligibility is based on the Vice President’s determination that an individual is an Eligible Employee. Admission requires that the person is not a U.S. Person and has explicit Vice President approval; membership becomes effective on the Entry Date, with timing structured to avoid PIRP-DC Accounts being treated as deferred compensation under Section 409A of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code. Membership status is classified as Active when the individual is employed as an Eligible Employee, is not a U.S. Person, and has current Vice President approval; if any of these conditions are not met, the individual is an Inactive Member.

nodes.title: ARTICLE IV – CONTRIBUTIONS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE IV – CONTRIBUTIONS
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent provided in subsections (a) and (b) below , the Employer shall allocate Pay Credits and Interest Credits to a Member ’s PIRP-DC Account, each determined by the V ice President as follows –
nodes.summary:
- Article IV outlines how the Employer allocates Pay Credits and Interest Credits to each Member’s PIRP-DC Account, with determinations made by the Vice President.
- Pay Credits:
  - Eligibility: Must be an Active Member during the Plan Year.
  - Standard calculation: Annualized Salary as of the Plan Year’s Valuation Date multiplied by an applicable percentage (5%, 8%, 10%, 12%, or 18%).
  - Special rule effective January 1, 2021: For Eligible Employees who become Active Members on/after that date and have no Service completed while a U.S. Person, Pay Credits are based on “points” (age + years of Service, measured in years and days) with the following tiers: <35 = 5%; 35–39 = 6%; 40–44 = 7%; 45–49 = 8%; 50–54 = 9%; 55–59 = 10%; 60–64 = 11%; 65+ = 12% of Eligible Pay.
  - The Vice President sets the applicable percentage at Entry Date (or re-entry) and may change it each subsequent Plan Year; assignments are at the Vice President’s sole discretion, and employees have no legally binding right to an initial or increased percentage.
  - Pay Credits must cease during a Plan Year as needed to comply with the Internal Revenue Code Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit and other plan limitations (Section 9.14).
- Interest Credits:
  - Eligibility: Must be an Active or Inactive Member during the year and have had a prior-year PIRP-DC Account balance as of the prior Plan Year’s Valuation Date.
  - The method for determining the Interest Credit amount is referenced but not fully included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Contributions.
nodes.heading: 4.01 Contributions.
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent provided in subsections (a) and (b) below , the Employer shall allocate Pay Credits and Interest Credits to a Member ’s PIRP-DC Account, each determined by the V ice President as follows –
nodes.summary:
- Article IV defines how Contributions are allocated to Members’ PIRP-DC Accounts through Pay Credits and Interest Credits, both determined by the Vice President (VP).
- Pay Credits:
  - Eligibility: Must be an Active Member during the Plan Year.
  - Amount: Annualized Salary as of the Valuation Date multiplied by an applicable percentage (5%, 8%, 10%, 12%, or 18%) set by the VP at their sole discretion; may be reset each Plan Year; no guaranteed right to any initial or increased percentage.
  - Special rule (effective Jan 1, 2021): For Eligible Employees who become Active on/after that date and have no Service while a U.S. Person, Pay Credits are based on “points” (age + years of Service, in whole years and days) with the following schedule: <35: 5%; 35–39: 6%; 40–44: 7%; 45–49: 8%; 50–54: 9%; 55–59: 10%; 60–64: 11%; 65+: 12% of Eligible Pay.
  - Limits: Pay Credits cease as needed to comply with IRC Section 401(a)(17) compensation limits and Section 9.14.
- Interest Credits:
  - Eligibility: Must be an Active or Inactive Member during the Plan Year with a prior-year balance.
  - Amount: Interest Rate for the period since the last Valuation Date multiplied by the PIRP-DC Account balance as of that last Valuation Date.
- Timing and proration:
  - Credits are determined as soon as administratively practicable after each Valuation Date.
  - Pay Credits are prorated for fractional years of Active Membership; Interest Credits are prorated for fractional years of Membership, based on days in status over total days in the Plan Year.
  - Paid leave counts as Active Membership for Pay Credit purposes; unpaid leave does not and may reduce or eliminate Pay Credits for that period.
  - In a Member’s final year, prorated Pay and Interest Credits are determined as of the Distribution Valuation Date.
  - The VP’s calculations are conclusive and binding on Members and their Dependents.
- Offsets (Section 4.02):
  - The Corporation may reduce any payment/benefit by the Member’s obligations to the Corporation, by material benefits under other retirement plans (including governmental) covering the same Service/Salary used for DC Program Pay Credits, and by termination indemnity or similar payments reasonably related to Service counted for DC Program credits.
  - Reductions may be applied to Pay Credits, Interest Credits, PIRP-DC Account balances, and distributions.
  - All determinations under this section are in the VP’s sole independent discretion.

nodes.title: Offsets.
nodes.heading: 4.02 Offsets.
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding Section 4.01, the Corporation may reduce the amount of any payment or benefit that is or would become payable to or on behalf of a Member by the amount of any obligation of the Member to the Corporation or by the amount of –
nodes.summary:
- Pay and Interest Credits are calculated by the Vice President after each Valuation Date, with Interest Credits based on the Interest Rate applied to the PIRP-DC Account balance since the prior Valuation Date.
- Credits are prorated for fractional years:
  - Pay Credits are prorated based on the fraction of the year the Member is in Active Membership.
  - Interest Credits are prorated based on the fraction of the year the Member is in Membership.
  - Fractional year is determined by days of Membership/Active Membership divided by total days in the Plan Year.
- Paid leave counts as Active Membership for Pay Credit purposes; unpaid leave does not, which may reduce or eliminate Pay Credits for that period.
- In a Member’s final year, Pay and Interest Credits are determined as of the Distribution Valuation Date and prorated for the fractional final year.
- The Vice President’s calculations of Pay and Interest Credits are conclusive and binding on Members and their Dependents.
- Offsets: The Corporation may reduce payments/benefits by:
  - Any obligations the Member owes the Corporation.
  - Material benefits accrued under other retirement plans (including government-sponsored) to the extent they relate to Service or Salary already used for DC Program Pay Credits.
  - Termination indemnities or similar payments related to termination that relate to Service used for DC Program Pay Credits.
- Such reductions may be applied to Pay/Interest Credits, the PIRP-DC Account balance, or distributions, with all determinations (including materiality) made at the Vice President’s sole discretion.

nodes.title: ARTICLE V – MEMBER ACCOUNTS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE V – MEMBER ACCOUNTS
nodes.start_phrase: Pay Credits and Interest Credits shall be credited to a Member ’s PIRP-DC Account as of the V aluation Date to which such credits relate (or , in the case of Pay Credits and Interest Credits that relate to the Member ’s final year of Membership, as of the Member ’s Distribution V aluation Date) or as soon as administratively practicable thereafter .
nodes.summary:
- Article V outlines how Member PIRP-DC Accounts are recorded, vested, and subject to special vesting rules.
- Section 5.01 (Accounting for Members’ Interests): Pay Credits and Interest Credits are credited as of the relevant Valuation Date (or the Distribution Valuation Date in a Member’s final year), or as soon as administratively practicable. The PIRP-DC Account is a notional bookkeeping device reflecting the Employer’s liability; no assets are segregated, and the account is unfunded, uninsured, and unsecured.
- Section 5.02 (Vesting): A Member is fully vested after 3 years of Service, or earlier upon death or disability while employed by the Employer or PepsiCo Organization. Disability is determined by the Vice President under appropriate standards.
- Section 5.03 (Special Vesting for Approved Transfers and Status Changes):
  - Automatic special vesting applies to Active Members with an Approved Transfer as of the last business day before the earlier of the transfer or the date the Member becomes a U.S. Person due to the transfer.
  - For Status Changes, an Active Member may request special vesting; it is effective only if both the request and the Vice President’s approval are finalized before the effective date.
  - Special vesting vests the Member to the same extent as under Section 5.02 as of the special vesting date.
  - All special vesting rights are subject to maintaining full exemption from IRC Section 409A; Section 5.03 does not apply where inconsistent with that requirement.

nodes.title: Accounting for Members’ Interests.
nodes.heading: 5.01 Accounting for Members’ Interests.
nodes.start_phrase: Pay Credits and Interest Credits shall be credited to a Member ’s PIRP-DC Account as of the V aluation Date to which such credits relate (or , in the case of Pay Credits and Interest Credits that relate to the Member ’s final year of Membership, as of the Member ’s Distribution V aluation Date) or as soon as administratively practicable thereafter .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how Member PIRP-DC Accounts are maintained as bookkeeping records only; no assets are reserved, segregated, funded, insured, or otherwise secured.
- Specifies crediting rules: Pay Credits and Interest Credits are posted as of the relevant Valuation Date (or the Member’s Distribution Valuation Date for the final year of Membership), or as soon as administratively practicable thereafter.
- Defines vesting: subject to Sections 4.02 and 9.14, Members become fully vested after 3 years of Service, or earlier upon death or disability while employed by the Employer or PepsiCo Organization; disability is determined by the Vice President under appropriate standards.
- Provides special vesting rules for Approved Transfers: automatic special vesting applies to an Active Member as of the last business day before the earlier of the Approved Transfer or the date the Member would become a U.S. Person in connection with the transfer.
- Provides special vesting rules for Status Changes: an Active Member may request special vesting effective as of the last business day before the Status Change, provided both the request and the Vice President’s approval are finalized before that date.
- Clarifies that when special vesting applies, the Member becomes vested to the same extent as under the standard vesting rule (Section 5.02) as of the applicable special vesting date.
- States that all rights under the special vesting provisions must preserve the Plan’s complete exemption from U.S. Internal Revenue Code Section 409A; if inconsistent, the special vesting provisions will not apply.

nodes.title: Vesting.
nodes.heading: 5.02 Vesting.
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to Sections 4.02 and 9.14, a Member shall be fully vested in, and have a nonforfeitable right to, his PIRP-DC Account upon completing 3 years of Service, or if earlier , upon the death or disability of the Member while employed by the Employer or PepsiCo Or ganization.
nodes.summary:
- Defines how Pay Credits and Interest Credits are posted to a Member’s PIRP-DC Account on the applicable Valuation Date (or Distribution Valuation Date for a final year), or as soon as administratively practicable.
- Clarifies that the PIRP-DC Account is a notional bookkeeping device reflecting the employer’s liability; no assets are reserved, segregated, funded, insured, or otherwise secured for it.
- Establishes standard vesting: a Member becomes fully vested after 3 years of Service, or earlier upon death or disability while employed; disability is determined by the Vice President under appropriate standards.
- Provides special vesting for Approved Transfers: automatic vesting as of the last business day before the earlier of the transfer or the date the Member would become a U.S. Person in connection with the transfer.
- Allows special vesting for Status Changes upon Member request and Vice President approval, both finalized before the vesting date; effective as of the last business day before the Status Change.
- Specifies that special vesting confers the same vesting extent as standard vesting would on that date.
- Imposes an overriding condition that all allocations, benefits, and rights must remain fully exempt from IRC Section 409A; special vesting does not apply where inconsistent with this exemption.

nodes.title: Special Vesting for Approved Transfers and Status Changes.
nodes.heading: 5.03 Special V esting for Approved T ransfers and Status Changes.
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding Section 5.02 above, in the case of an Active Member who will have an Approved T ransfer during a Plan Y ear, the Active Member shall automatically have special vesting apply as of the last business day before the earlier of – (a) the Active Member ’s Approved T ransfer , or (b) the day the Active Member would become a U.S. Person in connection with the Approved T ransfer .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how Members’ PIRP-DC Accounts are maintained and credited:
  - Pay Credits and Interest Credits are posted as of the applicable Valuation Date (or Distribution Valuation Date for a final year), or as soon as administratively practicable.
  - The PIRP-DC Account is a notional bookkeeping device reflecting credits and the Employer’s liability; it is unfunded, unsecured, and not insured, with no segregated assets.

- Defines vesting rules:
  - Full vesting occurs after 3 years of Service, or earlier upon death or disability while employed by the Employer or PepsiCo Organization.
  - Disability status is determined by the Vice President under appropriate standards.

- Provides special vesting provisions:
  - Automatic special vesting for Approved Transfers: applies on the last business day before the earlier of the transfer date or the date the Member would become a U.S. Person due to the transfer.
  - Special vesting for Status Changes: may be applied upon Member request and Vice President approval, effective the last business day before the Status Change; both request and approval must be finalized before the effective date.
  - Special vesting confers vesting to the same extent as under the standard vesting rule (Section 5.02), but only to the extent consistent with maintaining complete exemption from U.S. Internal Revenue Code Section 409A.

nodes.title: ARTICLE VI – DISTRIBUTION OF BENEFITS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VI – DISTRIBUTION OF BENEFITS
nodes.start_phrase: A Member ’s PIRP-DC Account shall be distributed based upon first to occur of the Member ’s termination of employment with the PepsiCo Or ganization or death, as provided in Sections 6.02 and 6.03 respectively , subject to Section 4.06 (vesting).
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines Article VI – Distribution of Benefits for the PIRP-DC Account:

- Distributions are triggered by the earlier of a member’s termination of employment with the PepsiCo Organization or death, subject to vesting (Section 4.06), and are always paid in cash.
- Upon termination: benefits are paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the member’s Distribution Valuation Date. If termination is due to disability, the Vice President determines disability status and the termination date.
- Upon death: benefits are paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the Distribution Valuation Date. Payment goes to the member’s designated Dependant; if no valid designation exists or all designated Dependants predecease the member, payment goes to the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, and if none, to the estate. The Vice President determines the effectiveness of designations.
- Valuation: the PIRP-DC Account continues to receive Interest Credits and be debited for expenses under Article V until the Distribution Valuation Date.
- Dependant designation: members may designate, change, or revoke Dependants at any time before the change’s effective date. If married and designating someone other than the Eligible Spouse, written spousal consent is required; revocations do not require consent. All designations, changes, revocations, and any required spousal consents must follow Vice President–adopted rules, be made on VP-provided forms, and are not effective until filed with the Vice President.

nodes.title: Distribution Rules Generally.
nodes.heading: 6.01 Distribution Rules Generally .
nodes.start_phrase: A Member ’s PIRP-DC Account shall be distributed based upon first to occur of the Member ’s termination of employment with the PepsiCo Or ganization or death, as provided in Sections 6.02 and 6.03 respectively , subject to Section 4.06 (vesting).
nodes.summary:
- Article VI sets rules for distributing a Member’s PIRP-DC Account, triggered by termination of employment with the PepsiCo Organization or death, subject to vesting under Section 4.06, with all distributions paid in cash.
- Upon termination (including disability), the account is paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month immediately following the Member’s Distribution Valuation Date; for disability terminations, the Vice President determines disability status and the termination date.
- Upon death, the account is paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month immediately following the Distribution Valuation Date; payment goes to the designated Dependant(s). If no valid Dependant designation exists or all designated Dependants have predeceased the Member, payment goes to the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, or if none, to the estate; the Vice President determines the status of designations.
- Account valuation continues to accrue Interest Credits and be debited for expenses per Article V until the Distribution Valuation Date.
- Members may designate one or more Dependants for death benefits and may change or revoke the designation at any time before it becomes effective.
- If married, designating a Dependant other than the Eligible Spouse requires the Eligible Spouse’s written consent; revocations do not require spousal consent.
- All Dependant designations, changes, revocations, and any required spousal consents must follow Vice President–adopted rules, be made in writing on forms provided by the Vice President, and are not effective until filed with the Vice President.

nodes.title: Distributions Upon Termination of Employment.
nodes.heading: 6.02 Distributions Upon T ermination of Employment.
nodes.start_phrase: If a Member ’s PIRP-DC Account becomes distributable based upon his termination of employment with the PepsiCo Organization, such distribution shall be made in a single lump sum payment on the first of the month that immediately follows the Member ’s Distribution V aluation Date.
nodes.summary:
- Article VI governs distribution of benefits from a Member’s PIRP-DC Account.
- Distributions are triggered by the earlier of termination of employment with the PepsiCo Organization or death, and are subject to vesting rules (Section 4.06). All payments are in cash.
- Timing: Payments are made as a single lump sum on the first day of the month immediately following the Member’s Distribution Valuation Date.
- Termination due to disability: The Vice President determines whether the Member is disabled and the effective termination date.
- Death: Payment is made in a lump sum after the Distribution Valuation Date to the Member’s designated Dependant(s). If no valid designation exists or all designated Dependants have predeceased the Member, payment goes to the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner; if none, to the estate.
- Valuation: The account continues to receive Interest Credits and be debited for expenses (per Article V) until the Distribution Valuation Date.
- Dependant designation rules: A Member may designate, change, or revoke Dependants at any time before the election’s effective date. If married and designating a non-spouse Dependant, written consent of the Eligible Spouse is required; revocations do not require spousal consent. All designations/changes/consents must follow Vice President–adopted rules, be in writing on provided forms, and are not effective until filed with the Vice President.

nodes.title: Distributions Upon Death.
nodes.heading: 6.03 Distributions Upon Death.
nodes.start_phrase: If a Member ’s PIRP-DC Account becomes distributable based upon his death, such distribution shall be made in a single lump sum payment on the first day of the month that immediately follows the Member ’s Distribution V aluation Date.
nodes.summary:
- Article VI outlines distribution of benefits for PIRP-DC Accounts, payable only in cash and subject to vesting (Section 4.06).
- Distributions are triggered by the earlier of termination of employment or death.
- Payments are made as a single lump sum on the first day of the month immediately following the Member’s Distribution Valuation Date.
- For disability-related terminations, the Vice President determines disability status and the termination date.
- Account valuation continues with Interest Credits (and expense debits) under Article V until the Distribution Valuation Date.
- Upon death, amounts are paid to the Member’s designated Dependant(s); if none are designated or survive, payment goes to the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, or if neither exists, to the estate; determinations are made by the Vice President.
- Members may designate, change, or revoke Dependant(s) at any time; if married, naming a non-spouse Dependant requires written spousal consent (revocations do not). All designations/changes/consents must follow Vice President–adopted rules, be in writing on provided forms, and are effective only when filed with the Vice President.

nodes.title: Valuation.
nodes.heading: 6.04 Valuation.
nodes.start_phrase: In determining the amount of any individual distribution pursuant to this Article, the Member ’s PIRP-DC Account shall continue to be credited with Interest Credits (and debited for expenses) as specified in Article V until the Member ’s Distribution Valuation Date.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article VI outlines when and how PIRP-DC Accounts are distributed, subject to vesting (Section 4.06), and mandates all payouts be in cash.
- Triggers for distribution: upon a Member’s termination of employment with the PepsiCo Organization or upon death.
- Payment form and timing: distributions are made as a single lump sum on the first day of the month immediately following the Member’s Distribution Valuation Date.
- Disability terminations: whether a Member is disabled and the termination date are determined by the Vice President.
- Death benefits and payee order: amounts are paid to the Member’s designated Dependant(s); if no valid designation exists or all designated Dependants predecease the Member, payment goes to the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, and if none, to the estate.
- Valuation: the PIRP-DC Account continues to receive Interest Credits and be debited for expenses until the Distribution Valuation Date.
- Dependant designations: Members may designate, change, or revoke Dependants at any time before the effective date; if married, designating a non-spouse Dependant requires written consent of the Eligible Spouse (revocations do not). All actions must follow Vice President–adopted rules, be in writing on provided forms, and are not effective until filed with the Vice President.

nodes.title: Designation of Dependant.
nodes.heading: 6.05 Designation of Dependant.
nodes.start_phrase: A Member shall designate one or more Dependants who will be entitled to any amounts payable on his death.
nodes.summary:
- Article VI sets the rules for distributing PIRP-DC Account benefits.
- Distributions are triggered by the earlier of a member’s termination of employment with the PepsiCo Organization or death, subject to vesting (Section 4.06), and are paid in cash.
- Upon termination (including disability), benefits are paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the Distribution Valuation Date; the Vice President determines disability status and the termination date for disability cases.
- Upon death, benefits are paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the Distribution Valuation Date to the designated Dependant(s); if none are effectively designated or all have predeceased the member, payment goes to the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, or if none, to the estate. The Vice President determines whether a Dependant designation is in effect.
- The account continues to receive Interest Credits and be charged expenses (per Article V) until the Distribution Valuation Date used for payment.
- Members may designate, change, or revoke Dependant(s) for death benefits; if married and naming a non-spouse Dependant, written consent of the Eligible Spouse is required (revocations do not require consent). All such actions must follow Vice President rules, be in writing on prescribed forms, and are effective only when filed with the Vice President.

nodes.title: ARTICLE VII – ADMINISTRATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VII – ADMINISTRA TION
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the V ice President, who shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as he deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Article VII outlines Plan administration, centering authority in the Vice President.
- 7.01 Authority to Administer Plan:
  - The Vice President administers the Plan, may interpret it, and issue regulations, all in his sole discretion; his interpretations, determinations, and regulations are final and binding.
  - He may delegate any responsibilities or designate others to carry out duties; references to actions by the Vice President include actions by his delegates.
- 7.02 Facility of Payment:
  - If a person entitled to benefits is under legal disability or otherwise unable to manage finances, the Vice President may direct payments to the person’s legal representative or apply them for the person’s benefit as he deems advisable.
  - Such payments fully discharge the Plan’s liability for those benefits.
- 7.03 Claims Procedure:
  - The Vice President has exclusive, absolute discretionary authority to construe and interpret the Plan, decide eligibility, and determine benefit amounts; benefits are payable only if he decides the claimant is entitled.
  - His discretion is intended to be maximal; decisions are final, conclusive, and binding, and are reviewable only under the arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.
  - He may consider the Corporation’s intent when interpreting provisions, even if other documents suggest otherwise.
  - If a claim (by a member, putative member, dependent, or putative dependent) is denied in whole or part, a claims procedure will be provided by the Vice President or his designee; the Vice President has authority to modify the procedure (text ends mid-sentence).

nodes.title: Authority to Administer Plan.
nodes.heading: 7.01 Authority to Administer Plan.
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the V ice President, who shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as he deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Article VII outlines plan administration, vesting broad discretionary authority in the Vice President (VP).
- Section 7.01:
  - Administration by the VP: The VP interprets the Plan, issues regulations, and makes determinations in sole discretion; decisions are final and binding.
  - Delegation: The VP may delegate responsibilities to others; references to VP actions include actions by delegates/designees.
- Section 7.02 (Facility of Payment): If a beneficiary is legally disabled or otherwise unable to manage finances, the VP may direct payments to a legal representative or apply them for the person’s benefit; such payments fully discharge the Plan’s liability.
- Section 7.03 (Claims Procedure): The VP has exclusive, absolute discretion to interpret the Plan, decide eligibility, and determine benefit amounts; benefits are payable only if the VP decides the claimant is entitled. Decisions are final, binding, and reviewed, if at all, under an arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard. The VP may consider the Corporation’s intent in making determinations. If a claim (by a Member, putative Member, Dependant, or putative Dependant) is denied, a claims procedure will be provided; the VP may modify procedures (text truncated).

nodes.title: Facility of Payment.
nodes.heading: 7.02 Facility of Payment.
nodes.start_phrase: Whenever , in the opinion of the V ice President, a person entitled to receive any payment of a benefit hereunder is under a legal disability or is incapacitated in any way so as to be unable to manage his financial af fairs, the V ice President may direct that payments from the Plan be made to such person’ s legal representative for his benefit, or that the payment be applied for the benefit of such person in such manner as the V ice President considers advisable.
nodes.summary:
- Article VII outlines Plan administration, vesting broad authority in the Vice President.
- 7.01 Authority to Administer Plan:
  - The Vice President administers the Plan, interprets provisions, and issues regulations in sole discretion.
  - All interpretations and determinations are final, conclusive, and binding.
  - The Vice President may delegate duties and references to actions by the Vice President include actions by delegates.
- 7.02 Facility of Payment:
  - If a beneficiary is legally disabled or otherwise incapacitated, the Vice President may direct payments to a legal representative or apply them for the beneficiary’s benefit.
  - Such payments constitute a complete discharge of liability for the Plan.
- 7.03 Claims Procedure:
  - The Vice President has exclusive, absolute discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, decide eligibility, and determine benefit amounts; benefits are paid only if the Vice President decides the claimant is entitled.
  - Discretion is intended to be maximal and decisions are subject only to arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) review.
  - Decisions are final, conclusive, and binding; the Vice President may consider the Corporation’s intent when interpreting provisions.
  - If a claim is denied, the claimant will be provided the Plan’s claims procedure; the Vice President has discretion to modify the procedure (section text is truncated).

nodes.title: Claims Procedure.
nodes.heading: 7.03 Claims Pr ocedur e.
nodes.start_phrase: The V ice President shall have the exclusive discretionary authority to construe and to interpret the Plan, to decide all questions of eligibility for benefits and to determine the amount of such benefits, and his decisions on such matters are final and conclusive.
nodes.summary:
- Governance and authority: The Plan is administered by the Vice President, who has sole, absolute discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, issue regulations, decide eligibility and benefit amounts, and whose determinations are final and binding. The Vice President may delegate any duties to other persons or entities, and actions by delegates are treated as actions by the Vice President.
- Facility of payment: If a beneficiary is legally disabled or otherwise unable to manage finances, the Vice President may direct payments to a legal representative or apply benefits for the person’s benefit; such payments fully discharge the Plan’s liability.
- Claims procedure: The Vice President has exclusive discretion over claims and may modify procedures so long as core steps remain. Upon denial, the claimant receives written notice within 90 days (extendable to 180 days) with reasons, Plan provisions cited, what additional information is needed, and review procedures. On review, the claimant may submit relevant information; a decision is issued within 60 days (extendable to 120 days) with specific reasons and Plan citations, and notice of the right to free copies of relevant documents.
- Standard and scope of review: Any court/arbitration review is limited to the record before the Vice President at the time of determination and applies the arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard. Claimants must fully exhaust internal remedies before external review. The Vice President may consider the Corporation’s intent in interpreting provisions.
- Limitations period: Any claim or legal action for wrongful denial of benefits must be filed within two years of accrual, which occurs no later than the earliest of: receipt of the benefit calculation, the identified payment commencement date, or when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the claim’s basis. Failure to file within two years bars the claim.

nodes.title: Limitations on Actions.
nodes.heading: 7.04 Limitations on Actions.
nodes.start_phrase: Any claim filed under Article VII and any action filed in any court or other tribunal by or on behalf of a former or current Employee, Member , Dependant or any other individual, person or entity (collectively , a “Petitioner”) for the alleged wrongful denial of Plan benefits must be brought within two years of the date the Petitioner ’s cause of action first accrues.
nodes.summary:
- Sets out the Plan’s internal claims and appeals process overseen by the Vice President (or designee).
- Initial claim decision timelines: written notice within 90 days of receipt; may extend to 180 days with prior notice citing special circumstances and expected decision date.
- Required contents of denial notices: specific reasons, citations to Plan provisions, what additional information is needed and why, and a description of the review procedure with applicable time limits.
- Appeal/review process: claimant may submit comments, documents, and records; the Vice President must consider all relevant materials, whether or not submitted initially.
- Appeal decision timelines: decision within 60 days of review request; may extend up to an additional 60 days with prior notice of special circumstances and expected decision date.
- Final decision requirements: written in understandable language, include specific reasons and Plan provision references, and inform claimant of the right to receive free copies of all relevant documents.
- Judicial or tribunal review limited to the administrative record before the Vice President at the time of determination and conditioned on full exhaustion of internal procedures.
- Two-year statute of limitations for claims/actions alleging wrongful denial of benefits, running from the earliest of: receipt of the benefit calculation at issue, the identified payment commencement date, or actual/constructive knowledge of the claim’s factual basis; failure to file within two years bars the claim.
- Post-appeal correspondence or communications do not toll or extend the two-year limitations period.
- Venue restriction: any court or tribunal action must be brought in New York state or federal courts nearest the Corporation’s headquarters.
- Clarifies that specific references to the Vice President’s discretion do not limit the breadth of discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Mandatory exhaustion of the Plan’s claims procedures before filing in court or any tribunal; interpreted as broadly as possible to require exhaustion.
- Exhaustion not excused unless the claimant clearly submitted a claim or, for document requests, met strict conditions (required by Plan/law, written to and received by the Vice President, not provided within six months or a reasonable longer period, and clearly asserting a legal right).
- Individuals not treated as Members must clearly assert a claim to Member status to satisfy exhaustion steps.
- Exhaustion applies even if other, non-claim disputes are more significant, to actual or potential rights, and to novel disputes; if no specific procedure exists, the Vice President will establish one or apply Section 7.03 by analogy.
- The Vice President may create special arrangements to consider claims on a class basis or address unusual conflict concerns.

nodes.title: Restriction of Venue.
nodes.heading: 7.05 Restriction of V enue.
nodes.start_phrase: Any claim or action filed in court or any other tribunal in connection with the Plan by or on behalf of a Petitioner shall only be brought or filed in the state or federal courts of New Y ork, specifically the state or federal court, whichever applies, located nearest the Corporation’ s headquarters.
nodes.summary:
- Confirms that a two-year limitations period for filing court actions remains unchanged by any communications after the mandatory appeals process.
- Restricts venue: all Plan-related lawsuits or actions by/for a Petitioner must be filed exclusively in New York state or federal court located nearest the Corporation’s headquarters.
- Clarifies discretion: specific references to the Vice President’s discretion do not limit the breadth of that discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Mandates exhaustion: a Claimant must fully exhaust the Plan’s claims procedure (Section 7.03) before filing any Claim in court or another tribunal; courts are to interpret this exhaustion requirement as broadly as possible.
- Limits excuses for non-exhaustion:
  - No excuse for failure to respond unless the claimant clearly indicated to the Vice President that a Plan Claim was being submitted.
  - No excuse for document-related issues unless all conditions are met: the documents are legally/Plan-required; the request is written, addressed to, and received by the Vice President; the Vice President fails to provide them within six months (or a reasonable longer period); and the requester clearly asserted a legal right to the documents.
  - Individuals not treated as Members must clearly assert to the Vice President that they were entitled to Member status.
- Exhaustion applies even if:
  - Other, non-Claim disputes are more significant or heard concurrently.
  - The Vice President grants rights in novel disputes or particular situations.
  - Rights are actual or potential.
  - No specific procedures exist for the Claim—then the Vice President must promptly establish them or apply/analogize to Section 7.03 benefit-claim procedures.
- Allows the Vice President to make special arrangements to consider Claims on a class basis or to address unusual conflict-of-interest concerns.

nodes.title: Effect of Specific References.
nodes.heading: 7.06 Effect of Specific Refer ences.
nodes.start_phrase: Specific references in the Plan to the V ice President’ s discretion shall create no inference that the V ice President’ s discretion in any other respect, or in connection with any other provision, is less complete or broad.
nodes.summary:
- Post-appeal communications do not extend or affect the Plan’s two-year limitations period for legal action.
- Venue restriction: any court action related to the Plan must be filed exclusively in New York state or federal court located nearest the Corporation’s headquarters.
- Vice President’s discretion: specific mentions of the Vice President’s discretion do not limit the overall breadth of that discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Mandatory exhaustion: claimants must fully exhaust the Plan’s internal claims and appeals procedures before filing any claim in court or another tribunal; this exhaustion rule is to be applied as broadly as possible.
- Clarifications on exhaustion: 
  - It is not excused for failure to respond unless the claimant clearly indicated a Plan claim was being submitted.
  - It is not excused for document requests unless the documents are legally/Plan-required, the request is in writing to and received by the Vice President, the Vice President fails to provide them within six months (or a reasonable longer period), and the requester clearly asserted a legal right to the documents.
  - Individuals not treated as Members must clearly assert they were entitled to Membership.
- Scope of exhaustion: applies even if other, non-claim disputes are more significant; to rights the Vice President may extend in novel or particular situations; to actual or potential rights; and even when no specific procedures exist—then the Vice President will establish or analogize to existing Section 7.03 procedures.
- Administrative flexibility: the Vice President may arrange class-based claim consideration or address unusual conflict concerns.

nodes.title: Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court.
nodes.heading: 7.07 Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’ s Claims Pr ocedur es Befor e Filing in Court.
nodes.start_phrase: Before filing any Claim (as defined below in this Section), including a suit or other action, in a court or in another tribunal, a Claimant (as defined below in this Section) must first fully exhaust all of the Claimant’ s rights under the claims procedure in Section 7.03.
nodes.summary:
- Confirms a two-year limitations period for bringing claims that is not extended by communications after completing the Plan’s mandatory appeals process.
- Restricts venue: any court action relating to the Plan must be filed in New York state or federal court located nearest the Corporation’s headquarters.
- Clarifies that specific references to the Vice President’s discretion do not limit the breadth of that discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Mandates complete exhaustion of the Plan’s claims procedures before any lawsuit or tribunal action, with the exhaustion requirement to be applied as broadly as possible.
- Specifies when exhaustion will not be excused, including strict conditions for document requests (must be a written request to the Vice President for documents the Plan/law requires, received by the Vice President, with non-response within six months or a reasonable longer period, and a clear assertion of legal right). Individuals not treated as Members must clearly assert entitlement to Membership to satisfy notice.
- States exhaustion applies even if:
  - Other, non-claim disputes are more significant or will be considered at the same time,
  - The Vice President offers special rights in novel or particular situations,
  - Rights are only potential,
  - No specific procedures exist for the Claim, in which case the Vice President must establish them or apply the existing benefits-claim procedures by analogy.
- Allows the Vice President to make special arrangements for class consideration of Claims or to address conflicts, to maximize the requirement of exhaustion.
- Defines key terms:
  - Dispute: any claim, dispute, issue, assertion, action, or other matter.
  - Claim: a Dispute involving Plan interpretation, terms, legality, adoption/validity, administration, compliance with law, benefit requests/recovery, alleged breaches of legal duty, or any similar or Plan-related matter (including those deemed similar by the Vice President).
  - Claimant: broadly includes current/former eligible employees, Members, Dependents, their spouses/former spouses/estates/heirs/representatives, related persons/entities, and groups thereof.
- States the Plan’s good-faith intent to comply with law and imposes a contractual obligation to fully exhaust remedies to ensure efficient, uniform resolution and to avoid unnecessary litigation costs.

nodes.title: AMENDMENT AND TERMINATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VIII – AMENDMENT AND TERMINA TION
nodes.start_phrase: While the Corporation intends to continue the Plan indefinitely , it assumes no contractual obligation as to its continuance.
nodes.summary:
- Article VIII outlines the Corporation’s rights to amend and terminate the Plan.
- The Corporation intends to continue the Plan indefinitely but has no contractual obligation to do so.
- The Corporation may amend, terminate, or partially terminate the Plan at any time, to the fullest extent allowed by law.
- Member/Dependant account balances as of the amendment/termination date cannot be reduced, except to the extent the Member becomes entitled to amounts under another employer-maintained plan or practice.
- Specific forms and timing of payments are not protected by the non-reduction rule.
- Only the Corporation can amend the Plan, with or without retroactive effect; other Employers have no amendment rights.
- The Corporation can terminate the Plan entirely or only with respect to certain Employers; if fewer than all Employers are terminated, the Plan continues for employees of the remaining Employers.

nodes.title: Continuation of the Plan.
nodes.heading: 8.01 Continuation of the Plan.
nodes.start_phrase: While the Corporation intends to continue the Plan indefinitely , it assumes no contractual obligation as to its continuance.
nodes.summary:
- States the Corporation’s non-binding intent to continue the Plan indefinitely, while reserving the unilateral right to amend, terminate, or partially terminate the Plan at any time to the fullest extent allowed by law.
- Protects Members’ Plan account balances as of the amendment/termination date from reduction, except to the extent a Member becomes entitled to amounts under another employer-maintained plan or practice; specific forms or timing of payments are not protected.
- Grants the Corporation sole authority to amend the Plan, with or without retroactive effect, subject to the balance-protection rule; other Employers have no amendment rights.
- Allows the Corporation to terminate the Plan entirely or only for one or more participating Employers; if not terminated for all Employers, the Plan continues for employees of the remaining Employers.

nodes.title: Amendment.
nodes.heading: 8.02 Amendment.
nodes.start_phrase: The Corporation may , in its sole discretion, make any amendment or amendments to this Plan from time to time, with or without retroactive ef fect, subject to Section 8.01.
nodes.summary:
- States the Corporation’s intent to continue the Plan indefinitely but disclaims any contractual obligation to do so.
- Reserves the Corporation’s sole discretion to amend, terminate, or partially terminate the Plan at any time, to the fullest extent permitted by law.
- Protects Members’ and Dependants’ account balances as of the amendment/termination date from reduction, except to the extent a Member becomes entitled to benefits under another employer plan or practice.
- Clarifies that specific forms and timing of payments are not protected and may be changed.
- Authorizes the Corporation to amend the Plan with or without retroactive effect, subject to the balance-protection rule; other Employers have no amendment rights.
- Permits termination of the Plan in whole or as to one or more Employers; if terminated for fewer than all Employers, the Plan continues for remaining Employers’ employees.

nodes.title: Termination.
nodes.heading: 8.03 Termination.
nodes.start_phrase: The Corporation may terminate the Plan, either as to its participation or as to the participation of one or more Employers.
nodes.summary:
- Article VIII outlines the Corporation’s authority to amend, terminate, or partially terminate the Plan.
- Continuation: The Corporation intends to keep the Plan indefinitely but has no contractual obligation to do so. It may change or end the Plan at any time, provided Members’ and Dependants’ account balances as of the change/termination date are not reduced, except where a Member becomes entitled to amounts under another employer plan or practice. Specific payment forms and timing are not protected. Rights are as broad as allowed by law.
- Amendment (8.02): The Corporation alone may amend the Plan, with or without retroactive effect, subject to the protection in 8.01. Other Employers cannot amend the Plan.
- Termination (8.03): The Corporation may terminate the Plan entirely or only for certain Employers. If termination applies to fewer than all Employers, the Plan continues for employees of the remaining Employers.

nodes.title: MISCELLANEOUS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE IX – MISCELLANEOUS
nodes.start_phrase: The Employers’ obligations under the Plan shall not be funded, but shall constitute liabilities by the Employer payable when due out of the Employer ’s general funds.
nodes.summary:
- Declares the plan as unfunded; benefits are payable from employers’ general assets, giving members only unsecured creditor status.
- Assigns all plan administration and management costs to employers, allocated by each employer’s share of total members, unless the Corporation agrees otherwise.
- Defines employment termination for prolonged absences: deemed terminated after 12 months of non-death/discharge/retirement/quitting absence unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military or national service does not trigger termination while the employer considers the person employed or until permanent resignation.
- Authorizes withholding from benefits to satisfy taxes, assessments, or duties as determined by the Vice President.
- Clarifies the plan does not guarantee employment or continued employment and does not limit employers’ right to discharge employees with or without cause.
- Limits rights to those expressly provided by the plan; termination and resulting loss of membership do not create grounds for damages or increased damages against the employer or the PepsiCo organization.

nodes.title: Unfunded Plan.
nodes.heading: 9.01 Unfunded Plan.
nodes.start_phrase: The Employers’ obligations under the Plan shall not be funded, but shall constitute liabilities by the Employer payable when due out of the Employer ’s general funds.
nodes.summary:
- The plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the employer’s general assets, and participants have only the rights of unsecured general creditors.
- Administrative and management costs are borne by the employers and allocated proportionally based on each employer’s share of members, unless otherwise agreed by the Corporation.
- A member absent for reasons other than death, discharge, retirement, or quitting is deemed terminated after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military or national service absences are not deemed terminations while the employer considers the member employed or until permanent resignation.
- The plan may withhold from benefits any taxes, assessments, or duties determined to be owed.
- The plan does not create an employment contract or guarantee continued employment; employers may discharge employees with or without cause.
- No one has a right to benefits beyond the plan’s terms; termination and resulting loss of membership do not create grounds for damages against the employer or the PepsiCo organization.

nodes.title: Costs of the Plan.
nodes.heading: 9.02 Costs of the Plan.
nodes.start_phrase: Unless otherwise agreed by the Corporation, all costs, char ges and expenses of or incidental to the administration and management of the Plan shall be the costs, char ges and expenses of the Employers and shall be paid by each Employer based on the proportion of Members who are employed by such Employer as compared to the total number of Members at the time the cost or expense is incurred.
nodes.summary:
- The plan is unfunded; employers pay benefits from general assets, and participants have only unsecured creditor status.
- Plan administration and management costs are borne by employers (unless the Corporation agrees otherwise) and allocated based on each employer’s proportion of total members at the time costs are incurred.
- A member absent for reasons other than death, discharge, retirement, or quitting (e.g., sickness, accident, layoff, vacation) is deemed terminated after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; full-time military or national service does not constitute termination while the employer regards the individual as employed or until permanent resignation.
- The plan may withhold amounts from benefits to satisfy taxes, assessments, or duties as determined by the Vice President.
- The plan does not constitute an employment contract or guarantee continued employment; employers may discharge employees with or without cause.
- No person has rights to benefits beyond the plan’s terms; termination and resulting cessation of membership do not create grounds for damages or increased damages against the employer or the PepsiCo organization.

nodes.title: Temporary Absence of Member.
nodes.heading: 9.03 Temporary Absence of Member .
nodes.start_phrase: If a Member is absent from duty by reason other than death, dischar ge, retirement or quitting ( e.g., sickness, accident, layof f, vacation), he shall be deemed to have terminated employment on the date that is 12 months after the date on which he is absent, unless the V ice President determines otherwise.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the plan as unfunded; benefits are paid from employers’ general assets, and participants have only the status of unsecured general creditors.
- Allocates all administration and management costs to employers (unless the Corporation agrees otherwise), apportioned by each employer’s share of total members.
- Defines rules for temporary absences: deemed employment termination after 12 months of non-death/discharge/retirement/quitting absence unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military/national service does not trigger termination while the employer considers the member employed or until permanent resignation.
- Authorizes tax/assessment withholding from benefits as determined by the Vice President.
- Clarifies the plan does not guarantee employment or restrict employers’ right to discharge employees.
- Limits rights to those explicitly provided by the plan; termination and resulting loss of membership do not create grounds for damages against the employer or the PepsiCo organization.

nodes.title: Taxes, Etc.
nodes.heading: 9.04 Taxes, Etc.
nodes.start_phrase: In the event any tax or assessment or other duty is determined by the V ice President to be owing in respect of any benefit payable from the Plan, the Plan shall be entitled to withhold an amount not exceeding the amount of any such tax or assessment or other duty from the benefit payable and shall apply the same in satisfaction of said tax or assessment or other duty .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Plan as an unfunded obligation payable from each Employer’s general assets; Members’ benefit rights are no greater than those of unsecured general creditors.
- Allocates all administration and management expenses to Employers, pro rata based on each Employer’s share of total Members, unless the Corporation agrees otherwise.
- Defines treatment of temporary absences: absence for reasons other than death/discharge/retirement/quitting leads to deemed termination after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military or national service does not trigger termination while the Employer considers the person employed or until permanent resignation.
- Authorizes the Plan to withhold from benefits any taxes, assessments, or duties determined to be owed.
- Clarifies the Plan does not guarantee employment or continued employment; Employers may discharge employees with or without cause.
- Limits claims to those expressly provided by the Plan; cessation of membership upon termination of employment does not create grounds for damages against the Employer or the PepsiCo Organization.

nodes.title: Nonguarantee of Employment.
nodes.heading: 9.05 Nonguarantee of Employment.
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing in the Plan shall be construed as a contract of employment between an Employer and any of its employees, or as a right of any such employee to continue in the employment of the Employer , or as a limitation of the right of an Employer to dischar ge any of its employees, with or without cause.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the plan as unfunded; benefits are paid from employers’ general assets, and participants are unsecured general creditors.
- Allocates all administrative and management costs to employers (unless the Corporation agrees otherwise), prorated by each employer’s share of total members at the time costs are incurred.
- Defines termination for prolonged absence: a member absent for reasons other than death, discharge, retirement, or quitting is deemed terminated after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military/national service does not constitute termination while the employer considers the individual employed or until permanent resignation.
- Authorizes withholding from benefits to satisfy taxes, assessments, or duties as determined by the Vice President.
- Clarifies no guarantee of employment; the plan does not create an employment contract or limit employers’ right to discharge employees with or without cause.
- Limits rights to those explicitly provided in the plan; no additional claims or damages arise from cessation of membership upon termination, including against any PepsiCo Organization entity.

nodes.title: No Right to Benefits.
nodes.heading: 9.06 No Right to Benefits.
nodes.start_phrase: No person, whether or not being a Member , shall have any claim, right or interest under the Plan except as provided by the terms of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- The plan is unfunded; employer obligations are paid from general assets, and participants’ rights are no greater than those of unsecured general creditors.
- Plan administration costs are borne by the Employers, allocated based on each Employer’s share of total Members, unless the Corporation agrees otherwise.
- A Member absent for reasons other than death, discharge, retirement, or quitting (e.g., sickness, accident, layoff, vacation) is deemed terminated after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; full-time military or national service does not constitute termination while the Employer regards the individual as employed or until permanent resignation.
- The plan may withhold amounts from benefits to satisfy taxes, assessments, or duties as determined by the Vice President.
- The plan does not guarantee employment or restrict an Employer’s right to terminate employment with or without cause.
- No person has rights or claims beyond the plan’s terms; termination and resulting loss of membership do not create grounds for damages against the Employer or the PepsiCo Organization.

nodes.title: Charges on Benefits and Recovery of Excess Payments.
nodes.heading: 9.07 Charges on Benefits and Recovery of Excess Payments.
nodes.start_phrase: All benefits in respect of a Member under the Plan shall stand char ged with and be subject to deductions therefrom of all sums in respect of losses to a member of the PepsiCo Or ganization or Employer or otherwise caused by misdemeanor of the Member and on production by the member of the PepsiCo Or ganization or Employer of proof satisfactory to the V ice President that any such loss ought to be made good by a Member .
nodes.summary:
- Section 9.07 (Charges on Benefits and Recovery of Excess Payments):
  - Plan benefits may be reduced to reimburse the Employer or PepsiCo Organization for losses caused by a Member’s misconduct, upon proof satisfactory to the Vice President; deducted amounts are paid to the affected employer entity as a full discharge.
  - Any overpayment, premature, or misdirected payment (“Excess Payment”) must be returned to the Plan.
  - To recover Excess Payments (with interest), the Plan has nonexclusive rights including:
    - A constructive trust and first-priority equitable lien on the Excess Payment, its proceeds, or substitutes, enforceable even after transfers.
    - The right, at the Vice President’s discretion, to offset other amounts otherwise payable to the recipient.
    - The right to pursue legal or equitable actions in any competent court; recipients submit to such jurisdictions and waive related defenses.
  - Recipients must cooperate and take actions requested by the Vice President to facilitate recovery. These provisions maximize and do not limit the Plan’s recovery rights.

- Section 9.08 (Prohibited Misconduct) [partial]:
  - If the Vice President determines a Member engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time up to the second anniversary of termination, the Member forfeits all Pay Credits and Interest Credits (past, current, and future), and the Member’s PIRP-DC Account is adjusted to reflect the forfeiture.

nodes.title: Prohibited Misconduct.
nodes.heading: 9.08 Pr ohibited Misconduct.
nodes.start_phrase: (a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this Plan to the contrary , if the V ice President determines that a Member has engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time prior to the second anniversary of his termination of employment with the PepsiCo Or ganization, the Member shall forfeit all Pay Credits and Interest Credits (whether paid previously , being paid currently or payable in the future), and his PIRP-DC Account shall be adjusted to reflect such forfeiture and previously paid Pay Credits and Interest Credits shall be recovered.
nodes.summary:
- Charges on benefits and recovery of excess payments (Section 9.07):
  - Member benefits can be reduced to cover losses to PepsiCo or the Employer caused by the Member’s misdemeanor, upon proof satisfactory to the Vice President.
  - Any overpayment, premature, or misdirected payment (“Excess Payment”) must be returned to the Plan.
  - The Plan has a constructive trust and first-priority equitable lien (with interest) over Excess Payments and their proceeds.
  - The Plan may offset future amounts payable to the recipient to recover Excess Payments, at the Vice President’s discretion.
  - The Plan may pursue legal or equitable actions in any chosen jurisdiction; recipients submit to such jurisdiction.
  - Recipients must cooperate to restore Excess Payments with interest; the subsection maximizes the Plan’s recovery rights.

- Prohibited Misconduct and forfeiture (Section 9.08):
  - If the Vice President determines a Member engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time up to two years after termination, the Member forfeits all Pay Credits and Interest Credits (past, current, or future), and previously paid amounts will be recovered; Members agree to repay.
  - Prohibited Misconduct includes:
    - Participating (broadly defined) in businesses that market/sell/distribute/produce “Covered Products” (with a narrow non-competing retail/consumption exception).
    - Soliciting PepsiCo employees to leave or join other entities.
    - Using or disclosing PepsiCo confidential information outside job needs.
    - Acts contrary to PepsiCo’s interests (e.g., Code of Conduct violations, insider trading, gross misconduct).
    - Fraud.
  - Whistleblower protection: Members may communicate with government authorities, participate in investigations, and receive awards; attorney‑client privilege is preserved. DTSA safe harbor permits certain confidential or sealed disclosures of trade secrets, including in retaliation lawsuits under specified conditions.
  - Definitions:
    - “Participation” includes serving, advising, consulting, or endorsing competing entities/products.
    - “Covered Products” broadly include beverages (e.g., soft drinks, tea, water, juices, sports/energy/coffee/dairy drinks), juices/juice products, dairy, snacks (salty/sweet/meat/granola/cereal bars/cookies), hot cereals, pancake mixes/syrups, value‑added rice/pasta, ready‑to‑eat cereals, dry pasta, and products/services under development known to the Member.

- Notices (Section 9.09):
  - Notices to the Plan are sufficient if in writing and delivered to the Vice President.
  - Notices to Members may be sent to the last known address or via other reasonably available methods (e.g., electronic) as determined by the Vice President.

- Plan documentation (Section 9.10):
  - Members are entitled to a copy of the Plan upon request.

- Currency of payment (Section 9.11):
  - Benefits are paid in U.S. dollars or another eligible currency approved by the Vice President.
  - Currency conversion follows a methodology approved by the Vice President.

nodes.title: Notices.
nodes.heading: 9.09 Notices.
nodes.start_phrase: Any notice which under the Plan is required to be given to or served upon the Plan shall be deemed to be suf ficiently given to or served upon the Plan if it is in writing and delivered to the V ice President.
nodes.summary:
- Whistleblower and government cooperation: The Plan does not restrict Members from communicating with government authorities about possible legal violations, participating in investigations, or receiving whistleblower awards. The Corporation maintains its attorney-client privilege over protected information.
- Defend Trade Secrets Act notice: Individuals are immune from liability for disclosing trade secrets to government officials or attorneys solely to report or investigate suspected legal violations, or in sealed court filings. In retaliation lawsuits, trade secrets may be shared with the individual’s attorney and used in court if filed under seal and disclosed only by court order.
- Definitions:
  - “Participation” is broadly defined to include serving as a director, officer, employee, consultant, or contractor; providing input, advice, guidance, or suggestions; or offering recommendations/testimonials for a business entity.
  - “Covered Products” include a wide range of PepsiCo-related categories: beverages (e.g., CSDs, tea, water, juice drinks, sports/coffee/energy/value‑added dairy drinks), juices and juice products, dairy products, snacks (salty, sweet, meat snacks, granola/cereal bars, cookies), hot cereals, pancake mixes and syrups, value-added rice and pasta products, ready-to-eat cereals, dry pasta, and any product/service known to be under development by the PepsiCo Organization during the Member’s employment.
- Notices (Section 9.09): Notices to the Plan must be in writing and delivered to the Vice President. Member notices are sufficient if sent to the Member’s last known address on file or via another reasonably available method (e.g., electronic) determined by the Vice President.
- Plan documentation (Section 9.10): Members are entitled to a copy of the Plan upon request.
- Currency of payment (Section 9.11): Benefits are paid in U.S. dollars or another eligible currency approved by the Vice President, using an exchange rate methodology approved by the Vice President.

nodes.title: Plan Documentation.
nodes.heading: 9.10 Plan Documentation.
nodes.start_phrase: Every Member shall on demand be entitled to a copy of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Affirms whistleblower rights: members may report suspected legal violations to government authorities without notifying the corporation, participate in investigations, and receive government awards.
- Preserves attorney-client privilege: the corporation asserts and does not waive privilege over protected information.
- Details DTSA whistleblower immunity: individuals are not liable for disclosing trade secrets when (a) made confidentially to government officials or an attorney solely to report/investigate a suspected legal violation, or (b) filed under seal in legal proceedings; in retaliation suits, trade secrets may be shared with one’s attorney and used in court if filed under seal and not disclosed except by court order.
- Broadly defines “Participation” with a competing business to include serving in roles (director, officer, employee, consultant, contractor), providing input/advice, or offering recommendations/testimonials.
- Defines “Covered Products” tied to PepsiCo’s businesses worldwide, including a broad range of beverages (e.g., soft drinks, tea, water, juice drinks, sports/coffee/energy/value-added dairy drinks), juices, dairy, snacks (salty, sweet, meat, granola/cereal bars, cookies), hot cereals, pancake mixes/syrups, value-added rice and pasta products, ready-to-eat cereals, dry pasta, and any product/service known to be under development during the member’s employment.
- Sets notice procedures: notices to the Plan are effective if delivered in writing to the Vice President; notices to members may be sent to the last known address or via other methods (including electronic) reasonably available as determined by the Vice President.
- Provides member access to plan documents: each member is entitled to a copy of the Plan upon request.
- Specifies currency of payment: benefits are paid in U.S. dollars or another “eligible currency” approved by the Vice President, with conversions using an exchange-rate methodology approved by the Vice President.

nodes.title: Currency of Payment.
nodes.heading: 9.11 Curr ency of Payment.
nodes.start_phrase: Payment of benefits under the Plan shall be made in United States dollars, or other "eligible currency ," as approved by the Vice President.
nodes.summary:
- Whistleblower protections: Members may communicate with government authorities about possible legal violations, participate in investigations, and receive awards without notifying the Corporation; the Corporation maintains its attorney-client privilege.
- Defend Trade Secrets Act notice: Immunity from liability for disclosing trade secrets to government officials or attorneys for reporting/investigation, or in sealed court filings; in retaliation lawsuits, disclosure to an attorney and use in court is permitted if filed under seal and disclosed only by court order.
- Scope definitions: “Participation” in another business is broadly defined to include serving in roles (director, officer, employee, consultant, contractor), providing advice/input, or giving recommendations/testimonials. “Covered Products” are extensively listed, including a wide range of beverages, juices, dairy, snacks, cereals, pancake-related products, rice/pasta products, and any product/service under development by the PepsiCo Organization anywhere in the world during the Member’s employment.
