- Notices: How notices must be delivered to the Plan (in writing to the Vice President) and to Members (to last known address or other methods, including electronic, reasonably available as determined by the Vice President).
- Plan documentation: Members are entitled to a copy of the Plan on demand.
- Currency of payment: Benefits are paid in U.S. dollars or another eligible currency approved by the Vice President, with currency conversion based on a Vice President–approved methodology.

nodes.title: Governing Law.
nodes.heading: 9.12 Governing Law .
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall in all respects be governed by and interpreted according to the laws of the State of New Y ork and any applicable federal law as would be applied in cases that arise in the United States District Courts that sit in the State of New Y ork.
nodes.summary:
- Governing law: The Plan is governed by New York state law and applicable federal law as applied by U.S. District Courts in New York.
- ERISA exemption: The Plan is intended to be exempt from ERISA as an overseas plan for nonresident aliens. Active membership is limited to nonresident aliens working outside the U.S., and permanent administrative records are to be kept outside the U.S.
- Section 409A exemption: The Plan aims to remain fully exempt from IRC Section 409A. U.S. Persons cannot receive Benefit Enhancements tied to compensation or service while they are U.S. Persons. Interest Credits may accrue only on amounts attributable to non-U.S. Person service. Benefit Enhancements are determined after year-end once non-U.S. Person status is confirmed; in a benefit commencement year, the Vice President may authorize an enhancement if satisfied the member will not be a U.S. Person, otherwise benefits start without enhancement and may be adjusted the following year. These rules override any conflicting plan provisions, and the Vice President has broad authority to enforce them.
- Electronic signatures: Electronic signatures and electronic recordkeeping are permitted and carry the same legal effect as manual signatures and paper records, to the extent allowed by law.

nodes.title: Exemption from ERISA.
nodes.heading: 9.13 Exemption fr om ERISA.
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan is intended to be exempt from the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (“ERISA”), as a plan maintained outside of the United States primarily for the benefit of persons substantially all of whom are nonresident aliens of the United States.
nodes.summary:
- Governing Law: The plan is governed by and interpreted under New York law and applicable federal law as applied by U.S. District Courts in New York.
- ERISA Exemption: The plan is intended to be exempt from ERISA as a non-U.S. plan primarily for nonresident aliens. Active membership is limited to nonresident aliens working outside the U.S., and permanent records are to be maintained outside the U.S.
- Section 409A Exemption: The plan is designed to remain completely exempt from IRC Section 409A. No U.S. Person may receive any “Benefit Enhancement” (vesting, increase, or enhancement) based on compensation or service while a U.S. Person. Interest Credits may apply only to amounts derived from non-U.S.-person service. Benefit Enhancements are determined after year-end upon confirming non-U.S.-person status, with limited authority for the Vice President to allow an enhancement in the commencement year if non-U.S.-person status is confirmed; otherwise, benefits start without the enhancement and may be adjusted the following year. The Vice President has overriding authority to ensure Section 409A exemption, superseding any conflicting plan provisions.
- Electronic Signatures: Electronic signatures and electronic records by relevant parties (including the Vice President, Eligible Employees, and Dependents) have the same legal effect as manual signatures and paper records, to the fullest extent permitted by law.

nodes.title: Exemption from Section 409A.
nodes.heading: 9.14 Exemption fr om Section 409A.
nodes.start_phrase: In order to permit this Plan to be completely exempt from United States Internal Revenue Code section 409A (“Section 409A”), this Plan shall be subject to the special operating rules and limitations in this Section 9.14, ef fective for any period to which Section 409A applies.
nodes.summary:
- Governing Law: The Plan is governed by New York law and applicable federal law as applied by U.S. District Courts in New York.
- ERISA Exemption: The Plan is intended to be exempt from ERISA as an offshore plan for nonresident aliens; Active Membership is limited to nonresident aliens with assigned work locations outside the U.S., and permanent administrative records are to be maintained outside the U.S.
- Section 409A Exemption: The Plan is designed to be fully exempt from IRC Section 409A with special rules:
  - No Benefit Enhancements (vesting/increases) based on compensation or service while a Member is a U.S. Person.
  - Interest Credits may be granted to U.S. Persons only on PIRP-DC balances derived from Pay Credits for non-U.S. service (and related Interest Credits).
  - Benefit Enhancements for a year are determined only after confirming post-year-end that the Member was not a U.S. Person for that year.
  - In the benefit commencement year, the Vice President may authorize a Benefit Enhancement if satisfied the Member will not be a U.S. Person; otherwise benefits start without that year’s enhancement, with adjustments the following year if warranted.
  - The Section 409A exemption requirement overrides any conflicting Plan provisions, and the Vice President has broad authority to ensure compliance.
- Electronic Signatures: Electronic signatures and electronic recordkeeping are permitted and have the same legal effect as manual signatures and paper records, to the fullest extent allowed by law.

nodes.title: Electronic Signatures.
nodes.heading: 9.15 Electr onic Signatur es.
nodes.start_phrase: The words “signed,” “signature,” and words of like import in or related to this Plan or any other document or record to be signed in connection with or related to this Plan by the Corporation V ice President, Eligible Employee, Dependant, or any other individual shall be deemed to include electronic signatures and the keeping of records in electronic form, each of which shall be of the same legal ef fect, validity and enforceability as a manually executed signature or the use of a paper -based recordkeeping system, as the case may be, to the fullest extent permissible under applicable law .
nodes.summary:
- Governing Law: The plan is governed by New York law and applicable federal law as applied by U.S. District Courts in New York.
- ERISA Exemption: The plan is intended to be exempt from ERISA as a foreign plan maintained outside the U.S. primarily for nonresident aliens. Active membership is limited to nonresident aliens with assigned work locations outside the U.S., and permanent administrative records are to be kept outside the U.S.
- Section 409A Exemption: The plan is structured to remain fully exempt from IRC Section 409A. No U.S. Person may receive any benefit enhancement based on compensation or service while a U.S. Person. Interest credits may apply only to amounts derived from non-U.S.-Person service. Benefit enhancements for a calendar year are determined after confirming non-U.S.-Person status; in the benefit commencement year, the Vice President may authorize an enhancement upon satisfactory determination of non-U.S.-Person status, otherwise benefits commence without it and are adjusted the following year if appropriate. Provisions are to be interpreted to preserve the exemption, with the Vice President having overriding authority to ensure compliance.
- Electronic Signatures: Electronic signatures and electronic recordkeeping are recognized as legally valid and enforceable to the fullest extent permitted by law.
- Execution: The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan, DC Program (amended and restated) is adopted December 19, 2022, effective January 1, 2022 (or as otherwise stated), signed by Ronald Schellekens (EVP and CHRO) with legal approval by Jeffrey A. Arnold (Legal Director, Employee Benefits Counsel).

structure.start_phrase:
The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PepsiCo for the
benefit of salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan.
structure.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Nonqualified, unfunded PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) for salaried employees who participate in the qualified Salaried Plan, providing “make‑up” benefits where qualified plan payouts are limited by the Internal Revenue Code, and preserving certain pre‑1989 Salaried Plan formula benefits.
- 409A focus: This document governs the Section 409A Program—benefits earned/vested after 12/31/2004 or materially modified—ensuring compliance with 409A rules, including distribution timing and form constraints and six‑month delays for Key Employees.
- Plan history: Restated in 1989; comprehensively restated effective 1/1/2005 for 409A; merged with the PBG Pension Equalization Plan effective 12/31/2011 (with PBG 409A terms preserved via a dedicated appendix); restated as of 1/1/2022 without changing 409A time/form of payment.
- Key definitions: Extensive definitions for benefit calculations and eligibility (e.g., Accrued Benefit, Actuarial Equivalent, Credited Service, Covered Compensation, Highest Average Monthly Earnings, Normal/Early/Late 409A Retirement Pension, Disability, Separation from Service, Key Employee, Qualified Joint & Survivor Annuity, Single Life Annuity, Single Lump Sum).
- Participation and service: Rules for who participates, how Service and Credited Service are measured (including Elapsed Time Service), and special service crediting situations.
- Eligibility and benefit types: 
  - Normal, Early, Late, and Disability 409A Retirement Pensions
  - 409A Vested Pension
  - Pre‑Retirement Spouse’s and Domestic Partner’s 409A pensions
  - Vesting standards, reemployment impacts, forfeiture (including for Prohibited Misconduct), and cash‑out distributions under specified limits.
- Benefit amounts and calculations:
  - Primary 409A benefit formula and a PEP Guarantee
  - Survivor benefit amounts
  - Adjustments (e.g., actuarial reductions/increases), offsets, excludable employment rules, and coordination with any pre‑409A benefits.
- Distributions:
  - Permitted forms (e.g., annuities, lump sums) and timing under 409A
  - Election procedures and survivor option rules
  - Beneficiary designations
  - Required six‑month payment delay for Key Employees after Separation from Service
  - FICA and related income tax withholding timing.
- Administration and claims:
  - Authority of plan fiduciaries/committees and facility of payment provisions
  - Detailed ERISA claims and appeals procedures, mandatory exhaustion, limitations periods, and venue restrictions
  - Cross‑references and administrative coordination with appendices.
- Miscellaneous provisions:
  - No employment guarantee
  - Anti‑assignment of benefits
  - Unfunded status
  - Company action and indemnification
  - Compliance with Sections 409A and 457A, authorized transfers, and electronic signatures.
- Amendment/termination:
  - Plan continuation, amendment procedures, termination provisions, and change‑in‑control rules.
- ERISA structure and governing law: Clarifies ERISA plan framework and applicable law.
- Appendices covering special rules and populations:
  - Transition provisions; severance window service/earnings and payment timing; international and PIRP transfers; rehired Yum Band 4+; U.K. supplementary rules; pre‑2018 delay elections; pre‑2019 domestic partner definitions; 409A makeup for certain pre‑409A benefits; rules for certain international U.S. persons; termination for participants affected by the “Tiger” transaction.
  - PBG Appendix: history/purpose, definitions, participation, benefit amount, death benefits, and distributions specific to legacy PBG participants.
  - PAC Appendix: guiding principles for Benefit Plan Committee appointments.

It outlines Articles covering: Foreword; Definitions and Construction (e.g., Accrued Benefit, Actuarial Equivalent, Key Employee, Separation from Service, Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, PEP Guarantee); Participation and Service; Requirements for Benefits (normal, early, late, disability, vested, pre‑retirement spouse’s/domestic partner’s pensions, vesting, cashout distributions, forfeiture, reemployment); Amount of Retirement Pension (benefit formulas, offsets, adjustments, excludable employment); Distribution of Benefits (forms and timing, survivor options, beneficiary designations, required delay for Key Employees, FICA and related tax payments); Administration (plan authority, claims procedures, exhaustion requirement, limitations on actions, venue restrictions); Miscellaneous (employment non-guarantee, nonalienation, unfunded status, indemnification, Section 409A/457A compliance, electronic signatures); Amendment and Termination (including change in control); ERISA Plan Structure; Applicable Law; and Signature. nodes.title: Foreword
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE I
Foreword
nodes.start_phrase:
The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PepsiCo for the
benefit of salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) provides supplemental pension benefits to salaried employees who participate in the Salaried Plan, making up benefits limited by the Internal Revenue Code and, for certain employees, providing benefits based on the pre-1989 Salaried Plan formula.

- Historical restatements: The Plan was restated in 1989 and again effective January 1, 2005 to establish the Section 409A Program covering benefits earned/vested after December 31, 2004 or materially modified thereafter.

- Merger with PBG PEP: Effective December 31, 2011, the PBG Pension Equalization Plan merged into PEP. The 409A PBG PEP Document (as of April 1, 2009, amended through January 1, 2011) remains applicable to pre-merger 409A-governed benefits, with certain administrative provisions now governed by the main 409A PepsiCo PEP document. The merger and document updates did not change the time or form of payment for 409A benefits.

- Subsequent restatements: The 409A Program Document was restated effective January 1 of 2017, 2019, 2021, and most recently 2022.

- Interplay of 409A and Pre-409A Programs: Benefits not subject to Section 409A (generally earned/vested before January 1, 2005 and not materially modified) are governed by a separate Pre-409A Program document. Together they form a single plan, but amounts are tracked separately to preserve grandfathered status and exemption from Section 409A.

- Alignment with Salaried Plan freeze: Because PEP generally makes up benefits limited under the Salaried Plan, accruals and eligibility to “grow into” enhancements are tied to the Salaried Plan. The Salaried Plan freeze effective end of day December 31, 2025 also freezes all PEP accruals at that time. Post-2025 growth into enhancements under PEP follows the Salaried Plan’s operational rules. Certain participants may have additional accrual opportunities via the PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2) or Appendix provisions.

- Definitions and construction (Article II): Introduces defined terms and interpretation rules. Examples:
  - Accrued Benefit: Pension payable at Normal Retirement Date based on Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Credited Service.
  - Actuarial Equivalent: Benefits of equal value determined using specified actuarial factors applied uniformly; annuity and inflation-protection factors are selected by the Plan Administrator and, effective January 1, 2009, are set forth in Schedule 1 (with prior factors in the Appendix). New rights/features do not automatically adopt these factors unless expressly provided.

nodes.title: Definitions and Construction
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE II
Definitions and Construction
nodes.start_phrase: This section provides definitions for certain words and phrases listed below .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Article II: Definitions and Construction for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Section 2.1 explains that defined terms (bold/underlined, initial capitals) have specific meanings throughout the Plan, including the Foreword, unless context requires otherwise.
- Defines “Accrued Benefit” as the pension payable at Normal Retirement Date per Article V, calculated using the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Credited Service as of the determination date.
- Defines “Actuarial Equivalent” as a benefit of equal value determined using specified actuarial factors, to be applied uniformly and consistently; new plan rights/features/benefits do not automatically adopt these factors unless expressly provided by amendment.
- For annuity forms (Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, optional survivor annuities, annuities with inflation protection, and period certain and life annuities), the Plan Administrator selects the actuarial factors.
- Effective January 1, 2009, the selected factors are set forth in Schedule 1 (prior factors in an Appendix), with ongoing review by the Plan Administrator.

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading: 2.1 Definitions
nodes.start_phrase: This section provides definitions for certain words and phrases listed below .
nodes.summary:
- Article II sets out defined terms and interpretation rules for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, establishing how capitalized terms are used across the Plan and cross-referencing the Salaried Plan where applicable.
- Actuarial Equivalent rules:
  - Plan Administrator discretion to set and amend actuarial factors for all forms of payment (annuities and lump sums), applied uniformly and potentially retroactively to accrued benefits.
  - Schedule 1 specifies mortality tables and interest rates: GAR 94/5% for 1/1/2009–12/31/2018; from 1/1/2019, Salaried Plan’s 2019 mortality table with 5% (most forms), 4.2% (5% inflation protection), 4.6% (7% inflation protection).
  - “Not-less-than” protection aligns with 2019 Salaried Plan Factors for annuity starting dates on/after 1/1/2019.
  - Lump-sum equivalents use the Salaried Plan’s current lump-sum factors (excluding transition factors); other adjustments follow Salaried Plan factors.
- Core benefit forms and timing:
  - Definitions for Pension (distinguishing 409A vs Pre-409A portions), Annuity, Single Life Annuity, Qualified Joint & Survivor Annuity, Single Lump Sum.
  - Retirement Pension types: Normal, Early (409A), Late (409A), Disability, and Vested; related ages/dates: Normal Retirement Age (65 or later when 5 years Elapsed Time Service), Normal/Late Retirement Dates, Annuity Starting Date (with reemployment handling).
- Eligibility, employment, and service:
  - Participant, Employee/Employer (per Salaried Plan), Company and PepsiCo Organization (Code §414 controlled group).
  - Service constructs: Service, Credited Service, Elapsed Time Service (illustrated), Separation from Service under 409A (20% service threshold), leave-of-absence rules (6 months or protected period; 29 months for qualifying medical leaves), board service not counted toward separation.
- Spouse/domestic partner definitions:
  - Eligible Spouse (federal-law spouse; opposite-sex requirement only pre‑9/16/2013).
  - Eligible Domestic Partner (effective 1/1/2019 for active/authorized leave participants): civil union, health-benefit enrollment, or other written criteria; cannot have both spouse and domestic partner; only one partner at a time; “applicable date” is earlier of annuity start or death. Pre‑2019 rules in Appendix.
  - Pre-Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s Pensions defined (including 409A portions).
- Earnings and Social Security measures:
  - Highest Average Monthly Earnings (Salaried Plan definition without 401(a)(17) cap) with special projection for severance-related leave earnings paid after separation.
  - Covered Compensation (per Salaried Plan), Primary Social Security Amount (assumptions for retirement/vested; actual initial disability benefit for disability; excludes spousal/dependent and post-separation changes), Taxable Wage Base.
- Key Employee (409A specified employee) identification:
  - Based on Code §416(i) officer/owner thresholds; annual determination each Dec 31 effective for 12 months starting April 1.
  - Administrative convenience: all Leadership Group 6+ also treated as Key Employees (subject to 200-person cap); transitional rules 2010–2018 across PepsiCo/PBG/PAS business classifications; special combination method for 2/26/2010–3/31/2010. Intended to comply with 409A specified employee rules.
- Governance and administration:
  - Plan, 409A Program vs Pre-409A Program; Plan Year; ERISA and Code references; Section 409A.
  - PepsiCo Administration Committee (PAC) as Plan Administrator: Chair is SVP Total Rewards (or functional successor), appoints four other experienced members per guiding principles; semiannual activity reporting to senior U.S.-based executives.
  - FICA Amount and Cashout Limit defined.
- Prohibited Misconduct:
  - Non-compete with “Covered Products,” employee non-solicitation, confidentiality breaches, acts contrary to company interests (e.g., Code of Conduct violations, insider trading), and fraud.
  - Carve-outs for lawful whistleblowing and Defend Trade Secrets Act immunity; broad “Participation” definition and expansive “Covered Products” list (beverages, snacks, cereals, pasta/rice, juices, related categories, and in-development products).
- Construction/interpretation rules:
  - Gender/number usage, “hereof/hereunder” refer to entire Plan, and “including” is non-limiting.
- Cross-references:
  - Frequent reliance on Salaried Plan provisions (definitions, factors) and Appendices for prior actuarial factors and pre‑2019 domestic partner rules.

nodes.title: Construction
nodes.heading: 2.2 Construction
nodes.start_phrase: The terms of the Plan shall be construed in accordance with this section.
nodes.summary:
- Defines key terms: “Taxable Wage Base” as the Social Security contribution and benefit base for the Plan Year; “Vested Pension” and its components—the “409A Vested Pension” (from the 409A Program) and the “Pre-409A Vested Pension” (from the Pre-409A Program).
- Clarifies cross-border applicability: references to U.S. governmental programs can include comparable foreign programs if the Plan Administrator deems the computations administratively feasible.
- Sets interpretive rules: gender and number are interchangeable as context requires; “hereof/hereunder” refer to the entire Plan; “including” means “including without limitation”; and provides a detailed hierarchy for articles/sections/subsections and how intra-document references should be read.
- Outlines participation: an employee is a Participant during periods when they would be currently entitled to a pension if employment ended, or would be except for the vesting requirement in Section 4.7; eligibility can later cease and is subject to all exclusions in the Salaried Plan.
- Describes service crediting for benefits: a Participant’s pension or pre-retirement spouse/domestic partner pension is based on Service determined under Part B, Article III of the Salaried Plan, with an exception for certain inbound transferees (“inpats”) so that their pre-transfer service is not disregarded (as otherwise might occur under the Salaried Plan).

nodes.title: Participation and Service
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE III
Participation and Service
nodes.start_phrase: An Employee shall be a Participant in the Plan during the period:
nodes.summary:
- Defines when an employee becomes a Participant: during any period they would be currently entitled to a Pension if employment ended, or would be entitled but for the vesting requirement in Section 4.7.
- Clarifies participation can cease later if eligibility changes, and all exclusions from eligibility under the Salaried Plan apply in determining eligibility here.
- States that pension entitlement—and, if the Participant dies before benefits start, entitlement to a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension—is determined under Article IV based on the Participant’s period of Service.
- Establishes that a Participant’s Service is determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan, with an exception for certain inbound expatriates (“inpats”).
- For inpats transferring to the U.S., any Salaried Plan provision that would disregard their pre-transfer Service for certain purposes will not apply under this Plan.

nodes.title: Participation
nodes.heading: 3.1 Participation
nodes.start_phrase: An Employee shall be a Participant in the Plan during the period:
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article III (Participation and Service) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Participation (Sec. 3.1): An employee is a Participant during any period when:
  - They would be currently entitled to a pension if employment ended at that time, or
  - They would be so entitled except for the vesting requirement in Section 4.7.
  - Participation can later cease if entitlement changes; eligibility is subject to all exclusions under the Salaried Plan.
- Service (Sec. 3.2): Entitlement to a pension or, if death occurs before benefit commencement, a pre‑retirement spouse’s or domestic partner’s pension is determined under Article IV based on Service.
  - A participant’s period of Service is generally determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Exception for “inpats”: A Salaried Plan rule that would disregard certain pre‑transfer Service for employees who transfer to the U.S. shall not apply (pre‑transfer Service is not disregarded for this Plan).

nodes.title: Service
nodes.heading: 3.2 Service
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant’ s entitlement to a Pension or , in the event the Participant dies before commencing a benefit hereunder , either a Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension for his Eligible Spouse or a Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension for his Eligible Domestic Partner , shall be determined under Article IV based upon his period of Service.
nodes.summary:
- Defines who is a Participant: an employee is a Participant during any period when they would be currently entitled to a pension if employment ended, or would be except for the vesting requirement (Section 4.7). Participation can cease if eligibility later changes, and all eligibility exclusions from the Salaried Plan apply.
- Service rules for benefit entitlement: eligibility for a Pension or, if the Participant dies before starting benefits, a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension is determined under Article IV based on Service, with Service generally determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
- Special Service provisions:
  - Inpats: rules that disregard pre-transfer Service for employees transferring to the U.S. do not apply to this Plan before January 1, 2015, unless applying them earlier is needed to avoid duplicating benefits.
  - Leaves of absence tied to a company severance program/agreement: if such leave would extend Service beyond the Separation from Service date, the Plan Administrator may project the Participant’s 409A Pension at separation by including that Service.
- Credited Service for benefit amounts: the amount of a Pension and any pre-retirement spouse/domestic partner benefit is based on Credited Service as determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
- Special Credited Service provisions:
  - Inpats: rules in Section 3.5 of Part B that disregard pre-transfer Credited Service do not apply to inpats who transferred to the U.S. before October 1, 2014, unless earlier application avoids duplicating benefits under the Salaried Plan.
  - Leaves of absence related to severance: similar projection authority at separation to include Credited Service extending beyond the Separation from Service date.

nodes.title: Credited Service
nodes.heading: 3.3 Credited Service
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to the next two sentences, the amount of a Participant’ s Pension, Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension shall be based upon the Participant’ s period of Credited Service, as determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and context: Excerpt from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program outlining how service is credited and eligibility for various pension benefits, including survivor benefits.
- Service and Credited Service:
  - Service used to determine the 409A Pension generally follows Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Leaves of absence tied to company severance programs: the Plan Administrator may project service/credited service beyond the Separation from Service date to calculate the 409A Pension.
  - Anti-duplication: certain provisions may apply earlier than January 1, 2015 if needed to avoid duplicating benefits with the Salaried Plan.
  - Inpats: the Salaried Plan rule that disregarded some pre-transfer credited service does not apply here for inpats who transferred to the U.S. before October 1, 2014, unless needed to prevent benefit duplication.
- Article IV – Requirements for Benefits:
  - Eligibility for pensions and for survivor benefits (Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner), with amounts determined under Article V.
  - Normal 409A Retirement Pension: available upon Separation from Service after reaching Normal Retirement Age.
  - Early 409A Retirement Pension: available upon Separation prior to Normal Retirement Age if at least age 55 with 10+ years of Elapsed Time Service.
  - 409A Vested Pension: available if vested under Section 4.7 and Separation occurs before eligibility for Normal or Early 409A pensions; no benefit if vesting is not met.
  - Late 409A Retirement Pension: no payments while working past Normal Retirement Age; payments begin at Late Retirement Date and are determined per Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried Plan.

nodes.title: Requirements for Benefits
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE IV
Requirements for Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant shall be eligible to receive a Pension and a surviving Eligible Spouse or surviving Eligible Domestic Partner , as applicable, shall be eligible for certain survivor benefits as provided in this Article.
nodes.summary:
- Article IV sets eligibility requirements for pensions and certain survivor benefits under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program; benefit amounts are determined under Article V.
- Survivors: A surviving Eligible Spouse or surviving Eligible Domestic Partner may qualify for specified survivor benefits as outlined in this Article.
- Normal 409A Retirement Pension: Available upon Separation from Service after attaining Normal Retirement Age.
- Early 409A Retirement Pension: Available upon Separation from Service before Normal Retirement Age, provided the Participant is at least age 55 and has at least 10 years of Elapsed Time Service.
- 409A Vested Pension: Available to Participants vested under Section 4.7 who Separate from Service before qualifying for Normal or Early 409A Retirement Pension; those who terminate before meeting the vesting requirement in Section 4.7 are not eligible for any Pension under the Plan.
- Late 409A Retirement Pension: For Participants who continue working past Normal Retirement Age without a Separation from Service; no Pension is payable until the Late Retirement Date, after which the benefit is determined per Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried Plan (with certain exceptions, text partially truncated).

nodes.heading:
ARTICLE IV
Requirements for Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant shall be eligible to receive a Pension and a surviving Eligible Spouse or surviving Eligible Domestic Partner , as applicable, shall be eligible for certain survivor benefits as provided in this Article.
nodes.summary:

nodes.title: Normal 409A Retirement Pension
nodes.heading: 4.1 Normal 409A Retirement Pension
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant shall be eligible for a Normal 409A Retirement Pension if he Separates from Service after attaining Normal Retirement Age.
nodes.summary:
- Article IV outlines eligibility requirements for pension benefits and certain survivor benefits under the plan.
- Surviving Eligible Spouses and Eligible Domestic Partners may receive survivor benefits as provided in this Article; benefit amounts are determined under Article V.
- Normal 409A Retirement Pension: available upon Separation from Service after reaching Normal Retirement Age.
- Early 409A Retirement Pension: available upon Separation from Service before Normal Retirement Age, provided the participant is at least age 55 and has at least 10 years of Elapsed Time Service.
- 409A Vested Pension: available to participants vested under Section 4.7 who separate before qualifying for Normal or Early 409A Retirement; participants not meeting the vesting requirement are ineligible for any pension under the plan.
- Late 409A Retirement Pension: for participants who continue working past Normal Retirement Age; payments begin at the Late Retirement Date and are determined per Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried Plan (with certain exceptions noted but truncated in the excerpt).
- The section relies on defined terms (e.g., Separation from Service, Normal Retirement Age, Elapsed Time Service) and cross-references Article V and Section 4.7 for calculations and vesting.

nodes.title: Early 409A Retirement Pension
nodes.heading: 4.2 Early 409A Retirement Pension
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant shall be eligible for an Early 409A Retirement Pension if he Separates from Service prior to attaining Normal Retirement Age but after attaining at least age 55 and completing 10 or more years of Elapsed T ime Service.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines Article IV of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, specifying eligibility requirements for benefits. It states that participants and, where applicable, surviving eligible spouses or domestic partners may receive benefits, with amounts determined under Article V. It defines four pension eligibility categories tied to separation from service and age/service criteria:
- Normal 409A Retirement Pension: available upon separation after reaching Normal Retirement Age.
- Early 409A Retirement Pension: available upon separation before Normal Retirement Age but after age 55 with at least 10 years of Elapsed Time Service.
- 409A Vested Pension: available to participants vested under Section 4.7 who separate before qualifying for Normal or Early retirement; those not meeting vesting under Section 4.7 are ineligible for any pension.
- Late 409A Retirement Pension: for participants who continue working past Normal Retirement Age; no payments begin until the Late Retirement Date, with benefit determination referencing Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried Plan (with certain exceptions).

nodes.title: 409A Vested Pension
nodes.heading: 4.3 409A V ested Pension
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant who is vested under Section 4.7 shall be eligible to receive a 409A V ested Pension if he Separates from Service before he is eligible for a Normal 409A Retirement Pension or an Early 409A Retirement Pension.
nodes.summary:
- Article IV sets out eligibility requirements for pensions and certain survivor benefits under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Surviving Eligible Spouses or Eligible Domestic Partners may receive survivor benefits; benefit amounts are determined under Article V.
- 4.1 Normal 409A Retirement Pension: Available if a participant Separates from Service after reaching Normal Retirement Age.
- 4.2 Early 409A Retirement Pension: Available if a participant Separates from Service before Normal Retirement Age, after reaching at least age 55 and completing 10 or more years of Elapsed Time Service.
- 4.3 409A Vested Pension: Available to participants vested under Section 4.7 who Separate from Service before qualifying for Normal or Early 409A Retirement Pensions; participants who terminate employment before meeting the vesting requirement are not eligible for any pension under the plan.
- 4.4 Late 409A Retirement Pension: For participants who continue working past Normal Retirement Age without a Separation from Service; pension begins at the Late Retirement Date and is determined in accordance with Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried Plan (with certain exclusions noted).

nodes.title: Late 409A Retirement Pension
nodes.heading: 4.4 Late 409A Retirement Pension
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant who continues without a Separation from Service after his Normal Retirement Age shall not receive a Pension until his Late Retirement Date.
nodes.summary:
- Article IV outlines eligibility requirements for pensions and certain survivor benefits under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, with benefit amounts determined under Article V.
- Normal 409A Retirement Pension: Payable when a participant Separates from Service after reaching Normal Retirement Age.
- Early 409A Retirement Pension: Available upon Separation from Service after age 55 with at least 10 years of Elapsed Time Service but before Normal Retirement Age.
- 409A Vested Pension: Available to participants vested under Section 4.7 who separate before qualifying for Normal or Early 409A Retirement; those not vested under Section 4.7 are ineligible for any pension.
- Late 409A Retirement Pension: For participants who continue working past Normal Retirement Age; benefits begin at the Late Retirement Date and are determined per Part B, Section 4.4 of the Salaried Plan, without certain ERISA suspension notice or specific plan adjustments.
- 409A Disability Pension: Available if the participant meets disability criteria under Part B of the Salaried Plan; composed of (1) Pre-Separation Accruals (service up to Separation) and, if applicable, (2) Post-LTD Accruals (service credited after Separation due to disability) until the earliest of age 65, commencement under the Salaried Plan, or recovery.
- Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension: Payable if the participant dies before the Annuity Starting Date; begins the first day of the month following the later of the participant’s death or when the participant would have turned 55, and continues for the Eligible Spouse’s lifetime (subject to Section 4.9). The subsection addressing Active, Disabled, and Retired Employees begins but is truncated.

nodes.title: 409A Disability Pension
nodes.heading: 4.5 409A Disability Pension
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant shall be eligible for a 409A Disability Pension if he meets the requirements for a Disability Pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan.
nodes.summary:
- References compliance with ERISA section 203(a)(3)(B) regarding notice of suspension of benefits and potential adjustments under Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
- Section 4.5 outlines the 409A Disability Pension:
  - Eligibility aligns with the Disability Pension rules under Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Benefit is split into:
    - Pre-Separation Accruals: benefits based on Credited Service up to the Separation from Service date.
    - Post-LTD Accruals: benefits for Credited Service after Separation related to disability, accruing until the earliest of age 65, benefit commencement under Part B, or recovery from disability.
- Section 4.6 details the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension:
  - Payable only if the Participant dies before the Annuity Starting Date.
  - Commences the first day of the month after the later of the Participant’s death or the date the Participant attains/would have attained age 55.
  - Continues monthly for the life of the Eligible Spouse, subject to Section 4.9.
  - Applies to active, disabled, and retired employees (subsection (a) introduction).

nodes.title: Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension
nodes.heading: 4.6 Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension
nodes.start_phrase: A Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension is payable under this section only in the event the Participant dies prior to his Annuity Starting Date.
nodes.summary:
- Mentions compliance with ERISA section 203(a)(3)(B) (notice of suspension of benefits) and potential adjustments under Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
- Section 4.5 (409A Disability Pension): 
  - Eligibility mirrors the Disability Pension rules under Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Benefit consists of two components:
    - Pre-Separation Accruals: benefits tied to Credited Service through the Participant’s Separation from Service.
    - Post-LTD Accruals: benefits tied to Credited Service after Separation due to disability, accruing until the earliest of age 65, commencement of Part B benefits, or recovery from disability.
- Section 4.6 (Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension):
  - Payable only if the Participant dies before his Annuity Starting Date.
  - Commences the first day of the month following the later of the Participant’s death or when the Participant would have turned age 55.
  - Continues monthly for the life of the Eligible Spouse, subject to Section 4.9.
  - For spouses of active, disabled, or retired employees: payable if entitled under Part B; amount determined per Section 5.3 after applying Section 5.6.
  - For spouses of vested terminated employees: payable if entitled under Part B; amount determined per Section 5.3 after applying Section 5.6. If Pre-Retirement Spouse’s coverage is in effect, the Participant’s pension under Section 5.2(b) is reduced by an annual, age-based charge for each year of coverage (pro rata for partial years; no reduction within 90 days after termination): 
    - Up to age 35: 0%
    - Ages 35–39: 0.075%
    - Ages 40–44: 0.1%
    - Ages 45–49: 0.175%
    - Ages 50–54: 0.3%
    - Ages 55–59: 0.5%
    - Ages 60–64: 0.5%
- Document is part of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

nodes.title: Vesting
nodes.heading: 4.7 Vesting
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to Section 8.7 (Section 457A), a Participant shall be fully vested in, and have a nonforfeitable right to, his Accrued Benefit at the time he becomes fully vested in his accrued benefit under Part B of the Salaried Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Vesting: Participants become fully vested in their Accrued Benefit under the 409A Program when they are fully vested in their accrued benefit under Part B of the Salaried Plan, subject to Section 8.7 (Section 457A).
- Time of Payment: 409A Pension distributions begin at the time specified in Section 6.1 (subject to Section 6.6). Any interest attributable to payment delays under Salaried Plan Section 3.1(e) accrues entirely under the 409A Program and is paid at the same time and in the same form as the 409A Pension. Interest on delayed Pre‑409A Pension amounts is limited to what can be paid under 409A rules. No interest is paid for delays caused by the participant or if prohibited by an IRS 409A correction program.
- Cashout Distributions (small benefits): Notwithstanding other payment forms, special rules apply to small annuity benefits. If, at the Annuity Starting Date, the actuarial equivalent lump-sum value of a participant’s 409A Pension is at or below the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator will distribute a cashout (details continue beyond the excerpt).
- Document context: These provisions are part of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, coordinating with the Salaried Plan and ensuring compliance with Internal Revenue Code sections 409A and 457A.

nodes.title: Time of Payment
nodes.heading: 4.8 Time of Payment
nodes.start_phrase: The distribution of a Participant’ s 409A Pension shall commence as of the time specified in Section 6.1, subject to Section 6.6.
nodes.summary:
- Vesting: Participants become fully vested in their Accrued Benefit under the 409A Program when they are fully vested in their accrued benefit under Part B of the Salaried Plan, subject to Section 8.7 (relating to Section 457A).
- Time of payment: 409A Pension distributions commence as specified in Section 6.1, subject to Section 6.6.
- Interest on delayed payments: Any interest attributable to a delay in payment under Part A, Section 3.1(e) of the Salaried Plan accrues entirely under the 409A Program and is paid at the same time and in the same form as the 409A Pension.
- Limits on interest: Interest adjustments for delayed payment of the Pre-409A Pension are restricted to amounts and timing permitted under Section 409A; no interest is payable if the delay is caused by the participant or if interest is barred by an IRS Section 409A correction program. These rules override contrary Salaried Plan provisions, including Part A, Section 3.1(e).
- Cashout distributions (small benefits): Despite other form-of-payment options in Article VI, small annuity benefits are subject to cashout rules; if the actuarial lump-sum value of a participant’s 409A Pension at the Annuity Starting Date does not exceed the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator will distribute a cashout (section continues with details).

nodes.title: Cashout Distributions
nodes.heading: 4.9 Cashout Distributions
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding the availability or applicability of a dif ferent form of payment under Article VI, the following rules shall apply in the case of certain small benefit Annuity payments:
nodes.summary:
- Section 4.7 (Vesting): A participant becomes fully vested in the 409A Accrued Benefit when fully vested in the corresponding accrued benefit under Part B of the Salaried Plan, subject to Section 8.7 (Section 457A).
- Section 4.8 (Time of Payment): 409A Pension payments begin per Section 6.1, subject to any six-month delay in Section 6.6. Any interest due to delayed payment under Salaried Plan Part A, Section 3.1(e), accrues entirely under the 409A Program and is paid with the 409A Pension, only as permitted under Code Section 409A. No interest is paid for delays caused by the participant or prohibited by IRS correction programs.
- Section 4.9 (Cashout Distributions for small benefits):
  - Participant’s 409A Pension: If the actuarial lump sum value at the Annuity Starting Date is at or below the Cashout Limit (or $15,000 for Annuity Starting Dates before December 1, 2012), it is paid as a lump sum.
  - Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension: Same small-benefit cashout rule (Cashout Limit, or $15,000 before December 1, 2012).
  - Special discretionary cashouts of 409A Vested Pensions: The Plan Administrator may cash out in a lump sum (i) on December 1, 2012, or (ii) on the first day of a month in 2013 or later years, if the benefit has not started, the lump sum value is at or below the Cashout Limit, and calculation/distribution is practicable; selections must be documented in writing by specified deadlines.
  - Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension: Lump sum cashout if the actuarial value is at or below the Cashout Limit.
  - Exception effective January 1, 2018: No cashout if the participant is eligible for a “PEP Kicker” or “Qualified Kicker” under a “Severance Program” (as defined in Appendix Article E).
  - Compliance provisions: Cashouts are intended as “limited cashouts” under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(j)(4)(v); the participant’s entire “accountable benefit” across all nonaccount balance 409A plans must be considered and fully cashed out; any required six-month delay still applies; no direct or indirect election is permitted by the participant, spouse, or domestic partner.
- Section 4.10 (Reemployment): If a participant already receiving an annuity under Section 6.1(b) is reemployed and re-eligible for Part B of the Salaried Plan, the existing 409A Pension continues in the same form; any additional 409A benefit accrued after reemployment is payable based on the subsequent Separation from Service.
- Section 4.11 (Forfeiture of Benefits): For Post-2008 Accruals, if the participant engages in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of Separation from Service, all such accruals are forfeited (including amounts previously paid), and the 409A Pension is adjusted with recovery of prior payments.
- Section 4.12 (Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension): Payable only if the participant dies before the Annuity Starting Date under either program; begins the first of the month following the later of the participant’s death or when the participant would have turned age 55, and is subject to the cashout rules in Section 4.9.

nodes.title: Reemployment of Certain Participants
nodes.heading: 4.10 Reemployment of Certain Participants
nodes.start_phrase: In the case of a current or former Participant who is receiving his Pension as an Annuity under Section 6.1(b), and who is reemployed and is eligible to re-participate in Part B of the Salaried Plan after his Annuity Starting Date, payment of his 409A Pension will continue to be paid in the same form as it was paid prior to his reemployment.
nodes.summary:
- Covers portions of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program addressing payment rules, forfeiture, and survivor benefits.
- Cash-out: Notes that a Participant’s 409A Pension or a Pre-Retirement Eligible Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension may be cashed out under a referenced section.
- Reemployment (Section 4.10): If a Participant already receiving an annuity under Section 6.1(b) is rehired and eligible to re-participate in Part B of the Salaried Plan after the annuity start date, payments continue in the same form; any additional 409A Pension earned during reemployment is payable based on the subsequent Separation from Service.
- Forfeiture (Section 4.11): For Post-2008 Accruals, if the Plan Administrator determines the Participant engaged in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of Separation from Service, all such accruals are forfeited (whether already paid, being paid, or payable), the 409A Pension is adjusted accordingly, and previously paid Post-2008 amounts are recoverable.
- Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension (Section 4.12): Payable only if the Participant dies before the annuity starting date under either the 409A or Pre-409A Program; benefit begins on the first day of the month following the later of the Participant’s death or the date the Participant reaches (or would have reached) age 55, subject to Section 4.9.

nodes.title: Forfeiture of Benefits
nodes.heading: 4.11 Forfeiture of Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: Effective beginning with benefits accrued after December 31, 2008 (“Post-2008 Accruals”), and notwithstanding any other provision of this Plan to the contrary , if the Plan Administrator determines that a Participant has engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time prior to the second anniversary of his or her Separation from Service, the Participant shall forfeit all Post-2008 Accruals (whether paid previously , being paid currently or payable in the future), and his or her 409A Pension shall be adjusted to reflect such forfeiture and previously paid Post-2008 Accruals shall be recovered.
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines three main provisions of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program: (1) Reemployment rules for participants already receiving an annuity: if a participant is reemployed and eligible to re-participate in Part B of the Salaried Plan after their annuity start date, their 409A Pension continues in the same payment form, and any additional 409A Pension earned during reemployment is payable based on the subsequent separation from service. (2) Forfeiture due to Prohibited Misconduct: for benefits accrued after December 31, 2008, if the Plan Administrator determines the participant engaged in Prohibited Misconduct any time before the second anniversary of separation, all such post‑2008 accruals are forfeited, the 409A Pension is adjusted, and amounts previously paid are subject to recovery. (3) Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension: payable only if the participant dies before their annuity starting date under either the 409A or Pre‑409A program; payments begin on the first day of the month following the later of the participant’s death or the date the participant would have reached age 55, subject to the plan’s cash‑out and related provisions referenced in Section 4.9.

nodes.title: Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension
nodes.heading: 4.12 Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s 409A Pension
nodes.start_phrase: A Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s 409A Pension is payable under this section only in the event the Participant dies prior to his Annuity Starting Date under either the 409A Program or the Pre-409A Program.
nodes.summary:
- Reemployment rules: If a participant already receiving a 409A annuity is reemployed and re-eligible for Part B of the Salaried Plan, payments continue in the same form during reemployment; any additional 409A benefit earned is payable after the subsequent separation from service.
- Forfeiture for misconduct: Post-2008 Accruals are forfeited if the Plan Administrator determines the participant engaged in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of separation; previously paid Post-2008 amounts are recoverable and the 409A Pension is adjusted accordingly.
- Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension:
  - Payable only if the participant dies before the Annuity Starting Date under the 409A or Pre-409A program.
  - Commences the first day of the month after the later of the participant’s death or the date the participant would have turned 55, and continues for the life of the Eligible Domestic Partner, subject to any cashout rules in Section 4.9.
  - For active, disabled, and retired employees: Amount determined under Section 5.8, after applying Section 5.6, mirroring Part B survivor provisions.
  - For vested terminated employees: Same determination rules; if this coverage is elected/in effect, the participant’s pension under Section 5.2(b) is reduced by an annual charge based on attained age (with pro rata for partial years), and no reduction for coverage in the 180 days following termination. The schedule lists increasing annual percentage charges by age bands.
- Article V – Amount of Retirement Pension:
  - When payable, the 409A Pension is determined under Section 5.1 or 5.3, subject to plan freeze (Article I) and adjustments in Sections 4.6(b) and 5.4.
  - Section 5.1 formula (subject to Section 8.7 on Section 457A): 409A Pension = Total Pension − Salaried Plan Pension − Pre-409A Pension (not below zero).
  - Basis of determination includes early/late commencement reductions at the 409A Annuity Starting Date, relative value of payment forms, actuarial equivalence, and coordination to avoid duplication and reflect timing/form of any prior payments.
- Cross-references note that certain pensions (including Pre-Retirement Eligible Domestic Partner’s benefits) may be cashed out under Section 4.9.

nodes.title: Amount of Retirement Pension
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE V
Amount of Retirement Pension
nodes.start_phrase: When a 409A Pension becomes payable to or on behalf of a Participant under this Plan, the amount of such 409A Pension shall be determined under Section 5.1 or 5.3 (whichever is applicable), subject to any adjustments required under Sections 4.6(b) and 5.4 and subject to the freeze of the Plan described in Article I.
nodes.summary:
- Article V sets out how the Amount of Retirement Pension (a 409A Pension) is determined when payable under the plan.
- The pension amount is determined under Section 5.1 or 5.3, subject to adjustments in Sections 4.6(b) and 5.4 and the plan freeze in Article I.
- Section 5.1 (subject to Section 8.7/Section 457A) defines the Participant’s 409A Pension as:
  - Total Pension
  - minus Salaried Plan Pension
  - minus Pre-409A Pension
  - with the result not less than zero.
- The calculation basis must:
  - Apply early/late commencement reductions as of the Annuity Starting Date.
  - Reflect, when applicable and customary, the relative value of different payment forms.
  - Convert offsets in (a)(2) and (3) to their Actuarial Equivalent, as appropriate and customary.
  - Follow Plan Administrator–authorized rules that consider the time and form of any prior payments and eliminate duplication of benefits.
- The text references defined terms and additional calculation details in subsections not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Participant’s 409A Pension
nodes.heading: 5.1 Participant’ s 409A Pension
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to Section 8.7 (Section 457A), a Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be determined as follows –
nodes.summary:
- Article V sets how a 409A Retirement Pension amount is determined when payable, referencing Sections 5.1 or 5.3, with adjustments under Sections 4.6(b) and 5.4, and subject to the plan freeze in Article I.
- Section 5.1 defines a Participant’s 409A Pension (subject to Section 8.7/Section 457A) as: Total Pension minus Salaried Plan Pension minus Pre-409A Pension, not below zero.
- The calculation basis must: apply early/late commencement factors as of the Annuity Starting Date; reflect the relative value of different payment forms; make actuarial-equivalent adjustments; follow Plan Administrator rules to account for timing/form of prior payments and prevent benefit duplication.
- For Annuity Starting Dates after December 31, 2018, the 409A Pension can include a makeup where the Participant’s Pre-409A Pension used harsher early reduction factors than the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors (including portions from the PEP Guarantee).
- Key definitions for Section 5.1:
  - Total Pension: the greater of (i) the Part B Salaried Plan pension ignoring IRC 401(a)(17) and 415 limits and ignoring the deferral adjustment in Part B Section 5.7(d), or (ii) the PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2); comparisons reflect relative value of payment forms.
  - Salaried Plan Pension: the pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Pre-409A Pension: the amount determined under Section 5.6.
- Section 5.2 (PEP Guarantee):
  - Eligibility: applies only to Participants with at least $75,000 in 1988 pensionable earnings from an Employer; defines “1988 pensionable earnings” per the 1988 Salaried Plan and excludes pay from non-Employer periods.
  - Benefit determination: calculated under stated formulas with special rules; for those actively employed in a classification eligible for the Salaried Plan before July 1, 1975, the benefit is the greater of specified amounts (details continue beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: PEP Guarantee
nodes.heading: 5.2 PEP Guarantee
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant who is eligible under subsection (a) below shall be entitled to a PEP Guarantee benefit determined under subsection (b) below .
nodes.summary:
- Defines key terms used in benefit calculations: “Salaried Plan Pension” (as determined under Part B of the Salaried Plan) and “Pre-409A Pension” (as determined under Section 5.6).
- Establishes the PEP Guarantee:
  - Eligibility: Applies only to Participants with at least $75,000 in 1988 pensionable earnings from an Employer (as defined under the 1988 Salaried Plan rules; excludes pay from entities when not an Employer).
  - Benefit determination: Uses specified formulas, with special rules.
    - Formula A: 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME) for first 10 years of Credited Service + 1% of HAME for each additional year, minus 1-2/3% of Primary Social Security Amount times years of Credited Service up to 30. For a Vested Pension, first project service to Normal Retirement Age using HAME and Social Security at separation, then prorate by actual service over projected service.
    - Formula B (for those in an eligible Salaried Plan classification before July 1, 1975): Pension is the greater of (A) 1.5% of HAME × years of Credited Service − 50% of Primary Social Security Amount, or (B) 3% of HAME × years of Credited Service up to 15 − 50% of Primary Social Security Amount. For Disability Pensions, use Credited Service per the Salaried Plan and HAME/Social Security at disability date. For Vested Pensions, a stated subparagraph does not apply.
  - Special calculation rules:
    - Automatic 50% survivor annuity for an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner with no reduction to the Participant’s annuity; if the survivor is more than 10 years younger, reduce the survivor benefit by 0.8% per full year from 11–20 years younger and an additional 0.4% per full year beyond 20.
    - Reductions for:
      - Early retirement: 3/12 of 1% (0.25%) per month before Normal Retirement Date.
      - Vested Pensions: actuarial equivalence if commencing early and specified reductions for pre-retirement spouse/domestic partner coverage.
      - Elected forms with higher survivor benefits than 50%: reduce to actuarial equivalence of the standard benefit.
      - Non-spouse/domestic partner survivor forms: reduce to the actuarial equivalent of a single life annuity.
      - Inflation-protected annuities: reduce to the actuarial equivalent of the same annuity without inflation protection.
    - Lump sum conversion: Lump sum equals the actuarial equivalent of the PEP Guarantee, reflecting survivor benefits and early retirement reductions.
    - Actuarial equivalence standard: Intended to preserve substantially the value of pre-1989 plan benefits and conform to Section 409A rules, including the Treasury regulation for subsidized joint and survivor annuities.
- Sets the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension amount:
  - Calculation: Equals the Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension minus the Salaried Plan’s Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension, further reduced (not below zero) by any portion derived from the Pre-409A Program.
  - Basis: Applies appropriate early/late commencement reductions and other actuarial equivalence adjustments as determined by the Plan Administrator, considering time and form of any prior payments.
  - Notes that definitions specific to this section apply (not shown in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Amount of Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension
nodes.heading: 5.3 Amount of Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension
nodes.start_phrase: The monthly amount of the Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension payable to a surviving Eligible Spouse under Section 4.6 shall be determined under subsection (a) below .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how a surviving Eligible Spouse’s “Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension” is calculated, coordinated with Section 409A (including the special rule for subsidized joint and survivor annuities).
- Calculation formula: Eligible Spouse’s Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension minus (i) the Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension and (ii) the portion derived from the Pre-409A Program, floored at zero.
- Requires timing and actuarial adjustments: accounts for early/late commencement and applies Actuarial Equivalence and Plan Administrator rules, including consideration of prior payments and form of payment.
- Definitions:
  - Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is the greater of (a) the Part B Salaried Plan pre-retirement spouse’s pension ignoring Code §§401(a)(17) and 415 limits and a specified actuarial adjustment, or (b) the PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension; determined as if payable at the Participant’s Normal Retirement Date, then adjusted for actual commencement timing.
  - Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension: the amount under the Salaried Plan.
  - Pre-409A Program portion: the amount under the Pre-409A Program.
- PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension (by reference to Section 5.2):
  - Normal rule: equal to the survivor annuity under a QJSA as if the Participant separated at death (or earlier actual separation), commenced the QJSA at the survivor benefit start date, and died the next day.
  - Special rule for active/disabled employees (Section 4.6(a)): minimum 25% of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee; Credited Service per Part B Section 3.3(c)(2); Highest Average Monthly Earnings, Primary Social Security Amount, and Covered Compensation measured at death; no early commencement reduction.
  - Applies principles similar to Section 5.1(b) and the last sentence of Section 5.2(b)(2).
- Certain Adjustments (Section 5.4):
  - Defines “specified plan” as the Salaried Plan or similar nonqualified plans within the PepsiCo Organization not based on participant pay deferrals.
  - Rehired participants: if reemployed after Annuity Starting Date and Salaried Plan benefits are recalculated for additional service, the PEP Pension is recalculated to the maximum extent allowed under Section 409A; PEP Guarantee is adjusted for in-service and prior distributions consistent with the Salaried Plan while accounting for this Plan and any specified plans.
  - Provides for adjustments when pensions under other specified plans are increased after PEP benefits are determined (text partially truncated).

nodes.title: Certain Adjustments
nodes.heading: 5.4 Certain Adjustments
nodes.start_phrase: Pensions determined under the foregoing sections of this Article are subject to adjustment as provided in this section.
nodes.summary:
- Sets rules for a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension: Covered Compensation measured as of the participant’s date of death; no early commencement reduction; determination of the spouse’s 409A Pension follows principles akin to Section 5.1(b) and the last sentence of Section 5.2(b)(2).
- Establishes “Certain Adjustments” to pensions, defining a “specified plan” as the Salaried Plan or a similar nonqualified plan (sponsored by a PepsiCo entity and not based on employee deferrals).
- Rehired participants: If the Salaried Plan benefit is recalculated after the Annuity Starting Date due to additional Credited Service, the PEP Pension (and PEP Guarantee) is correspondingly recalculated, accounting for in-service/prior distributions and benefits under this and specified plans, to the maximum extent permitted by Section 409A.
- Increases under other plans: If a specified plan later increases a participant’s benefit (e.g., by court order or administrator action), the PEP benefit is recalculated under Section 409A; any overpayment is subject to recovery; aims to prevent duplicative payments across this Plan and specified plans.
- No offsets violating Section 409A (effective Jan 1, 2009): Non-duplication/transfer rules from the Salaried Plan apply to Total Pension calculations only if they do not change the time or form of 409A payments; the Company intends to implement legally permissible, 409A-compliant coordination under qualifying plans to avoid prohibited changes, in which case offset limits do not apply.

nodes.title: Excludable Employment
nodes.heading: 5.5 Excludable Employment
nodes.start_phrase: An executive who has signed a written agreement with the Company pursuant to which the individual either (i) waives eligibility under the Plan (even if the individual otherwise meets the definition of Employee under the Plan), or (ii) agrees not to participate in the Plan, shall not thereafter become entitled to a benefit or to any increase in benefits in connection with such employment (whichever applies).
nodes.summary: This excerpt from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program covers three topics. First, Excludable Employment (Section 5.5) allows executives to sign written agreements waiving eligibility or agreeing not to participate in the Plan, with such waivers effective whether signed before or after eligibility/participation and applicable to agreements entered on or after January 1, 2009. Second, Pre-409A Pension (Section 5.6) defines the grandfathered portion of a participant’s pension under Treasury Regulation §1.409A-6(a)(3)(i) and (iv) and states it will be determined using principles parallel to those in Sections 5.1(b) and the last sentence of 5.2(b)(2). Third, Offsets (Section 5.7) permits the Company to reduce plan payments by amounts the participant owes the Company if the debt arose during employment, within Code Section 409A limits, and with reductions timed to when the debt would otherwise be due; it also addresses coordination where a participant has multiple 409A benefits with different payment timings.

nodes.title: Pre-409A Pension
nodes.heading: 5.6 Pre-409A Pension
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant’ s Pre-409A Pension is the portion of the Participant’ s Pension that is grandfathered under T reasury Regulation § 1.409A-6(a)(3)(i) and (iv).
nodes.summary:
- The excerpt is from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program and addresses eligibility exclusions, grandfathered benefits, and offsets.
- Section 5.5 (Excludable Employment): Executives who sign written agreements waiving eligibility or agreeing not to participate cannot later claim benefits or benefit increases from that employment. Such agreements can be executed before or after eligibility/participation, may take any effective form, and apply to agreements entered into on or after January 1, 2009.
- Section 5.6 (Pre-409A Pension): Defines the portion of a participant’s pension that is grandfathered under Treasury Regulation §1.409A-6(a)(3)(i) and (iv), with determination guided by principles referenced in Sections 5.1(b) and the last sentence of 5.2(b)(2).
- Section 5.7 (Offsets): Allows the Company to reduce plan payments by amounts the participant owes the Company if the debt arose during employment, within Code §409A limits, and with reductions timed and sized to match when the debt would have been due and collectible. It also addresses coordination when a participant has a prior 409A benefit paid earlier or under different payment terms than a subsequent 409A benefit.

nodes.title: Offsets
nodes.heading: 5.7 Offsets
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding any other provision of the Plan, the Company may reduce the amount of any payment or benefit that is or would be payable to or on behalf of a Participant by the amount of any obligation of the Participant to the Company that is or becomes due and payable, provided that (1) the obligation of the Participant to the Company was incurred during the employment relationship, (2) the reduction during any Plan Y ear may not exceed the amount allowed under Code Section 409A and (3) the reduction is made at the same time and in the same amount as the obligation otherwise would have been due and collectable from the Participant.
nodes.summary:
- Excludable Employment (Sec. 5.5): Executives who sign written agreements waiving eligibility or agreeing not to participate in the Plan are permanently barred from receiving benefits or benefit increases tied to that employment. Such agreements can be executed before or after eligibility/participation, may take any effective form, and apply to agreements entered on or after January 1, 2009.
- Pre-409A Pension (Sec. 5.6): Defines the portion of a Participant’s Pension that is grandfathered under Treasury Regulation §1.409A-6(a)(3)(i) and (iv). Its determination follows principles referenced in Sections 5.1(b) and the last sentence of 5.2(b)(2).
- Offsets (Sec. 5.7): The Company may reduce payments/benefits by amounts the Participant owes the Company if incurred during employment, within Code §409A limits, and timed to when the debt would have been collectible. Additional 409A Benefits must also be offset by any Prior 409A Benefits, with the offset calculated at the annuity starting date, reflecting early/late commencement factors, relative value of payment forms where applicable, and actuarial equivalence under Plan Administrator rules (e.g., Pre-Separation Accruals offset Post-Disability Accruals).
- Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension (Sec. 5.8): For a surviving Eligible Domestic Partner (per Sec. 4.12), the monthly benefit equals the Total Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension minus the Salaried Plan component, then further reduced (not below zero) by the portion derived from the Pre-409A Program.

nodes.title: Amount of Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension
nodes.heading: 5.8 Amount of Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension
nodes.start_phrase: The monthly amount of the Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s 409A Pension payable to a surviving Eligible Domestic Partner under Section 4.12 shall be determined under subsection (a) below .
nodes.summary:
- Offsets of additional 409A Benefits: Any additional 409A benefit is reduced by the Prior 409A Benefit as of the annuity starting date, reflecting early/late commencement factors, relative value of payment forms, and actuarial equivalence per Plan Administrator rules; example given where Pre‑Separation Accruals offset Post‑Disability Accruals.
- Pre‑Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension (Section 5.8):
  - Calculation: Equals (a) Total Pre‑Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension minus (b) the amount provided under the Salaried Plan, then minus (c) the portion derived from the Pre‑409A Program, floored at zero.
  - Determination basis: Applies early/late commencement adjustments and actuarial equivalence; Plan Administrator may adjust to reflect time/form of any prior payments.
  - Key definitions:
    - “Total” amount is the greater of: (i) the Salaried Plan benefit ignoring Code §§401(a)(17) and 415 limits and a specified actuarial adjustment, or (ii) the PEP Guarantee‑based Pre‑Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension; first compared at the Participant’s Normal Retirement Date, then adjusted for earlier/later commencement.
    - “Salaried Plan” amount and “Pre‑409A Program” amount are the respective plan‑determined benefits.
  - PEP Guarantee rules:
    - Normal rule: Benefit equals the survivor annuity under a hypothetical QJSA if the Participant separated at death (or earlier separation date), commenced the QJSA when the survivor benefit begins, and died the next day.
    - Special rule for active/disabled: Minimum of 25% of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee; Credited Service and compensation/SSA measures determined as of death; no early commencement reduction. Principles akin to Sections 5.1(b) and the last sentence of 5.2(b)(2) apply.
- Article VI — Distribution of Benefits:
  - Governs distributions of 409A Pensions and continuation to beneficiaries.
  - Pre‑Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s Pensions under the 409A Program are paid as life annuities (subject to cashout rules); Pre‑409A Pension distributions follow the Pre‑409A Program.
  - Form/timing (Section 6.1):
    - Default: 409A Retirement Pension paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month on/after the Retirement Date, subject to key employee delay.
    - Prior elections: Grandfathered payment elections made by December 31, 2007 (and at least six months before, in a prior calendar year) control form/timing of payment.

nodes.title: Distribution of Benefits
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE VI
Distribution of Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: The terms of this Article govern (i) the distribution of benefits to a Participant who becomes entitled to a 409A Pension, and (ii) the continuation of benefits (if any) to such Participant’ s beneficiary following the Participant’ s death.
nodes.summary:
- Article VI sets rules for distributing benefits under the 409A Program and for continuing benefits to a beneficiary after a Participant’s death.
- Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pensions from the 409A Program are paid as lifetime annuities to the eligible spouse/partner, subject to cashout provisions in Section 4.9.
- Distributions of any Pre-409A Pension are governed by the separate Pre-409A Program.
- Section 6.1 (Form and Timing): By default, a Participant’s 409A Retirement Pension is paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month on or after the Retirement Date, subject to a delay for Key Employees under Section 6.6.
- Prior payment elections: If a qualifying election was made by December 31, 2007, at least six months before and in a calendar year prior to the Annuity Starting Date, benefits will be paid according to that election (election options are referenced but the text is truncated).

nodes.title: Distribution of Benefits - Introduction
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE VI
Distribution of Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: The terms of this Article govern (i) the distribution of benefits to a Participant who becomes entitled to a 409A Pension, and (ii) the continuation of benefits (if any) to such Participant’ s beneficiary following the Participant’ s death.
nodes.summary:
Distribution of Benefits
The terms of this Article govern (i) the distribution of benefits to a Participant who becomes entitled to a
409A Pension, and (ii) the continuation of benefits (if any) to such Participant’ s beneficiary following the Participant’ s
death. A Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension derived from the 409A
Program shall be payable as an Annuity for the life of the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner , as applicable,
in all cases, subject to Section 4.9 (cashout distributions). The distribution of a Pre-409A Pension is governed by the
terms of the Pre-409A Program.
