nodes.title: Form and Timing of Distributions
nodes.heading: 6.1 Form and T iming of Distributions
nodes.start_phrase: Benefits under the 409A Program shall be distributed as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article VI governs how benefits under the 409A Program are distributed to participants and, if applicable, continued to beneficiaries after a participant’s death. Pre-Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s Pensions from the 409A Program are paid as life annuities (subject to cashout rules in Section 4.9). Distributions of Pre-409A Pensions follow the Pre-409A Program rules.
- 409A Retirement Pension (Section 6.1(a)):
  - Default: Single lump sum on the first day of the month coincident with or next following the Retirement Date, subject to the Key Employee delay (Section 6.6) and cashouts (Section 4.9).
  - Prior elections: If a participant made a valid payment election by December 31, 2007 and at least six months before (and in a prior calendar year to) the Annuity Starting Date, the benefit is paid per that election (annuity and/or alternative commencement date). Elections are disregarded if the participant only qualifies for a Vested Pension at Separation.
  - Annuity defaults if elected: Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity (QJSA) if married; Single Life Annuity if unmarried, unless an optional form under Section 6.2 is elected per procedures in Section 6.3(a). Marital status is determined on the Annuity Starting Date.
  - Late commencement due to an election increases the benefit for earnings using the plan’s actuarial interest rate through the payment check date.
- 409A Vested Pension (Section 6.1(b); subject to Sections 4.9 and 6.6):
  - Separation before age 55 with at least 5 years of Service: Annuity begins on the first of the month coincident with or following age 55 (Annuity Starting Date).
  - Separation at ages 55–64 with at least 5 but less than 10 years of Service: Annuity begins on the first of the month following Separation.
  - Default forms: QJSA if married; Single Life if unmarried. An unmarried participant with an Eligible Domestic Partner may elect a 50% or 75% Survivor Annuity with the partner as beneficiary (per Section 6.2). Marital/partner status measured at the Annuity Starting Date. Optional forms may be elected under Section 6.2 following Section 6.3(a) procedures.
- 409A Disability Pension (Section 6.1(c)):
  - Pre-Separation Accruals: Paid on the first day of the month following the later of age 55 or Separation; available forms mirror those for Vested or Retirement Pensions under Section 6.2 (with distinctions for married/domestic partner vs. single).
  - Post-LTD Accruals: Paid as a lump sum on the first day of the month following attainment of age 65.
- Available Forms of Payment (Section 6.2):
  - Applies to Retirement Pensions subject to a valid prior election (Section 6.1(a)(2)) and to Vested Pensions (Section 6.1(b)).
  - Retirement Pension: Participant may choose among optional forms by valid election per Section 6.3(a).
  - Vested Pension: If married on the Annuity Starting Date, the participant may elect only certain specified optional forms (paragraph (1), (2)(ii), or (2)(iii)) with the Eligible Spouse as beneficiary; if not married but with an Eligible Domestic Partner, designated optional forms are available. Further details continue beyond the excerpt.
- Cross-references: Cashout distributions (Section 4.9), election procedures (Section 6.3(a)), and Key Employee payment delay (Section 6.6).

nodes.title: Available Forms of Payment
nodes.heading: 6.2 Available Forms of Payment
nodes.start_phrase: This section sets forth the payment options available to a Participant who is entitled to a Retirement Pension under paragraph 6.1(a)(2) above or a V ested Pension under subsection 6.1(b) above.
nodes.summary:
- Defines Disability Pension payment timing under the 409A Program:
  - Pre-Separation Accruals: paid starting the first day of the month after the later of age 55 or Separation from Service; payable in the same optional forms available for Vested or Retirement Pensions (Section 6.2), with options varying by marital/domestic partner status.
  - Post-LTD Accruals: paid as a lump sum on the first day of the month following attainment of age 65.
- Specifies available forms of payment for Retirement and Vested Pensions (Section 6.2):
  - Eligibility constraints:
    - Retirement Pension: may elect any optional form per Section 6.3(a).
    - Vested Pension:
      - Married at Annuity Starting Date: may elect Single Life, 75% Survivor, or 50% Survivor with Eligible Spouse as beneficiary; no other forms.
      - Not married with Eligible Domestic Partner: may elect 75% or 50% Survivor with the partner as beneficiary; no other forms.
      - Not married and no Eligible Domestic Partner: must receive a Single Life Annuity.
    - All optional annuities are actuarially equivalent to a Single Life Annuity.
  - Optional forms:
    - Single Life Annuity: monthly payments end at death.
    - Survivor Options: reduced lifetime benefit to participant, then to beneficiary for life at:
      - 100% continuation,
      - 75% continuation,
      - 50% continuation (Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if beneficiary is Eligible Spouse).
    - Ten Years Certain and Life: reduced lifetime benefit with at least 120 monthly payments; remaining guaranteed payments go to primary (or contingent) beneficiary if the participant dies before 120 payments.
- Provides optional inflation protection for annuities:
  - 5% or 7% thresholds: benefit initially reduced; annual increases apply only if prior-year inflation exceeds the elected threshold, equal to the excess over 5% or 7%.
  - Adjustments occur each January 1 starting with the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date.
  - Inflation measured over the 12 months ending September 30, using the same methodology as Social Security COLAs in effect on the plan’s Effective Date.
  - Inflation protection carries over to survivor benefits and is irrevocable once elected.
- Outlines procedures for Annuity Starting Date elections (Section 6.3):
  - Details how to make valid elections for optional forms (subsection (a)) and special rules for multiple Annuity Starting Dates (subsection (b)).
  - An election is deemed received on the date it is postmarked or actually received by the Plan Administrator.

nodes.title: Procedures for Elections
nodes.heading: 6.3 Procedures for Elections
nodes.start_phrase: This section sets forth the procedures for making Annuity Starting Date elections ( i.e., elections under Section 6.2).
nodes.summary:
- Inflation protection options: Participants can elect 5% or 7% inflation protection. Monthly benefits are initially reduced, then increased annually if the prior year’s inflation exceeds the elected threshold, by the amount over 5% or 7%.
- Timing and measurement: Increases apply each January 1 starting with the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date. Inflation is measured over the 12 months ending September 30, using the same method as Social Security COLAs in effect on the plan’s Effective Date.
- Survivor benefits and irrevocability: Elected inflation protection carries over to survivor benefits. Elections of inflation protection are irrevocable by the participant or surviving beneficiary.
- Election procedures (Section 6.3): Defines how and when Annuity Starting Date elections are made and deemed received (postmark or actual receipt by close of business). Spousal consent is not required.
- Optional form election requirements: Must be in writing, signed, and received at least one day before the Annuity Starting Date; must specify the payment form and any beneficiary per Section 6.5. Electronic elections and affirmations may be accepted if permitted by the Plan Administrator.
- Multiple Annuity Starting Dates: Elections at an Annuity Starting Date apply to all unpaid accruals then due. For rehired participants who continue an annuity in pay status or previously received a lump sum (other than a specific cashout), a later Annuity Starting Date and elections apply only to benefits accrued after rehire; earlier accruals continue under prior elections.
- Marital status determination (effective Jan 1, 2014): Participant is presumed unmarried on the Annuity Starting Date unless the participant provides satisfactory advance notice of being married; the Plan Administrator may adopt different rules.
- Survivor options (Section 6.4): Introduces special rules for survivor options, beginning with effects of certain deaths when an optional annuity with survivor benefits has been elected (details continue beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Special Rules for Survivor Options
nodes.heading: 6.4 Special Rules for Survivor Options
nodes.start_phrase: The following special rules shall apply for the survivor options available under Section 6.2.
nodes.summary:
- Rehire and subsequent Annuity Starting Date elections: New elections after a subsequent Separation from Service apply only to benefits accrued after rehire; prior unpaid accruals continue under the original elections made at the initial Annuity Starting Date.
- Marital status determination (effective January 1, 2014): Participant is presumed unmarried on the Annuity Starting Date unless satisfactory advance notice of marriage is provided to the Plan. Notice is given with the form election or via Plan Administrator procedures. The Plan Administrator may adopt different rules.
- Special survivor option rules (Section 6.2):
  - Death timing effects: If the Participant or beneficiary dies before the Annuity Starting Date, the survivor-option election is disregarded. If the Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date but before payments actually commence, the elected survivor form applies; survivor payments start the first day of the month following death, with any back payments to the Participant’s estate.
  - 120-payment feature (Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv)): If the Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date without a surviving primary or contingent beneficiary and before 120 payments are made, remaining payments go to the Participant’s estate. If payments to a beneficiary have begun and that beneficiary dies before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
  - Age difference limits for non-spouse/partner beneficiaries: The 100% survivor option is unavailable if the beneficiary is more than 10 years younger than the Participant; the 75% survivor option is unavailable if the beneficiary is more than 19 years younger.
- Beneficiary designation requirements: Participants electing a survivor form must designate beneficiaries on the applicable election form (may name primary and contingent for Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv)). Changes/revocations are allowed until the Annuity Starting Date and are effective upon filing per Plan rules. If no valid designation exists for a survivor option, the default beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner. Participants entitled only to a Vested Pension cannot name a beneficiary; if an optional form is allowed, the beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date.
- Key Employee distribution delay (Section 409A): For Participants classified as Key Employees at Separation from Service (or other applicable determination time), 409A Retirement Pension payments begin on the earliest first day of a month at least six months after Separation from Service, or earlier upon the Participant’s death.

nodes.title: Designation of Beneficiary
nodes.heading: 6.5 Designation of Beneficiary
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant who has elected under Section 6.2 to receive all or part of his Retirement Pension in a form of payment that includes a survivor option shall designate a beneficiary who will be entitled to any amounts payable on his death.
nodes.summary:
- Beneficiary designation rules for optional forms of payment: participants must designate beneficiaries on the applicable election form; survivor option in Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv) allows naming both primary and contingent beneficiaries.
- Participants (active or former) may change or revoke beneficiary designations any time before the Annuity Starting Date, following Plan Administrator rules; designations are not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator.
- Default beneficiary provisions: if no valid designation exists and a survivor option under Section 6.2(a)(2) is elected, the beneficiary defaults to the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner.
- Limitations for Vested Pension participants: they cannot name a beneficiary; if permitted to elect an optional form under Section 6.2, the beneficiary on the Annuity Starting Date is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner.
- Required delay for Key Employees under Section 409A: if classified as a Key Employee at Separation from Service, distributions of a 409A Retirement Pension begin on the earliest first day of a month at least six months after separation, or earlier upon death.

nodes.title: Required Delay for Key Employees
nodes.heading: 6.6 Required Delay for Key Employees
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding Section 6.1 above, if a Participant is classified as a Key Employee upon his Separation from Service (or at such other time for determining Key Employee status as may apply under Section 409A), then distributions to the Participant shall commence as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Beneficiary designation rules for optional payment forms:
  - Participants choosing an optional form of payment must designate a beneficiary on the applicable election form (plan-specific or Salaried Plan form).
  - For the survivor option under Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv), both a primary and contingent beneficiary may be named.
  - Participants (active or former) may change or revoke beneficiary designations any time before their Annuity Starting Date, following Plan Administrator rules.
  - A designation is not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator.
  - If no beneficiary is properly designated and a survivor option under Section 6.2(a)(2) is elected, the default beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner.
  - Participants entitled to a Vested Pension cannot name a beneficiary; if allowed to elect an optional form under Section 6.2, the default beneficiary at the Annuity Starting Date is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner.

- Required delay for Key Employees (Section 6.6, Section 409A compliance):
  - If classified as a Key Employee at Separation from Service, distribution timing is delayed:
    - 409A Retirement Pension: begins on the earliest first of the month at least six months after Separation, or earlier upon death. Pre-2009 exception if it starts concurrently with the Salaried Plan pension per Section 6.1(b)(3)(i).
    - 409A Vested Pension: begins per Section 6.1(b), or if later, the earliest first of the month at least six months after Separation, or earlier upon death. Pre-2009 exception similar to above.
  - Interest for delayed payments: amounts delayed accrue earnings at the interest rate used for Actuarial Equivalent lump sum calculations through the date the payment check is prepared.
  - Payment mechanics: delayed amounts plus accrued interest are paid in a lump sum when distributions commence; if the Participant dies, payment to the beneficiary or estate follows Plan terms with interest through the payment date.

nodes.title: Payment of FICA and Related Income Taxes
nodes.heading: 6.7 Payment of FICA and Related Income T axes
nodes.start_phrase: As provided in subsections (a) through (c) below , a portion of a Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be paid as a single lump sum and remitted directly to the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”) in satisfaction of the Participant’ s FICA Amount and the related withholding of income tax at source on wages (imposed under Code Section 3401 or the corresponding withholding provisions of the applicable state, local or foreign tax laws as a result of the payment of the FICA Amount) and the additional withholding of income tax at source on wages that is attributable to the pyramiding of wages and taxes.
nodes.summary:
- Section 6.7 (Payment of FICA and Related Income Taxes): A portion of a Participant’s 409A Pension is paid as a single lump sum and remitted directly to the IRS to cover the Participant’s FICA tax, related income tax withholding triggered by that FICA payment, and any additional withholding due to pyramiding.
- Timing (6.7(a)): The lump sum equal to the FICA Amount and related income tax withholding is paid from the Participant’s 409A Pension and deposited with the IRS when those taxes are due; Key Employee status does not affect this timing.
- Pension Reduction (6.7(b)): The Participant’s 409A Pension is reduced by the actuarial equivalent of the lump-sum tax payment, effective as of the tax payment date; this reduction may occur after pension payments have already begun.
- No Effect on Pension Commencement (6.7(A)): The tax-related lump-sum payment does not alter the commencement date or schedule of the Participant’s (actuarially reduced) 409A Pension, including any required delay for Key Employees.
- Article VII Administration (7.1): The Plan Administrator has authority to interpret the Plan, issue regulations, maintain records, and make benefit calculations, relying on participant-provided information; its determinations are final and binding. The Company and Plan Administrator are not fiduciaries, and ERISA section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply.
- Facility of Payment (7.2): If a payee is under legal disability or otherwise incapacitated, the Plan Administrator may pay the individual, their legal representative, or apply payments for their benefit; such payments discharge the Plan’s liability.
- Claims Procedure (7.3): The Plan Administrator (or its designee) holds exclusive discretionary authority to construe and interpret the Plan (section begins in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Administration
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE VII
Administration
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the Plan Administrator , which shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as it deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Plan Administrator’s authority to administer the Plan, interpret its provisions, issue regulations, maintain records, calculate benefits, and rely on participant-provided written information (e.g., mailing address, age, marital status). The Administrator’s interpretations and determinations are final and binding.
- Clarifies that neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is a fiduciary of the Plan, and that ERISA section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply to the Plan, the Company, or the Plan Administrator.
- Provides a “Facility of Payment” rule allowing the Plan Administrator, when a payee is legally disabled or otherwise incapacitated, to pay the individual, the individual’s legal representative, or to apply payments for the individual’s benefit; such payments fully discharge the Plan’s liability for those amounts.
- Begins a “Claims Procedure” section granting the Plan Administrator (or its designee) exclusive discretionary authority to construe and interpret the Plan (section text is truncated).

nodes.title: Authority to Administer Plan
nodes.heading: 7.1 Authority to Administer Plan
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the Plan Administrator , which shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as it deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Article VII (Administration) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program outlines governance and administrative powers.
- The Plan Administrator has broad authority to administer the Plan, interpret provisions, issue regulations, maintain records, and calculate benefits, relying on participant-provided information (e.g., address, age, marital status). Its interpretations and determinations are final and binding.
- Neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is a fiduciary of the Plan, and ERISA Section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply to the Plan, including with respect to the Company and the Plan Administrator.
- Facility of Payment: If a payee is under legal disability or otherwise incapacitated, the Plan Administrator may pay the individual, their legal representative, or apply payments for their benefit; such payments fully discharge the Plan’s liability for those amounts.
- Claims Procedure: The Plan Administrator, or its designee, holds exclusive discretionary authority to construe and interpret the Plan (section text is partially truncated).

nodes.title: Facility of Payment
nodes.heading: 7.2 Facility of Payment
nodes.start_phrase: Whenever , in the Plan Administrator ’s opinion, a person entitled to receive any payment of a benefit or installment thereof hereunder is under a legal disability or is incapacitated in any way so as to be unable to manage his financial af fairs, the Plan Administrator may make payments to such person or to the legal representative of such person for his benefit, or the Plan Administrator may apply the payment for the benefit of such person in such manner as it considers advisable.
nodes.summary:
- Article VII outlines Plan administration.
- Section 7.1 (Authority to Administer): The Plan Administrator oversees the Plan, with authority to interpret provisions, issue regulations, maintain records, and calculate benefits. It may rely on participant-provided information (e.g., address, age, marital status). Its interpretations and determinations are final and binding. Neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is a fiduciary, and ERISA §406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply to them under this Plan.
- Section 7.2 (Facility of Payment): If a payee is legally disabled or otherwise incapacitated, the Plan Administrator may pay the individual, their legal representative, or apply amounts for their benefit. Such payments fully discharge the Plan’s liability for those amounts.
- Section 7.3 (Claims Procedure): The Plan Administrator, or its designee, has exclusive discretionary authority to construe and interpret the Plan (section text is truncated).

nodes.title: Claims Procedure
nodes.heading: 7.3 Claims Procedure
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator , or a party designated by the Plan Administrator , shall have the exclusive discretionary authority to construe and to interpret the Plan, to decide all questions of eligibility for benefits and to determine the amount of such benefits.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the Plan Administrator has broad, final, and binding authority to interpret the Plan, issue regulations, maintain records, calculate benefits, and rely on participant-provided information (e.g., address, age, marital status).
- States that neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is a fiduciary under the Plan, and ERISA section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply to the Plan, the Company, or the Plan Administrator.
- Provides “facility of payment” rules allowing the Plan Administrator to direct payments to or for the benefit of a person under legal disability or incapacity (including to a legal representative), with such payments fully discharging Plan liability.
- Details an expansive claims and appeals process:
  - The Plan Administrator (or its designee) has exclusive, absolute discretion to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility and benefit amounts, and consider the Company’s intent; benefits are payable only if the Administrator so decides.
  - Any review by a court is under the arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.
  - Claims must be submitted in writing (or other acceptable form); initial determinations within 90 days, extendable to 180 days with prior notice.
  - Denial notices must state reasons, cite Plan provisions, identify needed additional information, and describe review procedures and ERISA civil action rights.
  - Claimants have 60 days to request review; a full and fair review allows submission of additional relevant material, which must be considered.
  - Decisions on review within 60 days, extendable to 120 days with notice; final decisions are written, include reasons and specific Plan citations, and inform claimants of their right to free access to relevant documents.
  - Any ERISA-required special deadline extensions apply as under the Salaried Plan; judicial/arbitral review is limited to the administrative record; exhaustion of internal remedies is required; notices may be provided using DOL-approved methods.
- Clarifies that specific references to the Plan Administrator’s discretion do not imply limitations on its discretion elsewhere in the Plan.

nodes.title: Effect of Specific References
nodes.heading: 7.4 Effect of Specific References
nodes.start_phrase: Specific references in the Plan to the Plan Administrator ’s discretion shall create no inference that the Plan Administrator ’s discretion in any other respect, or in connection with any other provision, is less complete or broad.
nodes.summary:
- Sets timelines for claim appeal decisions: a final decision must be made within 60 days of receiving a review request, with a possible one-time extension of up to an additional 60 days when special circumstances exist. Claimants must be notified of any extension before the initial 60 days end, with reasons and the new decision date.
- Specifies required content of the final written decision: understandable language, specific reasons, citations to relevant Plan provisions, and notice of the claimant’s right to free access to and copies of all documents, records, and information relevant to the claim.
- Confirms that any ERISA-required special extensions applying to deadlines in the claims process also apply to this Plan to the same extent they apply under the Salaried Plan.
- Limits judicial/arbitral review to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator at the time of its decision and conditions any external review on the claimant’s full exhaustion of internal remedies (per Section 7.5).
- Allows required notices to claimants to be sent using methods approved under DOL Regulation 2520.104b-1 or other applicable guidance.
- Clarifies that specific references to the Plan Administrator’s discretion do not limit the breadth of its discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Identifies the document as part of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

nodes.title: Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court
nodes.heading: 7.5 Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’ s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court
nodes.start_phrase: Before filing any Claim (including a suit or other action) in court or in another tribunal, a Claimant must first fully exhaust all of the Claimant’ s rights under the claims procedures of Section 7.3.
nodes.summary:
- Mandatory exhaustion of the Plan’s internal claims procedures (Section 7.3) before filing any lawsuit or tribunal action; exhaustion is to be enforced as broadly as possible.
- Exhaustion is not excused unless a claimant clearly submitted a claim or properly requested documents under strict conditions (written request to and received by the Plan Administrator, ERISA entitlement, six-month response window or reasonable extension, clear assertion of ERISA rights/entitlement, and materiality to a colorable claim). Individuals not treated as Participants must clearly assert participant entitlement.
- After exhaustion, any court or tribunal review is limited, to the maximum extent permitted, to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator.
- Exhaustion applies even when:
  - Other non-claim disputes are more significant or are considered concurrently.
  - Rights are novel, discretionary, actual, or potential.
  - No specific claims procedures exist for the issue (the Plan Administrator will establish or analogize to Section 7.3 procedures).
- The Plan Administrator may create special procedures for class claims or conflict situations to preserve the exhaustion requirement.
- Broad definitions:
  - Dispute: any claim, dispute, issue, assertion, action, or other matter.
  - Claim: any Dispute involving Plan interpretation, terms, validity, administration, alleged ERISA/legal violations, benefit requests/recoveries, fiduciary breach assertions, or any related matters as deemed by the Plan Administrator.
  - Claimant: broadly includes actual or putative employees/participants, former participants, beneficiaries and related parties (spouses, former spouses, domestic partners, estates, heirs, representatives), and groups thereof.
- Statement of intent to operate consistent with ERISA and to impose a contractual obligation of complete exhaustion to ensure efficient, uniform resolution and limit unnecessary litigation costs.
- Two-year limitations period (Section 7.6) for:
  - Benefit denial claims under Section 7.3 and court actions alleging wrongful denial or interference/violation of ERISA-protected rights.
  - Accrual for benefit claims: the earliest of receipt of the benefit calculation, the identified payment start date, actual or constructive knowledge of operative facts, or the first payment/provision/denial.
  - Accrual for ERISA interference claims: when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the alleged interfering acts or facts.

nodes.title: Limitations on Actions
nodes.heading: 7.6 Limitations on Actions
nodes.start_phrase: Any claim filed under section 7.3 and any action filed in state or federal court by or on behalf of a former or current Employee, Participant, beneficiary or any other individual, person or entity (collectively , a “Petitioner”) for the alleged wrongful denial of Plan benefits or for the alleged interference with or violation of ERISA-protected rights must be brought within two years of the date the Petitioner ’s cause of action first accrues.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Claimant” broadly to include any current or former employee or participant, their beneficiaries (including spouses, former spouses, domestic partners), estates, heirs, representatives, related entities or individuals, and groups thereof, who have a claim under the plan.
- Establishes a two-year statute of limitations (Section 7.6) for:
  - Claims under the plan’s internal claims/appeals process (Section 7.3) and court actions alleging wrongful denial of benefits or interference with ERISA rights.
  - “Petitioner” includes any current or former employee, participant, beneficiary, or any other individual, person, or entity bringing such claims.
- Specifies accrual rules for the two-year period:
  - Benefit claims: accrue at the earliest of (i) receipt of the benefit calculation, (ii) the payment commencement date identified by the Plan Administrator, (iii) when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the relevant acts/omissions or facts, or (iv) when the benefit was first paid, provided, or denied.
  - ERISA interference claims: accrue when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the acts/omissions or facts constituting the alleged interference.
  - Other claims: must be brought within two years of when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the acts/omissions or facts giving rise to the claim.
- Failure to file within two years bars the claim; communications during or after the mandatory appeal process do not extend or toll this deadline.
- Restricts venue (Section 7.7): all court or tribunal actions related to the plan must be filed exclusively in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York for claims filed on or after January 1, 2011.
- Document context: excerpt from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

nodes.title: Restriction on Venue
nodes.heading: 7.7 Restriction on V enue
nodes.start_phrase: Any claim or action filed in court or any other tribunal in connection with the Plan by or on behalf of a Petitioner (as defined in Section 7.6 above) shall only be brought or filed in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New Y ork, ef fective for claims or actions filed on or after January 1, 2011.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes a two-year statute of limitations for any plan-related claim not covered by prior subsections, running from the claimant’s actual or constructive knowledge of the relevant acts or facts.
- States that failing to file within this two-year period bars the Petitioner or their representative from bringing the claim.
- Clarifies that correspondence or communications related to the mandatory appeals process (Section 7.3) do not toll or affect the two-year deadline.
- Imposes an exclusive venue requirement: any court or tribunal action connected to the Plan by or on behalf of a Petitioner (as defined in Section 7.6) must be filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, effective for filings on or after January 1, 2011.
- Extract is from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE VIII
Miscellaneous
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE VIII
Miscellaneous
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing contained in this Plan shall be construed as a contract of employment between an Employer and any Employee, or as a right of any Employee to be continued in the employment of an Employer , or as a limitation of the right of an Employer to discharge any of its Employees, with or without cause.
nodes.summary:
- Article VIII (Miscellaneous) outlines key legal provisions of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- 8.1 Nonguarantee of Employment: Participation in the Plan does not create an employment contract or guarantee continued employment; the Employer may terminate employment with or without cause.
- 8.2 Nonalienation of Benefits: Plan benefits cannot be anticipated, assigned, transferred, pledged, garnished, or otherwise alienated, whether voluntarily or involuntarily; attempts to do so—including in divorce, separation, or child support contexts—are void, and the Company is not liable for participants’ debts or obligations.
- 8.3 Unfunded Plan: Obligations are unfunded and paid from the Company’s general assets; participants have the status of unsecured general creditors.
- 8.4 Action by the Company: Actions under the Plan may be taken by the Company’s Board of Directors or its Compensation Committee.

nodes.title: Nonguarantee of Employment
nodes.heading: 8.1 Nonguarantee of Employment
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing contained in this Plan shall be construed as a contract of employment between an Employer and any Employee, or as a right of any Employee to be continued in the employment of an Employer , or as a limitation of the right of an Employer to discharge any of its Employees, with or without cause.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies that participation in the plan does not guarantee employment, continuation of employment, or limit the employer’s right to terminate employment with or without cause.
- Establishes strict anti-alienation of benefits: plan benefits cannot be assigned, transferred, pledged, garnished, or otherwise encumbered, including in divorce, separation, or child support contexts; attempts to do so are void, and the Company is not liable for participants’ debts or obligations.
- Confirms the plan is unfunded: obligations are paid from the Company’s general assets, and participants’ rights are no greater than those of unsecured general creditors.
- Specifies that Company actions under the plan may be taken by the Board of Directors or the Compensation Committee.

nodes.title: Nonalienation of Benefits
nodes.heading: 8.2 Nonalienation of Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: Benefits payable under the Plan or the right to receive future benefits under the Plan shall not be subject in any manner to anticipation, alienation, sale, transfer , assignment, pledge, encumbrance, charge, garnishment, execution, or levy of any kind,
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies that the plan does not guarantee employment; employers may terminate employees with or without cause.
- Establishes strict non-alienation of benefits: plan benefits cannot be assigned, transferred, pledged, garnished, or otherwise encumbered, including in divorce or child support matters; attempts are void and the company is not liable for participants’ debts.
- States the plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the company’s general assets and participants have the status of unsecured general creditors.
- Provides that company actions under the plan may be taken by the Board of Directors or the Compensation Committee.

nodes.title: Unfunded Plan
nodes.heading: 8.3 Unfunded Plan
nodes.start_phrase: The Company’ s obligations under the Plan shall not be funded, but shall constitute liabilities by the Company payable when due out of the Company’ s general funds.
nodes.summary:
- States the plan does not guarantee employment; it creates no employment contract and does not limit the employer’s right to terminate employment with or without cause.
- Establishes a strict anti-alienation rule: plan benefits cannot be assigned, transferred, pledged, garnished, or otherwise encumbered, including in divorce or child-support contexts; the company is not liable for participants’ debts or obligations.
- Confirms the plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the company’s general assets, and participants have the status of unsecured general creditors.
- Provides that company actions under the plan may be taken by the Board of Directors or the Compensation Committee.

nodes.title: Action by the Company
nodes.heading: 8.4 Action by the Company
nodes.start_phrase: Any action by the Company under this Plan may be made by the Board of Directors of the Company or by the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors, with a report of any actions taken by it to the Board of Directors.
nodes.summary:
- Article VIII (Miscellaneous) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Employment is not guaranteed by the Plan; employers may terminate employees with or without cause.
- Benefits are non-assignable and protected from anticipation, transfer, garnishment, or similar claims, including in divorce or child-support contexts; the Company is not liable for beneficiaries’ debts.
- The Plan is unfunded; obligations are paid from the Company’s general assets, and participants are unsecured general creditors.
- Company actions under the Plan may be taken by the Board, the Compensation Committee, or duly authorized delegates.
- The Company will indemnify employees administering the Plan who act in good faith, to the extent permitted by law.
- The Plan is intended to comply with Internal Revenue Code Section 409A; if deemed noncompliant, no liability attaches for good-faith actions or decisions.
- To ensure 409A compliance and clarity, the Plan specifies certain benefit calculations (e.g., treatment of salary continuation in window severance programs for Highest Average Monthly Earnings per Appendix B) and prohibits any duplication of benefits or double-counting of benefit-determining elements (such as pensionable earnings or service).

nodes.title: Indemnification
nodes.heading: 8.5 Indemnification
nodes.start_phrase: Unless the Board of Directors of the Company shall determine otherwise, the Company shall indemnify , to the full extent permitted by law , any employee acting in good faith within the scope of his employment in carrying out the administration of the Plan.
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines governance and compliance provisions of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program. It specifies that actions related to the Plan may be taken by the Board of Directors or by persons duly authorized by Board resolution, with actions reported to the Board. It includes an indemnification clause under which the Company, unless the Board decides otherwise, will indemnify employees administering the Plan in good faith to the fullest extent permitted by law. The Plan is intended to comply with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code; if it is deemed noncompliant, neither the Company, the Board, the Plan Administrator, nor their agents are liable for good-faith decisions. To ensure 409A compliance, the document clarifies benefit calculations in specific scenarios (e.g., treatment of salary continuation in window severance programs when determining Highest Average Monthly Earnings per Appendix B) and emphasizes that no duplication of benefits or double-counting of earnings or service is permitted.

nodes.title: Compliance with Section 409A
nodes.heading: 8.6 Compliance with Section 409A
nodes.start_phrase: It is the intention of the Company that the Plan shall be construed in accordance with the applicable requirements of Section 409A.
nodes.summary:
- Authority and delegation: Actions related to the plan may be taken by the Board of Directors or by persons duly authorized by Board resolution, with reporting of actions back to the Board.
- Indemnification (Section 8.5): The Company will indemnify employees acting in good faith within the scope of their duties in administering the plan, to the fullest extent permitted by law, unless the Board decides otherwise.
- Compliance with Section 409A (Section 8.6):
  - Intent to comply: The plan is intended to meet Section 409A requirements; no liability for good-faith actions if a provision is later found noncompliant.
  - Non-duplication of benefits: Specific rules (e.g., treatment of salary continuation in window severance programs when calculating Highest Average Monthly Earnings per Appendix B) are included to ensure compliance, and no benefit element (earnings, service, etc.) may be counted more than once under any plan provision or through integration with the Salaried Plan; specific provisions control over any contrary interpretation.
- Section 457A protections for international transfers (Section 8.7): For participants transferring to certain non-U.S. PepsiCo entities (a “Covered Transfer”):
  - Automatic vesting of the participant’s pension occurs on the last business day before the transfer.
  - Post-transfer benefit enhancements tied to service or age attainment are credited only at the end of the plan year and only as permitted.
  - Participants have no legal right to such enhancements until they are eligible and credited, aiming to avoid application of Section 457A.

nodes.title: Section 457A
nodes.heading: 8.7 Section 457A
nodes.start_phrase: To avoid the application of Code section 457A (“Section 457A”) to a Participant’ s Pension, the following shall apply to a Participant who transfers to a work location outside of the United States to provide services to a member of the PepsiCo Organization that is neither a United States corporation nor a pass- through entity that is wholly owned by a United States corporation (“Covered T ransfer”):
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines administrative and compliance provisions of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program:

- Anti-duplication of benefits: If any compensation element is or could be recognized elsewhere under the Plan (including through integration with the Salaried Plan), the specific governing provision controls and duplicate recognition is prohibited.

- Section 457A compliance for international assignments: For Participants who transfer to non-U.S. entities within the PepsiCo Organization that are neither U.S. corporations nor wholly owned pass-throughs (“Covered Transfer”):
  - Automatic vesting occurs as of the last business day before the transfer.
  - Post-transfer benefit enhancements tied to service or age attainment (“Benefit Enhancement”) are not credited until the last day of the Plan Year and only to the extent permissible; Participants have no legal right to enhancements that would be includable in income under Section 457A.
  - The Company may issue an “applicable communication” overriding these rules for a given transfer.
  - The deferred-credit rule ceases when the Participant returns to a qualifying U.S. entity or as otherwise specified in an applicable communication.

- Authorized transfers outside the PepsiCo Organization: Liability for benefits accrued while employed by PepsiCo remains with the Company unless an agreement with the new employer provides otherwise.

- Electronic signatures and records: Electronic signatures and electronic recordkeeping are authorized and have the same legal effect, validity, and enforceability as manual signatures and paper records.

nodes.title: Authorized Transfers
nodes.heading: 8.8 Authorized T ransfers
nodes.start_phrase: If a Participant transfers to an entity that is not part of the PepsiCo Organization, the liability for any benefits accrued while the Participant was employed by the PepsiCo Organization shall remain with the Company , except as otherwise expressly provided by an agreement between the Company and the Participant’ s new employer .
nodes.summary:
- Sets limits on Benefit Enhancements following a “Covered Transfer,” to avoid creating compensation includable in income under Internal Revenue Code Section 457A.
- Allows the Company to exempt specific Covered Transfers from these limits through an “applicable communication” issued to affected participants or groups.
- Specifies when the post-transfer restriction in subsection (b) ends: upon the participant’s return to service with a U.S. PepsiCo entity (including a wholly owned pass-through) or on a stated effective date in an applicable communication.
- Defines “Authorized Transfers”: if a participant moves to a non-PepsiCo employer, the Company retains liability for benefits accrued while employed at PepsiCo, unless an agreement with the new employer provides otherwise.
- Confirms that electronic signatures and electronic records are valid and enforceable equivalents to manual signatures for all plan-related documents.

nodes.title: Electronic Signatures
nodes.heading: 8.9 Electronic Signatures
nodes.start_phrase: The words “signed,” “signature,” and words of like import in or related to this Plan or any other document or record to be signed in connection with or related to this Plan by the Company , Plan Administrator , Employee or other individual shall be deemed to include electronic signatures and the keeping of records in electronic form, each of which shall be of the same legal ef fect, validity and enforceability as a manually executed signature or the use of a paper-based recordkeeping system, as the case may be, to the fullest extent permissible under applicable law .
nodes.summary:
- Addresses limits on post–Covered Transfer benefit enhancements to avoid amounts becoming includable in income under Section 457A.
- Allows the Company to issue an “applicable communication” (to an individual, a group, or all Participants) stating that certain subsections governing Covered Transfers do not apply to a specific transfer.
- States that the restrictions in subsection (b) end on the earlier of: (i) the Participant’s return to service with a U.S. PepsiCo entity (including a wholly owned pass‑through of a U.S. corporation), or (ii) the effective date specified in an applicable communication.
- Clarifies “Authorized Transfers”: when a Participant moves to a non‑PepsiCo entity, PepsiCo retains liability for benefits accrued while employed by PepsiCo, unless an agreement with the new employer provides otherwise.
- Confirms the validity and enforceability of electronic signatures and electronic recordkeeping for the Plan, equivalent to manual signatures and paper records, to the fullest extent permitted by law.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE IX
Amendment and Termination
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE IX
Amendment and T ermination
nodes.start_phrase: This Article governs the Company’ s right to amend and or terminate the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Article IX outlines the Company’s rights to amend or terminate the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, subject at all times to Section 409A restrictions and applicable law.
- The Company intends to continue the Plan indefinitely but assumes no contractual obligation to do so.
- The Company may amend, terminate, or partially terminate the Plan at any time; however, such changes cannot reduce the amount of benefits a Participant or beneficiary is entitled to under Article IV as of the change date, unless an equal benefit is provided under another plan or the change is necessary to comply with Section 409A. Protection applies to benefit amounts, not specific forms of payment.
- The Company has sole authority to amend the Plan, including with retroactive effect, to maintain Section 409A compliance; other Employers cannot amend the Plan.
- The Company may terminate the Plan in whole or in part, including as to its own participation or that of one or more Employers (the text on termination scope is partially cut off).

nodes.title: Continuation of the Plan
nodes.heading: 9.1 Continuation of the Plan
nodes.start_phrase: While the Company and the Employers intend to continue the Plan indefinitely , they assume no contractual obligation as to its continuance.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Company’s authority to amend, terminate, or partially terminate the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, with such powers constrained by and exercised in compliance with Section 409A and applicable law.
- States the intent to continue the Plan indefinitely but clarifies there is no contractual obligation to do so (per Section 8.4).
- Protects accrued benefit amounts under Article IV as of the amendment/termination date from being adversely affected, unless an equivalent amount becomes payable under another Company plan, and allows changes as necessary to comply with Section 409A; specific forms of payment are not protected.
- Authorizes the Company to make amendments at any time, including retroactively, to maintain Section 409A compliance; other Employers have no amendment rights.
- Allows the Company to terminate the Plan as to itself or one or more Employers, and with respect to a group of participants (termination provision text continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Amendments
nodes.heading: 9.2 Amendments
nodes.start_phrase: The Company may , in its sole discretion, make any amendment or amendments to this Plan from time to time, with or without retroactive ef fect, including any amendment necessary to ensure continued compliance with Section 409A.
nodes.summary:
- Article IX sets out the Company’s authority to amend or terminate the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, strictly subject to Section 409A and applicable law.
- The Company intends to continue the Plan but assumes no obligation to do so and may amend, terminate, or partially terminate it at any time.
- Participant protections: amendments or terminations cannot reduce the benefit amount a participant/beneficiary is entitled to under Article IV as of the effective date, except as needed for Section 409A compliance or if an equivalent benefit is provided under another Company plan; specific forms of payment are not protected.
- Amendment power: the Company alone may amend the Plan, with or without retroactive effect, including to maintain Section 409A compliance; other Employers cannot amend.
- Termination scope: the Company may terminate the Plan as to itself or one or more participating Employers, and potentially for certain groups (text truncated).

nodes.title: Termination
nodes.heading: 9.3 Termination
nodes.start_phrase: The Company may terminate the Plan, (i) either as to its participation or as to the participation of one or more Employers, (ii) with respect to a group of Employees who experience a change in control in accordance with T reasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), or (iii) as otherwise permitted under Code Section 409A.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines Article IX of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, governing amendment and termination. Key points:
- All amendment and termination actions must comply with Internal Revenue Code Section 409A; the Company’s authority is as broad as law permits.
- Continuation: The Company intends to maintain the Plan indefinitely but has no obligation to do so and may amend, terminate, or partially terminate at any time. Accrued benefit amounts under Article IV as of the amendment/termination date will not be reduced unless necessary for 409A compliance or replaced by an equal benefit under another plan; specific payment forms are not protected.
- Amendments: The Company alone may amend the Plan, with or without retroactive effect, including to ensure 409A compliance; other Employers cannot amend.
- Termination: The Company may terminate (a) as to itself or one/more Employers, (b) for a group of employees experiencing a change in control per Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), or (c) as otherwise allowed under 409A. If not all Employers are terminated, the Plan continues for the rest. Distributions upon termination remain subject to 409A restrictions.
- Change in Control: The Company reserves maximum permissible discretion under 409A to terminate the Plan and make distributions in connection with a Change in Control (as defined in 409A). These terms are the exclusive basis for distributions related to Change in Control for benefits under this 409A Program.

nodes.title: Change in Control
nodes.heading: 9.4 Change in Control
nodes.start_phrase: The Company intends to have the maximum discretionary authority to terminate the Plan and make distributions in connection with a Change in Control (defined as provided in Section 409A), and the maximum flexibility with respect to how and to what extent to carry this out following a Change in Control as is permissible under Section 409A.
nodes.summary: This excerpt from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program sets out termination and Change in Control provisions compliant with Code Section 409A. It states that plan termination and distributions may occur in connection with a Change in Control as defined under Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B) and otherwise permitted by 409A. If the plan is terminated for fewer than all participating employers, it continues for employees of the remaining employers. Any distributions upon termination are subject to 409A restrictions. The Company reserves maximum discretion, within 409A limits, to terminate the plan and make distributions following a Change in Control, and these are the exclusive terms governing such distributions for benefits under this 409A Program.

nodes.start_phrase: This Plan document in conjunction with the plan document(s) for the Pre-409A Program encompasses three separate plans within the meaning of ERISA, as are set forth in subsections (a), (b) and (c).

- Excess Benefit Plan (ERISA §3(36)): Provides benefits to Salaried Plan participants above Internal Revenue Code §415 limits.
- Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan: A top‑hat plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees (ERISA §§201(2), 401(a)(1)), providing benefits above the Code §401(a)(17) compensation cap (after accounting for the Excess Benefit Plan); for ERISA reporting, referred to as PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.

nodes.title: Excess Benefit Plan
nodes.heading: (a) Excess Benefit Plan
nodes.start_phrase: An excess benefit plan within the meaning of section 3(36) of ERISA, maintained solely for the purpose of providing benefits for Salaried Plan participants in excess of the limitations on benefits imposed by section 415 of the Code.
nodes.summary:
- Article X outlines the ERISA plan structure for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, to be read together with the Pre‑409A Program documents.
- Effective July 1, 1996, the program is divided into three separate ERISA plans; prior to that date, the plans described in (b) and (c) were combined as a single ERISA plan.
- Excess Benefit Plan (ERISA §3(36)): Provides benefits to Salaried Plan participants that exceed the Internal Revenue Code §415 limits.
- Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan: A “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees (ERISA §§201(2), 401(a)(1)), providing benefits above the IRC §401(a)(17) compensation limits under the Salaried Plan, after considering benefits from the Excess Benefit Plan; for ERISA reporting, this portion may be called the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
- Preservation Top Hat Plan: Another “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees (ERISA §§201(2), 401(a)(1)), intended to preserve certain benefits for Salaried Plan participants (details truncated in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan
nodes.heading: (b) Excess Compensation T op Hat Plan
nodes.start_phrase: A plan maintained by the Company primarily for the purpose of providing deferred compensation for a select group of management or highly compensated employees within the meaning of sections 201(2) and 401(a)(1) of ERISA.
nodes.summary:
- Article X defines the ERISA plan structure of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (409A Program), together with Pre‑409A program documents, as comprising three separate ERISA plans.
- The separation into distinct plans became effective July 1, 1996; prior to that, the plans now described in (b) and (c) were a single ERISA plan.
- Excess Benefit Plan (a): An ERISA §3(36) excess benefit plan maintained solely to provide benefits to Salaried Plan participants above Internal Revenue Code §415 limits.
- Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan (b): A “top hat” plan under ERISA §§201(2) and 401(a)(1) for a select group of management or highly compensated employees, providing benefits above Internal Revenue Code §401(a)(17) compensation limits under the Salaried Plan (after accounting for the Excess Benefit Plan); for ERISA reporting, referred to as PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
- Preservation Top Hat Plan (c): A “top hat” plan under the same ERISA provisions for a select group, intended to preserve benefits for certain Salaried Plan participants (details truncated in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Preservation Top Hat Plan
nodes.heading: (c) Preservation T op Hat Plan
nodes.start_phrase: A plan maintained by the Company primarily for the purpose of providing deferred compensation for a select group of management or highly compensated employees within the meaning of sections 201(2) and 401(a)(1) of ERISA.
nodes.summary:
- Defines the ERISA plan structure of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, which, together with Pre-409A documents, comprises three separate ERISA plans effective July 1, 1996 (with items (b) and (c) previously a single plan).
- Excess Benefit Plan: An ERISA section 3(36) excess benefit plan providing benefits to Salaried Plan participants above Internal Revenue Code (IRC) section 415 limits.
- Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan: A “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees (ERISA sections 201(2), 401(a)(1)), providing benefits above IRC section 401(a)(17) compensation limits (after considering Excess Benefit Plan benefits); referred to for ERISA reporting as PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
- Preservation Top Hat Plan: A “top hat” plan preserving pre-1989 benefit accrual levels for specified Salaried Plan participants (as in section 5.2(a)), after applying benefits from the Excess Benefit Plan and the Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan; referred to for ERISA reporting as PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan II.
- Establishes allocation order of benefits: first to the Excess Benefit Plan, then to the Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan, and finally to the Preservation Top Hat Plan.
- States the three plans are severable for any and all purposes as directed by the Company.
- Clarifies that lump sum termination benefits paid in connection with Special Early Retirement under a temporary Company severance program are treated as part of the Company’s unfunded severance plan (an ERISA “welfare benefit plan” under section 3(1)), exist only for the duration/purpose of the temporary program, and are not subject to top hat reporting or pension plan ERISA requirements.

- Article XI sets the governing law for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- The Plan’s construction, administration, validity, enforceability, and determination are governed by ERISA and other applicable federal law as applied in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.
- Where ERISA does not preempt state law, the internal laws of the State of New York apply.
- Includes a severability clause stating that if any provision is found void, invalid, or unlawful, the remainder of the Plan remains in effect.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE A - Transition Provisions
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE A - 
Transition Provisions
nodes.start_phrase: This Article A provides the transition rules for the Plan that were ef fective at some time during the period beginning January 1, 2005 and ending December 31, 2008 (the “T ransition Period”).
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article A outlines transition provisions for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program during the Transition Period of January 1, 2005 through December 31, 2008, with each rule having specified effective dates.
- Section A.1 (Scope) states that these rules apply only within the Transition Period and that effective periods for each provision are identified.
- Section A.2 (Transition Rules for Article II – Definitions) modifies definitions used during the Transition Period:
  - Actuarial Equivalent: For calculating pensions payable as a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, other survivor annuities, inflation-protected annuities, or Single Life Annuities, the Plan Administrator used the actuarial factors from the Salaried Plan.
  - Key Employee: Adds operating rules for identifying Key Employees; specifically for the 2005 plan year, all participants (and former participants) classified or grandfathered as Band IV and above at any time in 2005 were treated as Key Employees for Separation from Service distributions.

nodes.title: Scope.
nodes.heading: A.1 Scope .
nodes.start_phrase: This Article A provides the transition rules for the Plan that were ef fective at some time during the period beginning January 1, 2005 and ending December 31, 2008 (the “T ransition Period”).
nodes.summary: Appendix Article A outlines transition provisions for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program during January 1, 2005 through December 31, 2008. It specifies that, for this Transition Period, actuarial equivalence used the Salaried Plan’s actuarial factors when calculating benefits payable as a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, other survivor annuity options, inflation-protected annuities, or a Single Life Annuity. It also adds temporary rules for identifying Key Employees, including a 2005 rule deeming all participants (and former participants) classified or grandfathered as Band IV and above at any time during 2005 as Key Employees for separation-from-service distributions, to ensure none were missed. Each provision indicates its effective timeframe within the Transition Period.

nodes.title: Transition Rules for Article II (Definitions).
nodes.heading: A.2 Transition Rules for Article II (Definitions) .
nodes.start_phrase: In addition to the provisions provided in Article II for determining actuarial equivalence under the Plan, for the duration of the T ransition Period, to determine the amount of a Pension payable in the form of a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity or optional form of survivor annuity , as an annuity with inflation protection, or as a Single Life Annuity , the Plan Administrator used the actuarial factors under the Salaried Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Appendix Article A as transition provisions for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, effective during January 1, 2005 to December 31, 2008 (the Transition Period), with timing for each provision specified.
- Article II (Definitions) transition rules:
  - Actuarial Equivalent: For the Transition Period, the Plan Administrator used actuarial factors from the Salaried Plan to determine amounts for Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuities, other survivor annuities, inflation-protected annuities, and Single Life Annuities.
  - Key Employee identification:
    - 2005: Treated all participants (and former participants) classified/grandfathered as Band IV and above at any time in 2005 as Key Employees for separation distributions.
    - 2006–2007: Treated as Key Employees (i) anyone classified/grandfathered as Band IV and above at any time prior to the plan year of separation, and/or (ii) anyone who would be a Key Employee as of separation based on IRC 415(c)(3) compensation, using a two-year lookback for Q1 separations and a one-year lookback for Q2–Q4 separations.
- Article VI (Distributions) transition rule: 409A pensions that otherwise would have been paid during the Transition Period under the main plan provisions (but for permissible 409A transition rules) are to be paid on March 1, 2009.
- Article VII (Administration) transition rule: Replaces Section 8.6(a) during the Transition Period to require operation in full compliance with IRC Section 409A and to preserve the grandfathered (Pre-409A) status; any action violating 409A or adversely affecting grandfathering is void, and plan rights/effects must be adjusted to avoid such violations or adverse effects.

nodes.title: Transition Rules for Article VI (Distributions):
nodes.heading: A.3 Transition Rules for Article VI (Distributions) :
nodes.start_phrase: 409A Pensions that would have been paid out during the T ransition Period under the provisions set forth in the main body of the Plan (but for the application of permissible transition rules under Section 409A) shall be paid out on March 1, 2009.
nodes.summary:
- Defines compensation measurement for determinations as the prior calendar year (e.g., Q2 2006 uses 2005 compensation).
- Sets transition rules for distributions: 409A-affected pensions that would have been paid during the Transition Period under the main Plan (absent permissible 409A transition rules) will be paid on March 1, 2009.
- Replaces Section 8.6(a) during the Transition Period to mandate:
  - Ongoing operation of the Plan in full compliance with Section 409A.
  - Preservation of the grandfathered (pre-409A) status of deferrals under the Pre-409A Program.
  - Any action violating 409A or harming grandfathered status is void; plan rights/effects must be adjusted as needed to avoid violations or adverse impacts on grandfathering.
- Extract is from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program (page 97).

nodes.title: Transition Rules for Article VII (Administration):
nodes.heading: A.4 Transition Rules for Article VII (Administration) :
nodes.start_phrase: Effective during the T ransition Period, the language of Section 8.6(a) shall be replaced in its entirety with the following language:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how “prior calendar year” compensation is determined for plan calculations (e.g., a Q2 2006 determination uses 2005 compensation).
- Sets Transition Rules for distributions: any 409A pensions that would have been paid during the Transition Period under the main plan (absent permissible 409A transition rules) will instead be paid on March 1, 2009.
- Replaces Section 8.6(a) during the Transition Period with a strict Section 409A compliance mandate:
  - The plan must operate in full compliance with Section 409A and preserve the grandfathered (Pre-409A) status of prior deferrals.
  - Any action violating 409A or harming grandfathered status is void; plan rights/effects may be altered to avoid violations.
  - Required 409A provisions not expressly stated are deemed included; the same applies to provisions needed to preserve grandfathering.
  - This compliance section controls over any contrary plan terms outside the section.
- Introduces Transition Rules for Severance Benefits during the Transition Period, including a definitions subsection:
  - Clarifies that capitalized, bold/underlined terms in this section use the definitions provided; other capitalized terms follow the main plan unless context dictates otherwise.
  - Defines “Special Early Retirement” as retirement at age ≥50 but <55 with 10 years of Elapsed Time Service; notes a specific rule for 2008 Severance at Section A.5(d) (details continue beyond the excerpt).
- Overall focus is on aligning plan operations, distributions, and severance-related provisions with Section 409A while protecting grandfathered Pre-409A benefits during the Transition Period.

nodes.title: Transition Rules for Severance Benefits.
nodes.heading: A.5 Transition Rules for Severance Benefits .
nodes.start_phrase: Effective during the T ransition Period, the following provisions shall apply according to their specified terms.
nodes.summary:
- 409A compliance and grandfathering: Any Plan provision that violates Section 409A or harms the grandfathered Pre‑409A Program is void; any required 409A (or grandfathering) terms not expressly stated are deemed included and control over conflicting Plan terms.
- Transition Period rules for severance window programs: Detailed timing and form-of-payment rules for Participants who terminated in 2005, 2007, or 2008.
- Defined term: Special Early Retirement means age 50–54 with 10 years of Elapsed Time Service; for 2008 severance, age and service are rounded up to the nearest whole year when determining eligibility.
- 2005 severance:
  - Non‑retirement eligible: 409A Pension paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), timed with the Salaried Plan benefit; if otherwise payable in 2007, pay at the later of January 1, 2007 or age 55. Forms per Section 6.2.
  - Retirement eligible as of Feb. 5, 2006: lump sum on the first day of the month after Separation from Service.
  - Retirement eligible due to additional credited service: lump sum on the first day of the month after Separation from Service.
  - Special Early Retirement eligible: lump sum on the first day of the month after Separation from Service.
- 2007 severance:
  - Non‑retirement eligible: Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b); forms per Section 6.2.
  - Retirement eligible at separation: lump sum on the first day of the month after separation, unless a valid Prior Payment Election under Section 6.1(a)(2) applies.
  - Become retirement eligible during paid leave: Vested Pension starting the first day of the month after the later of age 55 or separation; forms per Section 6.2. PEP Kicker (make‑whole for lost accruals) paid as a single lump sum on the same timing; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
  - Special Early Retirement eligible at separation: Vested Pension starting the first day of the month after age 55; forms per Section 6.2. PEP Kicker as lump sum after age 55; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
  - Become Special Early Retirement eligible during paid leave: same age‑55 timing and forms; PEP Kicker lump sum after age 55; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
- 2008 severance:
  - Non‑retirement eligible: Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b); forms per Section 6.2.
  - Retirement eligible at separation: lump sum on the first day of the month after separation; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
  - Become retirement eligible during paid leave: Vested Pension on the first day of the month after the later of age 55 or separation; forms per Section 6.2. PEP Kicker as lump sum on the same timing; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
  - Special Early Retirement eligible at separation or during paid leave: Vested Pension on the first day of the month after age 55; forms per Section 6.2. PEP Kicker as lump sum after age 55; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
- Key Employee delay: If the Participant is a “Key Employee,” any payment on account of Separation from Service is delayed per Section 6.6 (six‑month delay rule).
- Administrative/IRS compliance: Payments under this section were scheduled for the calendar year of termination as provided; Company elections complied with IRS Notice 2005‑1 and Section 409A (and Plan Section 19(c)).

nodes.title: Certain Participants
nodes.heading: A.6 Certain Participants
nodes.start_phrase: The following transition rules shall apply only with respect to the following described Participants:
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Transition rules within the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program applying to specific participant situations and to 409A Disability Pension pre-separation accruals.

- A.6 Certain Participants:
  - 2005 Band VI limited-duration assignments: Participants who terminated in 2005 while classified as Band VI (or equivalent) and served in limited-duration roles under five years are (i) deemed to have five years of PEP credited service and (ii) deemed vested under the Plan.
  - 2007 lump-sum election under Salaried Plan: For participants who, on October 9, 2007, elected a November 1, 2007 annuity start date with a single lump sum under the Salaried Plan, the portion of the Equalization Plan benefit not subject to Code Section 409A is paid as a single lump sum six months after the Salaried Plan annuity start date.
  - 2004 fixed payment date election: For participants who, on September 3, 2004, chose a February 1, 2005 fixed payment date, that date is the Plan benefit commencement date, and the benefit calculation includes service for consulting to be performed for the Company even if that consulting occurs after the payment date.

- A.7 Transition Rules for Article VI (409A Disability Pension—Pre-Separation Accruals):
  - Distribution timing and form: Payments of the portion representing pre-separation accruals begin March 1, 2009, using the same forms of payment available for a vested pension (with options differing for married vs. unmarried participants per Section 6.2).
  - Additional death benefit: If a participant receiving these pre-separation accrual payments dies before his expected mortality date (as defined by the Plan’s January 1, 2009 mortality table), the beneficiary receives a lump-sum actuarial equivalent of payments that would have been made from death to the expected mortality date, payable within 30 days of death. Participants may designate a beneficiary specifically for this additional benefit notwithstanding general Section 6.5 provisions.

nodes.title: Transition Rules for Article VI (409A Disability Pension Pre-Separation Accruals):
nodes.heading: A.7 Transition Rules for Article VI (409A Disability Pension Pre-Separation Accruals ):
nodes.start_phrase: The portion of a Participant’ s 409A Disability Pension representing Pre-Separation Accruals that would have been paid out during the T ransition Period under the provisions set forth in the main body of the Plan (but for the application of permissible transition rules under Section 409A) shall commence on March 1, 2009.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, addressing transition rules for 409A Disability Pension Pre-Separation Accruals.
- Consulting Services Note: Indicates a participant may be required to provide consulting services to the Company even if performed after a specified payment date (referencing an earlier paragraph).
- Transition Rules (A.7) for Article VI:
  - Distribution Timing: Payments of the 409A Disability Pension attributable to Pre-Separation Accruals that would have been paid during the Transition Period begin on March 1, 2009.
  - Forms of Payment: Available forms mirror those for a Vested Pension under Section 6.2, with options differing for married vs. unmarried participants.
- Additional Benefit on Early Death:
  - If a participant receiving Pre-Separation Accrual payments dies before their expected mortality date (per the plan’s January 1, 2009 mortality table), the beneficiary receives a lump-sum actuarial equivalent of the foregone annuity payments from death to the expected mortality date.
  - Payment to beneficiary must be made within 30 days of the participant’s death.
  - Beneficiary Designation: Participant may specifically designate a beneficiary for this additional benefit (overriding general Section 6.5 rules); if none is designated, defaults to the Section 6.5 beneficiary, then to the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, and if none, to the estate.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE B - Computation of Earnings and Service During Certain Severance Windows
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE B - 
Computation of Earnings and Service During Certain Severance W indows
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases, in boldface and underlined, appear in this Appendix B with initial capitals they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Appendix Article B governs how earnings and service are computed for participants during designated severance “windows” under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Definitions:
  - Severance Program: A program that pays severance benefits while a participant is on a severance leave of absence; the Plan Administrator may recognize this leave as Service (Section B.3) and Credited Service (Section B.4).
  - Eligible Bonus: An annual incentive payment under the Severance Program that is identified as includible in calculating a participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings.
  - Capitalized terms not defined here follow the main Plan unless context requires otherwise.
- Inclusion of compensation (B.2):
  - The Plan Administrator may allow salary continuation and any Eligible Bonus payable during the first 12 months of a severance leave under a Severance Program to be included in the participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings.
  - These amounts may be counted even if actually paid after that initial 12‑month period or after the participant’s leave/separation (text truncated).

nodes.title: Definitions:
nodes.heading: B.1 Definitions :
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases, in boldface and underlined, appear in this Appendix B with initial capitals they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Appendix Article B explains how earnings and service are computed during certain severance “window” periods under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Key definitions:
  - Severance Program: A company program providing severance benefits during a severance leave that the Plan Administrator determines qualifies for recognition as Service (Section B.3) and Credited Service (Section B.4).
  - Eligible Bonus: An annual incentive payable under the Severance Program that is designated as includible in determining a participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings.
- Earnings inclusion rule: The Plan Administrator may specify that, for participants in a company severance window program, salary continuation and any Eligible Bonus payable during the first 12 months of the severance leave are included in the participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings, even if such amounts are received after that period.

nodes.title: Inclusion of Salary and Eligible Bonus:
nodes.heading: B.2 Inclusion of Salary and Eligible Bonus :
