nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator may specify that, pursuant to a Participant’ s participation in a severance window program provided by the Company , if a Participant receives a severance benefit pursuant to a Severance Program, all salary continuation and any Eligible Bonus that is payable during the first 12 months of a leave of absence period provided to the Participant under such Severance Program will be counted toward the Participant’ s Highest A verage Monthly Earnings, even if such salary or other earnings are to be received after a Participant’ s Separation from Service.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Appendix B sets rules for how earnings and service are computed during certain severance windows under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Key definitions:
  - Severance Program: A company program that pays severance while a participant is on a qualifying severance leave, recognized for Service and Credited Service under this appendix.
  - Eligible Bonus: An annual incentive under the Severance Program that counts toward Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME).
- Earnings treatment (B.2):
  - Salary continuation and Eligible Bonus payable during the first 12 months of a severance leave can be included in HAME, even if paid after Separation from Service.
  - If a 409A Pension is paid at Separation before all severance amounts are received, HAME is determined using the full projected salary continuation and Eligible Bonus for the first 12 months of leave.
  - The Plan Administrator will allocate projected earnings across Plan Years to avoid bunching.
- Credited Service treatment (B.3):
  - The first 12 months of severance can count as Credited Service for calculating the Participant’s Pension and any Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Eligible Domestic Partner’s Pension, even if this period occurs after Separation from Service.
- Service treatment (B.4):
  - The first 12 months of severance can also count as Service for plan purposes (section continues beyond the excerpt).
- Administrative discretion:
  - In all cases, application of these inclusions is at the Plan Administrator’s discretion and may be specified in connection with a company severance window program.

nodes.title: Inclusion of Credited Service:
nodes.heading: B.3 Inclusion of Credited Service :
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator may specify that, pursuant to a Participant’ s participation in a severance window program provided by the Company , if a Participant receives a severance benefit under a Severance Program, all Credited Service earned or to be earned during the first 12 months of the period of severance will be counted toward the Participant’ s Credited Service for purposes of determining the Participant’ s Pension and a Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension or Pre-Retirement Eligible Domestic Partner ’s Pension, even if the period of time counted as Credited Service under the Severance Program occurs after a Participant’ s Separation from Service.
nodes.summary:
- Explains how to determine a participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for 409A pension payments made at Separation from Service when salary continuation and eligible bonus under a Severance Program are still payable: include the full projected salary continuation and eligible bonus for the first 12 months of the severance-related leave and allocate those projected amounts across Plan Years to avoid bunching.
- Authorizes the Plan Administrator, in connection with a severance window program, to count all Credited Service earned or to be earned during the first 12 months of severance toward the participant’s Credited Service for calculating the Pension and any Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Eligible Domestic Partner’s Pension, even if that period occurs after Separation from Service.
- Similarly authorizes the Plan Administrator to count all Service earned or to be earned during the first 12 months of severance toward the participant’s Service for plan purposes (text continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Inclusion of Service:
nodes.heading: B.4 Inclusion of Service :
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator may specify that, pursuant to a Participant’ s participation in a severance window program provided by the Company , if a Participant receives a severance benefit under a Severance Program, all Service earned or to be earned during the first 12 months of the period of severance will be counted toward the Participant’ s Service for purposes
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME) are determined when a 409A Pension is paid at Separation from Service before all severance salary continuation/Eligible Bonus is paid: projected salary continuation and eligible bonus for the first 12 months of severance are included, and the Plan Administrator allocates these projected amounts across Plan Years to avoid bunching.
- Authorizes the Plan Administrator, under a severance window program, to credit up to the first 12 months of the severance period as Credited Service for calculating the Participant’s Pension and any Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Eligible Domestic Partner’s Pension, even if that period occurs after Separation from Service.
- Similarly permits inclusion of up to the first 12 months of the severance period as Service for those same benefit determinations, even if post-separation.
- Requires an actuarial reduction if additional Credited Service or earnings from the Severance Program are included in the pension calculation before the service is performed or the earnings are actually paid; the adjustment uses the Salaried Plan’s early payment rate.

nodes.title: Reduction to Reflect Early Payment:
nodes.heading: B.5 Reduction to Reflect Early Payment :
nodes.start_phrase: If the Participant receives either (1) additional Credited Service or (2) additional earnings that are included in Highest A verage Monthly Earnings under Sections B.2 or B.3 of this Article B, as a result of a severance benefit provided under a Severance Program and such additional Credited Service or earnings are included in the calculation of the Participant’ s Pension prior to the time that the Credited Service is actually performed by the Participant, or the earnings are actually paid to the Participant, the Pension paid to the Participant shall be adjusted actuarially to reflect the receipt of the portion of the Pension attributable to such Credited Service or earnings received on account of the Severance Program prior to the time such Credited Service is performed or such earnings are actually paid to the Participant.
nodes.summary: The excerpt clarifies that service credited under a severance program counts toward a participant’s pension and pre-retirement survivor benefits (spouse or eligible domestic partner) even if the credited period occurs after separation from service. It also establishes that if severance-related credited service or earnings (including amounts used in Highest Average Monthly Earnings) are included in the pension calculation before the service is performed or earnings are paid, the pension will be actuarially reduced to reflect early payment, using the early-payment rate from the Salaried Plan.

nodes.title:
APPENDIX ARTICLE C
International and PIRP Transfer Participants
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE C
International and PIRP T ransfer Participants
nodes.start_phrase: This Article provides special rules for calculating the benefit of an individual who is either an “International T ransfer Participant” under Section C.2 below or a “PIRP T ransfer Participant” under Section C.4 below .
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article C sets special rules for calculating benefits for two participant categories: International Transfer Participants (Section C.2) and PIRP Transfer Participants (Section C.4).
- Benefit determination:
  - International Transfer Participants’ benefits are calculated under Section C.3, subject to Section C.6.
  - PIRP Transfer Participants’ benefits are calculated under Section C.5.
- Once determined, benefits are subject to the Plan’s normal conditions and paid under the Plan’s normal terms.
- All benefits under this Article are subject to Internal Revenue Code section 409A, including amounts accrued prior to January 1, 2005.
- Effective dates:
  - Provisions for International Transfer Participants are effective April 1, 2007.
  - Provisions for PIRP Transfer Participants are effective January 1, 2016 (and may consider service/years before that date).
- Partial definition provided for International Transfer Participants:
  - Generally includes individuals transferred to an “April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary” who would qualify as an Employee under specific Salaried Plan definitions (as of January 1, 2014) for U.S. citizens or resident aliens on qualifying temporary international assignments, subject to certain exceptions (text truncated).

nodes.title: Scope:
nodes.heading: C.1 Scope :
nodes.start_phrase: This Article provides special rules for calculating the benefit of an individual who is either an “International T ransfer Participant” under Section C.2 below or a “PIRP T ransfer Participant” under Section C.4 below .
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article C establishes special benefit-calculation rules for two categories of participants: International Transfer Participants (defined in Section C.2) and PIRP Transfer Participants (defined in Section C.4).
- Benefits are calculated under Section C.3 for International Transfer Participants (subject to Section C.6) and under Section C.5 for PIRP Transfer Participants.
- Once calculated under this Article, benefits are subject to the Plan’s normal conditions and payment terms.
- All benefits under this Article are subject to Internal Revenue Code section 409A, including amounts accrued before January 1, 2005.
- Effective dates: provisions for International Transfer Participants are effective April 1, 2007; provisions for PIRP Transfer Participants are effective January 1, 2016 (and may consider service before that date).
- The excerpt begins defining an International Transfer Participant: generally, a participant who, after a transfer to an “April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary” (as defined in the Salaried Plan Part B), would meet the Salaried Plan’s Employee definition paragraph (2)(vi) as of January 1, 2014 (U.S. citizen or resident alien on a qualifying temporary international assignment), subject to further conditions not fully shown in the excerpt.
- The Article relies on cross-references to definitions in the Salaried Plan (Part B), including the “Employer” and “Employee” definitions as in effect on January 1, 2014.

nodes.title: International Transfer Participants:
nodes.heading: C.2 International T ransfer Participants :
nodes.start_phrase: An individual described in subsection (a) or (b) above may still qualify as an International T ransfer Participant if his transfer to an April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary occurred prior to April 1, 2007 (the ef fective date of this Article), provided he satisfied the terms of subsection (a) or (b) above on the date of his transfer .
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article C establishes special benefit calculation rules for two groups: International Transfer Participants and PIRP Transfer Participants.
- Benefits determined under this article are paid under the Plan’s normal terms and are subject to Internal Revenue Code section 409A (including amounts accrued before January 1, 2005).
- Effective dates: International Transfer provisions effective April 1, 2007; PIRP Transfer provisions effective January 1, 2016 (with ability to consider service from earlier years).
- International Transfer Participant definition:
  - General rule: Individuals transferred to an “April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary” who would qualify as Employees under the Salaried Plan §2.1 Part B(2)(vi) (U.S. citizen or resident alien on qualifying temporary international assignment) but for being in a Band 4 (or equivalent) or higher position.
  - Special Mexico rule: Also includes certain transferees to a Mexico-based April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary who (i) are in Band 4+ roles, (ii) have Mexico as home country per Expat Centre for Excellence records, and (iii) have assignments not limited to 5 years or less.
  - Individuals transferred before April 1, 2007 can qualify if they met the above criteria at the time of transfer.
- Benefit formula for International Transfer Participants: Calculated using a methodology substantially similar to Plan Section 5.1, subject to exceptions within Section C.3 and further subject to Section C.6.
- The excerpt references PIRP Transfer Participant definitions and formulas in Sections C.4 and C.5, respectively, but their details are not included in the provided text.

nodes.title: Benefit Formula for International Transfer Participants:
nodes.heading: C.3 Benefit Formula for International T ransfer Participants :
nodes.start_phrase: Except as provided in this Section C.3, an International T ransfer Participant’ s benefit under the Plan shall be determined using a calculation methodology that is substantially similar to that which applies under Section 5.1 of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Document segment from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program detailing rules for “International Transfer Participants” assigned to an “April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary.”
- Eligibility:
  - Standard rule: Employee on assignment to an April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary in a Band 4 (or equivalent) or higher position.
  - Special rule for certain permanent assignments to Mexico: Individual would meet the Salaried Plan Employee definition (Section 2.1, Part B, para. (2)(vi) as of Jan 1, 2014) but for being in Band 4+; Mexico listed as home country with the Expat Centre for Excellence; and assignment not limited to 5 years or less.
  - Retroactivity: Individuals transferred before April 1, 2007 qualify if they met the applicable criteria at the time of transfer.
- Benefit formula:
  - Generally follows Section 5.1 of the Plan.
  - “Total Pension” is determined as if the participant continued to accrue Credited Service and Earnings under the Salaried Plan while working for the foreign subsidiary, ignoring the actual cessation date of such accruals.
  - Exception: For transfers occurring prior to 1992, Credited Service and Earnings with the foreign subsidiary before 1992 are excluded.
- Plan benefit calculation for International Transfer Participants:
  - Start with the Total Pension (expressed as a lump sum at the Plan benefit commencement date).
  - Subtract: (1) the actual Salaried Plan benefit (lump sum at commencement), and (2) any amounts received from a “qualifying plan” under Section 3.5(c)(4) of Part B of the Salaried Plan related to the foreign assignment (also expressed as a lump sum at commencement).
- Notes an upcoming section (C.4) for definitions related to PIRP Transfer Participants (content not included here).

nodes.title: Definitions Related to PIRP Transfer Participants:
nodes.heading: C.4 Definitions Related to PIRP T ransfer Participants :
nodes.start_phrase: The following definitions apply for purposes of Sections C.1, C.4 and C.5 of this Article.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how “Total Pension” is determined for International Transfer Participants: treated as if the employee continued to accrue Credited Service and Earnings under the Salaried Plan while working for an April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary; excludes foreign service/earnings prior to 1992 if the transfer occurred before 1992.
- Defines the Plan benefit for International Transfer Participants as the Total Pension (valued as a lump sum at benefit commencement) reduced by: (1) the actual Salaried Plan benefit (lump-sum equivalent), and (2) any payments from a qualifying plan tied to the foreign assignment (lump-sum equivalent), to avoid duplication.
- Provides definitions for PIRP Transfer Participants and related terms within the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program:
  - Accrued Benefit (single-life annuity at age 65), PIRP-DB (defined benefit component of the PepsiCo International Retirement Program), PIRP-DB Employer, PIRP-DB Pensionable Service, PIRP-DB Salary.
  - PIRP Transfer Participant categories:
    - Incoming: moved from a PIRP-DB-eligible role to a Salaried Plan-eligible role in the Year of Transfer; PIRP-DB accrual blocked by Section 9.14; would otherwise receive a PIRP-DB enhancement based on Salary/Service; PIRP-DB benefit not already paid by Dec 1, 2016 unless the PIRP-DB Vice President treats it as unpaid.
    - Outgoing: moved from a Salaried Plan-eligible role to a PIRP-DB-eligible role under similar Year of Transfer and Section 9.14 blocking conditions; same enhancement and unpaid-benefit criteria.
  - PIRP-DB Vice President (role holder under PIRP-DB), U.S. Person (as defined in PIRP-DB), Year of Transfer.
- Sets the benefit formula for PIRP Transfer Participants:
  - Generally follows Section 5.1 methodology, with modifications for transfer situations.
  - Total Pension is calculated as if the participant were eligible under the Salaried Plan for the entire Year of Transfer, crediting: (i) actual Salaried Plan Credited Service and Earnings, plus (ii) additional compensation/service that would have counted as PIRP-DB Salary and Pensionable Service absent Section 9.14.
  - Adds a rule (partially truncated in the excerpt) addressing PIRP-DB Salary that cannot be recognized due to Section 9.14 when tied to Pensionable Service not recognized under this Plan, indicating further adjustments to the participant’s Total Pension.

nodes.title: Benefit Formula for PIRP Transfer Participants:
nodes.heading: C.5 Benefit Formula for PIRP T ransfer Participants :
nodes.start_phrase: Except as provided in this Section C.5, a PIRP T ransfer Participant’ s benefit under the Plan shall be determined using a calculation methodology that is substantially similar to that which applies under Section 5.1 of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Year of Transfer” as the year in which a transfer described in subsection (f) occurs.
- Establishes the benefit formula for PIRP Transfer Participants, generally mirroring the methodology in Section 5.1 of the Plan, with special rules to coordinate benefits between the Salaried Plan and PIRP/PIRP-DB.
- Total Pension calculation:
  - First, compute as if the participant were an eligible employee under the Salaried Plan for the entire Year of Transfer, using actual Salaried Plan Credited Service and Earnings plus additional compensation/service that would have been recognized as PIRP-DB Salary/Pensionable Service if PIRP-DB Section 9.14 did not apply.
  - If PIRP-DB Salary or Pensionable Service in a year cannot be recognized because of PIRP-DB Section 9.14, the increase in the participant’s PIRP accrued benefit blocked by that section is added to the participant’s accrued benefit under this Plan. For separations on or after January 1, 2017, this results in a Company‑determined increase to Total Pension.
  - Prevents double counting and requires avoidance of duplicative benefits with PIRP-DB or other Company plans, while prohibiting any offset that would violate Code Section 409A.
- Benefit payable under this Plan:
  - Derived by applying the normal Article V reductions to the Total Pension.
  - For separations on or after January 1, 2017, if early retirement eligibility under PIRP-DB would have increased the PIRP-DB benefit but is blocked by Section 9.14, an appropriate Company‑determined increase is added to this Plan’s benefit (net of any early retirement increase already due under this Plan), again avoiding duplication and complying with Code Section 409A.
- Permits alternative arrangements: The Company and a participant who would qualify as an International Transfer Participant may, by written agreement, disregard this Article and adopt another benefit arrangement under the Plan that complies with Code Section 409A.

nodes.title: Alternative Arrangements Permitted:
nodes.heading: C.6 Alternative Arrangements Permitted :
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding any provision of this Article or the Plan to the contrary , the Company and a Participant who would qualify as an International T ransfer Participant under Section C.2 above may agree in writing to disregard the provisions of this Article in favor of another mutually agreed upon benefit arrangement under the Plan that complies with Code Section 409A, in which case this Article shall not apply .
nodes.summary:
- If a PIRP Transfer Participant’s projected PIRP-DB benefit increase is blocked by PIRP-DB Section 9.14, the Company will, at its discretion, provide a corresponding increase to the participant’s benefit under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (409A Program), payable at the time and in the form provided by this Plan.
- The increase is calculated net of any expected enhancement under this Plan related to Early Retirement eligibility and must avoid duplicating benefits provided under PIRP-DB (after Section 9.14) or any other Company or affiliate plan, while not applying any offset that would violate Code Section 409A.
- Alternative arrangements permitted: the Company and a participant who would qualify as an International Transfer Participant under Section C.2 may agree in writing to disregard this Article and adopt a different, mutually agreed benefit arrangement under the Plan that complies with Code Section 409A.

nodes.title:
APPENDIX ARTICLE D
Band 4 or Higher Rehired Yum Participants
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE D
Band 4 or Higher Rehired Y um Participants
nodes.start_phrase: Effective May 1, 2009, this Article provides special rules for calculating the benefit of a transferred Participant whose transfer would be an Eligible T ransfer under Section TRI.2(e) of the Part B of the Salaried Plan but for the fact that such individual is reemployed by the Company on or after May 1, 2009, into a position that is classified as Band 4 (or its equivalent) or higher .
nodes.summary:
- Effective May 1, 2009, establishes special benefit-calculation rules for transferred participants who are rehired into Band 4 (or equivalent) or higher positions.
- If the participant’s transfer would have been an Eligible Transfer under Part B, Section TRI.2(e) but for the Band 4+ rehire, then for Total Pension calculations only, the reemployment position is deemed below Band 4 so the transfer qualifies as an Eligible Transfer.
- This deeming does not apply to the calculation of the Salaried Plan Pension.
- Participants thus qualify for imputed service under Section TRI.4(b) and (c).
- All other benefits are administered under the Plan’s usual conditions and payment terms.
- All benefits under this Article are subject to Internal Revenue Code section 409A.

nodes.title: Scope:
nodes.heading: D.1 Scope:
nodes.start_phrase: Effective May 1, 2009, this Article provides special rules for calculating the benefit of a transferred Participant whose transfer would be an Eligible T ransfer under Section TRI.2(e) of the Part B of the Salaried Plan but for the fact that such individual is reemployed by the Company on or after May 1, 2009, into a position that is classified as Band 4 (or its equivalent) or higher .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Appendix Article D for Band 4 (or equivalent) and higher rehired YUM participants
- Effective date: May 1, 2009
- Applies to transferred participants rehired on/after that date into Band 4+ roles whose transfers would otherwise qualify as Eligible Transfers under Part B, Section TRI.2(e) of the Salaried Plan
- For Total Pension calculation under Section 5.1(c)(1), the rehired position is deemed below Band 4 to preserve Eligible Transfer treatment and eligibility for imputed service under Sections TRI.4(b) and (c)
- This deeming does not apply to the Salaried Plan Pension calculation under Section 5.1(c)(2)
- All other benefits are subject to the plan’s usual conditions and payment terms
- Benefits paid under this Article are subject to Internal Revenue Code section 409A

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE E - Time and Form of Payment for Benefits Paid During Severance Windows
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE E - 
Time and Form of Payment for Benefits Paid During Severance W indows
nodes.start_phrase: This Article E sets forth the time and form of payment provisions that apply to benefits under the Plan that are paid to a Covered Participant (as defined in Section E.2 below).
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article E sets rules for the time and form of payment of benefits during severance windows under the Plan.
- Scope: Applies to Participants terminated in a Severance Program or under an Individual Severance Agreement on or after January 1, 2009 (or January 1, 2012 for Participants covered by Appendix Article PBG).
- Clarifies that severance-related additional benefits are not permanent features of the Plan.
- Interpretation: Capitalized terms follow definitions in this appendix or the main Plan unless context dictates otherwise.
- Key definitions:
  - Applicable Summary Plan Description: The SPD detailing a specific Severance Program.
  - Covered Participant: A Participant whose employment is terminated and who is eligible for Special Early Retirement either under a Severance Program (per the Applicable SPD) or under an Individual Severance Agreement.

nodes.title: Scope.
nodes.heading: E.1 Scope .
nodes.start_phrase: This Article E sets forth the time and form of payment provisions that apply to benefits under the Plan that are paid to a Covered Participant (as defined in Section E.2 below).
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article E governs the time and form of payment of benefits made during severance windows under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Scope: Applies to benefits paid to “Covered Participants” whose employment is terminated in a Severance Program or under an Individual Severance Agreement and who qualify for Special Early Retirement.
- Effective dates: Applies to terminations on or after January 1, 2009; for Participants covered by Appendix Article PBG, on or after January 1, 2012.
- Non-permanence: Clarifies that any additional benefits provided under Severance Programs or Individual Severance Agreements are not permanent features of the Plan.
- Definitions provided:
  - “Applicable Summary Plan Description” (SPD) is the SPD that sets the terms for a specific Severance Program.
  - “Covered Participant” is a Participant whose employment is terminated and who is eligible for Special Early Retirement either under a Severance Program per the Applicable SPD or under an Individual Severance Agreement.
- Interpretation: Capitalized terms not defined in Article E use the meanings from the main Plan unless context requires otherwise.

nodes.title: Definitions:
nodes.heading: E.2 Definitions :
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this Appendix E with initial capitals, they shall have the meaning set forth below unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
nodes.summary:
- Document scope: Appendix Article E of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program sets the time and form of payment rules for benefits paid during severance windows to certain terminated participants. It applies to terminations qualifying under a Severance Program or an Individual Severance Agreement on or after January 1, 2009 (or January 1, 2012 for those covered by Appendix Article PBG). It clarifies that any additional severance-related benefits are not permanent plan features.
- Key definitions:
  - Applicable Summary Plan Description: The SPD governing a specific Severance Program.
  - Covered Participant: A participant whose employment ends and who qualifies for Special Early Retirement via a Severance Program (per the applicable SPD) or an Individual Severance Agreement.
  - Individual Severance Agreement: A company-participant agreement detailing termination terms and either confirming Special Early Retirement eligibility under PEP or specifying pension benefits tied to the termination.
  - Kicker: The Special Early Retirement benefit equal to (early retirement benefit under the Salaried Plan and this Plan as of the Termination Date) minus (the vested pension under the Salaried Plan and this Plan as of the Termination Date). It is split into:
    - PEP Kicker: Replaces benefits that could have been earned under this Plan absent early separation.
    - Qualified Kicker: Replaces benefits that could have been earned under the Salaried Plan absent early separation.
    - Early retirement reduction factors for ages before 55 use the 56-to-55 monthly reduction rate unless a Severance Program uses a different factor in the Salaried Plan or an Individual Severance Agreement specifies otherwise.
  - Severance Program: As defined in Appendix Section ERW.2(f) of Part B of the Salaried Plan (legacy PepsiCo Appendix).
  - Special Early Retirement: Retirement meeting the SPD’s special early retirement conditions or expressly recognized in an Individual Severance Agreement.
  - Termination Date: The later of the Separation from Service or the projected end of any authorized severance leave under the applicable SPD or Individual Severance Agreement, determined using the formulas in effect when the legally binding right to special early retirement benefits arises (or as set by the Plan Administrator if special early retirement does not apply). Once set, it generally does not change after separation unless expressly provided.
- Payment rules for 409A Pension (excluding the Kicker for this section):
  - Non-retirement-eligible at Separation: Paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), following the form-of-payment rules in Section 6.2.
  - Retirement-eligible at Separation: If eligible for Normal, Early, or Late Retirement under Article IV, paid as a Retirement Pension (details continue beyond the provided text).

nodes.title: Time and Form of Payment for 409A Pension:
nodes.heading: E.3 Time and Form of Payment for 409A Pension :
nodes.start_phrase: If a Covered Participant is not eligible for Retirement as of his Separation from Service, the Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be paid as a V ested Pension under Section 6.1(b) according to the form of payment provisions applicable to V ested Pensions under Section 6.2.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how a Participant’s Termination Date is determined when severance leave-of-absence formulas apply: it is set as of the Separation from Service date using formulas in the Applicable Summary Plan Description (SPD) or Individual Severance Agreement tied to special early retirement rights, or by the Plan Administrator if special early retirement doesn’t apply. Once set, the Termination Date does not change after Separation unless expressly provided in the SPD or Individual Severance Agreement.
- Defines timing and form of payment for a Covered Participant’s 409A Pension (calculated without the Kicker for this section):
  - Non-retirement eligible at Separation: paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), with form of payment per Section 6.2.
  - Retirement eligible (Normal, Early, or Late) at Separation: paid as a Retirement Pension under Section 6.1(a)(1), or per a valid prior payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2) if one exists.
  - Becomes Normal/Early retirement eligible after Separation (including during paid leave of absence): paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), form per Section 6.2.
  - Special Early Retirement eligible at Separation or becomes so during paid leave window: paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), form per Section 6.2.
- Sets timing and form of payment for Kicker benefits:
  - PEP Kicker: paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the later of the Participant’s 55th birthday or Separation from Service; a valid Prior Payment Election under Section 6.1(a)(2) controls even if the 409A Pension is paid as a Vested Pension under E.3(b)(2).
  - References both PEP Kicker and Qualified Kicker, though only the PEP Kicker payment details appear in the excerpt; a death-related provision begins but is truncated.

nodes.title: Time and Form of Payment of Kicker Benefits:
nodes.heading: E.4 Time and Form of Payment of Kicker Benefits :
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant’ s PEP Kicker shall be paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’ s 55 birthday , or (ii) the Participant’ s Separation from Service; provided, however , that if the Participant made a valid Prior Payment Election under Section 6.1(a)(2), the Participant’ s PEP Kicker shall be paid according to such election (even in cases where the Participant’ s 409A Pension is paid according to Section E.3(b)(2) above).
nodes.summary:
- Defines how a Covered Participant’s 409A Pension is paid when retirement eligibility (Normal, Early, or Special Early) is reached after Separation from Service, including during any paid leave period:
  - If a valid prior payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2) exists, the 409A Pension is paid as a Retirement Pension per that election.
  - Otherwise, the 409A Pension is paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), following the form-of-payment rules in Section 6.2.
  - Special Early Retirement eligibility at or after Separation also results in payment as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) and Section 6.2.

- Sets timing and form of “Kicker” benefits:
  - PEP Kicker: Paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the later of age 55 or Separation from Service; if a valid prior payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2) applies, it governs. If the participant dies after qualifying but before payment, it is paid in a single lump sum 60 days after death to the Surviving Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, or otherwise to the estate.
  - Qualified Kicker: Paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month on or after the Termination Date, unless an Applicable Summary Plan Description or Individual Severance Agreement specifies a different time and/or form, in which case those terms control. Death benefits mirror the PEP Kicker rules.

- Requires a payment delay for “Key Employees” for any payments triggered by Separation from Service, in accordance with Section 6.6, unless an exemption from Section 409A applies.

nodes.title: Delay for Key Employees:
nodes.heading: E.5 Delay for Key Employees :
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding any provision of this Appendix E to the contrary , if a Participant is determined to be a Key Employee, any payment under this Article E that is made on account of his Separation from Service shall be subject to the required delay in payment for Key Employees under Section 6.6, except to the extent that the payment qualifies for an exemption from the application of Section 409A.
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines payment rules under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (409A Program) for “PEP Kicker” and “Qualified Kicker” benefits. If a participant dies after qualifying but before payment, both kickers are paid in a single lump sum 60 days after death to the surviving spouse or eligible domestic partner, or otherwise to the estate. The Qualified Kicker is generally paid as a lump sum on the first day of the month coincident with or following the participant’s termination date, unless an applicable summary plan description or individual severance agreement specifies a different time or form. Additionally, if the participant is a “Key Employee,” any payment triggered by separation from service is delayed per Section 6.6 to comply with Section 409A, unless an exemption applies.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE F - U.K. Supplementary Appendix Participants with U.S. Service
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE F - 
U.K. Supplementary Appendix Participants with U.S. Service
nodes.start_phrase: This Article applies to “Covered U.K. Employees” as defined in Section F .2 below .
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article F covers the U.K. Supplementary Appendix for participants with U.S. service within the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Scope (F.1): Applies to “Covered U.K. Employees” (defined in F.2). Benefits for such employees are determined under Section F.3, then paid per the Plan’s normal timing and form. All benefits are subject to Internal Revenue Code section 409A. The Article was restated effective January 1, 2016; the original version was effective January 1, 2011 for service before 2016.
- Definition of “Covered U.K. Employee” (F.2): A participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan who:
  - Becomes subject to U.S. income tax by engaging in U.S. service (e.g., transfer to a U.S. role).
  - Continues accruing benefits under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan after beginning U.S. service.
  - Would have accrued benefits under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix for that period but for the unavailability of accruals during U.S. service.
  - Subsequently either (A) is localized in the U.S. as a PepsiCo employee, or (B) terminates employment with PepsiCo before starting an assignment outside the U.S.
  - After satisfying these conditions, is designated accordingly (designation text continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Scope:
nodes.heading: F.1 Scope:
nodes.start_phrase: This Article applies to “Covered U.K. Employees” as defined in Section F .2 below .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Appendix Article F of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program for U.K. participants who have U.S. service.
- Scope (F.1): Applies to “Covered U.K. Employees”; benefits are determined under Section F.3, then paid under the Plan’s standard time and form rules; all benefits are subject to Internal Revenue Code section 409A; the Article is restated effective January 1, 2016 (originally effective January 1, 2011 for pre‑2016 service).
- Definition (F.2): A “Covered U.K. Employee” is a participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan who:
  - Becomes subject to U.S. income taxes by transferring to a U.S. role or otherwise (“Engages in U.S. Service”),
  - Continues accruing benefits under the U.K. Pension Plan after engaging in U.S. Service,
  - Would have accrued under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix for that period but for the unavailability of accruals during U.S. Service,
  - Subsequently either becomes localized in the U.S. as a PepsiCo employee or terminates employment before starting any assignment outside the U.S.,
  - And, after satisfying these conditions, is designated by the company (designation language truncated).
- Indicates that benefit determination specifics are in Section F.3 (not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: “Covered U.K. Employee” Defined:
nodes.heading: F.2 “Covered U.K. Employee” Defined :
nodes.start_phrase: A “Covered U.K. Employee” is a participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan (“U.K. Participant”) who – (i) becomes subject to United States income taxes, e.g., by transferring to a position with the Company in the United States or otherwise (hereinafter referenced as “Engages in U.S. Service”), (ii) continues to accrue benefits under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan after he Engages in U.S. Service, (iii) would have also accrued a benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix for such period following when he Engages in U.S. Service (except for the unavailability of accruals under such Appendix for the period a U.K. Participant Engages in U.S. Service), (iv) subsequently either – (A) is localized in the United States as an employee of the PepsiCo Organization, or (B) terminates employment with the PepsiCo Organization (provided this occurs before the date the U.K. Participant commences an assignment with the PepsiCo Organization that is located outside the United States, as defined in the Code), and (v) only after fully satisfying all of the preceding clauses, is then designated by the Company (in its completely unfettered discretion) as a Covered U.K. Employee and thereby granted a legally binding right to a benefit under this Article F at the time of the designation.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Establishes special pension equalization rules (Article F) for certain participants in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan who become subject to U.S. income tax (“U.S. Service”). Benefits are paid under normal plan timing/form and are subject to Internal Revenue Code section 409A. Article F was restated effective January 1, 2016 (originally effective January 1, 2011 for pre‑2016 service).
- Covered U.K. Employee definition: A U.K. Participant who (i) becomes subject to U.S. income taxes (Engages in U.S. Service), (ii) continues accruing under the U.K. Pension Plan during U.S. Service, (iii) would have accrued under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix but for accrual unavailability during U.S. Service, (iv) then either is localized in the U.S. or terminates PepsiCo employment before starting an assignment outside the U.S., and (v) after satisfying all prior conditions, is affirmatively designated by the Company, in its sole discretion, and granted a legally binding right to an Article F benefit.
- Key timing definitions: 
  - U.S. Commencement Date: first day the participant becomes subject to U.S. income taxes.
  - U.S. Cessation Date: when no longer subject to U.S. income taxes or, if earlier, when Article F benefits commence.
- Benefit determination: Calculated as of the Modified U.S. Cessation Date by taking the Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit minus the Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit.
  - Modified U.S. Cessation Date: earliest of (i) date no longer subject to U.S. taxes, (ii) date first localized in the U.S. or terminates employment (per clause iv), (iii) date an assignment outside the U.S. begins, or (iv) date Article F benefits commence.
  - Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit: the total benefit that would be payable under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix based on all service and compensation counted under the U.K. Pension Plan through the Modified U.S. Cessation Date (including amounts limited only by U.K. law), expressed as a single lump sum payable at the Article F benefit commencement date.
  - Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit: referenced as an offset; its definition is not included in the excerpt.
- Administration notes: Company designation as a Covered U.K. Employee is entirely discretionary; once determined, benefits are paid under standard plan rules and in compliance with section 409A.

nodes.title: Benefit for Covered U.K. Employees:
nodes.heading: F.3 Benefit for Covered U.K. Employees :
nodes.start_phrase: A Covered U.K. Employee’ s benefit under the Plan shall be determined by calculating, as of his Modified U.S. Cessation Date, his “T otal U.K. Supplementary Benefit” and then subtracting from this amount his “Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit.”
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article F of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program addressing special pension equalization benefits for U.K. employees designated, at the Company’s sole discretion, as “Covered U.K. Employees” while they engage in U.S. Service.
- U.S. Service timing: Defines U.S. Commencement Date (first day subject to U.S. income tax) and U.S. Cessation Date (when no longer subject to U.S. income tax or, if earlier, when Article F benefits commence).
- Benefit formula: As of the Modified U.S. Cessation Date, the Article F benefit equals the Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit minus the Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit, both expressed as single lump sums payable at the Article F benefit commencement date.
- Modified U.S. Cessation Date triggers: Earliest of (i) no longer subject to U.S. income taxes, (ii) first meeting a specified condition in Section F.2(iv), (iii) starting an assignment outside the U.S., or (iv) commencement of Article F benefits.
- Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit: The total benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix based on all service and compensation with the Company through the Modified U.S. Cessation Date that counts (or would count but for U.K. legal limits) under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan, converted to a lump sum as of Article F benefit commencement.
- Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit: The accrued benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date, valued as a lump sum as of Article F benefit commencement.
- Operating rules on offsets: Generally, accruals in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan after the U.S. Cessation Date do not reduce Article F benefits; however, any excess post-Cessation accruals that more than fully offset Supplementary Appendix accruals may offset Article F benefits to the extent permitted under Internal Revenue Code Section 409A.
- Valuation standards: Lump-sum values under Article F must be determined using actuarial assumptions that comply with the referenced section (aligned with Section 409A requirements).

nodes.title: Operating Rules:
nodes.heading: F.4 Operating Rules:
nodes.start_phrase: The following operating rules apply to the calculation in Section F .3. above.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit” as the single-sum value of the participant’s benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date, payable when Article F benefits begin, and calculated under Section F.4.
- Operating rules for calculating the Article F benefit:
  - Post–U.S. Cessation Date accruals in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan generally do not reduce the Article F benefit; however, any excess offset that would have applied under the U.K. Supplementary Appendix can reduce the Article F benefit, to the extent compliant with IRC Section 409A.
  - Lump-sum values must use IRC Section 417(e) actuarial assumptions as applied under the Salaried Plan on the relevant determination date.
  - The Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit is determined assuming the employee voluntarily terminated all PepsiCo service immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date.
  - Mid-year amendments to the U.K. plans that would change the Section F.3 calculation are deferred to take effect prospectively the following year if needed to comply with Section 409A.
  - If an individual returns to U.S. service and again qualifies as a Covered U.K. Employee, Article F terms are reapplied; any new benefit is reduced by the lump-sum value of prior Article F benefits to prevent duplication.
  - If later covered by other plan provisions instead of Article F, any new benefit under those provisions is reduced by the prior Article F lump-sum value to avoid duplication.
- No Other Benefits: While classified (or but for specific clauses would be classified) as a Covered U.K. Employee, the individual is not entitled to other benefits under this Plan or the Salaried Plan; before all requirements are met to be a Covered U.K. Employee, there is no legally binding right to an Article F benefit, and the Company may in its discretion prevent entitlement (e.g., by not designating the individual).

nodes.title: No Other Benefits :
nodes.heading: F.5 No Other Benefits :
nodes.start_phrase: A Covered U.K. Employee shall not be entitled to any other benefits under this Plan or the Salaried Plan while he is a Covered U.K. Employee (or while he would be a Covered U.K. Employee if clauses (iv) and (v) of Section F .2. were not included in the definition of Covered U.K. Employee).
nodes.summary:
- Coordination of benefits after status change: If a Covered U.K. Employee has already earned an Article F benefit, reaches their U.S. Cessation Date, and later returns to a role eligible under other plan provisions, the “Other Provisions” apply for the new service period, but any new benefit is offset by the lump-sum value of the prior Article F benefit to prevent double-counting.
- No concurrent plan benefits: While someone is a Covered U.K. Employee (or would be but for specified clauses in Section F.2), they are not entitled to any other benefits under this Plan or the Salaried Plan.
- No vested right before requirements met: Until an individual satisfies all conditions to be a Covered U.K. Employee, they have no legally binding right to an Article F benefit.
- Company discretion: The Company may, at its sole discretion and at any time before the status is achieved, take actions (including declining to designate the individual as a Covered U.K. Employee) that prevent entitlement to an Article F benefit, regardless of services performed or other factors.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE G - Delay Election For Certain Pre-2018 Terminees
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE G -
Delay Election For Certain Pre-2018 T erminees
nodes.start_phrase: This Article provides an opportunity for certain Participants, who Separated from Service before January 1, 2018 and who are eligible to receive a 409A V ested Pension, to make a one-time election to delay the distribution of their 409A V ested Pension as permitted by Code section 409A(a)(4)(C).
nodes.summary: Appendix Article G of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program outlines a one-time “Delay Election” for certain participants who separated from service before January 1, 2018 and are eligible for a 409A Vested Pension. Effective January 1, 2018 and permitted under IRC §409A(a)(4)(C), this provision allows deferral of the pension’s distribution. Eligibility requires: (a) separation before January 1, 2018; (b) a Scheduled Payment Date (as determined by the Plan Administrator) that is at least 12 months after the date the participant will make the election; and (c) selection and notification by the Company in its sole discretion. To be valid, the election must become fully effective and irrevocable at least 12 months before the previously scheduled payment date and must specify a new payment commencement date at least five years later than the original Scheduled Payment Date (with the sentence appearing truncated before any upper limit is stated).

nodes.title: Scope :
nodes.heading: G.1 Scope :
nodes.start_phrase: This Article provides an opportunity for certain Participants, who Separated from Service before January 1, 2018 and who are eligible to receive a 409A V ested Pension, to make a one-time election to delay the distribution of their 409A V ested Pension as permitted by Code section 409A(a)(4)(C).
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article G establishes a one-time Delay Election, effective January 1, 2018, allowing certain Participants who separated from service before January 1, 2018 and are eligible for a 409A Vested Pension to defer distribution under Code section 409A(a)(4)(C).
- Eligibility requires: (a) separation from service before January 1, 2018; (b) a Scheduled Payment Date (as determined by the Plan Administrator) that is at least 12 months after the date of election; and (c) selection and notification by the Company, in its sole discretion, to make the Delay Election.
- To be effective, the Delay Election must: (a) become fully effective and irrevocable at least 12 months before the previously scheduled payment date; and (b) set a new payment commencement date at least five years later than the original Scheduled Payment Date (with an upper limit not shown in the excerpt).
- This appendix pertains to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

nodes.title: Eligibility for Making a Delay Election .
nodes.heading: G.2 Eligibility for Making a Delay Election .
nodes.start_phrase: To be eligible to make a Delay Election, a Participant must:
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article G of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program establishes a one-time “Delay Election” for certain participants who terminated employment before January 1, 2018 and are eligible for a 409A Vested Pension, allowing them to defer distribution in accordance with IRC section 409A(a)(4)(C). Effective January 1, 2018.
- Eligibility criteria:
  - Separated from service prior to January 1, 2018.
  - Eligible for a 409A Vested Pension with a Scheduled Payment Date (as determined by the Plan Administrator) that is at least 12 months after the date the election is made.
  - Selected and notified by the Company, in its sole discretion, to make the Delay Election.
- Election requirements:
  - Must become fully effective and irrevocable at least 12 months before the previously scheduled payment date.
  - Must set a new payment commencement date at least five years later than the prior Scheduled Payment Date (the excerpt notes an additional “not later than …” limit but is cut off).

nodes.title: Requirements for Making a Delay Election
nodes.heading: G.3 Requirements for Making a Delay Election
nodes.start_phrase: To be ef fective, a request for a Delay Election must:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes a one-time “Delay Election” for certain participants who separated from service before January 1, 2018 and are eligible for a 409A Vested Pension, allowing them to defer distribution under IRC 409A(a)(4)(C); effective January 1, 2018.
- Eligibility requires: (a) separation before 1/1/2018; (b) a Scheduled Payment Date at least 12 months after the election is made; and (c) selection and notification by the Company in its sole discretion.
- Election requirements: must become fully effective and irrevocable at least 12 months before the existing Scheduled Payment Date, and must set a New Scheduled Payment Date at least 5 years later than the original date, but no later than the first of the month on or after the participant’s 65th birthday.
- No change to form of payment permitted through the Delay Election, except: (a) annuity form is determined by marital status as of the New Scheduled Payment Date; and (b) any early commencement reduction is determined relative to the New Scheduled Payment Date.
- Benefits subject to a valid Delay Election remain subject to the Plan’s cashout provisions in Section 4.9.

nodes.title: No Change in Form
nodes.heading: G.4 No Change in Form
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant is not permitted to use a Delay Election to change the form of payment of his or her distribution, except that:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the “New Scheduled Payment Date,” defined as no later than the first day of the month coincident with or immediately following the participant’s 65th birthday.
- Clarifies that a Delay Election cannot change the form of payment, with two exceptions:
  - The form of annuity is determined by the participant’s marital status as of the New Scheduled Payment Date (per Section 6.3(c)).
  - Any early commencement reduction is calculated by reference to the New Scheduled Payment Date (per Section 5.1(b)).
- States that benefits subject to a Delay Election remain subject to the plan’s cashout distribution rules in Section 4.9.
- Identifies the context as part of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

nodes.title: Cashout Provisions Not Superseded .
nodes.heading: G.5 Cashout Provisions Not Superseded .
nodes.start_phrase: A benefit to which an ef fective Delay Election applies remains subject to the cashout distribution provisions in Section 4.9.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “New Scheduled Payment Date,” tied to the first of the month on or immediately after the participant’s 65th birthday, in the context of a Delay Election.
- States that a Delay Election cannot change the form of benefit payment, with two clarifications:
  - The annuity form is determined by the participant’s marital status as of the New Scheduled Payment Date (per Section 6.3(c)).
  - Any early commencement reduction is calculated by reference to the New Scheduled Payment Date (per Section 5.1(b)).
- Confirms that benefits subject to a valid Delay Election remain subject to the plan’s cashout distribution rules in Section 4.9.
- Applies to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE H – Definitions of Eligible Domestic Partner Applicable Prior to January 1, 2019
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE H –
Definitions of Eligible Domestic Partner Applicable Prior to January 1, 2019
nodes.start_phrase: This Article H provides the definition of Eligible Domestic Partner for periods prior to January 1, 2019.
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article H defines “Eligible Domestic Partner” for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program for periods prior to January 1, 2019.
- H.1 (Scope): Clarifies the article applies only to pre‑2019 periods.
- H.2 (Definition framework): Explains that different paragraphs govern different date ranges; paragraph e will contain general rules and paragraph f defined terms (not shown in the excerpt).
- Jan 1, 2016–Dec 31, 2018: The Plan does not recognize Eligible Domestic Partner status due to the 2015 Supreme Court decision recognizing a constitutional right to same‑sex marriage.
- Limited 2016 exception: For 2016 only, a participant with a domestic partner or civil union in place as of Dec 31, 2015 (as defined in a subsequent paragraph) and who was an employee (actively employed or on authorized leave) or participant during the 2015 Plan Year may have that individual treated as an Eligible Domestic Partner for applicable 2016 dates.
- Jun 26, 2013–Dec 31, 2015: Provides rules (partially shown) addressing civil unions for participants residing in states that did not permit same‑sex marriage; the detailed criteria are truncated in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Scope .
nodes.heading: H.1 Scope .
nodes.start_phrase: This Article H provides the definition of Eligible Domestic Partner for periods prior to January 1, 2019.
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article H sets definitions and rules for who qualifies as an “Eligible Domestic Partner” under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program for periods prior to January 1, 2019.
- H.1 (Scope) limits the applicability to pre-2019 periods.
- H.2 (Definition) structures the rules by:
  - Date-specific provisions in paragraphs a–d,
  - General rules in paragraph e,
  - Defined terms in paragraph f.
- January 1, 2016–December 31, 2018: The Plan does not recognize Eligible Domestic Partner status due to the 2015 Supreme Court ruling on same-sex marriage.
  - Limited 2016 Plan Year exception: If a participant had a qualifying domestic partner or civil union as of December 31, 2015, and was an active employee/on authorized leave or a participant during the 2015 Plan Year, that partner could be treated as an Eligible Domestic Partner for applicable dates in 2016.
- June 26, 2013–December 31, 2015: Begins to outline provisions for civil unions, including scenarios where the participant resides in a state that did not permit same-sex marriage (full details continue beyond the excerpt).
- The excerpt emphasizes conditions such as the participant’s residency, the validity of the relationship on the applicable date, and employment/participation status.

nodes.title: Definition of Eligible Domestic Partner .
nodes.heading: H.2 Definition of Eligible Domestic Partner .
nodes.start_phrase: Paragraphs a, b, c and d are ef fective for the dates indicated in the paragraph.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Appendix Article H defines “Eligible Domestic Partner” for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program for periods before January 1, 2019, with dated provisions, general rules, and defined terms.

- 2016–2018: Domestic partner status not recognized due to the 2015 Supreme Court decision on same-sex marriage. Limited 2016 exception for Participants who, as of December 31, 2015, had a qualifying same-sex domestic partner or civil union relationship under prior plan rules and were active employees/on authorized leave or plan participants during 2015.

- June 26, 2013–December 31, 2015:
  - If the Participant resides in a state that does not permit same-sex marriage but does permit same-sex civil unions, an Eligible Domestic Partner is the individual in a valid same-sex civil union; no eligibility unless in such a union.
  - If the state permits neither same-sex marriage nor civil unions, eligibility may be based on a legally binding same-sex domestic partner agreement meeting Company requirements; without such an agreement, no eligibility.

- January 1, 2013–June 25, 2013:
  - Includes individuals qualifying as above, plus spouses in valid same-sex marriages (recognized where entered).
  - If residing in a state permitting same-sex marriage, Eligible Domestic Partner status is allowed only if in a valid same-sex marriage, unless that state began permitting such marriages less than 12 months before the applicable date.

- Pre-2013: No Eligible Domestic Partner status under the plan.

- Additional rules (apply notwithstanding the dated provisions):
  - Opposite-sex partners are not Eligible Domestic Partners.
  - Participants residing in states permitting same-sex marriage are not permitted to have an Eligible Domestic Partner (must marry to qualify), with a 12-month transition rule for newly permitting states (for dates prior to 2016).
  
- Defined terms:
  - “Applicable date” is the earlier of the Participant’s annuity starting date or date of death.
  - “State” includes any domestic or foreign jurisdiction with authority to sanction marriages or civil unions.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE I – 409A PEP Makeup for Certain Pre-409A Benefits
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE I –
409A PEP Makeup for Certain Pre-409A Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: To ensure there will be no “material modification” of the Pre-409A Program, this Article provides a makeup benefit under the 409A Program that applies to certain participants in the Pre-409A Program (“Pre-409A Participants”) in lieu of updating the Pre-409A Program’ s actuarial factors for early commencement of Vested Pensions to be consistent with the “2019 Salaried Program Factors” (as that term is defined in the definition of Actuarial Equivalent).
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Establishes a “makeup” benefit within the 409A Program for certain participants in the legacy Pre-409A Program to avoid a “material modification” of that legacy program. The makeup substitutes for updating the Pre-409A Program’s early retirement actuarial reduction factors to match the “2019 Salaried Program Factors” used for Actuarial Equivalence.
- Coordination with main plan: For individuals who participate in both the Pre-409A and 409A Programs, the early commencement reduction makeup for vested annuity pensions is already provided under the main plan text. This appendix supplies the makeup only for affected Pre-409A Participants who would not otherwise receive a 409A Program benefit.
- Eligibility (as outlined in the excerpt):
  - Must be a Pre-409A Participant receiving a Pre-409A “Vested Pension.”
  - The pension must be paid as an annuity starting before the participant’s Normal Retirement Date, with a commencement date on or after January 1, 2019.
  - The annuity must be subject to an early commencement reduction under the Pre-409A Program (additional specifics continue beyond the excerpt).
- Overall intent: Preserve Section 409A compliance and benefit parity for early annuity commencements by delivering a targeted makeup benefit rather than altering the legacy plan’s actuarial factors.

nodes.title: Scope:
nodes.heading: I.1 Scope:
nodes.start_phrase: To ensure there will be no “material modification” of the Pre-409A Program, this Article provides a makeup benefit under the 409A Program that applies to certain participants in the Pre-409A Program (“Pre-409A Participants”) in lieu of updating the Pre-409A Program’ s actuarial factors for early commencement of Vested Pensions to be consistent with the “2019 Salaried Program Factors” (as that term is defined in the definition of Actuarial Equivalent).
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Appendix Article I of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program to provide a “makeup” benefit for certain Pre‑409A Participants.
- Purpose: avoid a “material modification” of the Pre‑409A Program by not updating its early commencement actuarial factors; instead, a 409A Program makeup offsets early retirement reductions to align outcomes with the 2019 Salaried Program Factors.
- Application: 
  - If a participant is in both the Pre‑409A and 409A Programs, the makeup is provided under the main plan text.
  - If a participant is only in the Pre‑409A Program and otherwise not entitled to 409A benefits, this Article grants the makeup.
- Eligibility (as described in the excerpt):
  - Must be a Pre‑409A Participant receiving a Pre‑409A “Vested Pension” as an annuity starting before the Normal Retirement Date, on or after January 1, 2019.
  - The annuity must be reduced for early commencement under the Pre‑409A Program’s terms (further details continue beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Eligibility Under This Article :
nodes.heading: I.2 Eligibility Under This Article :
nodes.start_phrase: To be eligible under this Article, an individual must be a Pre-409A Participant:
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Establishes a “makeup” benefit under the 409A Program to avoid materially modifying the Pre‑409A Program by not updating its early retirement actuarial factors. Instead, for certain Pre‑409A Participants, the plan provides a 409A makeup amount that aligns outcomes with the “2019 Salaried Program Factors.”
- Interaction with main plan: If a Pre‑409A Participant is also otherwise a participant in the 409A Program, the makeup is handled in the main plan text; this Article applies to affected Pre‑409A Participants who would not otherwise receive a 409A benefit.
- Eligibility criteria:
  - The individual is a Pre‑409A Participant receiving a Vested Pension annuity that starts before Normal Retirement Date but on or after January 1, 2019.
  - The early commencement reduction applied under the Pre‑409A Program is greater than it would be using the 2019 Salaried Program Factors.
  - The individual does not otherwise have a 409A Pension payable on or after January 1, 2019 (either because they are only entitled to a Pre‑409A Pension, or any 409A Pension began before January 1, 2019).
  - Such individuals are defined as “Eligible Persons.”
- Benefit amount and form:
  - Paid as a single lump sum.
  - Calculated as the Actuarial Equivalent of the difference between:
    1) The Single Life Annuity the person would receive if the 2019 Salaried Program Factors applied to their Pre‑409A Vested Pension (including any portion from the PEP Guarantee), and
    2) The Single Life Annuity actually payable under the Pre‑409A Program using its existing early commencement factors.

nodes.title: Benefit Amount Under This Article :
nodes.heading: I.3 Benefit Amount Under This Article :
nodes.start_phrase: The benefit amount for an Eligible Person under this Article shall be the single lump sum that is the Actuarial Equivalent of the dif ference between:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes who qualifies as an “Eligible Person” under the Article: individuals whose early commencement reduction under the Pre‑409A Program would be smaller if the 2019 Salaried Program early commencement factors applied, and who otherwise would not have a 409A Pension payable on or after January 1, 2019 because their only PEP Pension is a Pre‑409A Pension or their 409A Pension already began before January 1, 2019.
- Defines the benefit as a single lump sum equal to the actuarial equivalent of the difference between:
  - The Single Life Annuity the person would receive under the Pre‑409A Program if the 2019 Salaried Program early commencement factors applied (including any portion from the PEP Guarantee), and
  - The actual Single Life Annuity payable under the Pre‑409A Program using the then‑applicable early commencement factors (including any PEP Guarantee portion).
- Specifies the valuation timing: the lump sum is calculated as of the applicable commencement date; if that date is December 1, 2019 but the individual’s actual Pre‑409A Annuity Starting Date is earlier, the amount is determined at that earlier date and rolled forward with actuarial equivalent interest to December 1, 2019.
- Clarifies that only the new 2019 Salaried Program Factors effective January 1, 2019 are used—no alternative pre‑2019 factors.
- Sets payment timing: the lump sum is payable on the latest of (i) the first of the month following Separation from Service or (ii) December 1, 2019 (additional items may follow beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Time of Payment Under This Article :
nodes.heading: I.4 Time of Payment Under This Article :
nodes.start_phrase: The lump sum benefit calculated under this Appendix shall be payable as of the Eligible Person’ s applicable commencement date, which is the latest of the following:
nodes.summary:
- Defines how to calculate an Actuarial Equivalent lump-sum “make-up” benefit under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program for participants whose Pre-409A Pension annuities (with Annuity Starting Dates on or after January 1, 2019) were reduced using pre-2019 factors.
- Calculation rules: lump sum is based on the Single Life Annuity and includes any portion derived from the PEP Guarantee; it uses only the 2019 Salaried Program Factors (no pre-2019 alternatives). The valuation date is the applicable commencement date; if that date is December 1, 2019 but the participant’s actual Pre-409A Annuity Starting Date was earlier, the lump sum is first determined as of that earlier date and then brought forward with Actuarial Equivalent interest to December 1, 2019.
- Time of payment (I.4): the lump sum is payable as of the latest of (a) the first of the month after Separation from Service, (b) December 1, 2019, or (c) the first of the month after age 55 (with the age-55 rule not applying to benefits derived from Article PBG).
- If the commencement date is under (a), actual payment may be delayed per Plan section 6.6(a); interest is added for any delay per section 6.6(c).
- Non-duplication (I.5): the make-up benefit is reduced (but not below zero) to prevent any duplication where a participant’s 409A Pension already provides all or part of the same make-up (e.g., via early retirement reduction factors) or where the Plan Administrator determines duplication would otherwise occur; reductions are made at the Administrator’s discretion to eliminate overlap.

nodes.title: Non-Duplication of Benefits :
nodes.heading: I.5 Non-Duplication of Benefits :
nodes.start_phrase: The foregoing Sections of this Article are intended to provide a make-up benefit under the 409A Program for applying an early commencement reduction under the Pre-409A Program using factors that predate the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors, with respect to a Pre-409A Pension that is paid in the form of an annuity and that has an Annuity Starting Date of January 1, 2019 or later .
nodes.summary:
- Sets an alternative benefit commencement option: the first day of the month after the Eligible Person turns age 55, except for benefits derived from Article PBG.
- Provides that if the applicable commencement date is the one described in subsection (a), actual payment may be delayed under Plan Section 6.6(a), with interest added for the delay per Section 6.6(c).
- Establishes a Non-Duplication of Benefits rule: this Article is intended to provide a make-up benefit under the 409A Program to offset early commencement reductions applied under the Pre-409A Program using factors predating the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors, for Pre-409A Pensions paid as annuities with Annuity Starting Dates on or after January 1, 2019.
- Prohibits duplicative payments: if a participant’s 409A Pension already effectively provides some or all of the makeup (e.g., via early retirement reduction factors) or if granting the makeup would duplicate benefits, the Plan Administrator will reduce the makeup benefit (not below zero) to eliminate duplication; this rule overrides any conflicting plan provisions.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE J - Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE J - 
Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons
nodes.start_phrase: This Article applies to “Covered International Employees” as defined in Section J.2 below .
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines Appendix Article J of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, covering “Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons.” 

- Scope (J.1): Applies to “Covered International Employees,” with benefits determined under Section J.3 and distributed under Section J.4.
- Definitions (J.2): A “Covered International Employee” is an employee of a Designated PepsiCo Affiliate who:
  - Is ineligible to participate in PERP,
  - Would be barred from earning a benefit under PIRP-DB Section 9.14 due to U.S. Person status,
  - Is initially selected by the Vice President based on special circumstances affecting their ability to receive retirement benefits, and
  - Is subsequently determined by the Vice President to be entitled to this status.
  The Vice President has unfettered discretion over these selections and determinations.

The text signals that benefit calculation and distribution rules follow in Sections J.3 and J.4, respectively.

nodes.title: Scope :
nodes.heading: J.1 Scope :
nodes.start_phrase: This Article applies to “Covered International Employees” as defined in Section J.2 below .
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article J covers special pension equalization provisions for “Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons” under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Scope (J.1): Applies to “Covered International Employees.” Their benefits are determined under Section J.3 and distributed under Section J.4.
- Definitions (J.2): A “Covered International Employee” is an employee of a Designated PepsiCo Affiliate who:
  - Is ineligible to participate in PERP,
  - Would be barred from earning a benefit under PIRP-DB by Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB due to U.S. Person status,
  - Is initially selected by the Vice President as eligible based on special circumstances affecting the employee’s ability to receive retirement benefits, and
  - Is subsequently determined by the Vice President to be entitled to Covered International Employee status.
- The Vice President has unfettered discretion over the initial selection and subsequent determination of Covered International Employee status.

nodes.title: Definitions :
nodes.heading: J.2 Definitions :
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this Article J with initial capital letters, they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context:
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Article J governs pension treatment for certain international employees who are U.S. Persons, specifying eligibility, benefit determination, and (by reference) distribution rules.
- Eligibility and key definitions:
  - Covered International Employee: An employee of a non-U.S. Designated PepsiCo Affiliate who is ineligible for PERP, barred from PIRP-DB due to U.S. Person status, initially selected and then formally determined by the Vice President (in unfettered discretion) to be covered. No legally binding right to a benefit exists before the Vice President’s final determination, consistent with Code Sections 409A and 457A.
  - Designated PepsiCo Affiliate: A non-U.S. employing entity designated by the Vice President.
  - PERP and PIRP-DB are defined plan references; Selected International Employee is someone meeting initial criteria but not yet finally determined; U.S. Person status follows PIRP-DB; the Vice President is as defined under PIRP-DB.
- Benefit determination for Covered International Employees:
  - Calculated under the main Plan rules as if the employee were a Plan Participant, including distinctions between Vested vs. Retirement Pension, subject to modifications:
    - Apply benefit factors as if eligible for the Salaried Plan throughout relevant employment (subject to listed modifications).
    - Usual offsets under Section 5.1(a)(2) and (3) (Salaried Pension Plan and Pre-409A Plan) do not apply unless a specific “Reduction Amount” is listed in the Benefit Information Table; if listed, that amount is applied.
    - The PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2) does not apply.
    - If a “Service Start Date” is specified in the Benefit Information Table, it overrides actual service start for pension calculations.
- Distribution provisions are to be applied under Section J.4 (not included in the excerpt).
- Administrative notes: Final coverage determination is made in conjunction with the employee’s retirement and not before the year of the Section J.4 distribution date.

nodes.title: Benefit for Covered International Employees :
nodes.heading: J.3 Benefit for Covered International Employees :
nodes.start_phrase: A Covered International Employee’ s benefit under the Plan shall be determined by calculating the Pension to which he would be entitled under the main part of the Plan (which shall include treating the Covered International Employee as a Plan Participant and reflecting the dif ferences in the calculation of a Participant’ s Pension that is a Vested Pension versus a Retirement Pension), but giving ef fect to the following modifications.
nodes.summary:
- Defines how benefits for Covered International Employees are calculated under the Plan, using the main plan rules (including treatment as a Plan Participant and distinctions between Vested vs. Retirement Pension), with specific modifications.
- Modifications include:
  - Apply benefit-determining factors tied to the Salaried Plan as if the employee were always eligible, unless otherwise modified.
  - Standard offsets under Section 5.1(a)(2) and (3) do not apply unless a specific “Reduction Amount” is listed; if listed, the reduction equals that amount.
  - The PEP Guarantee formula (Section 5.2) does not apply.
  - If a “Service Start Date” is listed, service before that date is disregarded.
  - If an “Earnings Start Date” is listed, earnings before that date are disregarded.
  - If a “Minimum Lump Sum” is listed, the lump-sum value of the Pension will not be less than that amount.
- Benefit Information Table entry provided for GPID 01170077: no Reduction Amount, no special Service/Earnings Start Dates, and a Minimum Lump Sum of $1,126,465.
- Distribution timing and form: paid as a Single Lump Sum on the first day of the month coincident with or following Separation from Service, subject to the key employee delay rules in Section 6.6.
- Section J.5 “Operating Rules” is cited but its content is not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Time and Form of Distributions :
nodes.heading: J.4 Time and Form of Distributions :
nodes.start_phrase: A Covered International Employee’ s Pension under this Appendix J shall be distributed as a Single Lump Sum on the first day of the month that is coincident with or next follows the Participant’ s Separation from Service, subject to Section 6.6 of the main part of the Plan (delay for Key Employees).
nodes.summary:
- Appendix J sets special rules for Covered International Employees in the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- If a Service Start Date is specified, any service before that date is excluded from pension calculations.
- If an Earnings Start Date is specified, any earnings before that date are excluded from pension calculations.
- If a Minimum Lump Sum is specified, the participant’s pension, when converted to a single lump sum, will not be less than that minimum.
- The Benefit Information Table provides individualized parameters (GPID, Reduction Amount, Service Start Date, Earnings Start Date, Minimum Lump Sum); for GPID 01170077, the Minimum Lump Sum is $1,126,465, with N/A entries for the other fields.
- Distributions are made as a Single Lump Sum on the first day of the month coincident with or next following Separation from Service, subject to a delay for Key Employees under Section 6.6.
