- Section J.5 (Operating Rules) is referenced but not detailed in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Operating Rules:
nodes.heading: J.5 Operating Rules:
nodes.start_phrase: The following operating rules apply to the calculation of a Covered International Employee’ s Pension under this Appendix J.
nodes.summary:
- Appendix J of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program sets rules for Covered International Employees’ pension calculations and payments.
- Service Start Date and Earnings Start Date, if specified, override actual commencement dates; any service or earnings before those indicated dates are excluded from pension calculations.
- If a Minimum Lump Sum is specified, the pension converted to a Single Lump Sum cannot be less than that amount.
- Benefit Information Table defines applicable parameters (GPID, Reduction Amount, Service Start Date, Earnings Start Date, Minimum Lump Sum); shown entry: GPID 01170077 with a Minimum Lump Sum of $1,126,465 and other fields N/A.
- Distribution timing: pension is paid as a Single Lump Sum on the first day of the month coincident with or following Separation from Service, subject to the key employee delay under Section 6.6.
- Actuarial assumptions for lump sum valuation must follow Code Section 417(e) as applied under the Salaried Plan at the determination date.
- Freeze provision: accruals, rights, and benefits under Appendix J are fully frozen effective December 31, 2025, consistent with the Salaried Plan freeze.
- Exclusivity: while designated/covered as an International Employee, the individual is not entitled to other benefits under this Plan, the Salaried Plan, PIRP-DB, or termination indemnity arrangements.

nodes.title: No Other Benefits :
nodes.heading: J.6 No Other Benefits :
nodes.start_phrase: A Designated/Covered International Employee shall not be entitled to any other benefits under this Plan, the Salaried Plan, PIRP-DB or a termination indemnity arrangement while he is a Designated International Employee or a Covered International Employee.
nodes.summary:
- Defines operating rules for calculating a Covered International Employee’s Pension under Appendix J of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Specifies that Single Lump Sum values must be determined using actuarial assumptions compliant with IRC Section 417(e), matching the assumptions the Salaried Plan would use for a retirement lump sum on the applicable determination date.
- States that Covered International Employee pensions are fully subject to the Salaried Plan freeze effective December 31, 2025, with accruals, rights, and benefits frozen to the same extent as under the Salaried Plan.
- Clarifies that while an individual is a Designated or Covered International Employee, they are not entitled to any other benefits under this Plan, the Salaried Plan, PIRP-DB, or any termination indemnity arrangement.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE K - Termination of 409A Program with Respect to Participants Affected by the Tiger Transaction
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE K - 
Termination of 409A Program with Respect to Participants Affected by the T iger T ransaction
nodes.start_phrase: This Article K provides for the termination and liquidation, in accordance with T reasury Regulation § 1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), of the portion of the 409A Program that relates to certain Participants who are af fected by the “Closing” of the “T iger T ransaction” (as those terms are defined below).
nodes.summary: The appendix establishes that, effective upon the Closing of the “Tiger Transaction,” PepsiCo’s 409A Program will be terminated and liquidated for participants affected by that transaction, in compliance with Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B). It defines key terms used in this context: “Affected Participant” (those experiencing a change in control due to the Closing), the “Agreement” (the Unit Purchase Agreement dated August 2, 2021 among PepsiCo, Inc., Bengal Beverages LP, Bengal Debt Merger Sub, LLC, and Naked Juice Co.), and “Closing” (the consummation of the Tiger Transaction per Section 2.3 of the Agreement).

nodes.title: Scope .
nodes.heading: K.1 Scope .
nodes.start_phrase: This Article K provides for the termination and liquidation, in accordance with T reasury Regulation § 1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), of the portion of the 409A Program that relates to certain Participants who are af fected by the “Closing” of the “T iger T ransaction” (as those terms are defined below).
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article K sets terms for terminating and liquidating the portion of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan’s 409A Program that applies to participants affected by the “Tiger Transaction,” in compliance with Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).
- It becomes effective upon the “Closing” of the Tiger Transaction.
- Definitions provided include:
  - “Affected Participant”: a participant who experiences a change in control event under §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B) as a result of the Closing.
  - “Agreement”: the Unit Purchase Agreement dated August 2, 2021 among PepsiCo, Inc., Bengal Beverages LP, Bengal Debt Merger Sub, LLC (a wholly owned subsidiary of the buyer), and Naked Juice Co.
  - “Closing”: the consummation of the Tiger Transaction as described in Section 2.3 of the Agreement.
- Terms not defined in Article K use meanings from the main Plan unless context indicates otherwise.

nodes.title: Definitions .
nodes.heading: K.2 Definitions .
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this Appendix Article K with initial capitals, they shall have the meaning set forth below unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
nodes.summary: Appendix Article K to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program sets out the termination and liquidation of the portion of the 409A Program covering participants affected by the “Tiger Transaction,” effective upon the transaction’s Closing. It defines key terms, including Affected Participant (those experiencing the change in control due to the Closing), the Agreement (the August 2, 2021 Unit Purchase Agreement among PepsiCo, Bengal Beverages LP, Bengal Debt Merger Sub, LLC, and Naked Juice Co.), Closing, Related Amendments (other 409A arrangements treated as a single plan under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(c)(2)), and Tiger Transaction (a change in control under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(i)(5) for certain PepsiCo businesses). Upon Closing, the plan is irrevocably terminated for all Affected Participants pursuant to Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), with all necessary actions deemed taken. Each Affected Participant will receive a single lump-sum payment of their entire interest within 12 months of Closing, determined by treating the participant as having a Separation from Service at Closing and calculating the lump sum as of the selected distribution date within that 12-month period, all in full compliance with Section 409A regulations.

nodes.title: The Termination .
nodes.heading: K.3 The T ermination .
nodes.start_phrase: Contingent only upon the occurrence of the Closing, the 409A Program is hereby irrevocably terminated with respect to all Af fected Participants.
nodes.summary:
- Defines key terms related to a change-in-control program termination, including “Related Amendments” (coordinated terminations of arrangements treated as a single 409A plan) and “Tiger Transaction” (a change in control under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(i)(5) affecting certain PepsiCo businesses).
- Provides for irrevocable termination and liquidation of the 409A Program upon the Closing of the Tiger Transaction for all Affected Participants, with payment of each participant’s entire interest as a single lump sum within 12 months of Closing, treating participants as having a Separation from Service at Closing, in full compliance with Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).
- Merges the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (PBG PEP) into the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan effective December 31, 2011, with PepsiCo PEP as the surviving plan; certain administrative and legal articles from the main plan govern PBG benefits; effective January 1, 2019, optional annuity equivalence adjustments follow main plan rules; merger does not change 409A time/form of payments.
- States plan history and purpose: PBG PEP established April 6, 1999 as successor to PepsiCo PEP following PBG’s IPO; provides nonqualified, unfunded supplemental pension benefits for salaried employees whose qualified plan benefits are limited by IRC §§401(a)(17) and 415, includes pre-1989 formula coverage, and recognizes 2009 provisions for pay deferral offsets (EID) and certain executives.
- Clarifies ERISA status: portion is an “excess benefit plan” (ERISA §4(b)(5)); remainder is a top-hat plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees.
- Explains effect of amendments/restatements: defines the Prior Plan as in effect on October 3, 2004; “Grandfathered Benefit” (pre-2005 accruals) is paid under prior terms; post‑2004 accruals are a separate 409A plan; good‑faith 409A administration from 2005–2008; new terms apply from January 1, 2009 for amounts accrued and vested after 2004.
- Provides comprehensive definitions and construction rules, including Actuarial Equivalent, Annuity, Company, Compensation Limitation, Effective Time (Feb. 26, 2010), EID, Plan Administrator, Primary Social Security Amount (detailed estimation rules), Salaried Plan (Part C), Section 409A, Separation from Service, Single Lump Sum, and a detailed “Specified Employee” identification methodology (including administrative convenience caps and transition rules for 2010–2011) consistent with Treas. Reg. §1.409A-1(i).
- Sets participation criteria: Salaried Plan participants affected by §401(a)(17) or §415 limits; certain EID deferrers (4/1/2009–12/31/2010); individuals who would have been “Grandfathered” but for E3–E8 or MP status as of 3/31/2009; and those with 1988 pensionable earnings ≥ $75,000.
- Details retirement benefit determination:
  - Core PEP Pension equals the excess of a hypothetical Salaried Plan benefit (ignoring §401(a)(17), §415, specified EID exclusions, and certain 2009 “Grandfathered” exclusions) over the actual Salaried Plan benefit, with formulas for same vs. different time/form as the Salaried Plan.
  - PEP Guarantee for eligible high-1988 earners: 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings for first 10 years of Credited Service plus 1% for each additional year, minus 1⅔% of Primary Social Security Amount per year up to 30; includes survivor benefits, early retirement reductions, actuarial equivalence for alternate forms, lump-sum conversion rules, and adjustments for 2009 plan changes.
- Provides adjustment rules: recalculation for rehires; coordination with other specified qualified and nonqualified plans; non‑duplication offsets applied only to the extent 409A‑compliant; ability to recoup overpayments if other plan benefits increase after initial PEP calculation.
- Addresses reemployment after Annuity Starting Date: non‑Grandfathered PEP payments continue; subsequent accruals offset by present value of prior PEP payments.
- Establishes vesting aligned with the Salaried Plan; includes forfeiture/clawback for defined “Misconduct” (e.g., confidentiality breaches, competition, disparagement, insider trading, gross misconduct), with a carve‑out for lawful communications with government authorities.
- Sets death benefits: if death occurs before Annuity Starting Date, pays the incremental death benefit that would apply under the Salaried Plan; non‑Grandfathered portion paid as a Single Lump Sum at death; beneficiaries follow Salaried Plan (including Eligible Domestic Partners for deaths on/after Jan. 1, 2013).
- Specifies distribution rules for non‑Grandfathered benefits:
  - Default: Single Lump Sum upon Separation from Service.
  - Special cohorts: (i) certain 2005–2008 separations paid 1/1/2009; (ii) limited annuity elections (Single Life, 50/75/100% J&S, 10‑Year Certain & Life) if irrevocably elected by 12/31/2008 and retirement age/service conditions met after 7/1/2009; (iii) 2008 reorganization involuntary separations—lump sum at end of “Transition Period.”
  - Specified Employee six‑month delay; payment‑timing administrative safe harbors.
- Clarifies survivor option mechanics: effect of death pre‑/post‑election; permitted age gaps for non‑spouse/domestic partner beneficiaries; beneficiary designation procedures.
- Describes lump‑sum valuation: generally per Salaried Plan’s lump‑sum methodology; for vested pensions before 2012, uses applicable segment rates; special December 2008 interest/mortality for the 2008 reorganization, with a floor of month‑of‑distribution value.
- Provides Section 162(m) deduction‑limit postponement of payments with 6% simple interest during the delay.
- Adds an Appendix for Transferred and Transition Individuals (Article IPO) under the 1999 Employee Programs Agreement: preserves participation, service, compensation, and other benefit‑affecting determinations from the PepsiCo Prior Plan without duplicating benefits.
- Notes a “Special Cases” appendix article (effective January 28, 2002).

nodes.title: Special Cases
nodes.heading: Article B – Special Cases
nodes.start_phrase: This Article B of the Appendix supplements the main portion of the Plan document and is ef fective as of January 28, 2002.
nodes.summary:
- Defines terms by reference to the underlying Agreement: Close of the Distribution Date, Transferred Individual, and Transition Individual.
- Rights of Transferred and Transition Individuals in the spin-off: Transferred Individuals in the PepsiCo Prior Plan automatically become Participants as of the Effective Date; no break in service or credited service for Transferred or Transition Individuals; service, compensation, and other benefit-affecting determinations recognized from the PepsiCo Prior Plan as of the Close of the Distribution Date continue under this Plan, subject to no duplication of benefits; Transition Individuals’ benefits governed by Agreement section 8.02.
- Article B (Special Cases), effective January 28, 2002: Applies to certain highly compensated Band IV hires around that date designated by the SVP of HR for a supplemental retirement benefit. Establishes a “top-up” PEP Pension equal to the hypothetical Salaried Plan benefit without compensation and Section 415 limits as if employment began September 10, 1990, minus (i) the actual Salaried Plan benefit and (ii) deferred, vested benefits under any PepsiCo, affiliates, Tricon, or YUM! qualified/nonqualified defined benefit plans (adjusted for differing commencement dates). Provides a death benefit payable as a single lump sum, reduced by survivor benefits from those other plans. Empowers the Plan Administrator to adjust amounts so the aggregate does not exceed the intended level as if continuous employment from September 10, 1990 to Separation from Service.
- Article C (Transfers To/From PepsiCo, Inc.), applicable only to transfers before February 26, 2010: Supplements/overrides main Plan rules for Participants moving between the Company and PepsiCo, Inc. For transfers to PepsiCo, Inc., the PEP Pension is determined as of the transfer date per Article IV (including the Salaried Plan offset) and becomes payable at Separation from Service per Article VI. For transfers from PepsiCo, Inc., the PEP Pension is determined at Separation from Service per Article IV and reduced by benefits under PepsiCo, Inc. plans based on the same credited service to ensure the total does not exceed what would have been earned if solely employed by the Company.

nodes.title: Transfers From/To PepsiCo, Inc.
nodes.heading: Article C – T ransfers From/T o PepsiCo, Inc.
nodes.start_phrase: The provisions of this Article C shall only apply to transfers that occur before February 26, 2010 and shall not apply to any transfer to PepsiCo, Inc. or from PepsiCo, Inc. that occurs on or after such date.
nodes.summary:
- Article C: Transfers From/To PepsiCo, Inc. (pre–February 26, 2010 only)
  - Scope: Applies only to transfers occurring before February 26, 2010; supplements and overrides the main Plan for participants transferring between the Company and PepsiCo, Inc.
  - Benefit determination for transfers to PepsiCo, Inc.: PEP Pension is calculated as of the transfer date under Article IV, including the Salaried Plan offset, regardless of whether the Salaried Plan benefit is moved to a PepsiCo qualified plan; becomes payable upon Separation from Service per Article VI.
  - Benefit determination for transfers from PepsiCo, Inc.: PEP Pension is calculated at Separation from Service under Article IV and reduced by benefits accrued under PepsiCo qualified or nonqualified plans tied to overlapping credited service, so the combined benefits do not exceed what would have been earned with continuous Company employment. For transfers on/after January 1, 2005, the benefit cannot be less than the Company-only benefit. The Plan Administrator may make adjustments to effect this intent.

- Appendix Article PAC: Guiding Principles for Benefit Plan Committee (PAC) Appointments
  - Scope: Supplements the Plan on appointing PAC members.
  - General eligibility: Must be a PepsiCo Organization employee at Leadership Group 1 or above, able to devote sufficient time, and possess the character and temperament to act prudently and solely in participants’ and beneficiaries’ interests.
  - Additional guidelines: Each member should have benefit plan administration or translatable experience; collectively, the PAC should have ERISA health/welfare and retirement plan expertise; members must be able to evaluate the reasonableness of plan expenses.
  - Candidate identification: The PAC Chair may consult the Controller, CFO, and CHRO to identify qualified candidates.

nodes.title: Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE P AC
Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments
nodes.start_phrase: This Article P AC supplements the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan document with respect to the appointment of the members of the P AC.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt presents Appendix Article PAC, which sets guiding principles for appointing members to PepsiCo’s Benefit Plan Committee (PAC) for the Pension Equalization Plan 409A Program. It covers:
- Scope: supplements the plan document regarding PAC member appointments.
- General eligibility: members must be PepsiCo employees at Leadership Group 1 or higher, able to devote sufficient time, and possess the character to act prudently and solely in participants’ and beneficiaries’ interests.
- Additional membership guidelines: individuals should have experience in benefit plan administration or transferable experience relevant to ERISA; the committee collectively should have expertise across ERISA health, welfare, and retirement plans; and members should be able to evaluate the reasonableness of plan expenses.
- Chair’s process: the PAC Chair may consult internal leaders (Controller, CFO, CHRO) to identify qualified candidates.
- Legal note: the guidelines are advisory for the Chair and do not alter ERISA’s legal standards.

The excerpt then transitions to Exhibit 10.14, introducing the PepsiCo Executive Income Deferral Program (409A) Plan Document, amended and restated effective January 1, 2022.

structure.start_phrase: PepsiCo, Inc. (the “Company”) established the PepsiCo Executive Income Deferral Program (the “Plan”) in 1972 to permit eligible executives to defer certain cash awards made under its executive compensation programs.
structure.summary:
- Plan overview: PepsiCo Executive Income Deferral Program (409A Program), a nonqualified deferred compensation plan for executives, amended and restated effective January 1, 2022.
- Scope and purpose: Establishes terms under which eligible executives may defer base and bonus compensation, how deferrals are recorded and credited, and when and how distributions are made, in compliance with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code and applicable securities rules.
- Key definitions: Comprehensive glossary covering Accounts and Deferral Subaccounts, Base and Bonus Compensation, Eligible Executive/Participant, Beneficiary, Employer/Company/PepsiCo Organization, Disability, Retirement, Separation from Service, Unforeseeable Emergency, Key Employee, NAV/Valuation Dates, Election Forms, Performance Periods, Prohibited Misconduct, Recordkeeper, and related legal references (Code, ERISA, Section 409A, Section 16).
- Eligibility and participation: Criteria for becoming and remaining eligible; termination of eligibility/participation; treatment upon acquisitions and divestitures; special rules for certain executive groups.
- Deferral elections: How, when, and in what form executives may elect to defer compensation; timing rules for initial and annual elections; period of deferral; payout form options; and “Second Look” elections permitting limited changes consistent with 409A.
- Participant accounts and investments: Recordkeeping of individual deferral balances; available investment (deemed) options and NAV-based allocations; methods of crediting earnings; vesting rules; and forfeiture of earnings in cases of prohibited misconduct.
- Distribution rules: Payment triggers and mechanics for specified dates, Separation from Service, death, retirement, disability, and Unforeseeable Emergency; valuation procedures; compliance overlays for tax code Section 162(m) and securities law Section 16; determination of actual payment dates.
- Plan administration: Authority and responsibilities of the Plan Administrator; decision-making powers; indemnification and liability limits; tax withholding; and express compliance mandates with Section 409A and Section 16.
- Claims and appeals: Procedures for filing benefit claims, appeal rights for denied claims, special procedures for disability determinations, requirement to exhaust administrative remedies, limitations periods, and venue restrictions.
- Amendment and termination: Company’s rights to amend or terminate the plan and conditions for doing so.
- Miscellaneous provisions: Clarification of participants’ rights (unfunded, unsecured obligations of the employer), coordination with other plans, releases/receipts, governing law, adoption by related employers, interpretive rules (gender/tense/examples), assignment restrictions, and facility-of-payment provisions.
- Appendices: Listing of participating employers; special provisions for PBG and PAS executives; and rules for participants affected by a January 20, 2022 transaction.

nodes.title: INTRODUCTION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE I – INTRODUCTION
nodes.start_phrase:
PepsiCo, Inc. (the “Company”) established the PepsiCo Executive Income Deferral Program (the “Plan”) in 1972 to permit
eligible executives to defer certain cash awards made under its executive compensation programs.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the PepsiCo Executive Income Deferral Program’s purpose and history: created in 1972 to allow eligible executives to defer certain cash awards.
- Defines two components of the single plan:
  - Pre-409A Program: covers deferrals earned/vested on or before December 31, 2004; governed by separate pre-409A documents.
  - 409A Program: covers deferrals earned/vested after December 31, 2004; governed by this document effective January 1, 2005.
- Clarifies applicability: this document governs actions and events (including distribution triggers) on or after January 1, 2005 for 409A-subject deferrals; participants only prior to 2005 remain under Pre-409A documents.
- Requires separate tracking of Pre-409A and 409A amounts to maintain the Pre-409A Program’s exemption from Section 409A; administration will reflect this separation.
- Notes the most recent restatement effective January 1, 2022 (with some later effective dates), reflecting the sale of the juice business and updating provisions on exhaustion of administrative remedies.
- States tax and ERISA intent: the Plan is a nonqualified, unfunded, unsecured deferred compensation plan for federal tax purposes and a “top-hat” plan under ERISA (Sections 201(2), 301(a)(3), 401(a)(1)) for a select group of management or highly compensated employees.

nodes.title: DEFINITIONS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE II – DEFINITIONS
nodes.start_phrase:
When used in this Plan, the following underlined terms shall have the meanings set forth below unless a dif ferent meaning is
plainly required by the context:
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article II of the PepsiCo Executive Income Deferral Program sets out defined terms for a nonqualified deferred compensation plan, including portions subject to Section 409A (409A Program) and a Pre-409A Program.
- Governance and roles: Defines the Plan Administrator (Compensation Committee and the Company’s SVP, Total Rewards, with authority to delegate), the Recordkeeper’s responsibilities, and references to applicable laws (ERISA, Internal Revenue Code, Section 409A, and the Securities Exchange Act).
- Employers and organizational definitions: Identifies the Company (PepsiCo, Inc.), “Employer” entities within the PepsiCo Organization (controlled group under Code 414(b), (c)), and a definition of the U.S. for plan purposes.
- Participants and eligibility: Defines Executive, Eligible Executive (cross-referenced to Section 3.01(a)), Participant (active and otherwise), Beneficiary, and Employer; sets U.S.-based, USD-payroll, and citizenship/residency criteria with limitations for certain non-U.S. assignments.
- Compensation eligible for deferral: Defines Base Compensation and Bonus Compensation as adjusted amounts generally payable in U.S. dollars from U.S. payroll, with Plan Administrator authority to specify permissible subtractions consistent with Section 409A.
- Accounts and investments: Establishes each Participant’s Account and Deferral Subaccounts (by each deferral), rules for creating/combining subaccounts, and NAV for phantom investment funds used to credit earnings/losses.
- Elections and payout timing: Details the Election Form (including electronic methods), Specific Payment Dates (lump sum or start of installments), Second Look Election (referenced), Performance Period, and Plan Year.
- Valuation and distribution timing: Sets Valuation Dates (generally daily) and Distribution Valuation Dates (currently Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, Oct 1), including timing and change constraints to remain 409A-compliant.
- Key Employee rules: Describes identification under Code 416(i) with an effective period (Apr 1 to Mar 31), officer/owner thresholds, and an administrative convenience rule treating LG6/Band IV+ as Key Employees, capped at 200.
- Employment status and triggers: Defines Separation from Service (409A standard with a 20% control test and board-service carve-out), Retirement (age/service thresholds with rehire bridging rules), Disability (per PepsiCo Disability Plan plus duration for distribution), and Unforeseeable Emergency (409A standard).
- Prohibited Misconduct: Details non-compete (broad “Participation” and extensive “Covered Products”), non-solicitation of employees, confidentiality obligations with whistleblower and DTSA carveouts, violations of Company Code of Conduct/insider trading/other gross misconduct, and fraud.
- Cross-references and administrative safeguards: Notes Plan Administrator authority to set guidelines (e.g., for subtractions from pay and emergency determinations), maintain compliance with Section 409A, and lists primary Employers in an appendix.

nodes.title: ELIGIBILITY AND PARTICIPATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE III – ELIGIBILITY AND P ARTICIP ATION
nodes.start_phrase: For Plan Y ears beginning on and after January 1, 2020 and for Performance Periods ending after December 31, 2019, subject to Paragraph (3) below, Section 3.05 and the election timing rules of Article IV,
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article III outlines who can participate in the Plan, when eligibility begins and ends, how participation terminates, treatment in corporate transactions, and special rules for Section 16 officers.

- 3.01 Eligibility to Participate:
  - Post-2019 rules (for Plan Years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2020 and Performance Periods ending after Dec 31, 2019):
    - Executive must, throughout the Deferral Window, be: (i) classified LG2 or above; (ii) employed during at least part of each of the two prior Plan Years; (iii) have earned over $200,000 total compensation (Base + Bonus) in each of those two prior years; and (iv) reasonably expect to earn over $200,000 in the election year.
  - Pre-2020 rules (for Plan Years/Performance Periods ending after Jan 1, 2006 and before the above):
    - Eligible to defer 30 days after hire or promotion into LG2+ (pre-2017, “LG2” means “Band II”), subject to Article IV timing; mid-year eligibility must meet Treas. Reg. §1.409A-2(a)(7)(ii) initial eligibility requirements.
  - Administrator discretion:
    - Plan Administrator may modify, limit, or expand eligible classes (criteria need not be uniform) and may remove eligibility only effective at Plan Year end.
    - An Executive with a valid irrevocable election remains Eligible for the rest of that Plan Year/Performance Period and until Bonus is deferred, even if status changes (fails criteria, paid outside U.S./from non-U.S. payroll, or transfers to an affiliate without a Separation from Service). Such events cut off elections not yet irrevocable to comply with 409A.
  - Status terms:
    - “Eligible Executive” applies while all requirements are met.
    - Active participation begins when amounts are first withheld under a submitted Election Form.

- 3.02 Termination of Eligibility to Defer:
  - Eligibility to make new deferrals/elections ends on the “Election Termination Date,” occurring as soon as administratively practicable after the earlier of: (a) Separation from Service; or (b) loss of eligibility under 3.01(a).
  - Irrevocable elections remain in effect; any election not yet required to be irrevocable is terminated to comply with 409A.

- 3.03 Termination of Participation:
  - A Participant ceases participation when the Account is fully paid out; however, participation continues if future deferrals are still to be credited (e.g., future-paid Bonus).

- 3.04 Acquisitions and Divestitures:
  - Transaction documents may specify participation outcomes. Absent such terms:
    - On a sale, Executives of the sold Business cease eligibility (subject to transitional extension under 3.01(a) if no Separation from Service due to the 20% affiliate rule).
    - On an acquisition, Executives of the acquired Business are not eligible unless designated in the Plan or related documents by the Plan Administrator.
  - Employer approval of an acquisition/divestiture agreement constitutes Company approval for Plan participation provisions within that agreement.

- 3.05 Special Rules for Section 16 Officers:
  - For Plan Years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2020 and Performance Periods ending after Dec 31, 2019, eligibility is determined under the Plan’s January 1, 2019 provisions (“2019 Provisions”) and this section.
  - To maintain the Plan’s Securities Act Section 4(a)(2) / Rule 506 exemption, the Plan will comply with Rule 506(b), including accredited investor determinations for Section 16 Officers (notwithstanding 3.01(a)(1)).
  - Newly eligible Section 16 Officers may use the special 30-day deferral election window under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-2(a)(7) for Base Compensation, consistent with the 2019 Provisions.

nodes.title: DEFERRAL OF COMPENSATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE IV – DEFERRAL OF COMPENSA TION
nodes.start_phrase: Effective on or after January 1, 2010, each Eligible Executive may make an election to defer under the Plan any whole percentage up to 75% of his or her Base Compensation in the manner described in Section 4.02.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article IV sets the rules for electing, timing, period, and form of deferring compensation, beneficiary designations, and subsequent changes (“Second Look Elections”) under a nonqualified deferral plan.

- Deferral eligibility and limits (Section 4.01):
  - Base Compensation: Eligible Executives may defer whole percentages up to 75% (Plan Administrator may set lower caps on specific elections).
  - Bonus Compensation: May defer up to 100% (administrator may set lower caps).
  - Pre-2020 special rules: limitations for newly promoted executives (to LG2+) on deferring bonus for the promotion year; performance-based criteria and Section 409A compliance required for bonus deferrals for performance periods ending before 2020.
  - Election Form must state deferral percentage, deferral period (4.03), form of payout (4.04), and any required information; investment direction may be indicated but is not required.

- Time and manner of election (Section 4.02):
  - Base pay: election due by December 31 preceding the Plan Year; pre-2020 30-day mid-year window for newly eligible executives, applicable only to post-election services.
  - Bonus pay: for performance periods ending after 2019, election due by the last day of the prior fiscal year; for periods ending before 2019, at least six months before period end.
  - Plan Administrator may set earlier submission policies (with limited waiver up to statutory deadlines); changes to such practices post-1/1/2019 subject to Section 7.06.
  - Elections are irrevocable once properly received (subject to limited administrator cancellation by December 31 preceding the Plan Year).
  - No in-year changes. Hardship distributions under a qualified plan may trigger cancellation of deferrals during the suspension period; new elections only for subsequent Plan Years.

- Beneficiary designations (Section 4.02(d)):
  - Must be written, signed, meet administrator/recordkeeper standards (including any spousal consent), and be on file before death.
  - Prior valid designations (Pre-409A/Pre-Effective Date) recognized; name-specific designations remain valid despite relationship changes.
  - Relationship-only designations valid only before June 3, 2002; after that date, such designations are invalid.
  - Absent percentage splits, unnamed portions are divided equally among listed beneficiaries. Changes permitted any time before death. If a beneficiary dies before full payout, remaining amounts go to that beneficiary’s estate.

- Period of deferral (Section 4.03):
  - Elect a Specific Payment Date or Separation from Service; deferral cannot extend beyond age 80.
  - Minimum deferral periods (deemed if shorter/unspecified): Base—at least 12 months after the end of the Plan Year of otherwise-pay; Bonus—at least 18 months after the otherwise payment date.

- Form of payout (Section 4.04):
  - Lump sum or installments (quarterly/semiannual/annual) for up to 20 years and not beyond age 80.
  - Installments may be fixed dollar or fixed years. If an election would exceed age 80 or 20 years, schedule is truncated with a final catch-up payment at age 80 or 20-year limit (interim amounts determined under Section 6.08).

- Second Look Elections (Section 4.05):
  - Participants may modify time and/or form of payment after a valid initial deferral, subject to strict 409A-compliant conditions.
  - Pre-2020: only one Second Look per deferral; later, multiple allowed if each meets requirements.
  - Key requirements:
    - Must be made at least 12 months before the originally scheduled payment date (Specific Payment Date) or, for Separation-based elections, at least 12 months before Separation and only if separation is for Retirement.
    - Must delay payment by at least five years from the prior scheduled date (or from Separation/last designated delay period for Separation-based schedules).
    - Pre-2013: could not specify Separation or a delay period as the payout date for a Second Look.
    - Changes between lump sum and installments, or installment length/frequency changes, must push the first payment at least five years later and cannot extend past age 80; installments are treated as a single payment under Section 409A.
  - Noncompliant Second Look Elections are void; original terms apply. Participants are responsible for initiating; administrator/recordkeeper may provide notices but have no duty and no discretion to waive 409A requirements.

nodes.title: INTERESTS OF PARTICIPANTS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE V – INTERESTS OF P ARTICIP ANTS
nodes.start_phrase: Each Participant shall have at least one separate Deferral Subaccount for each separate deferral of Base Compensation or Bonus Compensation made by the Participant under this Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how participant deferrals are tracked via separate, non-funded “Deferral Subaccounts” for each Base or Bonus Compensation deferral; accounts are bookkeeping only, with no segregated assets or insurance.
- Earnings, gains, expenses, and losses are credited/debited on each Valuation Date as if invested per the participant’s directions; all investments are “phantom” and used solely to measure account value and employer liability.
- Provides phantom investment options:
  - Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund: units based on the NAV of the PepsiCo Savings Plan fund; unit adjustments for corporate actions; no actual stock held and no shareholder rights.
  - Phantom AFR Fund (effective 12/29/2006): returns equal to 120% of the applicable federal long-term rate (annual compounding), with monthly rate setting and annual compounding from the investment date.
  - Other administrator-designated phantom funds, generally unitized and valued using fund NAV on Valuation Dates.
- Allows participants (or beneficiaries after death) to allocate deferrals among options and to reallocate existing balances:
  - Deferral elections allocated in 1% increments; defaults or proration apply to ensure exactly 100% allocation (shortfalls default to AFR; overages prorated).
  - Fund transfers via approved forms; increments may be whole percentages, shares, or dollars (from 1/1/2020); requests must total 100% and take effect on the next Valuation Date, subject to timing rules; the most recent valid request governs.
- Imposes special restrictions on the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund to address insider trading compliance, including potential altered effective dates, Rule 16b-3 safeguards, Sarbanes-Oxley blackout periods, and quarterly blackout periods aligned with earnings releases per the company’s insider trading policy (subject to Section 409A compliance).
- Confirms participants are always 100% vested in account value and not subject to forfeiture due to separation from service.
- Introduces forfeiture of earnings/gains for “Prohibited Misconduct”: for specified deferrals (Bonus 2006+; Base 2007+), if misconduct occurs before the second anniversary of separation, all credited and future net earnings/gains are forfeited and the account adjusted; payouts are limited to the lesser of total affected deferrals or their net value at the misconduct determination date.

nodes.title: DISTRIBUTIONS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VI – DISTRIBUTIONS
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant’ s Deferral Subaccount(s) that are governed by the terms of this 409A Program shall be distributed as provided in this Article, subject in all cases to Section 7.03(j) (relating to safeguards against insider trading) and Section 7.06 (relating to compliance with Section 16 of the Act).
nodes.summary:
- Scope and compliance: Article VI governs when and how Participants’ 409A-governed Deferral Subaccounts are distributed. All balances, including those hypothetically invested in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund, are paid in cash. Distributions must comply with Section 409A timing rules and are subject to insider trading safeguards (Section 7.03(j)) and Section 16 compliance (Section 7.06).

- Interpretive framework: The Article sets default rules to determine which distribution provision applies based on specific events and establishes precedence among sections to ensure the earliest permissible distribution under 409A.

- Section 6.02 – Specific Payment Date: Applies when a Participant elected a Specific Payment Date and that date arrives before Separation from Service (other than Retirement), Disability, or death. If the Participant separates (other than for Retirement or death) before the date or before the first installment/Second Look Election payment is processed, Section 6.03 applies instead. If death or Disability occurs first, Sections 6.04 or 6.06 apply to the extent they accelerate payment.

- Section 6.03 – Separation from Service: Applies when a Participant elected payout upon Separation from Service and then separates other than for Retirement or death, or when redirected from Section 6.02 per the above rule.

- Section 6.04 – Death: Governs upon a Participant’s death and takes precedence over Sections 6.02, 6.03, and 6.05 if it results in an earlier distribution.

- Section 6.05 – Retirement: Applies when a Participant elected payout upon Separation from Service and the separation is due to Retirement. May be superseded by Sections 6.04 (death) or 6.06 (Disability) if those would accelerate payment.

- Section 6.06 – Disability: Applies upon Disability and takes precedence over Sections 6.02, 6.03, and 6.5 if it would produce an earlier distribution. If death occurs after Disability, Section 6.04 takes precedence to the extent it accelerates payment.

- Section 6.07 – Unforeseeable Emergency: Applies when an Unforeseeable Emergency arises before distributions under Sections 6.02–6.06; emergency distribution rules govern in that circumstance (text thereafter is truncated).

- Notable terms: References a “Second Look Election” associated with installments or payments tied to a Specific Payment Date.

nodes.title: General
nodes.heading: 6.01 General:
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant’ s Deferral Subaccount(s) that are governed by the terms of this 409A Program shall be distributed as provided in this Article, subject in all cases to Section 7.03(j) (relating to safeguards against insider trading) and Section 7.06 (relating to compliance with Section 16 of the Act).
nodes.summary:
- Scope and compliance: Article VI governs distributions from Participants’ 409A-governed Deferral Subaccounts. All payouts are in cash (including balances tied to Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock). Distributions must comply with Section 409A timing rules and are subject to insider trading safeguards (Section 7.03(j)) and Section 16 compliance (Section 7.06).

- Event hierarchy and precedence rules:
  - 6.02 Specific Payment Date controls if reached before separation (other than Retirement), Disability, or death; if separation (non-Retirement) occurs first, 6.03 applies; if death occurs first, 6.04 applies to the extent it accelerates payment; if Disability occurs first, 6.06 applies to the extent it accelerates payment.
  - 6.03 Separation from Service (non-Retirement) applies when elected or as redirected from 6.02.
  - 6.04 Death applies upon death and takes precedence over 6.02, 6.03, and 6.05 if it results in an earlier distribution.
  - 6.05 Retirement applies when deferral is to Separation from Service and the Participant retires, subject to 6.04/6.06 precedence.
  - 6.06 Disability applies upon Disability and takes precedence over 6.02, 6.03, or 6.05 if it results in earlier distribution; if the Participant dies after Disability, 6.04 then controls.
  - 6.07 Unforeseeable Emergency applies before distributions under 6.02–6.06 and takes precedence to the extent it accelerates payment.

- Section 6.02 (Specific Payment Date):
  - Lump sum: Subaccount valued as of the last Distribution Valuation Date on or immediately before the Specific Payment Date; paid in a single lump sum on that date.
  - Installments (effective for events on/after Jan 1, 2009): First installment paid on the Specific Payment Date; remaining installments follow the elected schedule (subject to Plan constraints), with amounts determined under Section 6.08. If, before the last installment is processed, the Participant has a non-Retirement Separation, dies, or becomes Disabled, remaining balances shift to distribution under 6.03, 6.04, or 6.06 respectively, but only to the extent those sections provide an earlier payout. References include Second Look Elections.

- Section 6.03 (Separation from Service—non-Retirement, non-Disability, non-death) (effective for events on/after Jan 1, 2009):
  - For Subaccounts with a Specific Payment Date after the Separation: paid in a single lump sum on the first day of the calendar quarter following Separation.
  - If Separation is on or after a Specific Payment Date (including Second Look Elections), additional rules apply (text truncated in excerpt).

nodes.title: Distributions Based on a Specific Payment Date
nodes.heading: 6.02 Distributions Based on a Specific Payment Date:
nodes.start_phrase: This Section shall apply to distributions that are to be made upon the occurrence of a Specific Payment Date.
nodes.summary:
- Section 6.07 precedence: If applying Section 6.07 (Unforeseeable Emergency) would result in an earlier payout, it overrides Sections 6.02–6.06 for all or part of a Participant’s Account.

- Section 6.02 — Distributions based on a Specific Payment Date (before Disability, Separation from Service other than Retirement, or death):
  - Lump sum elections (per Sections 4.04/4.05): Deferral Subaccount is valued as of the last Distribution Valuation Date on or before the Specific Payment Date and paid in a single lump sum on that date.
  - Installment elections (effective for events on/after Jan 1, 2009): First installment is paid on the Specific Payment Date; subsequent installments follow the Participant’s elected schedule (subject to plan constraints), with each installment amount determined under Section 6.08.
  - Overrides/coordination: If, before the final installment is processed, the Participant Separates from Service (other than Retirement) or becomes entitled to a distribution due to death or Disability, the remaining balance linked to that Specific Payment Date is instead paid under Section 6.03, 6.04, or 6.06, as applicable; for death/Disability, this substitution applies only if it accelerates payment.
  - Cross-references to Sections 6.03 (Separation other than Retirement), 6.04 (death), 6.06 (Disability), and 6.07 (Unforeseeable Emergency).

- Section 6.03 — Distributions on account of Separation from Service (other than Retirement, Disability, or death) (effective for events on/after Jan 1, 2009):
  - Applies only to non-Retirement, non-Disability, non-death Separations; the Participant’s total Account is distributed under this section.
  - For Deferral Subaccounts with a Specific Payment Date after the Separation: paid in a single lump sum on the first day of the calendar quarter following Separation.
  - If Separation occurs on or after the Specific Payment Date (including one set via a Second Look Election): additional rules apply, but the text is truncated here.

nodes.title: Distributions on Account of a Separation from Service
nodes.heading: 6.03 Distributions on Account of a Separation from Service:
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant’ s total Account shall be distributed upon the occurrence of a Participant’ s Separation from Service (other than for Retirement, Disability or death) in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Section.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that Section 6.07 (Unforeseeable Emergency) overrides Sections 6.02–6.06 if it would produce an earlier distribution.
- Section 6.02 (Distributions Based on a Specific Payment Date):
  - Governs payouts triggered by a specified date if it occurs before disability, separation from service (other than retirement), or death.
  - Lump sums: value set as of the last Distribution Valuation Date on or before the Specific Payment Date; paid in a single lump sum on that date.
  - Installments (effective for dates on/after Jan 1, 2009): first installment paid on the Specific Payment Date; remaining installments follow the elected schedule unless superseded by separation (non-retirement), death, disability, or unforeseeable emergency. Installment amounts are determined under Section 6.08.
  - If, before the final installment is processed, the participant separates (non-retirement) or becomes entitled to death/disability distributions, the remaining balance is paid under Sections 6.03, 6.04, or 6.06, as applicable, but only if it accelerates payment for death/disability.
- Section 6.03 (Distributions on Account of a Separation from Service other than retirement, disability, or death; effective for events on/after Jan 1, 2009):
  - For subaccounts with a Specific Payment Date after separation: paid in a single lump sum on the first day of the calendar quarter following separation.
  - If separation occurs on or after the Specific Payment Date and installments had been elected:
    - If the first installment was already processed: remaining installment election is void; remaining balance paid as a lump sum per the above timing.
    - If the first installment was not yet processed: entire installment election is void; paid as a lump sum per the above timing.
  - Key Employees (as defined under Section 409A): payment due to separation may not occur earlier than the first day of the calendar quarter at least six months after separation.
  - If an account was fully paid out due to separation and a later deferral (e.g., bonus) is credited, that new balance is paid as a result of the prior separation in a lump sum on the first day of the calendar quarter following the crediting date, subject to the six‑month Key Employee delay.
- Section 6.04 (Distributions on Account of Death):
  - Default rule: previously a lump sum on the first day of the calendar quarter beginning after the first anniversary of death.
  - Effective Jan 1, 2019: lump sum must be paid in a window beginning the first day of the calendar quarter after death and ending December 31 of the year following the year of death.
  - If installments were in pay status at death, they continue per the governing election until the scheduled lump-sum payment time, at which point installments cease and the remaining balance is paid in a lump sum.
  - Payments after death are made to the designated Beneficiary; if some beneficiaries predecease the participant, surviving beneficiaries share the predeceased portions pro rata to their designated shares.
  - Begins to address rules if no beneficiary designation is in effect or all designated beneficiaries predecease the participant (text truncated).

nodes.title: Distributions on Account of Death
nodes.heading: 6.04 Distributions on Account of Death:
nodes.start_phrase: Upon a Participant’ s death, the value of the Participant’ s Account under the Plan shall be distributed in a single lump sum payment on the first day of the calendar quarter beginning after the first anniversary of the Participant’ s death.
nodes.summary:
- Treatment of installment elections upon Separation from Service:
  - If the first installment was processed before Separation from Service, the remaining installments are canceled and the balance is paid in a single lump sum per the plan’s general separation rules.
  - If the first installment was not yet processed before Separation from Service, the entire installment election is canceled and the Deferral Subaccount is paid in a single lump sum per the same rules.

- Key Employee six-month delay:
  - If the Participant is a “Key Employee” under Section 409A at Separation from Service, no payments due to that separation may be made before the first day of the calendar quarter at least six months after separation.

- Post-payout deferrals after Separation from Service:
  - If an Account was fully distributed due to Separation from Service and later receives a new deferral that could not have been credited earlier (e.g., bonus compensation), that new balance is paid as a result of the prior separation in a single lump sum on the first day of the next calendar quarter after the credit, subject to the Key Employee delay.

- Distributions upon death:
  - Default timing: a single lump sum. Previously scheduled for the first day of the calendar quarter after the first anniversary of death; effective January 1, 2019, payable in a window beginning the first day of the calendar quarter after death and ending December 31 of the year following death.
  - If installments were in progress at death, installments continue per the governing deferral election until the scheduled lump-sum payment time, at which point installments cease and the remaining balance is paid as a lump sum.
  - Payments are made to the designated Beneficiary(ies). If some designated Beneficiaries predecease the Participant, their portions are reallocated among surviving designated Beneficiaries in proportion to their respective shares.

- Default payees if no valid Beneficiary designation or all designated Beneficiaries predecease:
  - To the surviving spouse or eligible domestic partner if married/in a qualifying domestic partnership at death.
  - If not married/in a qualifying domestic partnership, to surviving children in equal shares.
  - If neither spouse/partner nor children survive, to the Participant’s estate.
  - The Plan Administrator determines marital status and “spouse” per the law of the Participant’s primary residence and defines “eligible domestic partner” (civil union, eligibility under company health benefits, or other specified criteria). The Administrator may require documentation to make these determinations.

- Beneficiary emergency access:
  - Before the final payout, a Beneficiary may apply for an Unforeseeable Emergency distribution under Section 6.07.

- Claims timing on death:
  - Any claim to death benefits must be received by the Recordkeeper or Plan Administrator at least 14 days before payment; later claims are untimely and unenforceable.

- Distributions upon Retirement:
  - If Retirement occurs before a Deferral Subaccount’s Specific Payment Date, the original time and form election remains in effect; distribution follows the plan’s Specific Payment Date rules in Section 6.02(a) or (b).
  - If payment was elected on account of Separation from Service, distribution of the related Deferral Subaccount is to commence as described (text partially cut off).

nodes.title: Distributions on Account of Retirement
nodes.heading: 6.05 Distributions on Account of Retirement:
nodes.start_phrase: If a Participant incurs a Separation from Service on account of his or her Retirement, the Participant’ s Account shall be distributed in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Section.
nodes.summary:
- Default payee rules if a named beneficiary predeceases the participant:
  - If married or in an eligible domestic partnership at death (for deaths on/after Jan 1, 2019): pay 100% to the surviving spouse/eligible domestic partner.
  - If not married/in a domestic partnership: pay to surviving children in equal shares.
  - If no spouse/partner and no living children: pay to the participant’s estate.
- Plan Administrator determinations:
  - Determines marital status and spouse under the law of the participant’s primary residence at death.
  - Defines “eligible domestic partner” (civil union under state law, eligibility for company health benefits as domestic partner, or other written criteria).
  - May request documents and information to make these determinations.
- Beneficiary may request an Unforeseeable Emergency distribution before death benefits are paid.
- Claims timing requirement: any claim to amounts on death must be received by the Recordkeeper or Plan Administrator at least 14 days before payment; later claims are unenforceable.
- Retirement distributions:
  - If retirement occurs before a Specific Payment Date: prior time/form elections continue; distributions follow Section 6.02 rules for Specific Payment Dates.
  - If distribution was elected on Separation from Service: payments start the first day of the calendar quarter following retirement, as a lump sum or installments per election; installments subject to acceleration for death, disability, or unforeseeable emergency.
  - Key Employees: payment due to retirement cannot begin earlier than the first day of the calendar quarter at least 6 months after retirement (Section 409A delay).
  - Any installments already in progress under a Specific Payment Date continue per election (subject to acceleration events).
- Disability distributions:
  - Lump sum of the account’s value (as of most recent Distribution Valuation Date) paid on the first date that is: (i) the participant is Disabled; (ii) at least 12 months after disability onset for the current cause; and (iii) after receipt of payments from a PepsiCo disability plan for that cause.
  - If on installments when disability occurs, installments continue per election until the lump sum date; then installments cease and remaining balance is paid in that lump sum.
- Unforeseeable Emergency distributions:
  - Participant or beneficiary may request accelerated payment before other distributable events.
  - Must submit written request and supporting materials; Recordkeeper decides within 60 days (or longer if warranted).
  - Distribution occurs as of the decision date and is limited to the amount necessary to satisfy the emergency.

nodes.title: Distributions on Account of Disability
nodes.heading: 6.06 Distributions on Account of Disability:
nodes.start_phrase: If a Participant incurs a Disability , the Participant’ s Account shall be distributed in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Section.
nodes.summary:
- Retirement distributions: Begin on the first day of the calendar quarter following Retirement, paid either as a lump sum or installments per the Participant’s deferral elections (Sections 4.04/4.05), with possible acceleration for death, Disability, or Unforeseeable Emergency (Sections 6.04, 6.06, 6.07).
- Key Employee delay: If classified as a Key Employee under Section 409A at Retirement, payment due to Retirement cannot begin before the first day of a calendar quarter at least six months after Retirement.
- Ongoing installments at Retirement: If the Participant is already receiving installments tied to a Specific Payment Date (Section 6.02) at Retirement, those installments continue per the election, subject to acceleration for death, Disability, or Unforeseeable Emergency.
- Disability distributions: Upon Disability, the Account is paid in a single lump sum equal to the value as of the most recent Distribution Valuation Date, on the earliest date that meets all of the following: (i) the Participant is Disabled, (ii) at least 12 months have passed since the first date Disabled from the current cause, and (iii) the Participant has received payments from a PepsiCo disability plan for that cause.
- Installments during Disability: If receiving installments when Disability occurs, those continue per the election until the scheduled Disability lump sum date; immediately before that date, installments cease and the remaining balance is paid in one lump sum.
- Unforeseeable Emergency distributions: Before amounts are otherwise distributable (Sections 6.02–6.06), a Participant or Beneficiary may request an accelerated payout due to an Unforeseeable Emergency by filing with the Recordkeeper; the Recordkeeper decides within 60 days (or longer if necessary). If approved, distribution occurs as of the determination date and is limited to the amount necessary to satisfy the emergency.

nodes.title: Distributions on Account of Unforeseeable Emergency
nodes.heading: 6.07 Distributions on Account of Unforeseeable Emer gency:
nodes.start_phrase: Prior to the time that an amount would become distributable under Sections 6.02 through 6.06, a Participant or Beneficiary may file a written request with the Recordkeeper for accelerated payment of all or a portion of the amount credited to the Participant’ s Account based upon an Unforeseeable Emer gency .
nodes.summary:
- Retirement distributions: Payments begin on the first day of the calendar quarter following Retirement, in a lump sum or installments per the participant’s election. Existing installment schedules tied to a Specific Payment Date (Section 6.02) continue at Retirement. If the participant is a Key Employee under Section 409A, payments triggered by Retirement cannot start before the first day of the calendar quarter at least six months post-Retirement. Installments remain subject to acceleration for death, Disability, or Unforeseeable Emergency (Sections 6.04, 6.06, 6.07).
- Disability distributions: Upon Disability, the account is paid in a single lump sum valued as of the most recent Distribution Valuation Date, on the first date that all are true: the participant is Disabled, at least 12 months have passed since the Disability’s first date, and the participant has received payments from a PepsiCo disability plan for the same cause. If the participant is receiving installments, they continue until the scheduled lump-sum date; installments then cease and the remaining balance is paid in that lump sum.
- Unforeseeable Emergency distributions: Participants/beneficiaries may request accelerated payment before other scheduled distributions. The Recordkeeper decides within 60 days (or longer if warranted). The payout equals only the amount necessary to satisfy the emergency plus anticipated taxes, reduced by insurance/reimbursements and assets that could be liquidated without causing severe hardship.
- Valuation rules: Accounts continue to be credited with earnings/gains and debited for expenses/losses until the applicable Distribution Valuation Date. Installment amounts (unless a fixed dollar election under Section 4.04) equal the subaccount value as of the preceding Distribution Valuation Date divided by the remaining number of installments; distributions reduce the subaccount as of that preceding valuation date.
- Section 162(m) compliance: The employer may delay distributions if deductibility would be disallowed under Code Section 162(m), applying consistent treatment to similarly situated employees. If delayed, all deferrals to the participant that could be delayed and were scheduled in the same tax year must also be delayed. Payments must then be made per the 162(m) schedule (including any applicable six‑month delay) once deductible.

nodes.title: Valuation
nodes.heading: 6.08 Valuation:
nodes.start_phrase: In determining the amount of any individual distribution pursuant to this Article, the Participant’ s Deferral Subaccount shall continue to be credited with earnings and gains (and debited for expenses and losses) as specified in Article V until the Distribution V aluation Date that is used in determining the amount of the distribution under this Article.
nodes.summary:
- Unforeseeable Emergency distributions are limited to the amount needed to satisfy the emergency plus related taxes, after considering available insurance/reimbursements and asset liquidation to the extent liquidation wouldn’t itself cause severe financial hardship.
- Valuation rules for distributions:
  - A Participant’s Deferral Subaccount continues to be credited with earnings/gains and debited for expenses/losses under Article V until the applicable Distribution Valuation Date.
  - If a section does not specify a Distribution Valuation Date, the date immediately preceding the distribution applies.
  - For installments (including partial/unforeseeable emergency distributions), the subaccount is reduced as of the close of the preceding Distribution Valuation Date.
  - Non-fixed installment amounts are determined by dividing the subaccount value (before reduction) on the preceding Distribution Valuation Date by the remaining number of installments.
  - Fixed dollar installment payments equal the elected amount, subject to Section 4.04 rules.
- Section 162(m) compliance:
  - Distributions may be delayed under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-2(b)(7)(i) if the employer reasonably anticipates the payment would not be tax-deductible under Code Section 162(m).
  - Conditions include consistent treatment of similarly situated employees, delaying all the participant’s payments in the same tax year that can be delayed under this rule, and paying according to the regulation’s schedule (including any applicable six-month delay) once the payment would be deductible.

nodes.title: Section 162(m) Compliance
nodes.heading: 6.09 Section 162(m) Compliance:
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding Sections 6.01 through 6.07 of this Article, Plan distributions may be delayed in accordance with the special rule in T reas. Reg. §1.409A-2(b)(7)(i) (the “162(m) Provision”).
nodes.summary:
- Unforeseeable Emergency distributions are limited to the amount necessary to satisfy the emergency, including reasonably anticipated taxes, after considering insurance/reimbursements and liquidation of assets that would not cause severe financial hardship.
- Valuation rules for distributions: a Participant’s Deferral Subaccount continues to be credited with earnings/gains and debited for expenses/losses (per Article V) up to the applicable Distribution Valuation Date. If not specified, the preceding Distribution Valuation Date applies.
- For installments, the subaccount is reduced as of the close of the preceding Distribution Valuation Date; the installment amount (unless a fixed-dollar election under Section 4.04) equals the subaccount value as of that date (before reduction) divided by the remaining number of installments. Fixed-dollar installments pay the elected amount subject to Section 4.04.
- Section 162(m) compliance: distributions may be delayed under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-2(b)(7)(i) if the employer reasonably anticipates the payment would be nondeductible under Code §162(m). Conditions include consistent treatment of similarly situated employees, delaying all the participant’s same-year deferrable payments that could be delayed under this rule, and paying according to the regulation’s timing (including any six‑month delay) once deductible.

nodes.title: Impact of Section 16 of the Act on Distributions
nodes.heading: 6.10 Impact of Section 16 of the Act on Distributions:
nodes.start_phrase: The provisions of Sections 5.03(c) and 7.06 shall apply in determining whether a Participant’ s distribution shall be delayed beyond the date applicable under the preceding provisions of this Article VI.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies that distributions to Participants may be delayed beyond the standard Article VI schedule if required by Sections 5.03(c) and 7.06, which govern delays related to Section 16 of the Act.
- Establishes the payment timing rule: amounts due on a specified date under Article VI must be paid no later than the later of (a) the end of the calendar year in which the specified date falls, or (b) the 15th day of the third month following that date.
- Prohibits Participants or Beneficiaries from selecting the taxable year in which the payment is received.

nodes.title: Actual Payment Date
nodes.heading: 6.11 Actual Payment Date:
nodes.start_phrase: An amount payable on a date specified in this Article VI shall be paid no later than the later of (a) the end of the calendar year in which the specified date occurs, or (b) the 15 day of the third calendar month following such specified date.
nodes.summary:
- Explains that, for purposes of potential distribution delays, Sections 5.03(c) and 7.06 control how Section 16 of the Act affects a Participant’s distribution timing under Article VI.
- Sets the actual payment deadline for amounts due under Article VI as the later of: (a) the end of the calendar year containing the specified payment date, or (b) the 15th day of the third calendar month after that specified date.
- Prohibits the Participant or Beneficiary from selecting the taxable year in which the payment is made.

nodes.title: PLAN ADMINISTRATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VII– PLAN ADMINISTRATION
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator is responsible for the administration of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Plan Administrator as responsible for administering the Plan, with authority to delegate responsibilities to others, provided the delegation defines its scope and complies with Section 7.06.
- Allows the Plan Administrator to act under procedures it adopts or those deemed legally permissible by the Company’s Law Department.
- Grants broad discretionary powers to:
  - Interpret, construe, and administer the Plan.
  - Decide eligibility, participation, and deferrals; make required allocations and determinations; and maintain Participant account records.
  - Compute and certify payment amounts and types to Participants/Beneficiaries, and determine payment timing and method.
  - Authorize disbursements and maintain necessary administrative records.
  - Issue rules consistent with the Plan and delegate duties to others.
  - Establish or change phantom investment options under Article V.
  - Hire agents, accountants, actuaries, consultants, and legal counsel.
  - Ensure compliance with Company insider trading policies (subject to Section 7.07 regarding Section 409A), including permitting the Plan Administrator or Recordkeeper to adjust effective dates of intra-fund transfers or distribution dates of deferrals.

nodes.title: Plan Administrator
nodes.heading: 7.01 Plan Administrator:
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator is responsible for the administration of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Plan Administrator as the party responsible for administering and managing the Plan, with authority to delegate specified responsibilities (delegations must define scope and comply with Section 7.06).
- Allows the Plan Administrator to act under procedures it adopts or those deemed legally permissible by the Company’s Law Department.
- Grants broad discretionary authority to interpret and administer the Plan; determine eligibility, participation, and deferrals; make required allocations and determinations; and maintain participant account records.
- Authorizes computation, certification, and timing/method of benefit payments to participants and beneficiaries, and approval of all Plan disbursements.
- Permits creation and publication of administrative rules consistent with the Plan and maintenance of all necessary records.
- Allows further delegation of duties to individuals or entities and the hiring of agents, accountants, actuaries, consultants, and legal counsel.
- Empowers establishment or modification of phantom investment options under Article V.
- Authorizes the Plan Administrator or Recordkeeper to take actions to ensure compliance with the Company’s insider trading policy, including altering effective dates of intra-fund transfers or distribution dates of deferrals, subject to Section 7.07 (Section 409A compliance).

nodes.title: Action
nodes.heading: 7.02 Action:
nodes.start_phrase: Action by the Plan Administrator may be taken in accordance with procedures that the Plan Administrator adopts from time to time or that the Company’ s Law Department determines are legally permissible.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Plan Administrator as the party responsible for overall plan administration, with authority to delegate specified responsibilities (subject to Section 7.06) and to act under procedures it adopts or that the Company’s Law Department deems permissible.
- Grants broad discretionary powers to the Plan Administrator (and permissible delegates) to interpret and administer the plan; determine eligibility, participation, deferrals, allocations; maintain participant account records; compute, certify, and schedule benefit payments; and authorize disbursements.
- Empowers the Plan Administrator to maintain records, issue administrative rules, delegate duties to others, establish or change phantom investment options (Article V), and retain professional advisors (agents, accountants, actuaries, consultants, legal counsel).
- Permits the Plan Administrator or Recordkeeper to take actions necessary to comply with the Company’s insider trading policy, including adjusting effective dates of intra-fund transfers and distribution dates of deferrals, provided such actions remain consistent with Section 7.07 (Section 409A compliance).

nodes.title: Powers of the Plan Administrator
nodes.heading: 7.03 Powers of the Plan Administrator:
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator shall administer and manage the Plan and shall have (and shall be permitted to delegate) all powers necessary to accomplish that purpose, including the following:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Plan Administrator’s role, including authority to administer the Plan and to delegate responsibilities, with delegations specifying scope and being subject to Section 7.06.
- Allows actions by the Plan Administrator pursuant to its own adopted procedures or those deemed legally permissible by the Company’s Law Department.
- Grants broad, discretionary powers to the Plan Administrator (and its delegates), including:
  - Interpreting and construing the Plan.
  - Deciding eligibility, participation, and deferral matters; making allocations and required determinations; maintaining participant account records.
  - Computing, certifying, and determining the timing and manner of benefit payments; authorizing disbursements.
  - Keeping necessary records; issuing Plan rules consistent with the Plan.
  - Delegating duties; establishing or changing phantom investment options under Article V.
  - Retaining advisors (agents, accountants, actuaries, consultants, legal counsel).
  - Taking actions to comply with Company insider trading policies, including altering effective dates of intra-fund transfers or distribution dates for Deferral Subaccounts, with minimal necessary disruption and subject to Section 7.07 (Section 409A compliance).
- Confirms the Plan Administrator’s exclusive and absolute discretion; benefits are payable only if it determines eligibility. Its decisions are final, conclusive, and binding; it may consider Company intent in interpreting provisions. Court review is under the arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.
- Provides that the Plan Administrator serves without bond or compensation; Plan and administration expenses are paid by Employers and may be charged to specific participant accounts. Committee members and delegates are not liable for others’ acts or for their own non-willful acts; Employers (other than the Company) indemnify Committee members and certain Company/affiliate employees serving as delegates for expenses and liabilities, including legal fees, arising from their service.
- Requires the Employer to withhold and/or collect applicable federal, state, and local taxes (including Social Security and Medicare) on deferred or accrued amounts, and to report deferrals and any taxable amounts on Form W-2 in accordance with Section 409A.

nodes.title: Compensation, Indemnity and Liability
nodes.heading: 7.04 Compensation, Indemnity and Liability:
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator will serve without bond and without compensation for services hereunder .
nodes.summary:
- Subaccounts may be adjusted with minimal disruption to normal Plan operations.
- The Plan Administrator (Committee) has exclusive, absolute, and discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility and benefits, and make all required determinations; benefits are paid only if the Administrator decides the applicant is entitled to them.
- The Administrator’s decisions are final, conclusive, and binding on all parties and will be reviewed by courts only under an arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.
- In making determinations, the Administrator may consider the Company’s intent regarding Plan provisions, even if other documents do not expressly contemplate consideration of such intent; the Administrator is accorded maximum possible discretion.
- The Plan Administrator serves without bond or compensation; all Plan and administrative expenses are paid by the Employers and may, if deemed appropriate, be charged to specific Participant Accounts.
- Committee members and delegated individuals are not liable for others’ acts or for their own actions absent willful misconduct; Employers (other than the Company) will indemnify them for expenses and liabilities, including reasonable legal fees, arising from Plan-related service.
- Employers must withhold required federal, state, and local taxes from Plan amounts and collect/remit Social Security and Medicare taxes on deferred/accrued amounts; deferrals and taxable amounts must be reported on Form W-2 in accordance with Section 409A rules.

nodes.title: Withholding
nodes.heading: 7.05 Withholding:
nodes.start_phrase: The Employer shall withhold from amounts due under this Plan, any amount necessary to enable the Employer to remit to the appropriate government entity or entities on behalf of the Participant as may be required by the federal income tax provisions of the Code, by an applicable state’ s income tax provisions, and by an applicable city , county or municipality’ s earnings or income tax provisions.
nodes.summary:
- Subaccounts and administrative actions may be used, with any changes kept to the minimum necessary to preserve normal Plan operations.
- Plan Administrator (the Committee) has exclusive, absolute, and discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility and benefit amounts, and make all determinations; benefits are paid only if the Administrator decides the applicant is entitled. The Administrator may consider the Company’s intent in interpreting provisions. Decisions are final, conclusive, and reviewed by courts only under an arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.
- Compensation, indemnity, and liability: the Plan Administrator serves without bond and without compensation; all Plan and administrative expenses are paid by Employers and may, if deemed appropriate, be charged to specific Participant Accounts. Committee members and delegates are not liable for others’ acts or their own except for willful misconduct. Employers (other than the Company) will indemnify Committee members and certain delegates/employees for expenses and liabilities, including legal fees, arising from their service.
- Withholding and tax reporting: the Employer must withhold required federal, state, and local taxes from Plan amounts; collect/remit Social Security and Medicare taxes on deferred or accrued amounts; and report deferrals and taxable amounts on Form W-2 in accordance with Section 409A rules and procedures.

nodes.title: Section 16 Compliance
nodes.heading: 7.06 Section 16 Compliance:
nodes.start_phrase: In General . This Plan is intended to be a formula plan for purposes of Section 16 of the Act.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Section 16 compliance by treating the plan as a “formula plan” intended to fit within Rule 16b-3, with administration by Compensation Committee delegates so initial Board Approval of the plan minimizes the need for transaction-specific approvals for Section 16 insiders.
- Defines “Covered Distributions” involving deferrals invested in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund where payment timing could create a Section 16 opposite-way match.
