Sets rules that, if Board Approval hasn’t been obtained or if the liquidation is a discretionary transaction, the distribution will be delayed only until the earlier of: (1) Board Approval of the liquidation (for non-discretionary transactions), or (2) when making the distribution would no longer violate Section 16 (e.g., the participant is no longer a Section 16 insider, the subaccount is no longer invested in the phantom stock fund, or sufficient time has elapsed to avoid a match).
- Mandates conformance with Section 409A effective January 1, 2009, while preserving the grandfathered, exempt status of deferrals under the Pre-409A Program; this compliance section controls over any conflicting plan provisions.

nodes.title: Conformance with Section 409A
nodes.heading: 7.07 Conformance with Section 409A:
nodes.start_phrase: Ef fective from and after January 1, 2009, at all times during each Plan Y ear, this Plan shall be operated (i) in accordance with the requirements of Section 409A, and (ii) to preserve the status of deferrals under the Pre-409A Program as being exempt from Section 409A, i.e., to preserve the grandfathered status of the Pre-409A Program.
nodes.summary:
- Section 16 compliance intent: The plan is designed as a “formula plan” under Section 16 of the Securities Exchange Act, administered by delegates of the Compensation Committee to allow broad Board Approval under Rule 16b‑3 to cover plan transactions and minimize the need for transaction‑specific approvals.
- Covered Distributions rules: For distributions involving amounts invested in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund that could create a matchable opposite-way transaction for a Participant subject to Section 16 (including where a Second Look Election applies or investment wasn’t locked at the original deferral), the distribution is delayed if liquidation lacks Board Approval or if it is a discretionary transaction. Payment is deferred only until the earlier of:
  - Board Approval of the liquidation (for non‑discretionary transactions), or
  - The date the payment would no longer violate Section 16 (e.g., the Participant is no longer subject to Section 16, the subaccount is no longer invested in the phantom stock fund, or sufficient time has elapsed to avoid matching).
- Section 409A conformance: Effective January 1, 2009, the plan operates in full compliance with IRC Section 409A and preserves grandfathered, pre‑409A deferrals as exempt. This 409A conformity provision controls over any conflicting plan terms.

nodes.title: CLAIMS PROCEDURE
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VIII – CLAIMS PROCEDURE
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator has the discretionary right to modify the claims process described in this Section in any manner so long as the claims review process, as modified, includes the basic steps described in this Section and Section 8.02.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Article VIII – Claims Procedure for the Plan.
- Grants the Plan Administrator discretion to modify the claims process, provided the core steps in Sections 8.01 and 8.02 are preserved.
- Defines who may file a claim (“Claimant”), including participants, putative participants, beneficiaries, and putative beneficiaries.
- Requires claims to be submitted in writing (or another acceptable form) to the Plan Administrator.
- Sets initial claim decision timeline: notice of approval/denial within 90 days, with a possible one-time 90-day extension if special circumstances are disclosed in advance.
- Specifies denial notice contents: reasons for denial, relevant Plan provisions, additional information needed to perfect the claim, and appeal steps.
- Provides appeal rights: Claimant has 60 days from denial to file a written appeal.
- Guarantees a “full and fair review” on appeal, allowing submission of comments, documents, and records, which must be considered even if not part of the initial determination.
- Sets appeal decision timeline: decision within 60 days, with a possible one-time 60-day extension for special circumstances; in all cases no later than 120 days after receipt of the appeal.
- Acknowledges COVID-19 relief: effective March 1, 2020 through at least November 1, 2022, federal Agencies extended certain Plan deadlines under ERISA §518 and Code §7508A(b) (EBSA Disaster Relief Notices 2020-01, 2021-01, and related guidance). Up to one year may be disregarded in calculating applicable timeframes, with the relief ending on the earlier of specific agency-defined dates (the excerpt’s sentence ends mid-clause).

nodes.title: Claims for Benefits
nodes.heading: 8.01 Claims for Benefits:
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator has the discretionary right to modify the claims process described in this Section in any manner so long as the claims review process, as modified, includes the basic steps described in this Section and Section 8.02.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Article VIII – Claims Procedure, outlining how to file and appeal benefit claims.
- Grants the Plan Administrator discretion to modify the claims process, provided the core steps in Sections 8.01 and 8.02 are maintained.
- Defines eligible “Claimants” broadly (participants, putative participants, beneficiaries, putative beneficiaries, and others).
- Requires claims to be submitted in writing (or another acceptable form) to the Plan Administrator.
- Initial claim determinations:
  - Denial notice due within 90 days of receipt, with one possible additional 90-day extension for special circumstances, with advance written notice stating reasons.
  - Denial notices must include the reasons, relevant Plan provisions, information needed to perfect the claim, and appeal procedures.
- Appeals of denied claims:
  - Claimant must file a written appeal within 60 days of receiving the denial.
  - Plan Administrator must provide a full and fair review, allowing submission of comments, documents, and records, considered even if not included initially.
  - Appeal decision due within 60 days, with one possible additional 60-day extension for special circumstances, with advance notice; in all cases, a decision no later than 120 days after receipt of the appeal.
  - Appeal decision notice must state the basis for the decision.
- COVID-19 deadline relief:
  - Notes DOL, Treasury, and IRS guidance effective March 1, 2020 through at least November 1, 2022, under ERISA §518 and Code §7508A(b), and EBSA Disaster Relief Notices 2020-01 and 2021-01.
  - Provides that up to one year may be disregarded for determining deadlines for plans, sponsors, administrators, participants, and beneficiaries due to the COVID-19 outbreak.
  - Plan will comply with these extensions as required; relief end-point language is introduced but truncated in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Appeals of Denied Claims
nodes.heading: 8.02 Appeals of Denied Claims:
nodes.start_phrase: Each Claimant whose claim for benefits has been denied may file a written appeal for a review of his or her claim by the Plan Administrator .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Plan Administrator’s discretion to modify the claims process, provided core steps in Sections 8.01 and 8.02 are preserved.
- Outlines initial claims process:
  - Claims must be submitted in writing (or another acceptable form) to the Plan Administrator.
  - Decision due within 90 days; may extend once for an additional 90 days with prior written notice stating special circumstances.
  - Denial notices must state the reasons, cite relevant Plan provisions, identify additional needed information, and explain appeal steps.
- Details appeal rights and procedures:
  - Claimant has 60 days from denial to file a written appeal.
  - Entitles Claimant to a full and fair review, including submitting comments, documents, and records, whether or not part of the initial determination.
  - Decision due within 60 days; may extend once for an additional 60 days with notice; in all cases no later than 120 days from appeal receipt. Decision notices must state the basis for the determination.
- Provides COVID-19 deadline relief:
  - Plan will follow DOL, Treasury, and IRS guidance permitting up to a one-year “disregarded period” for certain deadlines (including ERISA claims procedure deadlines and Plan notices/disclosures).
  - Relief ends on the earlier of one year from when relief first applied to the person or 60 days after the end of the National Emergency/Outbreak Period; no disregarded period exceeds one year; Outbreak Period ongoing as of November 1, 2022.
- Limits external review:
  - Any court, arbitrator, or tribunal review is limited to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator at the time of its determination.
  - Notices to claimants may be sent using methods permitted under DOL Reg. 2520.104b-1 or other applicable guidance.
- Sets special procedures for disability claims:
  - Disability-related claims and appeals follow DOL Reg. 2560.503-1 provisions specific to disability benefits (including cited subsections).
- Clarifies scope of discretion:
  - Specific references to the Plan Administrator’s discretion do not limit broader discretionary authority elsewhere in the Plan.
- Requires exhaustion of administrative remedies:
  - Claimants must fully exhaust the Plan’s claims procedures before filing in court or another tribunal.
  - Exhaustion is interpreted broadly; it is not excused for:
    - Failing to clearly submit a claim to the Plan Administrator, or
    - Failing to fulfill document requests unless strict conditions are met (ERISA requires the documents; written request addressed to and received by the Plan Administrator; failure to provide within six months or a reasonable longer period; and clear assertion of ERISA rights). Individuals not treated as Participants must clearly assert entitlement to Participant status.
  - Post-exhaustion litigation or review is, to the maximum extent permissible, limited to the administrative record.

nodes.title: Special Claims Procedures for Disability Determinations
nodes.heading: 8.03 Special Claims Procedures for Disability Determinations:
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding Sections 8.01 and 8.02, if the claim or appeal of the Claimant relates to Disability benefits, such claim or appeal shall be processed pursuant to the applicable provisions of Department of Labor Regulation Section 2560.503-1 relating to Disability benefits, including Sections 2560.503-1(d), 2560.503-1(f)(3), 2560.503-1(h)(4) and 2560.503-1(i)(3).
nodes.summary:
- Temporary deadline relief during the COVID-19 Outbreak Period: plan-related notices, disclosures, and ERISA claims procedure deadlines are tolled for the earlier of 1 year from when a person first became eligible for relief or 60 days after the National Emergency ends (still ongoing as of November 1, 2022). Notices may be delivered using DOL Reg. 2520.104b-1 methods.
- Any court, arbitration, or tribunal review of a claim is limited to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator at the time of decision and is conditioned on full exhaustion of plan remedies.
- Disability benefit claims and appeals follow the special procedures in DOL Reg. 2560.503-1, including subsections (d), (f)(3), (h)(4), and (i)(3).
- References to the Plan Administrator’s discretion do not limit the breadth of that discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Claimants must exhaust the Plan’s claims procedures before filing in court; the exhaustion requirement is to be interpreted as broadly as possible. Exhaustion is not excused unless strict conditions are met (e.g., clear, written ERISA document requests not fulfilled within a reasonable time, and clear indication of participant status or claim submission).
- After exhaustion, any judicial or tribunal review remains limited, to the maximum extent permissible, to the record before the Plan Administrator.

nodes.title: Effect of Specific References
nodes.heading: 8.04 Effect of Specific References:
nodes.start_phrase: Specific references in the Plan to the Plan Administrator ’s discretion shall create no inference that the Plan Administrator ’s discretion in any other respect, or in connection with any other provision, is less complete or broad.
nodes.summary:
- Temporary deadline relief tied to the COVID-19 National Emergency (Outbreak Period): certain plan notice/disclosure and ERISA claims-procedure deadlines are tolled, with any disregarded period capped at 1 year; Outbreak Period ongoing as of November 1, 2022.
- Court, arbitration, or tribunal review of claims is limited to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator at the time of its decision, contingent on the claimant’s full exhaustion of plan remedies.
- Claim-related notices may be delivered using methods approved under DOL Reg. 2520.104b-1.
- Disability benefit claims and appeals follow the special DOL Reg. 2560.503-1 procedures (including specified subsections).
- The Plan Administrator’s discretionary authority is broad; specific references do not limit discretion elsewhere in the plan.
- Mandatory exhaustion of the plan’s claims procedures before any lawsuit or tribunal action; the exhaustion requirement is to be interpreted as broadly as possible.
- Exhaustion is not excused unless the claimant clearly submitted a claim; document-request failures excuse exhaustion only if ERISA requires the documents, the written request was received by the Plan Administrator, the documents were not provided within 6 months (or a reasonable longer period), and the requester clearly asserted ERISA rights; non-participants must clearly claim entitlement to participant status.
- After exhaustion, any judicial or tribunal review remains limited, to the maximum extent permissible, to the existing administrative record.

nodes.title: Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court
nodes.heading: 8.05 Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court:
nodes.start_phrase: Before filing any Claim (including a suit or other action) in court or in another tribunal, a Claimant must first fully exhaust all of the Claimant’ s rights under the claims procedures of this Article.
nodes.summary:
- Provides COVID-19 Outbreak Period relief for Plan deadlines and notices/disclosures: certain timeframes are tolled until the earlier of one year from when a person first became eligible for relief or 60 days after the National Emergency ends (still ongoing as of Nov. 1, 2022), with a maximum disregarded period of one year.
- States that any judicial, arbitral, or tribunal review of a Plan claim is limited to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator at the time of determination; notices to claimants may be sent using methods approved under DOL Reg. 2520.104b-1.
- Establishes special claims and appeals procedures for disability benefits in accordance with DOL Reg. 2560.503-1, including specified subsections.
- Clarifies that specific references to the Plan Administrator’s discretion do not limit the breadth of its overall discretionary authority.
- Imposes a strict exhaustion requirement: claimants must fully exhaust Plan claims procedures before filing in court or another forum; exhaustion is to be interpreted as broadly as possible and is a contractual precondition to any recovery related to the Plan.
- Details when exhaustion will not be excused, including standards for recognizing a claim submission and strict conditions for document requests (written, directed to and received by the Plan Administrator, ERISA-required, reasonable response period).
- Limits post-exhaustion judicial or tribunal review to the record considered in the claims procedure.
- Confirms exhaustion applies even if other, non-claim disputes are at issue, to rights provided in novel situations, to actual or potential rights, and even where specific procedures have not yet been defined (the Plan Administrator will establish or analogize procedures).
- Allows the Plan Administrator to make special arrangements for class-based consideration or to address conflicts to preserve the exhaustion requirement.
- Defines key terms:
  - Dispute: any claim, dispute, issue, assertion, action, or related matter.
  - Claim: disputes involving Plan interpretation, validity of adoption, administration, ERISA compliance, benefit recovery, fiduciary breach, or similar/related matters as determined by the Plan Administrator.
  - Claimant: employees, former employees, participants, beneficiaries, their spouses/former spouses, estates/heirs/representatives, and related individuals or groups asserting a Claim.
- Affirms the Plan’s intent to operate in good faith and consistently with ERISA, emphasizing uniform resolution of claims and avoidance of unnecessary litigation through comprehensive exhaustion.

nodes.title: Limitations on Actions
nodes.heading: 8.06 Limitations on Actions:
nodes.start_phrase: Effective for claims and actions filed on or after April 1, 2016, any claim filed under Article VIII and any action filed in state or federal court by or on behalf of a former or current Employee, Participant, beneficiary or any other individual, person or entity (collectively , a “Petitioner”) for the alleged wrongful denial of Plan benefits or for the alleged interference with or violation of ERISA-protected rights must be brought within two years of the date the Petitioner ’s cause of action first accrues.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes a two-year statute of limitations (effective for filings on or after April 1, 2016) for any claim under Article VIII or court action by employees, participants, beneficiaries, or others alleging wrongful denial of plan benefits or interference with ERISA rights.
- Defines when a cause of action accrues:
  - For benefit claims: the earliest of (i) receipt of the benefits calculation at issue, (ii) the payment commencement date identified by the Plan Administrator, or (iii) when the petitioner has actual or constructive knowledge of the facts underlying the claim.
  - For interference with ERISA rights: when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the alleged interfering acts.
- States that failing to file within the two-year period bars the petitioner and any representative from bringing the claim.
- Clarifies that correspondence or communications after completing the mandatory appeals process do not extend or affect the two-year limitations period.
- Imposes a venue restriction (effective for claims/actions filed on or after January 1, 2019): any court or tribunal action related to the Plan must be brought exclusively in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

nodes.title: Restriction on Venue
nodes.heading: 8.07 Restriction on Venue:
nodes.start_phrase: Any claim or action filed in court or any other tribunal in connection with the Plan by or on behalf of a Petitioner (as defined in Section 8.06 above) shall only be brought or filed in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, ef fective for claims or actions filed on or after January 1, 2019.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes a two-year statute of limitations for ERISA-related claims (wrongful denial of Plan benefits or interference with ERISA-protected rights) for claims/actions filed on or after April 1, 2016.
- Defines when a cause of action accrues:
  - Benefits claims: no later than the earliest of (i) receipt of the benefit calculation at issue, (ii) the payment commencement date identified by the Plan Administrator, or (iii) the Petitioner’s actual or constructive knowledge of the underlying facts.
  - Interference claims: when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the alleged interfering acts.
- Failure to file within two years bars the Petitioner or any representative from bringing the claim; communications after the mandatory appeals process do not extend or affect the two-year period.
- “Petitioner” includes former/current employees, participants, beneficiaries, and any other individual, person, or entity acting on their behalf.
- Sets exclusive venue for litigation: all Plan-related court or tribunal actions by or on behalf of a Petitioner must be filed only in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, effective for filings on or after January 1, 2019.

nodes.title: AMENDMENT AND TERMINATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE IX– AMENDMENT AND TERMINATION
nodes.start_phrase: The Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company , or its delegate or delegates, has the right in its sole discretion to amend this Plan in whole or in part at any time and in any manner , including the manner of making deferral elections, the terms on which distributions are made, and the form and timing of distributions.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article IX outlines how the plan may be amended or terminated, with strict protections for amounts already credited and compliance with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code.
- Amendment authority: The Compensation Committee (or its delegates) may amend the plan at any time and in any manner, including rules for deferral elections and the form, timing, and terms of distributions.
- Protection of accrued amounts: No amendment may reduce a participant’s credited account balance as of the amendment date, except for clarifying amendments necessary to avoid an inappropriate windfall.
- Delegation: Effective September 25, 2019, the Company’s Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer (or equivalent acting role) is delegated authority to amend the plan, except for provisions related to Section 7.06 matters.
- Formalities and binding effect: Amendments must be in writing and adopted by the Committee or its delegates; all participants and beneficiaries are bound by them.
- Section 409A compliance: All amendments are subject to restrictions necessary to maintain compliance with Section 409A.
- Termination rights: The Company, through the Compensation Committee or the full Board, may discontinue or terminate the plan at any time, in whole or in part, including in response to tax law changes.
- No reduction of balances on termination: Termination (full or partial) cannot reduce amounts already credited to participant accounts; the termination resolution must specify distribution methods for existing balances.
- Change in Control distributions: Subject to Section 409A, the Company retains maximum permissible discretion to terminate the plan and make distributions in connection with a Section 409A-defined Change in Control; the stated terms are the exclusive basis for distributions tied to any change in control for deferrals under this 409A program.

nodes.title: Amendment of Plan
nodes.heading: 9.01 Amendment of Plan:
nodes.start_phrase: The Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company , or its delegate or delegates, has the right in its sole discretion to amend this Plan in whole or in part at any time and in any manner , including the manner of making deferral elections, the terms on which distributions are made, and the form and timing of distributions.
nodes.summary:
- Grants the Compensation Committee (or its delegates) broad authority to amend the Plan at any time, including rules for deferral elections and distribution form/timing.
- Protects vested amounts: amendments cannot reduce amounts already credited to participants’ accounts, except for clarifying changes necessary to prevent an inappropriate windfall.
- Delegates, as of September 25, 2019, amendment authority to the Company’s EVP & Chief Human Resources Officer (or acting equivalent), excluding provisions related to matters covered by Section 7.06.
- Requires all amendments to be in writing and adopted by the Committee or its delegates; all participants and beneficiaries are bound by such amendments.
- Subjects all amendments to Section 409A compliance constraints.
- Reserves the Company’s right, through the Compensation Committee or full Board, to terminate the Plan at any time, in whole or in part, for any reason (including tax law changes).
- Ensures termination (including partial termination) is binding on affected participants but cannot reduce amounts already credited; termination resolution must specify how credited amounts will be distributed.
- Affirms that termination provisions are also subject to Section 409A; provides maximum permitted discretion to terminate and make distributions upon a Section 409A-defined Change in Control.
- States that the specified Change in Control provision is the exclusive basis for distributions related to a change in control for deferrals under this 409A program.

nodes.title: Termination of Plan
nodes.heading: 9.02 Termination of Plan:
nodes.start_phrase: (a) The Company expects to continue this Plan, but does not obligate itself to do so.
nodes.summary:
- Amendment of the Plan (Article IX, 9.01):
  - The Compensation Committee (or its delegates) may amend the Plan at any time and in any manner, including deferral election methods and distribution terms/form/timing.
  - No amendment may reduce amounts already credited to a Participant’s Account, except for clarifying changes to avoid inappropriate windfalls.
  - As of September 25, 2019, the Company’s EVP and Chief Human Resources Officer (or functional successor) is delegated authority to amend the Plan, except for matters subject to Section 7.06.
  - Amendments must be in writing and adopted by the Committee or its delegates; all Participants and Beneficiaries are bound.
  - All amendments must comply with Section 409A.

- Termination of the Plan (Article IX, 9.02):
  - The Company may terminate or partially terminate the Plan at any time via the Compensation Committee or the full Board, including in response to tax law changes.
  - Termination cannot reduce amounts already credited to Participant Accounts; the termination resolution will specify distribution methods for credited amounts.
  - Termination and any related distributions must comply with Section 409A.
  - The Company retains maximum discretionary authority, to the extent permitted by Section 409A, to terminate and make distributions in connection with a Change in Control (as defined in Section 409A); these are the exclusive terms for change-in-control distributions under this 409A program.

- Limitation on Participant Rights (Article X, 10.01):
  - Participation does not guarantee continued employment or confer rights in employer assets beyond Plan provisions.
  - Employers may terminate employment without liability under the Plan, other than paying deferrals as provided.

- Unfunded Status and Employer Liability (Article X, 10.02):
  - The Plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the general assets of the Participant’s individual Employer.
  - Participants and Beneficiaries have no property interest in specific assets and are general unsecured creditors of the individual Employer; no other Employer guarantees or shares the obligation.
  - Upon transfer between Employers within the organization, liability for prior deferrals shifts to the new Employer; if transferring outside the PepsiCo Organization, liability remains with the last PepsiCo Employer.
  - For this section, “Employer” refers only to entities within the PepsiCo Organization.

- Coordination with Other Plans (Article X, 10.03):
  - The Plan does not affect eligibility for or benefits under other employer benefit plans unless those plans state otherwise or to prevent jeopardizing favorable tax status.

- Receipt and Release (Article X, 10.04):
  - Payments made under the Plan satisfy claims to the extent paid; the Plan Administrator may require a signed receipt and release as a condition of payment.

- Governing Law (Article X, 10.05):
  - The Plan is governed by applicable federal law and, where not preempted, by other applicable law (state law reference incomplete in excerpt).

nodes.title: MISCELLANEOUS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE X – MISCELLANEOUS
nodes.start_phrase: Participation in this Plan does not give any Participant the right to be retained in the Employer ’s employ (or any right or interest in this Plan or any assets of the Employer other than as herein provided).
nodes.summary:
- Participation in the plan does not confer employment rights or any ownership interest in employer assets; employers may terminate employment without plan-related liability beyond paying due deferrals.
- The plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the individual employer’s general assets. Participants and beneficiaries are general unsecured creditors with no priority over other unsecured creditors and no rights to specific assets.
- No cross-employer guarantees exist. When moving between PepsiCo employers, liability for prior deferrals transfers to the new employer; if moving to a non-PepsiCo entity, liability for prior deferrals remains with the last PepsiCo employer.
- Participation does not limit rights to other benefit plans unless those plans state otherwise or to preserve their tax-favored status.
- Payments made under the plan satisfy related claims to the extent paid; the plan administrator may require a receipt and release as a condition of payment.
- The plan is governed by applicable federal law and, where not preempted, additional applicable law (state law not specified in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Limitation on Participant’s Rights
nodes.heading: 10.01 Limitation on Participant’s Rights:
nodes.start_phrase: Participation in this Plan does not give any Participant the right to be retained in the Employer ’s employ (or any right or interest in this Plan or any assets of the Employer other than as herein provided).
nodes.summary:
- Article X – Miscellaneous provisions of a deferred compensation plan.
- Limitation on rights: Participation does not confer any right to continued employment or interest in employer assets beyond plan terms; employer may terminate employment without plan liability other than owed deferrals.
- Unfunded status: Benefits are paid from the individual employer’s general assets; no trust or segregation of assets; participants and beneficiaries are general unsecured creditors with no priority over other creditors.
- Employer liability: No cross-guarantee among employers; only the participant’s own employer is liable. On transfers within the PepsiCo Organization, liability for prior deferrals moves to the new employer; if transferring to a non-PepsiCo entity, liability remains with the last PepsiCo employer.
- Coordination with other plans: Rights to participate in other benefit plans are unaffected unless those plans state otherwise or compliance/tax-favored status would be compromised.
- Receipt and release: Payments to a participant satisfy claims against the plan administrator, recordkeeper, company, and employers to that extent; administrator may require a signed receipt/release as a condition of payment.
- Governing law: Plan is governed by applicable federal law and, where not preempted, by additional law (state law reference truncated).

nodes.title: Unfunded Obligation of Individual Employer
nodes.heading: 10.02 Unfunded Obligation of Individual Employer:
nodes.start_phrase: (a) The benefits provided by this Plan are unfunded.
nodes.summary:
- Article X – Miscellaneous outlines general legal and administrative provisions of the plan.
- 10.01 Limitation on Participant’s Rights: Participation does not guarantee continued employment or any rights in employer assets beyond those provided by the plan; the employer may terminate employment without plan-related liability other than paying due deferrals.
- 10.02 Unfunded Obligation: The plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the individual employer’s general assets. Participants and beneficiaries have no property interest in specific assets and are general unsecured creditors. No employer guarantees another’s obligations. Liability transfers between employers within the PepsiCo Organization upon an internal transfer; if a participant moves to a non-PepsiCo entity, liability for prior deferrals stays with the last PepsiCo employer.
- 10.03 Other Plans: Participation does not affect rights to other benefit plans unless those plans provide otherwise or tax-favored status would be jeopardized.
- 10.04 Receipt or Release: Payments constitute satisfaction of claims to the extent paid; the Plan Administrator may require a receipt and release as a condition of payment.
- 10.05 Governing Law: The plan is governed by applicable federal law and, to the extent not preempted, additional law (specific jurisdiction not shown in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Other Plans
nodes.heading: 10.03 Other Plans:
nodes.start_phrase: This Plan shall not af fect the right of any Eligible Executive or Participant to participate in and receive benefits under and in accordance with the provisions of any other employee benefit plans which are now or hereafter maintained by any Employer , unless the terms of such other employee benefit plan or plans specifically provide otherwise or it would cause such other plan to violate a requirement for tax favored treatment.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies that participation does not guarantee continued employment or rights to employer assets; participants only have rights to payment of deferrals as provided.
- States the plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the general assets of the participant’s individual employer, and participants are general unsecured creditors with no priority over other creditors.
- Limits liability to the participant’s individual employer within the PepsiCo Organization; no cross-guarantees by other employers. On internal transfers, liability for prior deferrals moves to the new PepsiCo employer; if transferring outside the PepsiCo Organization, liability remains with the last PepsiCo employer.
- Confirms that participation in this plan does not affect eligibility for other employee benefit plans unless those plans state otherwise or tax-favored status would be jeopardized.
- Provides that payments made under the plan fully satisfy related claims, and the plan administrator may require a receipt and release from participants as a condition of payment.
- Governing law is applicable federal law, and where not preempted, applicable state law (provision appears truncated in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Receipt or Release
nodes.heading: 10.04 Receipt or Release:
nodes.start_phrase: Any payment to a Participant in accordance with the provisions of this Plan shall, to the extent thereof, be in full satisfaction of all claims against the Plan Administrator , the Recordkeeper , the Company , and all Employers, and the Plan Administrator may require such Participant, as a condition precedent to such payment, to execute a receipt and release to such effect.
nodes.summary:
- Article X (Miscellaneous) outlines general legal provisions of the Plan.
- Participation does not guarantee continued employment or any rights in employer assets; the employer may terminate employment, with the participant’s claim limited to payment of deferrals per the Plan (10.01).
- The Plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the general assets of the participant’s employing entity. Participants are general unsecured creditors with no interest in specific assets, no preference over other creditors, and no guarantees by other employers (10.02(a)).
- When a participant transfers between employers within the organization, liability for prior deferrals moves to the new employer; however, “Employer” is limited to entities within the PepsiCo Organization. If a participant transfers outside PepsiCo, liability for prior deferrals remains with the last PepsiCo employer (10.02(b)).
- Participation in this Plan does not affect eligibility for other employee benefit plans unless those plans state otherwise or to avoid jeopardizing tax-favored status (10.03).
- Any payment made under the Plan fully satisfies related claims against the Plan Administrator, Recordkeeper, Company, and Employers; the Administrator may require a receipt and release as a condition of payment (10.04).
- The Plan is governed by applicable federal law and, where not preempted, by additional (unspecified in the excerpt) governing law (10.05).

nodes.title: Governing Law
nodes.heading: 10.05 Governing Law:
nodes.start_phrase: This Plan shall be construed, administered, and governed in all respects in accordance with applicable federal law and, to the extent not preempted by federal law , in accordance with the laws of the State of New Y ork.
nodes.summary:
- Confirms participation does not guarantee continued employment or any property interest in employer assets; employer may terminate employment without plan liability beyond owed deferrals.
- Clarifies the plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the general assets of the participant’s own employer; participants are general unsecured creditors with no trust or specific asset rights.
- States no cross-liability among employers; on transfers within the PepsiCo Organization, deferral liabilities move to the new PepsiCo employer; if transferring to a non-PepsiCo entity, liability remains with the last PepsiCo employer.
- Preserves participants’ rights to other benefit plans unless those plans specify otherwise or tax-qualified status would be affected.
- Allows the plan administrator to require a receipt and release; payments made satisfy all related claims against the administrator, recordkeeper, company, and employers.
- Establishes governing law: applicable federal law, then New York law; includes severability of invalid provisions.
- Permits adoption by related PepsiCo divisions, subsidiaries, or affiliates at the plan administrator’s discretion; administrator’s determinations are conclusive.
- Provides interpretation rules for gender/number and clarifies that “including” means “without limitation.”
- Binds successors and assigns but strictly prohibits assignment, pledge, or garnishment of benefits (subject to limited plan exceptions); administrator may make payments pursuant to divorce or court orders as cash is paid, reducing the participant’s account.
- Allows payments to a representative or for the benefit of an incapacitated participant/beneficiary, fully discharging the plan’s liability for those payments.

nodes.title: Adoption of Plan by Related Employers
nodes.heading: 10.06 Adoption of Plan by Related Employers:
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan Administrator may select as an Employer (other than the Company , which is automatically an Employer hereunder) any division of the Company , as well as any subsidiary or af filiate related to the Company by ownership (and that is a member of the PepsiCo Or ganization), and permit or cause such division, subsidiary or af filiate to adopt the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Governing law and severability: The plan is governed by New York law, and if any provision is deemed invalid, the remainder stays effective.
- Adoption by related employers: The Plan Administrator may allow divisions, subsidiaries, or affiliates within the PepsiCo Organization to adopt the plan, with the effective date and adoption requirements at the Administrator’s sole discretion; determinations are final and conclusive.
- Interpretation rules: Singular/plural and gendered terms are interchangeable; “including” is to be read as “including without limitation,” and examples do not limit scope.
- Successors and nonalienation: The plan binds parties and their successors, but participants’ account amounts cannot be assigned, transferred, pledged, or garnished (including in divorce/child support), except that the Administrator may make payments pursuant to court orders as cash is paid from a participant’s Deferral Subaccount, reducing the participant’s account.
- Facility of payment: If a participant or beneficiary is legally disabled or incapacitated, the Administrator may direct payment to the person, their legal representative, or for their benefit; such payment fully discharges the plan’s liability.

nodes.title: Gender, Tense and Examples
nodes.heading: 10.07 Gender, Tense and Examples:
nodes.start_phrase: In this Plan, whenever the context so indicates, the singular or plural number and the masculine, feminine, or neuter gender shall be deemed to include the other .
nodes.summary:
- Governing law and severability: The plan is governed by New York law; if any provision is invalid, the rest remain effective.
- Adoption by related employers: The Plan Administrator may allow any division, subsidiary, or affiliate within the PepsiCo Organization to adopt the plan, with the effective date and adoption requirements at the Administrator’s sole discretion; determinations are conclusive.
- Interpretive rules: Singular/plural and gendered terms are interchangeable as context requires; “including” and examples are to be read as “without limitation.”
- Successors and nonalienation: The plan binds parties and their successors, but participants’ benefits cannot be assigned, pledged, or otherwise transferred, including in divorce/child support contexts, except as allowed in specified sections. The Administrator may make payments pursuant to court orders from a participant’s Deferral Subaccount as cash is paid, reducing the account accordingly.
- Facility of payment: If a participant or beneficiary is legally disabled or incapacitated, the Administrator may direct payments to them, their legal representative, or for their benefit; such payments fully discharge the plan’s liability.

nodes.title: Successors and Assigns; Nonalienation of Benefits
nodes.heading: 10.08 Successors and Assigns; Nonalienation of Benefits:
nodes.start_phrase: This Plan inures to the benefit of and is binding upon the parties hereto and their successors, heirs and assigns; provided, however , that the amounts credited to the Account of a Participant are not (except as provided in Sections 5.06 and 7.05) subject in any manner to anticipation, alienation, sale, transfer , assignment, pledge, encumbrance, char ge, garnishment, execution or levy of any kind, either voluntary or involuntary , and any attempt to anticipate, alienate, sell, transfer , assign, pledge, encumber , charge or otherwise dispose of any right to any benefits payable hereunder , including, without limitation, any assignment or alienation in connection with a separation, divorce, child support or similar arrangement, will be null and void and not binding on the Plan or the Company or any Employer .
nodes.summary:
- Governing law and severability: The plan is governed by New York law; if any provision is invalid, the rest remain effective.
- Adoption by related employers: The Plan Administrator may, in its sole discretion, permit divisions, subsidiaries, or affiliates within the PepsiCo Organization to adopt the plan and determines the effective date; its determination of employer status is conclusive.
- Interpretation rules: Singular/plural and gendered terms include each other; “including” and examples are to be read as “without limitation.”
- Successors and non-alienation: The plan binds parties and their successors, but participant accounts cannot be assigned, pledged, or garnished (including in divorce/child support) except as allowed in specified sections; the Administrator may make payments pursuant to court orders tied to divorce, reducing the participant’s account accordingly.
- Facility of payment: If a participant or beneficiary is legally disabled or incapacitated, the Administrator may direct payments to the person, their legal representative, or for their benefit; such payments fully discharge the plan’s liability.

nodes.title: Facility of Payment
nodes.heading: 10.09 Facility of Payment:
nodes.start_phrase: Whenever , in the Plan Administrator ’s opinion, a Participant or Beneficiary entitled to receive any payment hereunder is under a legal disability or is incapacitated in any way so as to be unable to manage his or her financial af fairs, the Plan Administrator may direct the Employer to make payments to such person or to the legal representative of such person for his or her benefit, or to apply the payment for the benefit of such person in such manner as the Plan Administrator considers advisable.
nodes.summary:
- Governing law and severability: The plan is governed by New York law; if any provision is invalid, the remainder stays effective.
- Adoption by related employers: The Plan Administrator may designate divisions, subsidiaries, and affiliates within the PepsiCo Organization as participating Employers, set effective adoption dates, and make conclusive determinations on employer status.
- Rules of construction: Singular/plural and gender terms are interchangeable as context requires; “including” is interpreted as “including without limitation.”
- Nonalienation of benefits: Participants’ accounts cannot be assigned, pledged, garnished, or otherwise transferred (including in divorce/child support), except as permitted in specified sections; the Plan Administrator may make payments pursuant to court orders/divorce decrees as amounts are paid from a participant’s deferral subaccount, reducing the participant’s account accordingly.
- Facility of payment: If a participant or beneficiary is under a disability or otherwise unable to manage finances, payments may be made to the person, their legal representative, or applied for their benefit, fully discharging liability.
- Signature/authentication and amendment history: The 409A Program was initially adopted on November 18, 2005, amended and restated effective January 1, 2019, and again effective January 1, 2022. The document includes execution by PepsiCo’s EVP & CHRO (dated Dec. 19, 2022) and approvals from Legal and Tax leadership (dated Dec. 9, 2022).

nodes.title: SIGNATURE/AUTHENTICATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE XI – SIGNA TURE/AUTHENTICA TION
nodes.start_phrase: The 409A Program was first adopted and approved by the Compensation Committee of the Company’ s Board of Directors at the Compensation Committee’ s duly authorized meeting on November 18, 2005.
nodes.summary: Article XI confirms the signature and authentication of PepsiCo’s 409A Program. It records the program’s original adoption by the Board’s Compensation Committee on November 18, 2005, its amendment and restatement effective January 1, 2019 (authorized September 25, 2019), and a subsequent amendment and restatement effective January 1, 2022. The section includes execution by Ronald Schellekens, Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer (dated December 19, 2022), and approvals from the Law and Tax Department: Stacy Grindal, Sr. Legal Director, Compensation and Benefits Counsel (dated December 9, 2022), and Christine Griff, Vice President, Tax Counsel, Tax Department (dated December 9, 2022).

nodes.title: Purpose
nodes.heading: B.1 Purpose .
nodes.start_phrase: The purpose of this Article is to provide for a “home plan rules” approach for employees who move between, or are newly hired by , a PepsiCo Business, a PBG Business or P AS Business following the mer ger of The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc. and PepsiAmericas, Inc. into the Pepsi-Cola Metropolitan Company , Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary the Company , except as provided herein with respect to the deferral of Bonus Compensation under the Plan by PBG Executives and P AS Executives for the 2010 Plan Y ear.

Effective as of the “Effective Time.”

  - “Effective Time” tied to the respective August 3, 2009 merger agreements for PAS and PBG.
  - Defines PAS Business, PAS Executive, PBG Business, PBG Executive, and PepsiCo Business.
- Participating Employers: States that PBG and PAS Businesses are generally not Employers under the Plan, except for individuals hired by a PAS or PBG Business who were Executives immediately before their hire date.

nodes.heading: B.2 Definitions .

nodes.title: Participating Employers
nodes.heading: B.3 Participating Employers .
nodes.start_phrase: PBG Businesses and P AS Businesses are not Employers under the Plan, except with respect to:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes “home plan rules” for employees moving among PepsiCo, PBG, and PAS businesses following the mergers of The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc. and PepsiAmericas, Inc. into Pepsi-Cola Metropolitan Bottling Company, Inc.; effective as of the defined Effective Time. Includes a specific exception for 2010 bonus deferrals.
- Defines key terms for this appendix: Effective Time (by reference to the August 3, 2009 merger agreements), PAS Business/PAS Executive, PBG Business/PBG Executive, and PepsiCo Business.
- Clarifies participating employer status: PAS and PBG Businesses are generally not Employers under the Plan, except for (1) individuals hired by a PAS or PBG Business who were Executives immediately before hire, and (2) PAS/PBG Executives who elect to defer Bonus Compensation for the 2010 Plan Year and later.
- Sets eligibility rules:
  - Individuals hired by a PepsiCo Business after the Effective Time are eligible under the Plan upon meeting standard eligibility (and not eligible for another PepsiCo Organization nonqualified DC plan), unless they were employed immediately beforehand by a non-PepsiCo Business within the organization.
  - PAS/PBG Executives are generally ineligible, except that those hired by a PAS or PBG Business on/after the Effective Time who were Executives immediately before that hire may continue participating so long as they remain continuously employed within the PepsiCo Organization, as if they had remained Executives.
  - PAS/PBG Executives may defer Bonus Compensation beginning with the Plan Year starting January 1, 2010, and Base Compensation beginning with the Plan Year starting January 1, 2011, subject to the Plan’s main terms.
- Preserves Plan integrity: no special rights granted beyond those stated; does not override Section 3.04 of the main Plan.

nodes.title: Eligibility to Participate
nodes.heading: B.4 Eligibility to Participate .
nodes.start_phrase: PBG Executives and P AS Executives are eligible to participate in this Plan as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Defines eligibility and participation rules for PAS Executives and PBG Executives under a PepsiCo deferred compensation Plan.
- Individuals hired by a PepsiCo Business after the Effective Time may participate once eligibility requirements are met and generally may not participate in another PepsiCo entity’s nonqualified defined contribution plan, unless they were immediately prior employed by a PepsiCo Organization member that is not a PepsiCo Business.
- PAS and PBG Executives are generally ineligible to participate; exception: an individual hired by a PAS or PBG Business on/after the Effective Time who was an Executive immediately before that hire may continue participating for as long as continuously employed within the PepsiCo Organization, as if still an Executive.
- Deferral timing for PAS and PBG Executives: eligible to defer Bonus Compensation beginning with the performance period for the Plan Year starting January 1, 2010, and Base Compensation beginning with the Plan Year starting January 1, 2011.
- States that nothing in this section overrides Section 3.04 of the Plan or confers additional, unauthorized rights (No Special Rights clause).

nodes.title: No Special Rights
nodes.heading: B.5 No Special Rights .
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing in this Article is intended to override the provisions of Section 3.04 of the Plan or to otherwise confer any rights under the Plan not specifically authorized herein.
nodes.summary:
- Defines who is eligible to participate in the Plan after the Effective Time, focusing on hires by a PepsiCo Business who meet Plan eligibility requirements and generally excluding participation in other nonqualified defined contribution plans within the PepsiCo Organization.
- States that PBG Executives and PAS Executives are generally ineligible to participate, with an exception allowing individuals hired by a PBG or PAS Business on or after the Effective Time—who were Executives immediately before that hire—to continue participating as long as they remain continuously employed within the PepsiCo Organization.
- Establishes deferral eligibility for PAS and PBG Executives: they may defer Bonus Compensation beginning with the Performance Period tied to the Plan Year starting January 1, 2010, and Base Compensation beginning with the Plan Year starting January 1, 2011.
- Clarifies that nothing in this article grants special rights beyond the Plan’s main provisions, nor does it override Section 3.04.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE C – PARTICIPANTS AFFECTED BY JANUARY 20, 2022 TRANSACTION
nodes.heading: APPENDIX AR TICLE C – P ARTICIP ANTS AFFECTED BY JANUAR Y 20, 2022 TRANSACTION
nodes.start_phrase: This Article C provides for the termination and liquidation, in accordance with T reasury Regulation § 1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), of the portion of the 409A Program that relates to certain Participants who are af fected by the “Closing” of the “T ransaction” (as those terms are defined below).
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Establishes the termination and liquidation of the portion of the 409A Program applicable to participants affected by a change in control resulting from a specified transaction, effective as of the transaction’s Closing, in accordance with Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).

- Key definitions:
  - Affected Participant: A participant who experiences a change in control due to the Closing under §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).
  - Agreement: The Unit Purchase Agreement dated August 2, 2021 among PepsiCo, Inc., Bengal Beverages LP, Bengal Debt Merger Sub, LLC, and Naked Juice Co.
  - Closing: As defined in Section 2.3 of the Agreement.
  - Transaction: The set of transactions under the Agreement resulting in a change in control within the meaning of §1.409A-3(i)(5) for certain PepsiCo businesses.

- Termination mechanics:
  - The 409A Program is intended to be irrevocably terminated with respect to all Affected Participants effective January 18, 2023 (12 months after the Closing).
  - The plan sponsor may revoke the termination through January 17, 2023; absent timely revocation, the termination becomes irrevocable on January 18, 2023 pursuant to §1.409A-3.

- Distribution terms:
  - Upon irrevocable termination, each Affected Participant will receive a single lump-sum payment of their entire unpaid 409A Program interest on January 1, 2024, and in any event no later than January 17, 2024, in full compliance with §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).
  - The lump sum includes all remaining installments or other future-dated distributions otherwise payable.
  - Valuation for the January 1, 2024 payment follows the 409A Program’s standard lump-sum valuation rules in effect on that date.

nodes.title: Scope
nodes.heading: C.1 Scope .
nodes.start_phrase: This Article C provides for the termination and liquidation, in accordance with T reasury Regulation § 1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), of the portion of the 409A Program that relates to certain Participants who are af fected by the “Closing” of the “T ransaction” (as those terms are defined below).
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Terminates and liquidates the portion of the 409A Program covering participants affected by a change in control resulting from the Transaction’s Closing, in compliance with Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B). Article C is effective as of the Closing.

- Key definitions:
  - Affected Participant: Any participant who experiences the change in control due to the Closing, as defined under §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).
  - Agreement: Unit Purchase Agreement dated August 2, 2021 among PepsiCo, Inc., Bengal Beverages LP, Bengal Debt Merger Sub, LLC, and Naked Juice Co.
  - Closing: Consummation of the Transaction per Section 2.3 of the Agreement.
  - Transaction: The transactions under the Agreement that cause a change in control under §1.409A-3(i)(5) for certain PepsiCo businesses.

- Termination mechanics:
  - The 409A Program is intended to be irrevocably terminated for Affected Participants effective January 18, 2023 (12 months after the Closing).
  - The plan sponsor may revoke this termination through January 17, 2023; absent timely revocation, the termination becomes irrevocable on January 18, 2023 pursuant to §1.409A-3.

- Distribution mechanics:
  - Upon irrevocable termination, each Affected Participant will receive a single lump-sum payment of their entire unpaid 409A Program interest on January 1, 2024, and in any event no later than January 17, 2024, in full conformity with §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).
  - The lump sum includes all remaining installments or other future-dated distributions.
  - Amounts are valued using the Program’s standard lump-sum valuation rules in effect on January 1, 2024.

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading: C.2 Definitions .
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this Appendix Article C with initial capitals, they shall have the meaning set forth below unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
nodes.summary: Appendix Article C outlines the termination and liquidation of the portion of the 409A Program for participants affected by the change in control resulting from the “Transaction” consummated at the “Closing.” It defines key terms, including Affected Participant (those experiencing the change in control under Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B)), the Agreement (the August 2, 2021 Unit Purchase Agreement among PepsiCo, Inc., Bengal Beverages LP, Bengal Debt Merger Sub, LLC, and Naked Juice Co.), Closing (as in Section 2.3 of the Agreement), and Transaction (a change in control under §1.409A-3(i)(5) for certain former PepsiCo businesses). The 409A Program is intended to be irrevocably terminated for Affected Participants effective January 18, 2023 (12 months after the Closing), with the plan sponsor retaining the right to revoke this termination through January 17, 2023. If not revoked, this action becomes the irrevocable step to terminate and liquidate Affected Participants’ entire interests under §1.409A-3. Upon irrevocable termination, each Affected Participant will receive a single lump-sum payment of their entire unpaid interest on January 1, 2024, and in any case no later than January 17, 2024, in full compliance with §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B). The lump sum includes all remaining installments or future-dated distributions and will be valued under the program’s standard lump-sum valuation rules in effect on the distribution date.

nodes.title: The Termination
nodes.heading: C.3 The T ermination .
nodes.start_phrase: Pursuant to this Article C, the 409A Program is intended to be irrevocably terminated with respect to all Af fected Participants ef fective as of January 18, 2023 ( i.e., 12 months after the date of the Closing).
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Establishes the termination and liquidation of the portion of the company’s Section 409A deferred compensation program applicable to participants affected by the “Closing” of a specified transaction, effective as of the Closing, in accordance with Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).

- Key definitions:
  - “Affected Participant”: A participant who experiences a change in control due to the Closing under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).
  - “Agreement”: The Unit Purchase Agreement dated August 2, 2021 among PepsiCo, Inc., Bengal Beverages LP, Bengal Debt Merger Sub, LLC, and Naked Juice Co.
  - “Closing”: The consummation of the transaction as defined in Section 2.3 of the Agreement.
  - “Transaction”: The set of transactions under the Agreement that constitute a change in control within Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(i)(5) for certain PepsiCo businesses.

- Termination mechanics:
  - The 409A Program is intended to be irrevocably terminated for all Affected Participants effective January 18, 2023 (12 months after the Closing).
  - The plan sponsor retains the absolute right to revoke this termination through January 17, 2023; absent timely revocation, the termination becomes irrevocable on January 18, 2023 under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3.

- Distribution provisions:
  - Upon irrevocable termination, each Affected Participant will receive a single lump-sum payment of their entire unpaid interest under the 409A Program as of January 1, 2024, and in any case no later than January 17, 2024, in full compliance with Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).
  - The lump sum includes all remaining installments or amounts otherwise payable in the future.
  - Amounts are valued using the program’s regular lump-sum valuation rules in effect on the January 1, 2024 distribution date.

nodes.title: Distributions
nodes.heading: C.4 Distributions .
nodes.start_phrase: Provided the termination pursuant to Section C.3 above becomes irrevocable, and to carry out the liquidation of the Af fected Participants’ entire interests, each Af fected Participant will be paid the Participant’ s entire unpaid interest under the 409A Program as a single lump sum as of January 1, 2024 and, in any case, not later than January 17, 2024 (and otherwise in full conformity with T reasury Regulation § 1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B)).

It defines key terms, including “Affected Participant,” the “Agreement” (a Unit Purchase Agreement dated August 2, 2021 among PepsiCo, Inc., Bengal Beverages LP, Bengal Debt Merger Sub, LLC, and Naked Juice Co.), “Closing,” and the “Transaction” (a change in control under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(i)(5)). The plan’s 409A Program for Affected Participants is intended to be irrevocably terminated effective January 18, 2023 (12 months after the Closing), with the plan sponsor retaining the right to revoke through January 17, 2023; absent revocation, termination and liquidation proceed under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B). structure.title: PEPSICO, INC. SUBSIDIARIES (as of December 31, 2022)
structure.heading:
EXHIBIT 21
PEPSICO, INC. SUBSIDIARIES (as of December 31, 2022)
structure.start_phrase: Entity Name Jurisdiction
structure.summary:
- Exhibit 21 listing of PepsiCo, Inc. subsidiaries as of December 31, 2022, presenting entity names and jurisdictions.
- Comprehensive, global coverage across hundreds of subsidiaries involved in manufacturing, bottling, concentrate production, sales and distribution, logistics, real estate, R&D, services, finance/treasury, holding, and captive insurance.
- Major brand and business families represented: Frito-Lay (including international units and trading companies), Quaker Oats, Gatorade/Stokely-Van Camp, Tropicana/Alvalle, SodaStream (global network), Walkers/Smiths, Pioneer Foods (South Africa), Sabritas and Gamesa (Mexico/LatAm), Evercrisp (Chile), Ceres Fruit Juices, Simba (South Africa), Pipers Crisps, Bare Foods, Health Warrior, BFY Brands/PopCorners, CytoSport (Muscle Milk), Smartfoods, Stacy’s, South Beach Beverage, among others.
- Extensive Pepsi-Cola operating companies across the Americas, Europe, Africa, Middle East, and Asia-Pacific (e.g., Egypt, Pakistan, Korea, Thailand, Peru, Ecuador, Honduras), plus concentrate holding/manufacturing and financing entities in jurisdictions such as Singapore, Ireland, Curacao, and Bermuda.
- Large set of “Blue Cloud Distribution” entities covering nearly every U.S. state and D.C., reflecting PepsiCo’s alcohol distribution venture.
- Significant presence of finance, holding, and service entities in Delaware (U.S.), the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Ireland, Bermuda, Cayman Islands, Cyprus, Liechtenstein, Mauritius, Curacao, Barbados, Hong Kong, and UAE, indicating treasury, structuring, and regional headquarters functions.
- Regional support and shared-services hubs noted (e.g., Europe Support Center in Spain; Global Business Services in India and Poland; Asia R&D center in China).
- Inclusion of CIS/Eastern Europe assets such as Wimm-Bill-Dann and Lebedyansky (Russia), Sandora (Ukraine), and related holdings, plus subsidiaries in Central Asia and the Caucasus.
- Overall, the document evidences PepsiCo’s diversified, multinational corporate structure spanning snacks, beverages, and nutrition across operating, distribution, and corporate support layers worldwide.

(“PepsiCo”) and each other undersigned, an of ficer or director , or both, of PepsiCo, do hereby appoint David Flavell, Cynthia A. Nastanski and Heather A. Hammond, and each of them severally , its, his or her true and lawful attorney-in-fact to execute on behalf of PepsiCo and the undersigned the following documents and any and all amendments thereto (including post-ef fective amendments) deemed necessary or appropriate by any such attorney-in-fact:
structure.summary:
- Exhibit 24 (Power of Attorney): PepsiCo, Inc. and its officers/directors grant David Flavell, Cynthia A. Nastanski, and Heather A. Hammond (each, severally) broad authority as attorneys-in-fact to execute, amend (including post-effective amendments), and file a wide range of SEC documents and related materials on PepsiCo’s behalf. These include numerous Automatic Shelf Registration Statements; various registration statements for debt securities, warrants, guarantees, and equity issued under employee benefit and incentive plans; merger-related registration statements and Schedules 13E-3 (notably for the 2009 PBG and PepsiAmericas transactions); the Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022; and other periodic and current reports (Forms 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K), exchange listing and approval filings, and related documents. The attorneys-in-fact may file with the SEC, stock exchanges, and governmental agencies, act individually, and have full substitution/revocation power. The POA may be executed in counterparts, does not revoke prior POAs, is not revoked by later POAs unless specifically stated by date, and remains valid for each attorney-in-fact until they cease to be a PepsiCo employee. Executed February 8, 2023, by PepsiCo and its CEO, CFO, Principal Accounting Officer, and all listed directors.
- Exhibit 31 (CEO Certification): Section 302-type certification by CEO Ramon L. Laguarta (dated February 8, 2023) affirming review of the Form 10-K; accuracy and completeness of disclosures; fair presentation of financial statements; design and evaluation of disclosure controls and procedures and internal control over financial reporting; disclosure of any material changes in internal control during the fourth quarter; and disclosure to auditors/audit committee of significant deficiencies, material weaknesses, and any fraud involving management or key control personnel.

structure.summary:

- States the financial statements and other financial information fairly present, in all material respects, the company’s financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows for the periods presented.
- Confirms responsibility, with the other certifying officer, for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and procedures and internal control over financial reporting.
- Asserts that such controls were designed (or overseen in their design) to ensure material information is communicated appropriately and to provide reasonable assurance on reliable financial reporting in accordance with GAAP.
- Reports that the effectiveness of disclosure controls and procedures was evaluated, with conclusions presented in the report as of period-end.
- Discloses whether any changes in internal control over financial reporting occurred during the most recent fiscal quarter that materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, those controls.
- Confirms disclosure to auditors and the audit committee of all significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting, and of any fraud (material or not) involving management or employees with significant roles in internal controls.
